### Pattern 12 — Example Mapping: Translating Rule Cards to `Rule` Blocks Systematically

Example Mapping (Matt Wynne, 2015) is the structured Three Amigos workshop format that directly maps to the Gherkin `Rule` keyword. Each yellow Story card becomes a `Feature`, each blue Rule card becomes a `Rule` block, and each green Example card becomes a `Scenario` or `Scenario Outline` row. Red Question cards become open issues tracked outside the feature file.

```typescript
// src/example-mapping/mapping-validator.ts
// Validates that all Rule cards from an Example Mapping session have corresponding
// Rule blocks in the feature file — prevents Example Mapping output from being lost

import { readFileSync } from 'fs';

interface ExampleMappingOutput {
  storyTitle: string;
  featureFile: string;
  rules: Array<{
    ruleText: string;
    examples: string[];
  }>;
}

interface ValidationResult {
  missingRules: string[];
  missingExamples: Array<{ rule: string; example: string }>;
  isValid: boolean;
}

function extractRulesFromFeatureFile(content: string): Map<string, string[]> {
  const ruleMap = new Map<string, string[]>();
  let currentRule: string | null = null;

  for (const line of content.split('\n')) {
    const trimmed = line.trim();
    const ruleMatch = trimmed.match(/^Rule:\s+(.+)$/);
    const scenarioMatch = trimmed.match(/^(?:Scenario|Example)(?:\s+Outline)?:\s+(.+)$/);

    if (ruleMatch) {
      currentRule = ruleMatch[1].trim();
      ruleMap.set(currentRule, []);
    } else if (scenarioMatch && currentRule) {
      ruleMap.get(currentRule)!.push(scenarioMatch[1].trim());
    }
  }
  return ruleMap;
}

export function validateExampleMapping(
  mappingOutput: ExampleMappingOutput
): ValidationResult {
  const featureContent = readFileSync(mappingOutput.featureFile, 'utf-8');
  const featureRules = extractRulesFromFeatureFile(featureContent);

  const missingRules: string[] = [];
  const missingExamples: Array<{ rule: string; example: string }> = [];

  for (const { ruleText, examples } of mappingOutput.rules) {
    if (!featureRules.has(ruleText)) {
      missingRules.push(ruleText);
      continue;
    }
    const featureExamples = featureRules.get(ruleText)!;
    for (const example of examples) {
      // Fuzzy match: check if any scenario title contains key words from the example
      const isPresent = featureExamples.some(fe =>
        fe.toLowerCase().includes(example.toLowerCase().slice(0, 30))
      );
      if (!isPresent) {
        missingExamples.push({ rule: ruleText, example });
      }
    }
  }

  return {
    missingRules,
    missingExamples,
    isValid: missingRules.length === 0 && missingExamples.length === 0,
  };
}
```

**Tradeoff**: Automating Example Mapping validation catches the common failure mode of conducting a good Discovery session and then losing half the agreed examples during Formulation. The validator above is fuzzy — exact title matching is brittle because Gherkin titles are more verbose than Rule card text. Use the validator as a checklist reminder in code review, not as an automated gate. The cognitive value of having the mapping session output next to the feature file outweighs the implementation overhead.

**[community] The most productive Three Amigos format for distributed teams is the YAML card format: each Rule card is a YAML file checked into the repository alongside the feature file. This creates a reviewable, diffable artifact for each discovery session. Teams that use shared Miro boards or Mural lose the Rule card output when the board expires.** [community]

### Pattern 13 — Reporting: Cucumber JSON Output to Custom CI Dashboard Integration

The Cucumber JSON formatter (`--format json:reports/cucumber.json`) produces a structured report with all test results, step timings, and attachment metadata. This output is the integration point for custom dashboards, Jira ticket updates, Slack notifications, and historical trend analysis.

```typescript
// scripts/process-cucumber-results.ts
// Post-processing pipeline: parse Cucumber JSON, post summary to Slack

interface CucumberStep {
  result: { status: 'passed' | 'failed' | 'skipped' | 'pending'; duration: number };
  name: string;
}

interface CucumberElement {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  type: 'scenario' | 'background';
  steps: CucumberStep[];
  tags: Array<{ name: string }>;
}

interface CucumberFeature {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  uri: string;
  elements: CucumberElement[];
}

interface SuiteMetrics {
  totalScenarios: number;
  passed: number;
  failed: number;
  skipped: number;
  failedScenarios: Array<{ feature: string; scenario: string }>;
  durationMs: number;
}

function parseCucumberJson(jsonPath: string): SuiteMetrics {
  const raw = JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(jsonPath, 'utf-8')) as CucumberFeature[];
  const metrics: SuiteMetrics = {
    totalScenarios: 0,
    passed: 0,
    failed: 0,
    skipped: 0,
    failedScenarios: [],
    durationMs: 0,
  };

  for (const feature of raw) {
    for (const element of feature.elements) {
      if (element.type !== 'scenario') continue;

      metrics.totalScenarios++;
      const hasFailedStep = element.steps.some(s => s.result.status === 'failed');
      const allSkipped = element.steps.every(s =>
        s.result.status === 'skipped' || s.result.status === 'pending'
      );

      if (hasFailedStep) {
        metrics.failed++;
        metrics.failedScenarios.push({ feature: feature.name, scenario: element.name });
      } else if (allSkipped) {
        metrics.skipped++;
      } else {
        metrics.passed++;
      }

      metrics.durationMs += element.steps.reduce((sum, s) => sum + (s.result.duration ?? 0), 0);
    }
  }

  return metrics;
}

async function postSlackSummary(metrics: SuiteMetrics, webhookUrl: string): Promise<void> {
  const icon = metrics.failed === 0 ? ':white_check_mark:' : ':red_circle:';
  const message = `${icon} BDD Suite: ${metrics.passed}/${metrics.totalScenarios} passed ` +
    `(${metrics.failed} failed, ${metrics.skipped} skipped) — ` +
    `${Math.round(metrics.durationMs / 1000)}s`;

  await fetch(webhookUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ text: message }),
  });
}

const metrics = parseCucumberJson('reports/cucumber.json');
if (process.env.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL) {
  postSlackSummary(metrics, process.env.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL);
}
process.exit(metrics.failed > 0 ? 1 : 0);
```

**Tradeoff**: The Cucumber JSON format is the most widely supported output across CI tools (Azure DevOps, Jira Zephyr, Xray, ReportPortal). However, it embeds all binary attachments (screenshots) inline as base64 strings, making the JSON file very large for screenshot-heavy suites. Use `formatOptions.externalAttachments` to exclude binaries from the JSON report and process them separately. For long-term trend analysis, prefer the Cucumber Messages format (NdJSON) which is streamable and supports schema versioning.

**[community] Teams that use the Cucumber JSON report for Jira Xray integration discover that the format is technically deprecated by the Xray team in favor of Cucumber Messages (NdJSON). New Xray integrations should use the `--format @cucumber/pretty-formatter` + `--format message:reports/messages.ndjson` combination and import the NdJSON file.** [community]

### Pattern 14 — Accessibility Assertion Steps Using `axe-core` in Cucumber.js

BDD scenarios can capture accessibility requirements as first-class business rules. Using `axe-core` inside a Cucumber.js `Then` step, teams can express WCAG compliance as a living specification: the scenario is the requirement, and the step implementation is the automated verification.

```typescript
// src/steps/a11y/accessibility.steps.ts
import { Then, Before } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from '../../support/world';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';
import type { AxeResults, Result } from 'axe-core';

// Store axe results on world for multi-step assertions
Before({ name: 'a11y:init' }, function (this: AppWorld) {
  this.context.lastA11yResults = undefined;
});

Then(
  'the page should be accessible at WCAG {string} level',
  async function (this: AppWorld, wcagLevel: string) {
    if (!this.page) {
      throw new Error('[a11y] No page available — ensure @browser tag is on the scenario');
    }

    const levelMap: Record<string, string> = {
      'AA': 'wcag2aa',
      'A': 'wcag2a',
      'AAA': 'wcag2aaa',
    };

    const runOnly = levelMap[wcagLevel.toUpperCase()];
    if (!runOnly) {
      throw new Error(`[a11y] Unknown WCAG level: ${wcagLevel}. Use A, AA, or AAA`);
    }

    const results: AxeResults = await new AxeBuilder({ page: this.page })
      .withTags([runOnly, 'wcag21aa', 'best-practice'])
      .analyze();

    this.context.lastA11yResults = results;

    if (results.violations.length > 0) {
      const summary = formatViolationSummary(results.violations);
      await this.attach(summary, 'text/plain');
      throw new Error(`Accessibility violations found:\n${summary}`);
    }
  }
);

Then(
  'the page should have no {string} accessibility violations',
  async function (this: AppWorld, ruleId: string) {
    const results: AxeResults = await new AxeBuilder({ page: this.page! })
      .withRules([ruleId])
      .analyze();

    const violations = results.violations.filter(v => v.id === ruleId);
    if (violations.length > 0) {
      throw new Error(`Rule '${ruleId}' violated: ${violations[0].description}`);
    }
  }
);

function formatViolationSummary(violations: Result[]): string {
  return violations
    .map(v => `[${v.impact}] ${v.id}: ${v.description} (${v.nodes.length} elements)`)
    .join('\n');
}
```

```gherkin
# features/a11y/checkout-accessibility.feature
@browser @regression
Feature: Checkout page accessibility

  Scenario: Checkout form meets WCAG AA standard
    Given I am a registered customer with items in my cart
    When I navigate to the checkout page
    Then the page should be accessible at WCAG "AA" level

  Scenario: Payment form error messages are accessible
    Given I am on the checkout page
    When I submit the payment form without filling in required fields
    Then the page should have no "label" accessibility violations
    And the page should have no "color-contrast" accessibility violations
```

**Tradeoff**: Adding axe-core assertions to BDD scenarios makes accessibility a first-class requirement with a human-readable specification. The cost is increased test run time (axe analysis adds 100-500ms per call) and potential false positives from dynamic content (modals, toasts) that appear/disappear during analysis. Run accessibility scenarios in the `@regression` tier, not `@smoke`, to keep fast feedback fast. Consider a dedicated accessibility-focused scenario for critical pages rather than appending `Then the page should be accessible` to every scenario.

**[community] Teams that add a generic WCAG AA check to every scenario discover that a single component with a persistent color-contrast violation causes dozens of scenarios to fail simultaneously. Prefer focused accessibility scenarios that test specific interaction patterns. The axe `exclude()` API can suppress known acceptable violations during a phased remediation effort.** [community]

### Pattern 15 — BDD Retry and `@flaky` Tag Convention for Environmentally Sensitive Scenarios

Some BDD scenarios are legitimately environmentally sensitive — they depend on timing, third-party service latency, or shared state that cannot be fully controlled. Rather than hiding these with blanket retry policies, the `@flaky` tag convention makes the sensitivity explicit and enables targeted retry configuration.

```typescript
// src/support/retry-hooks.ts
// Retry logic for scenarios tagged @flaky — transparent retry with logging
import { Before, After, Status } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from './world';

// Note: Cucumber.js does not have built-in per-scenario retry in the hook API.
// Use the --retry CLI option for native retry. This hook logs retry context.
Before({ name: 'retry:log-attempt', tags: '@flaky' }, function (this: AppWorld, { pickle }) {
  const attempt = parseInt(process.env.CUCUMBER_RETRY_ATTEMPT ?? '0', 10);
  if (attempt > 0) {
    console.warn(
      `[retry] Retrying flaky scenario: "${pickle.name}" (attempt ${attempt + 1})`
    );
    // Reset scenario context for clean retry
    this.context = {};
  }
});

After({ name: 'retry:record-failure', tags: '@flaky' }, async function (
  this: AppWorld,
  { result, pickle }
) {
  if (result.status === Status.FAILED) {
    const attempt = parseInt(process.env.CUCUMBER_RETRY_ATTEMPT ?? '0', 10);
    console.error(
      `[retry] Flaky scenario STILL failing after attempt ${attempt + 1}: "${pickle.name}"`
    );

    // Attach failure context for investigation
    if (this.page) {
      const screenshot = await this.page.screenshot({ type: 'png' });
      await this.attach(screenshot, 'image/png');
    }
  }
});
```

```yaml
# cucumber.config.yaml — retry configuration
default:
  paths: ['features/**/*.feature']
  import: ['src/**/*.ts']
  retry: 0          # Default: no retry
  retryTagFilter: '@flaky'  # Only retry scenarios tagged @flaky

# CI profile: allow 1 retry for flaky scenarios
ci:
  retry: 1
  retryTagFilter: '@flaky'
  format:
    - progress-bar
    - 'junit:reports/junit.xml'
```

```gherkin
# features/email/confirmation.feature
@regression @flaky
Scenario: Order confirmation email arrives within 60 seconds
  Given I have completed a purchase
  When I wait up to 60 seconds for a confirmation email
  Then my inbox should contain an email with subject "Order confirmed"
  And the email body should include my order number
```

**Tradeoff**: The `@flaky` tag convention makes environmental sensitivity explicit and searchable — `grep -r "@flaky" features/` gives a prioritized list of scenarios requiring infrastructure improvement. The tag signals "this scenario needs attention", not "this failure is acceptable". Combine with a monthly audit: any `@flaky` scenario not improved within two sprints should be escalated or rewritten to avoid the environmental dependency. Using retry without the `@flaky` tag silently hides flakiness, making infrastructure problems invisible until they cascade.

**[community] Teams that apply `retry: 2` globally (without `retryTagFilter`) mask systematic flakiness in their entire suite. A scenario that passes on the 3rd attempt is a failure with extra steps — it indicates infrastructure issues (shared test DB contention, timing-dependent steps, non-idempotent setup) that need fixing. Reserve retry for genuinely environmental scenarios like email delivery and use `@flaky` to create peer pressure to fix them.** [community]

### Pattern 16 — Step Definition Organization: Feature-Co-Located vs. Shared Registry

Two distinct organizational patterns emerge in real BDD codebases: (1) step definitions co-located with their feature files, and (2) step definitions in a shared global registry. Each has clear tradeoffs that depend on project size and team structure.

```
# Pattern A — Feature-co-located structure (small-to-medium projects)
features/
  checkout/
    checkout.feature
    checkout.steps.ts    ← steps live next to the feature file
    checkout.hooks.ts
  user-auth/
    login.feature
    login.steps.ts
    login.hooks.ts
  support/
    world.ts
    parameter-types.ts   ← shared across all features
    global-hooks.ts      ← suite-level hooks (BeforeAll/AfterAll)

# Pattern B — Domain registry structure (large projects, multiple teams)
features/
  checkout/
    checkout.feature
  user-auth/
    login.feature
src/
  steps/                 ← separate from features, organized by domain
    checkout/
      checkout.steps.ts
      checkout.hooks.ts
    user-auth/
      login.steps.ts
  support/
    world.ts
    parameter-types.ts
```

```typescript
// src/support/step-registry-loader.ts
// Pattern B: explicit step registry for large projects — controls load order
// and prevents accidental step shadowing between domains

import type { IConfiguration } from '@cucumber/cucumber/api';

// Step registry: explicit ordering prevents shadowing bugs
export const stepRegistry: Partial<IConfiguration> = {
  import: [
    // 1. Support files first (World, parameter types)
    './src/support/world.ts',
    './src/support/parameter-types.ts',
    './src/support/global-hooks.ts',

    // 2. Shared utility steps (shared Given/Then steps used across domains)
    './src/steps/shared/*.steps.ts',

    // 3. Domain steps (order matters if steps could shadow each other)
    './src/steps/user-auth/*.steps.ts',
    './src/steps/checkout/*.steps.ts',
    './src/steps/admin/*.steps.ts',
    './src/steps/reporting/*.steps.ts',
  ],
};

// Detect ambiguous step definitions at startup (development only)
if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development') {
  process.on('unhandledRejection', (err: unknown) => {
    if (err instanceof Error && err.message.includes('Ambiguous')) {
      console.error('[step-registry] AMBIGUOUS STEP DETECTED:', err.message);
      console.error('[step-registry] Two step definitions match the same expression.');
      console.error('[step-registry] Review step-registry-loader.ts import order.');
    }
  });
}
```

**Tradeoff**: Co-located steps (Pattern A) make navigation easy — developers always know where to find steps for a feature. The cost is step reuse friction: shared steps between features need to live in `support/` or be duplicated. Shared registry (Pattern B) enables better reuse but requires discipline to prevent the registry from becoming a dumping ground of loosely coupled steps. For projects with 1-3 teams, Pattern A. For projects with 4+ teams working on separate domains, Pattern B with explicit load order. A hybrid approach works well at medium scale: co-locate domain-specific steps, centralize cross-domain steps in `src/steps/shared/`.

**[community] The biggest source of "Ambiguous step definition" errors in medium-to-large Cucumber.js projects is step definitions from different domains that accidentally share wording (e.g., `Given I am logged in` in the admin domain and `Given I am logged in` in the customer domain). The playwright-bdd scoped fixture approach (Pattern 9 in this cycle) is the systematic solution; for vanilla Cucumber.js, explicit step wording disambiguation (`Given I am logged in as a customer` vs `Given I am logged in as an admin`) is required.** [community]

### Pattern 1 — `BeforeStep` / `AfterStep` Hooks for Step-Level Attachments and Conditional Skip

`BeforeStep` and `AfterStep` hooks fire before and after every individual step within a scenario (not at the scenario level like `Before`/`After`). This enables step-level screenshot capture, network request logging, and conditional skipping of individual steps based on runtime state.

```typescript
// src/support/step-hooks.ts
// BeforeStep/AfterStep — available in @cucumber/cucumber since v8.1.0
import { BeforeStep, AfterStep, Status } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from './world';

// Capture a screenshot before every step in @visual-regression scenarios
BeforeStep(
  { name: 'visual:pre-step-screenshot', tags: '@visual-regression' },
  async function (this: AppWorld, { pickleStep }) {
    if (!this.page) return;
    const stepText = pickleStep.text.replace(/[^a-z0-9]/gi, '_').slice(0, 40);
    const stepIndex = (this.stepIndex = (this.stepIndex ?? 0) + 1);
    const screenshot = await this.page.screenshot({ type: 'png' });
    // Embed before-step screenshot with step text as title
    await this.attach(
      screenshot,
      { mediaType: 'image/png', fileName: `step-${stepIndex}-before-${stepText}.png` }
    );
  }
);

// Log all network requests made during each step for debugging
AfterStep(
  { name: 'debug:step-network-log', tags: '@debug-network' },
  async function (this: AppWorld, { result, pickleStep }) {
    const requests = this.stepRequests ?? [];
    if (requests.length > 0) {
      const summary = requests.map(r => `  ${r.method} ${r.url} → ${r.status}`).join('\n');
      await this.attach(
        `Step: "${pickleStep.text}"\nRequests:\n${summary}`,
        'text/plain'
      );
    }
    // Clear per-step request log
    this.stepRequests = [];
    if (result.status === Status.FAILED && this.page) {
      // Capture DOM snapshot on step failure for diff comparison
      const html = await this.page.content();
      await this.attach(html, 'text/html');
    }
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: `BeforeStep`/`AfterStep` provide surgical step-level observability that `Before`/`After` cannot offer. The cost is overhead per step — even a no-op `AfterStep` adds latency to every step in every scenario. Use `tags` filtering to restrict to specific scenario subsets (`@debug-network`, `@visual-regression`). Do NOT attach screenshots in `AfterStep` for all scenarios by default — this bloats the Cucumber HTML report with thousands of images and makes the report slow to load.

**When NOT to use**: Step-level hooks that interact with `this.page` (screenshots, DOM snapshots) will fail with a `TypeError` if the World's `page` is not yet initialized. Always guard with `if (!this.page) return`. Never use `BeforeStep` to perform navigation or data setup — this belongs in `Before` hooks or `Given` steps. [official]

---

### Pattern 2 — `world()` Functional Export Pattern (v10.8.0+)

The functional-style `world()` export (introduced in Cucumber.js v10.8.0) provides a composable alternative to `setWorldConstructor`. Instead of a class, a plain factory function is registered. This pattern works naturally with TypeScript module augmentation and avoids class inheritance complexity for larger World objects.

```typescript
// src/support/world.ts — functional world pattern
import { world, IWorldOptions } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { Browser, BrowserContext, Page } from '@playwright/test';
import type { DataFactory } from './data-factory';

// Shape of the world's state — typed interface, not class
interface AppWorldState {
  browser: Browser;
  context: BrowserContext;
  page: Page;
  dataFactory: DataFactory;
  currentOrderId?: string;
  customerId?: string;
  stepIndex?: number;
  stepRequests?: Array<{ method: string; url: string; status: number }>;
  userRole?: string;
  authToken?: string;
  lastResponse?: import('@playwright/test').APIResponse;
  graphqlResult?: unknown;
  graphqlVariables?: Record<string, unknown>;
}

// world() registers a factory function that returns the world state.
// IWorldOptions.attach and IWorldOptions.log are automatically available.
world(function (this: IWorldOptions & AppWorldState): void {
  // Properties are assigned to `this` — no constructor body needed.
  // Before hooks populate them.
});

// Re-export typed accessor for use in step definitions
export type { AppWorldState as AppWorld };
```

```typescript
// src/support/hooks.ts — using functional world
import { Before, After } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from './world';
import { DataFactory } from './data-factory';
import { chromium } from '@playwright/test';
import { request } from '@playwright/test';

Before(async function (this: AppWorld) {
  this.browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: !!process.env.CI });
  this.context = await this.browser.newContext();
  this.page = await this.context.newPage();

  const apiContext = await request.newContext({
    baseURL: process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
  });
  this.dataFactory = new DataFactory(
    apiContext,
    process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000'
  );
});

After(async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.dataFactory?.cleanup();
  await this.context?.close();
  await this.browser?.close();
});
```

**Tradeoff**: The functional `world()` export eliminates the need to manage class inheritance chains when multiple World extensions are needed (e.g., `AppWorld extends BaseWorld extends World`). It integrates naturally with TypeScript interface composition. The tradeoff is that IDEs provide weaker autocomplete because the world is typed via `this` rather than a class instance. For projects with a single small World, the class pattern remains simpler to reason about. For projects with 5+ domain mixins, functional composition wins.

**When NOT to use**: If your World needs to run initialization logic in the constructor (e.g., creating a unique run ID synchronously), the class pattern with a constructor is cleaner. Async initialization belongs in `Before` hooks regardless of which World pattern you use — `world()` does not change this constraint. [official]

---

### Pattern 3 — Zod Schema Validation in API Step Definitions

BDD step definitions for API scenarios frequently assert on response body shape. Raw dot-notation access (`response.body.orderId`) throws `TypeError` on shape changes with no useful error message. Integrating Zod schema validation provides descriptive failure messages that point directly to the broken field.

```typescript
// src/steps/api-order.steps.ts — Zod schema validation for API responses
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { z } from 'zod';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

// Schema definitions — doubles as documentation for expected response shape
const OrderCreatedSchema = z.object({
  orderId:   z.string().regex(/^ORD-[A-Z0-9]{8}$/, 'orderId must match ORD-XXXXXXXX'),
  status:    z.enum(['pending', 'confirmed', 'processing']),
  total:     z.number().positive('order total must be positive'),
  createdAt: z.string().datetime({ message: 'createdAt must be ISO 8601' }),
  items: z.array(z.object({
    productId:  z.string(),
    quantity:   z.number().int().positive(),
    unitPrice:  z.number().nonnegative(),
  })).nonempty('order must have at least one item'),
});

type OrderCreated = z.infer<typeof OrderCreatedSchema>;

When(
  'I create an order with item {string} at quantity {int}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, productId: string, qty: number) {
    this.lastResponse = await this.dataFactory['apiContext'].post('/api/orders', {
      data: { customerId: this.customerId, items: [{ productId, quantity: qty }] },
    });
  }
);

Then(
  'the response should be a valid order creation response',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    if (!this.lastResponse!.ok()) {
      throw new Error(
        `Expected 2xx but got ${this.lastResponse!.status()}: ${await this.lastResponse!.text()}`
      );
    }

    const body = await this.lastResponse!.json() as unknown;
    const result = OrderCreatedSchema.safeParse(body);

    if (!result.success) {
      // Zod formats all field-level errors — no cryptic TypeError
      const issues = result.error.issues
        .map(i => `  ${i.path.join('.')}: ${i.message}`)
        .join('\n');
      throw new Error(`Order response schema validation failed:\n${issues}`);
    }

    // Typed access after validation
    this.currentOrderId = (result.data as OrderCreated).orderId;
  }
);

Then(
  'the order total should be approximately {float}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, expected: number) {
    const body = await this.lastResponse!.json() as { total?: number };
    const actual = body.total ?? 0;
    if (Math.abs(actual - expected) > 0.01) {
      throw new Error(`Expected total ~${expected}, got ${actual}`);
    }
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Zod schema validation in step definitions converts opaque `Cannot read property 'X' of undefined` failures into structured `path.field: validation message` failures that developers can act on immediately. The cost is the Zod dependency and the discipline of maintaining schemas alongside API changes. The schemas serve double duty as living API documentation. When NOT to use: for very simple responses (a single boolean or status string), Zod adds more boilerplate than value — use a direct comparison. For full API contract testing (all endpoints, all error responses), use dedicated OpenAPI contract testing rather than per-step Zod schemas. [community]

---

### Pattern 4 — Soft Assertions: Collecting Multiple Failures Per Scenario

Standard Cucumber step definitions throw on the first assertion failure, stopping the scenario immediately. For scenarios that validate multiple independent properties (form validation, report content, dashboard widgets), soft assertions collect all failures and report them together — saving the developer from running the scenario N times to find N failures.

```typescript
// src/support/soft-assert.ts — soft assertion collector for BDD steps
export class SoftAssertionCollector {
  private readonly failures: string[] = [];

  check(condition: boolean, message: string): void {
    if (!condition) {
      this.failures.push(`  FAIL: ${message}`);
    }
  }

  checkEqual<T>(actual: T, expected: T, label: string): void {
    if (actual !== expected) {
      this.failures.push(`  FAIL: ${label}: expected "${expected}", got "${actual}"`);
    }
  }

  checkMatch(value: string, pattern: RegExp, label: string): void {
    if (!pattern.test(value)) {
      this.failures.push(`  FAIL: ${label}: "${value}" did not match ${pattern}`);
    }
  }

  // Call at the end of a Then step — throws if any failures accumulated
  throwIfFailed(context?: string): void {
    if (this.failures.length > 0) {
      const header = context
        ? `${context} — ${this.failures.length} assertion(s) failed:`
        : `${this.failures.length} assertion(s) failed:`;
      throw new Error(`${header}\n${this.failures.join('\n')}`);
    }
  }

  get count(): number { return this.failures.length; }
}
```

```typescript
// src/steps/dashboard.steps.ts — using soft assertions for multi-property validation
import { Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';
import { SoftAssertionCollector } from '../support/soft-assert';

Then(
  'the admin dashboard should display correct KPI summary',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    const soft = new SoftAssertionCollector();

    const totalOrders = await this.page.getByTestId('kpi-total-orders').textContent();
    const activeUsers = await this.page.getByTestId('kpi-active-users').textContent();
    const revenueToday = await this.page.getByTestId('kpi-revenue-today').textContent();
    const pendingRefunds = await this.page.getByTestId('kpi-pending-refunds').textContent();

    soft.checkMatch(totalOrders ?? '', /^\d+$/, 'total orders must be a number');
    soft.checkMatch(activeUsers ?? '', /^\d+$/, 'active users must be a number');
    soft.checkMatch(revenueToday ?? '', /^\$[\d,]+\.\d{2}$/, 'revenue must be currency format');
    soft.check((pendingRefunds ?? '') !== '', 'pending refunds widget must not be empty');

    soft.throwIfFailed('Admin dashboard KPI validation');
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Soft assertions reduce the number of test-debug cycles for multi-property validations. The cost is that a single `Then` step with many soft checks becomes a "hidden mini test suite" that obscures the BDD scenario's single-responsibility intent. Use soft assertions only when all checked properties belong to the same observable state (a dashboard panel, a confirmation page, an email body). Do NOT use soft assertions to combine what should be separate `Then` steps — each `Then` should express a distinct business expectation. If you find yourself with 10+ soft checks in one step, split them into multiple `Then` steps. [community]

---

### Pattern 5 — Stryker Mutation Testing to Validate BDD Assertion Quality

BDD scenarios that do not assert strongly enough pass even when the implementation is broken — they provide false confidence. Mutation testing (Stryker) verifies assertion quality by introducing small code mutations and checking whether the BDD suite catches them.

```typescript
// stryker.config.ts — Stryker mutation testing configuration targeting BDD step definitions
import type { Config } from '@stryker-mutator/api/core';

const config: Config = {
  packageManager: 'npm',
  reporters: ['html', 'clear-text', 'progress'],
  testRunner: 'cucumber',
  coverageAnalysis: 'perTest',

  // Mutate the application code — not the test code
  mutate: [
    'src/**/*.ts',
    '!src/steps/**/*.ts',    // Exclude step definitions from mutation
    '!src/support/**/*.ts',  // Exclude World and hooks
  ],

  cucumber: {
    // Run only @regression scenarios during mutation testing
    // @smoke is too narrow; @slow adds too much time
    tags: '@regression and not @slow and not @wip',
    profile: 'regression',
  },

  // Thresholds: mutation score below 70% fails the mutation CI job
  thresholds: {
    high: 80,
    low: 70,
    break: 65,  // CI hard failure below 65%
  },

  // Limit parallel workers to avoid OOM on large suites
  concurrency: 4,
  timeoutMS: 30_000,
  dryRunTimeoutMinutes: 5,
};

export default config;
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/mutation-testing.yml — weekly mutation CI job
name: BDD Mutation Testing

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 4 * * 0'  # Sundays at 4am — weekly quality gate
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  stryker:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '20', cache: 'npm' }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Run Stryker mutation tests
        run: npx stryker run
        env:
          CI: true
          BASE_URL: ${{ vars.TEST_BASE_URL }}
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: stryker-report
          path: reports/mutation/
          retention-days: 30
```

**Tradeoff**: Stryker mutation testing reveals BDD scenarios that have high step count but low assertion strength — the most common form of "BDD theater." A mutation score below 70% on business-logic code indicates that the BDD suite would not catch typical implementation bugs. The cost is that mutation testing is slow (10–60 minutes for a medium suite) and should not run on every PR. Weekly scheduling on the main branch is the right balance. When NOT to use: do not run mutation testing against infrastructure or integration code (database adapters, HTTP clients) — mutations there produce misleading scores because behavior depends on external systems. [community]

---

### Pattern 6 — Playwright Performance Metrics Assertions in BDD Scenarios

BDD scenarios traditionally assert on functional correctness. Performance requirements (page load time, Core Web Vitals thresholds) are often left to separate load testing tools. Playwright's CDP session API enables adding performance assertions directly to BDD scenarios — expressing performance as a business requirement.

```typescript
// src/steps/performance.steps.ts — LCP and CLS assertions via Playwright CDP
import { When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

interface NavMetrics {
  lcp: number;
  fcp: number;
  cls: number;
  ttfb: number;
}

// Attach metrics storage to World via declaration merging
declare module '../support/world' {
  interface AppWorld {
    navigationMetrics?: NavMetrics;
  }
}

When(
  'I navigate to the {string} page and capture performance metrics',
  async function (this: AppWorld, pageName: string) {
    const pageRoutes: Record<string, string> = {
      'product listing': '/products',
      'checkout':        '/checkout',
      'dashboard':       '/dashboard',
      'homepage':        '/',
    };

    const route = pageRoutes[pageName.toLowerCase()];
    if (!route) throw new Error(`Unknown page name: "${pageName}"`);

    const session = await this.context.newCDPSession(this.page);
    await session.send('Performance.enable');

    await this.page.goto(route, { waitUntil: 'networkidle' });

    const { metrics } = await session.send('Performance.getMetrics') as {
      metrics: Array<{ name: string; value: number }>;
    };
    const get = (name: string): number =>
      metrics.find(m => m.name === name)?.value ?? 0;

    this.navigationMetrics = {
      lcp:  get('LargestContentfulPaint') * 1000,
      fcp:  get('FirstContentfulPaint') * 1000,
      cls:  get('CumulativeLayoutShift'),
      ttfb: get('TimeToFirstByte') * 1000,
    };
    await session.detach();
  }
);

Then(
  'the Largest Contentful Paint should be under {int} milliseconds',
  function (this: AppWorld, thresholdMs: number) {
    if (!this.navigationMetrics) throw new Error('No metrics captured — run navigation step first');
    const { lcp } = this.navigationMetrics;
    if (lcp > thresholdMs) {
      throw new Error(
        `LCP ${lcp.toFixed(0)}ms exceeds ${thresholdMs}ms threshold ` +
        `(Google Good < 2500ms, Needs Improvement < 4000ms)`
      );
    }
  }
);

Then(
  'the Cumulative Layout Shift should be under {float}',
  function (this: AppWorld, threshold: number) {
    if (!this.navigationMetrics) throw new Error('No metrics captured');
    const { cls } = this.navigationMetrics;
    if (cls > threshold) {
      throw new Error(
        `CLS ${cls.toFixed(3)} exceeds ${threshold} threshold ` +
        `(Google Good < 0.1, Needs Improvement < 0.25)`
      );
    }
  }
);
```

```gherkin
# features/performance/critical-pages.feature
@performance @regression @slow
Feature: Core Web Vitals for critical pages

  Scenario: Checkout page meets Good LCP threshold
    Given I am a registered customer with items in my cart
    When I navigate to the "checkout" page and capture performance metrics
    Then the Largest Contentful Paint should be under 2500 milliseconds
    And the Cumulative Layout Shift should be under 0.1
```

**Tradeoff**: Expressing performance requirements as BDD scenarios makes them first-class acceptance criteria visible to product managers. The cost is that performance measurements in a headless browser differ from real-user measurements (no CPU throttling, no real network latency) and can be environment-dependent. Tag these scenarios `@slow` and run them separately from functional regression. Use the Good/Needs Improvement/Poor thresholds from Google's Core Web Vitals spec as the reference. Do NOT use performance BDD as a replacement for real-user monitoring (RUM) — it is a regression guard, not a production performance tool. [community]

---

### Pattern 7 — Higher-Order Step Definition Composition

Step definitions that share setup logic often duplicate the same code. Higher-order functions create step definition factories that encapsulate shared behavior, similar to fixture composition in pytest or Playwright.

```typescript
// src/steps/factories/auth-step-factory.ts
// Higher-order functions that generate step definitions for different user roles
import { Given } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

type UserRole = 'customer' | 'admin' | 'guest' | 'banned-customer';

interface RoleCredentials {
  email: string;
  password: string;
  seedOptions?: Record<string, unknown>;
}

const ROLE_CREDENTIALS: Record<UserRole, RoleCredentials> = {
  'customer':        { email: 'customer@test.example.com', password: 'TestPass123!' },
  'admin':           { email: 'admin@test.example.com',    password: 'AdminPass123!' },
  'guest':           { email: '',                          password: '' },
  'banned-customer': { email: '',                          password: '', seedOptions: { isBanned: true } },
};

// Factory: creates a Given step definition for a specific user role
function registerAuthStep(stepText: string, role: UserRole): void {
  Given(stepText, async function (this: AppWorld) {
    const creds = ROLE_CREDENTIALS[role];

    if (role === 'guest') {
      await this.page.context().clearCookies();
      return;
    }

    if (creds.seedOptions) {
      const customer = await this.dataFactory.createTestCustomer(creds.seedOptions);
      this.customerId = customer.customerId;
      await this.page.goto('/login');
      await this.page.getByTestId('email').fill(customer.email);
      await this.page.getByTestId('password').fill('TestPass123!');
      await this.page.getByTestId('submit').click();
      await this.page.waitForURL('/dashboard');
      return;
    }

    await this.page.goto('/login');
    await this.page.getByTestId('email').fill(creds.email);
    await this.page.getByTestId('password').fill(creds.password);
    await this.page.getByTestId('submit').click();
    await this.page.waitForURL(role === 'admin' ? '/admin' : '/dashboard');
    this.userRole = role;
  });
}

// Register all role variants — one factory call per role
registerAuthStep('I am logged in as a customer',       'customer');
registerAuthStep('I am logged in as an admin',          'admin');
registerAuthStep('I am browsing as a guest',            'guest');
registerAuthStep('I am logged in as a banned customer', 'banned-customer');
```

**Tradeoff**: The factory pattern eliminates copy-paste between authentication steps for different roles while keeping each step's behavior explicit and independently overridable. The cost is indirection — a developer reading the step definition list sees the string texts but must look at the factory to understand the implementation. Use factories for step families with 3+ members sharing significant logic. For 1-2 steps, write them explicitly. Never put non-trivial business logic in a step factory — factory parameters should only control setup variation (role, tier, state), not assertions. [community]

---

### Pattern 8 — DocString Content-Type for Structured Payload Steps

Gherkin DocStrings support a content-type annotation (backtick delimiter with `json` or `yaml`) that signals to step definitions what format to parse. Combined with typed parsing, this enables strongly-typed payload steps without relying on free-form string interpolation.

```gherkin
# features/orders/order-creation.feature
Feature: Order creation with structured payloads

  Scenario: Creating an order with a complex payload
    When I send a POST request to "/api/orders" with body:
      """json
      {
        "customerId": "cust-001",
        "shippingAddress": {
          "street": "123 Main St",
          "city": "Berlin",
          "country": "DE",
          "postalCode": "10115"
        },
        "items": [
          { "productId": "prod-42", "quantity": 2 },
          { "productId": "prod-17", "quantity": 1 }
        ],
        "promoCode": "WELCOME10"
      }
      """
    Then the response status is 201
```

```typescript
// src/steps/request.steps.ts — DocString content-type parsing
import { When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import yaml from 'js-yaml';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

// Cucumber passes DocString as an object with content and mediaType
interface DocString { content: string; mediaType?: string; }

When(
  'I send a POST request to {string} with body:',
  async function (this: AppWorld, path: string, docString: DocString) {
    let body: unknown;

    const mediaType = docString.mediaType?.toLowerCase() ?? '';
    if (mediaType.includes('json') || docString.content.trimStart().startsWith('{')) {
      try {
        body = JSON.parse(docString.content);
      } catch (e) {
        throw new Error(`DocString is not valid JSON: ${(e as Error).message}`);
      }
    } else if (mediaType.includes('yaml') || mediaType.includes('yml')) {
      try {
        body = yaml.load(docString.content);
      } catch (e) {
        throw new Error(`DocString is not valid YAML: ${(e as Error).message}`);
      }
    } else {
      body = docString.content; // Pass as raw string
    }

    this.lastResponse = await this.dataFactory['apiContext'].post(path, {
      data: body as Record<string, unknown>,
    });
  }
);

Then(
  'the response status is {int}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, expected: number) {
    const actual = this.lastResponse!.status();
    if (actual !== expected) {
      const body = await this.lastResponse!.text();
      throw new Error(`Expected HTTP ${expected}, got ${actual}. Body: ${body}`);
    }
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: DocString content-type annotations make feature files self-documenting about the format of embedded data and enable type-safe parsing in step definitions. The `"""json` triple-quote with type annotation provides editor syntax highlighting for JSON/YAML blocks in supporting editors. The tradeoff is that large JSON payloads in feature files make scenarios verbose and harder for non-technical stakeholders to read — these scenarios are better suited to developer-facing API test suites than business-facing acceptance tests. Use DocStrings for payloads that are genuinely part of the business rule (e.g., a healthcare record structure); avoid them for incidental test data. [official]

---

### Pattern 9 — BDD for GraphQL APIs

GraphQL APIs require different BDD step patterns than REST — queries and mutations use a single endpoint with variable-driven input. BDD for GraphQL benefits from reusable operation steps that separate the operation name from its variables.

```typescript
// src/steps/graphql.steps.ts — BDD step definitions for GraphQL APIs
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

const GRAPHQL_OPERATIONS: Record<string, string> = {
  GetOrder: `
    query GetOrder($orderId: ID!) {
      order(id: $orderId) { id status total items { productId quantity } }
    }`,
  CreateOrder: `
    mutation CreateOrder($input: CreateOrderInput!) {
      createOrder(input: $input) { id status total }
    }`,
  CancelOrder: `
    mutation CancelOrder($orderId: ID!, $reason: String!) {
      cancelOrder(orderId: $orderId, reason: $reason) { id status refundAmount }
    }`,
};

Given(
  'I set the GraphQL variable {string} to {string}',
  function (this: AppWorld, name: string, value: string) {
    this.graphqlVariables = { ...(this.graphqlVariables ?? {}), [name]: value };
  }
);

Given(
  'I set the GraphQL variable {string} to {int}',
  function (this: AppWorld, name: string, value: number) {
    this.graphqlVariables = { ...(this.graphqlVariables ?? {}), [name]: value };
  }
);

When(
  'I execute the GraphQL operation {string}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, operationName: string) {
    const query = GRAPHQL_OPERATIONS[operationName];
    if (!query) throw new Error(`Unknown GraphQL operation: "${operationName}"`);

    const response = await this.dataFactory['apiContext'].post('/graphql', {
      data: {
        query,
        variables: this.graphqlVariables ?? {},
        operationName,
      },
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${this.authToken ?? ''}` },
    });

    this.graphqlResult = await response.json() as unknown;
    // Reset variables after execution to prevent bleed to next step
    this.graphqlVariables = {};
  }
);

Then(
  'the GraphQL response should have no errors',
  function (this: AppWorld) {
    const result = this.graphqlResult as { errors?: Array<{ message: string }> } | undefined;
    if (result?.errors && result.errors.length > 0) {
      const msgs = result.errors.map(e => `  - ${e.message}`).join('\n');
      throw new Error(`GraphQL response contained errors:\n${msgs}`);
    }
  }
);

Then(
  'the GraphQL response field {string} should equal {string}',
  function (this: AppWorld, dotPath: string, expected: string) {
    const data = (this.graphqlResult as { data?: Record<string, unknown> })?.data ?? {};
    const actual = dotPath.split('.').reduce(
      (obj: unknown, key: string) => (obj as Record<string, unknown>)?.[key],
      data
    );
    if (String(actual) !== expected) {
      throw new Error(`GraphQL field "${dotPath}": expected "${expected}", got "${String(actual)}"`);
    }
  }
);
```

```gherkin
# features/graphql/order-query.feature
@api @graphql @regression
Feature: Order retrieval via GraphQL

  Background:
    Given I am authenticated as a registered customer

  Scenario: Querying a confirmed order returns correct status
    Given I have a confirmed order stored as "currentOrderId"
    And I set the GraphQL variable "orderId" to current order ID
    When I execute the GraphQL operation "GetOrder"
    Then the GraphQL response should have no errors
    And the GraphQL response field "order.status" should equal "confirmed"
```

**Tradeoff**: GraphQL BDD step definitions benefit from centralizing query strings in an operation registry (prevents scattered hardcoded queries in step files) and from separating variable setup (`Given`) from execution (`When`). The tradeoff is that the variable-setup pattern produces verbose multi-step `Given` blocks for complex mutations — prefer DocString variables for large inputs. Do NOT write GraphQL query strings directly in Gherkin `Given` steps — this violates the declarative principle and couples the scenario to the API's query language rather than business intent. [community]

---

### Pattern 10 — Named Hook Ordering with the `order` Option (v12.3.0+)

Cucumber.js v12.3.0 introduced `BeforeAll`/`AfterAll` named hooks with an `order` option that controls execution sequence when multiple `BeforeAll` hooks are registered across files. This is essential for large suites where infrastructure setup order matters (e.g., database must start before seed data loads).

```typescript
// src/support/infrastructure-hooks.ts — ordered BeforeAll hooks for suite setup
import { BeforeAll, AfterAll } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { chromium, type Browser } from '@playwright/test';

// Order 1 — lowest number runs first
// Database initialization must precede any application setup
BeforeAll(
  { name: 'infra:database-start', order: 1 },
  async function () {
    // createTestDatabase() defined elsewhere — starts a test DB container
    await (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>)['createTestDatabase']?.();
    console.log('[BeforeAll:1] Test database initialized');
  }
);

// Order 5 — application seed data after database is ready
BeforeAll(
  { name: 'infra:seed-reference-data', order: 5 },
  async function () {
    // Load product catalog, pricing tables — read-only reference data
    console.log('[BeforeAll:5] Reference fixtures loaded');
  }
);

// Order 10 — browser shared instance after infrastructure is ready
let sharedBrowser: Browser;

BeforeAll(
  { name: 'infra:browser-launch', order: 10 },
  async function () {
    sharedBrowser = await chromium.launch({ headless: !!process.env.CI });
    console.log('[BeforeAll:10] Shared browser launched');
  }
);

// AfterAll with matching names — executed in REVERSE order (10 → 5 → 1)
AfterAll({ name: 'infra:browser-close', order: 10 }, async function () {
  await sharedBrowser?.close();
});

AfterAll({ name: 'infra:database-stop', order: 1 }, async function () {
  console.log('[AfterAll:1] Test database stopped');
});

export { sharedBrowser };
```

```typescript
// src/support/hooks.ts — per-scenario hooks that rely on the shared browser
import { Before, After } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { sharedBrowser } from './infrastructure-hooks';
import type { AppWorld } from './world';

Before(async function (this: AppWorld) {
  // Create a fresh context per scenario from the shared browser
  this.context = await sharedBrowser.newContext({
    baseURL: process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
  });
  this.page = await this.context.newPage();
});

After(async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.context?.close();
});
```

**Tradeoff**: The `order` option on `BeforeAll`/`AfterAll` eliminates the brittle implicit ordering that arises when hooks are registered across multiple support files. In large suites with 10+ support files, implicit ordering (alphabetical file load order) causes intermittent failures when infrastructure is not ready. Explicit `order` values (1 = infrastructure, 5 = fixtures, 10 = clients) make dependencies self-documenting. When NOT to use: for suites with a single `BeforeAll` / `AfterAll` pair, `order` adds no value. For suites using the functional `world()` pattern where each `Before` creates its own infrastructure, `BeforeAll` ordering is irrelevant. [official]

### Pattern 11 — CI Flakiness Detection Script for BDD Suites

Flaky scenarios — those that sometimes pass and sometimes fail without code changes — are the most damaging long-term problem in BDD suites. A flakiness detection script runs the full suite multiple times and records per-scenario failure rates.

```typescript
// scripts/detect-flaky-scenarios.ts
// Usage: npx ts-node scripts/detect-flaky-scenarios.ts --runs 5 --threshold 0.2
import { execSync } from 'child_process';
import * as fs from 'fs';

interface FlakySummary {
  tag: string;
  failCount: number;
  passCount: number;
  failureRate: number;
}

const args = process.argv;
const RUNS = parseInt(args[args.indexOf('--runs') + 1] ?? '5', 10);
const THRESHOLD = parseFloat(args[args.indexOf('--threshold') + 1] ?? '0.2');

function runSuite(extraArgs = ''): { passed: boolean; jsonOutput: string } {
  const outFile = `tmp/flaky-check-${Date.now()}.json`;
  fs.mkdirSync('tmp', { recursive: true });
  try {
    execSync(
      `npx cucumber-js --profile regression --format json:${outFile} ${extraArgs}`,
      { stdio: 'pipe', timeout: 300_000 }
    );
    return { passed: true, jsonOutput: outFile };
  } catch {
    return { passed: false, jsonOutput: outFile };
  }
}

function parseFailedScenarios(jsonFile: string): Set<string> {
  const failed = new Set<string>();
  try {
    const content = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(jsonFile, 'utf8')) as Array<{
      elements?: Array<{ name: string; steps: Array<{ result: { status: string } }> }>;
    }>;
    for (const feature of content) {
      for (const scenario of feature.elements ?? []) {
        const hasFail = scenario.steps.some(s => s.result?.status === 'failed');
        if (hasFail) failed.add(scenario.name);
      }
    }
  } catch { /* file may not exist if suite crashed */ }
  return failed;
}

const scenarioFailCounts = new Map<string, number>();
const scenarioRunCounts = new Map<string, number>();

console.log(`Running suite ${RUNS} times to detect flakiness (threshold: ${THRESHOLD * 100}%)...`);

for (let run = 1; run <= RUNS; run++) {
  process.stdout.write(`  Run ${run}/${RUNS}...`);
  const { jsonOutput } = runSuite();
  const failed = parseFailedScenarios(jsonOutput);

  // We need all scenario names — run a dry-run once to get the full list
  if (run === 1) {
    // Seed all scenarios with 0 fail count on first pass
    try {
      const allJson = 'tmp/all-scenarios.json';
      execSync(`npx cucumber-js --dry-run --format json:${allJson}`, { stdio: 'pipe' });
      const allContent = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(allJson, 'utf8')) as Array<{
        elements?: Array<{ name: string }>;
      }>;
      for (const feature of allContent) {
        for (const scenario of feature.elements ?? []) {
          if (!scenarioRunCounts.has(scenario.name)) {
            scenarioRunCounts.set(scenario.name, 0);
            scenarioFailCounts.set(scenario.name, 0);
          }
        }
      }
    } catch { /* ignore dry-run errors */ }
  }

  for (const [name] of scenarioRunCounts) {
    scenarioRunCounts.set(name, (scenarioRunCounts.get(name) ?? 0) + 1);
    if (failed.has(name)) {
      scenarioFailCounts.set(name, (scenarioFailCounts.get(name) ?? 0) + 1);
    }
  }
  console.log(` ${failed.size} failed`);
}

const flaky: FlakySummary[] = [];
for (const [tag, runCount] of scenarioRunCounts) {
  const failCount = scenarioFailCounts.get(tag) ?? 0;
  if (runCount === 0) continue;
  const failureRate = failCount / runCount;
  // 0% = stable pass, 100% = stable fail — only in-between is flaky
  if (failureRate > 0 && failureRate < 1 && failureRate >= THRESHOLD) {
    flaky.push({ tag, failCount, passCount: runCount - failCount, failureRate });
  }
}

flaky.sort((a, b) => b.failureRate - a.failureRate);

if (flaky.length > 0) {
  console.error(`\nFlaky scenarios (failure rate >= ${THRESHOLD * 100}%):`);
  for (const s of flaky) {
    console.error(`  "${s.tag}": ${(s.failureRate * 100).toFixed(0)}% flaky (${s.failCount}/${s.failCount + s.passCount} runs)`);
  }
  fs.writeFileSync('reports/flaky-scenarios.json', JSON.stringify(flaky, null, 2));
  process.exit(1);
} else {
  console.log(`\nNo flaky scenarios detected at >= ${THRESHOLD * 100}% threshold.`);
}
```

**Tradeoff**: The flakiness detection script provides empirical failure-rate data for each scenario, replacing "I think it's flaky" gut feelings with numbers. The cost is that running the full suite N times multiplies CI time — run this weekly, not on every PR. Use the output to prioritize remediation: fix 50%+ flaky scenarios first (infrastructure problems), then 20-49% (timing issues), then tag residual flakiness with `@flaky` to enable targeted retry. Do NOT apply `retry: 2` globally without first running this detection script — global retry masks systematic failures. [community]

### Pattern 12 — BDD with Temporal Workflows: Testing Time-Sensitive Business Logic

Temporal.io workflows encapsulate long-running, time-sensitive business processes (order fulfillment, subscription billing, SLA escalation). BDD scenarios for Temporal workflows use `TestWorkflowEnvironment` to control virtual time and assert on workflow state.

```typescript
// src/steps/temporal.steps.ts — BDD step definitions for Temporal.io workflows
import { Given, When, Then, Before, After } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { TestWorkflowEnvironment } from '@temporalio/testing';
import { Worker } from '@temporalio/worker';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

// Extend World with Temporal-specific fields
declare module '../support/world' {
  interface AppWorld {
    temporalEnv?: TestWorkflowEnvironment;
    temporalWorker?: Worker;
    workflowId?: string;
  }
}

Before({ tags: '@temporal' }, async function (this: AppWorld) {
  // createTimeSkipping() starts a local Temporal server with virtual clock
  this.temporalEnv = await TestWorkflowEnvironment.createTimeSkipping();
  this.temporalWorker = await Worker.create({
    connection: this.temporalEnv.nativeConnection,
    taskQueue: 'test-fulfillment',
    workflowsPath: require.resolve('../../src/workflows'),
    activities: require('../../src/workflows/activities'),
  });
  void this.temporalWorker.run(); // Non-blocking — worker runs in background
});

After({ tags: '@temporal' }, async function (this: AppWorld) {
  this.temporalWorker?.shutdown();
  await this.temporalEnv?.teardown();
});

When(
  'the order fulfillment workflow starts for order {string}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, orderId: string) {
    if (!this.temporalEnv) throw new Error('Temporal environment not initialized');
    const { client } = this.temporalEnv;
    const handle = await client.workflow.start('orderFulfillmentWorkflow', {
      taskQueue: 'test-fulfillment',
      workflowId: `fulfillment-${orderId}`,
      args: [{ orderId, customerId: this.customerId ?? 'cust-001' }],
    });
    this.workflowId = handle.workflowId;
  }
);

When(
  '{int} days pass without shipping confirmation',
  async function (this: AppWorld, days: number) {
    if (!this.temporalEnv) throw new Error('Temporal environment not initialized');
    // sleep() advances the virtual clock — no real waiting required
    await this.temporalEnv.sleep(`${days} days`);
  }
);

Then(
  'the workflow should have sent an escalation notification',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    if (!this.temporalEnv || !this.workflowId) throw new Error('Missing Temporal context');
    const handle = this.temporalEnv.client.workflow.getHandle(this.workflowId);
    const log = await handle.query<string[]>('getNotificationLog');
    const hasEscalation = log.some(entry => entry.toLowerCase().includes('escalation'));
    if (!hasEscalation) {
      throw new Error(
        `Expected escalation in notification log.\nLog entries:\n  ${log.join('\n  ')}`
      );
    }
  }
);

Then(
  'the workflow status should be {string}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, expectedStatus: string) {
    if (!this.temporalEnv || !this.workflowId) throw new Error('Missing Temporal context');
    const handle = this.temporalEnv.client.workflow.getHandle(this.workflowId);
    const desc = await handle.describe();
    const actual = desc.status.name.toLowerCase();
    if (actual !== expectedStatus.toLowerCase()) {
      throw new Error(`Expected workflow status "${expectedStatus}", got "${actual}"`);
    }
  }
);
```

```gherkin
# features/fulfillment/sla-escalation.feature
@temporal @regression @slow
Feature: Order fulfillment SLA enforcement

  Background:
    Given a Temporal test environment is running

  Scenario: Escalation triggers after 3-day shipping delay
    Given I have a confirmed order "ORD-SLA001"
    When the order fulfillment workflow starts for order "ORD-SLA001"
    And 3 days pass without shipping confirmation
    Then the workflow should have sent an escalation notification
    And the workflow status should be "running"
```

**Tradeoff**: Temporal's `TestWorkflowEnvironment.sleep()` advances virtual time instantly — testing a 30-day subscription billing cycle takes milliseconds, not a month. This makes BDD the right tool for expressing SLA and time-based business rules. The cost is Temporal-specific infrastructure: `@temporalio/testing` must be installed and local Temporal server binary must be available (bundled with the SDK). When NOT to use: this pattern is only relevant for teams using Temporal.io. For simpler time-dependent scenarios (session expiry, token TTL), Playwright's `page.clock` API is the lighter alternative. [community]

---

### Pattern 13 — Cucumber `--shard` and Sharded HTML Report Merge Strategy

Cucumber.js v12.2+ native `--shard N/M` splits the scenario list across M parallel CI workers. Each shard produces its own JSON report. Merging N JSON files into a single navigable HTML report uses the `multiple-cucumber-html-reporter` package.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/bdd-sharded.yml — sharded regression run with merged report
name: BDD Regression (Sharded)

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  bdd-shard:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]
      fail-fast: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '20', cache: 'npm' }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Run shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4
        run: |
          npx cucumber-js \
            --profile regression \
            --shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4 \
            --format json:reports/shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
        env:
          CI: 'true'
          BASE_URL: ${{ vars.TEST_BASE_URL }}
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: shard-report-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: reports/shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json

  merge-reports:
    needs: bdd-shard
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '20', cache: 'npm' }
      - run: npm ci
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: shard-report-*
          path: reports/shards/
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Merge shard JSON reports into single HTML
        run: npx ts-node scripts/merge-reports.ts
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: merged-bdd-report
          path: reports/merged/
          retention-days: 30
```

```typescript
// scripts/merge-reports.ts — merge N Cucumber JSON shard files into one HTML report
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';
import reporter from 'multiple-cucumber-html-reporter';

const SHARD_DIR = 'reports/shards';
const OUTPUT_DIR = 'reports/merged';

const shardFiles = fs.readdirSync(SHARD_DIR)
  .filter(f => f.endsWith('.json'))
  .map(f => path.join(SHARD_DIR, f));

if (shardFiles.length === 0) {
  console.error('No shard JSON files found in', SHARD_DIR);
  process.exit(1);
}

// Concatenate feature arrays from all shard JSON files
const mergedFeatures: unknown[] = [];
for (const file of shardFiles) {
  try {
    const content = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8')) as unknown[];
    mergedFeatures.push(...content);
    console.log(`  Merged: ${path.basename(file)} (${content.length} features)`);
  } catch (e) {
    console.warn(`  Skipping invalid JSON in ${path.basename(file)}:`, (e as Error).message);
  }
}

const mergedJsonPath = path.join(SHARD_DIR, 'merged.json');
fs.writeFileSync(mergedJsonPath, JSON.stringify(mergedFeatures, null, 2));

reporter.generate({
  jsonDir: SHARD_DIR,
  reportPath: OUTPUT_DIR,
  metadata: {
    browser:  { name: 'chromium', version: 'latest' },
    platform: { name: 'ubuntu', version: 'latest' },
  },
  customData: {
    title: 'BDD Regression Suite',
    data: [
      { label: 'Branch',  value: process.env.GITHUB_REF_NAME ?? 'local' },
      { label: 'Commit',  value: (process.env.GITHUB_SHA ?? 'local').slice(0, 8) },
      { label: 'Shards',  value: String(shardFiles.length) },
    ],
  },
});

console.log(`\nMerged ${shardFiles.length} shards into ${OUTPUT_DIR}/index.html`);
```

**Tradeoff**: Native `--shard` in Cucumber.js v12.2+ requires no external parallelization tooling and integrates cleanly with GitHub Actions matrix jobs. The JSON merge step preserves all scenario details including embedded screenshots and attachments. The cost is a sequential `merge-reports` job after all shards complete — adds 1–2 minutes to the pipeline. Alternative: write HTML directly per shard and publish each as a separate artifact — better when debugging individual shard failures matters more than a unified view. [official]

---

### Pattern 14 — Step Definition Inheritance via TypeScript Abstract Base Classes

For large BDD suites with multiple domains (checkout, admin, reporting), abstract base classes share common step utilities (navigation helpers, toast assertions, modal dismissal) while domain-specific subclasses add specialized interactions.

```typescript
// src/steps/base/BaseStepContext.ts — abstract base with shared utilities
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import type { AppWorld } from '../../support/world';

export abstract class BaseStepContext {
  protected constructor(protected readonly world: AppWorld) {}

  // Shared: navigate and wait for network idle
  protected async navigateTo(path: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.world.page.goto(path);
    await this.world.page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
  }

  // Shared: assert a toast/status notification with specific text
  protected async expectToast(text: string): Promise<void> {
    const toast = this.world.page.getByRole('status');
    await expect(toast).toContainText(text, { timeout: 5_000 });
  }

  // Shared: dismiss any open modal/dialog
  protected async dismissModal(): Promise<void> {
    const closeButton = this.world.page.getByRole('button', { name: /close|dismiss/i });
    if (await closeButton.isVisible()) await closeButton.click();
  }
}
```

```typescript
// src/steps/checkout/CheckoutStepContext.ts — domain step context extending base
import { BaseStepContext } from '../base/BaseStepContext';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import type { AppWorld } from '../../support/world';

export class CheckoutStepContext extends BaseStepContext {
  constructor(world: AppWorld) { super(world); }

  async proceedToCheckout(): Promise<void> {
    await this.navigateTo('/cart');
    await this.world.page.getByTestId('proceed-to-checkout').click();
    await this.world.page.waitForURL('/checkout');
  }

  async fillValidCardDetails(): Promise<void> {
    await this.world.page.getByTestId('card-number').fill('4242424242424242');
    await this.world.page.getByTestId('card-expiry').fill('12/28');
    await this.world.page.getByTestId('card-cvv').fill('123');
  }

  async confirmOrder(): Promise<void> {
    await this.world.page.getByTestId('confirm-order').click();
    await this.world.page.waitForURL(/\/order\/confirmation/);
  }

  async expectConfirmationToast(): Promise<void> {
    await this.expectToast('Order confirmed!');
  }
}
```

```typescript
// src/steps/checkout/checkout.steps.ts — step definitions using the context class
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from '../../support/world';
import { CheckoutStepContext } from './CheckoutStepContext';

// Helper creates a fresh context per step — lightweight, no constructor overhead
const ctx = (world: AppWorld): CheckoutStepContext => new CheckoutStepContext(world);

When('I proceed to checkout',
  async function (this: AppWorld) { await ctx(this).proceedToCheckout(); }
);

When('I enter valid credit card details',
  async function (this: AppWorld) { await ctx(this).fillValidCardDetails(); }
);

When('I confirm the order',
  async function (this: AppWorld) { await ctx(this).confirmOrder(); }
);

Then('I should see the order success notification',
  async function (this: AppWorld) { await ctx(this).expectConfirmationToast(); }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: TypeScript abstract base classes for step helpers provide compile-time enforcement of shared interfaces without polluting the global World namespace. All domain step helpers extend `BaseStepContext` and inherit navigation and toast utilities. The cost is class instantiation per step and the `ctx(this)` indirection that requires developers to know where to find the implementation. For small suites, this is over-engineering — write utilities as plain functions. For suites with 5+ domains where utility drift is already a problem, the abstract base class prevents divergence. Never put assertions in the base class — assertions belong in `Then` steps. [community]

---

### Pattern 15 — BDD for WebSocket and Real-Time Scenarios

Real-time features (live notifications, collaborative editing, event streams) require WebSocket step definitions that connect, send, and assert on messages. Playwright's `page.waitForEvent('websocket')` API intercepts connections at the browser level.

```typescript
// src/steps/websocket.steps.ts — BDD step definitions for real-time features
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { WebSocket } from 'playwright';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

declare module '../support/world' {
  interface AppWorld {
    wsConnections: Map<string, WebSocket>;
    wsMessages: Map<string, string[]>;
  }
}

Given(
  'I am connected to the live order updates WebSocket',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    this.wsConnections ??= new Map();
    this.wsMessages ??= new Map();

    // Wait for a WebSocket connection to the orders endpoint
    const wsPromise = this.page.waitForEvent('websocket', ws =>
      ws.url().includes('/ws/orders')
    );
    await this.page.goto('/dashboard');
    const ws = await wsPromise;

    this.wsConnections.set('orders', ws);
    this.wsMessages.set('orders', []);

    ws.on('framereceived', ({ payload }) => {
      const msgs = this.wsMessages.get('orders') ?? [];
      msgs.push(typeof payload === 'string' ? payload : payload.toString('utf8'));
    });
  }
);

When(
  'the server pushes an order status update for order {string} to {string}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, orderId: string, newStatus: string) {
    // Trigger via API — server pushes to connected WS clients
    await this.dataFactory['apiContext'].post('/api/test/push-order-update', {
      data: { orderId, status: newStatus },
    });
  }
);

Then(
  'I should receive a WebSocket message with order {string} status {string}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, orderId: string, expectedStatus: string) {
    const maxWaitMs = 5_000;
    const pollMs = 100;
    const deadline = Date.now() + maxWaitMs;

    while (Date.now() < deadline) {
      for (const raw of this.wsMessages.get('orders') ?? []) {
        try {
          const msg = JSON.parse(raw) as { orderId?: string; status?: string };
          if (msg.orderId === orderId && msg.status === expectedStatus) return;
        } catch { /* skip non-JSON frames */ }
      }
      await new Promise(res => setTimeout(res, pollMs));
    }

    const received = (this.wsMessages.get('orders') ?? []).join(', ') || '(none)';
    throw new Error(
      `No WS message for order "${orderId}" with status "${expectedStatus}" within ${maxWaitMs}ms.\n` +
      `Messages received: ${received}`
    );
  }
);

Then(
  'the live order count on the dashboard should update to {int}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, expectedCount: number) {
    await this.page.getByTestId('live-order-count').waitFor({ timeout: 5_000 });
    const countText = await this.page.getByTestId('live-order-count').textContent();
    const actual = parseInt(countText ?? '0', 10);
    if (actual !== expectedCount) {
      throw new Error(`Expected live order count ${expectedCount}, got ${actual}`);
    }
  }
);
```

```gherkin
# features/realtime/live-order-updates.feature
@realtime @regression @slow
Feature: Live order status notifications via WebSocket

  Background:
    Given I am logged in as a customer
    And I am connected to the live order updates WebSocket

  Scenario: Dashboard updates live when order ships
    Given I have a confirmed order "ORD-RT001"
    When the server pushes an order status update for order "ORD-RT001" to "shipped"
    Then I should receive a WebSocket message with order "ORD-RT001" status "shipped"
    And the live order count on the dashboard should update to 1
```

**Tradeoff**: Playwright's `page.waitForEvent('websocket')` intercepts connections at the browser level — no test-specific WebSocket client needed. The poll-and-assert pattern avoids fixed sleeps. The cost is that WebSocket scenarios are environmentally sensitive (server push timing varies) — tag them `@slow` and add `retryTagFilter: '@realtime'` to the CI profile. Set `maxWaitMs` based on the 99th-percentile server push latency, not an arbitrary constant. Do NOT poll forever with no deadline — always bound the wait explicitly. [community]

---

## Community Gotchas — Cycle 28

### Gotcha 1 — `BeforeAll` hooks run even when `--tags` filter excludes all scenarios [community]

**WHY**: Cucumber.js initializes `BeforeAll` hooks before evaluating tag filters. If your `BeforeAll` starts a database or browser, it runs even when `--tags @smoke` matches zero scenarios in the suite. This wastes CI time and can cause confusing failures ("infrastructure started but no scenarios ran"). Fix: add a guard in `BeforeAll` that exits early if the tag filter is restrictive. Alternatively, use a pre-flight `--dry-run --tags @smoke 2>&1 | grep "scenarios"` check before launching the full suite, and skip infrastructure boot when the count is 0.

### Gotcha 2 — Parallel workers share environment variables but NOT in-memory singletons [community]

**WHY**: When using `--parallel`, each worker is a separate Node.js child process. A module-level singleton (a shared WireMock instance, a DB connection pool defined at module top-level) is NOT shared between workers — each worker gets its own copy. Teams expecting to share one WireMock server across all workers discover they have N independent instances each with separate stub registrations, causing "unexpected request" errors in workers that did not register the stub. Fix: use per-scenario infrastructure created in `Before` hooks, or use a shared network-accessible test server and assign each worker a unique port via the `CUCUMBER_WORKER_ID` environment variable.

### Gotcha 3 — `Scenario Outline` parameter substitution does NOT apply to `Background` steps [community]

**WHY**: `Background` steps run before every scenario, including each row of a `Scenario Outline`, but `<placeholder>` substitution from the `Examples` table only applies to the `Scenario Outline` steps themselves. Teams write `Background: Given I am logged in as "<role>"` expecting each Examples row to substitute `<role>` — this does not work and Cucumber treats the literal text `<role>` as the step text. The result is an "Undefined step" error that is confusing because the same text works inside the `Scenario Outline` block. Fix: move parameterized setup into the first `Given` step of the `Scenario Outline`, or use a conditional step definition that reads from the World.

### Gotcha 4 — `attach()` in `AfterStep` throws when the browser context is already closed [community]

**WHY**: If a step throws an unhandled rejection that causes Playwright to automatically close its browser context, the `page` object is in a "target closed" state by the time `AfterStep` fires. Calling `this.page.screenshot()` in `AfterStep` then throws `Target closed`, producing a secondary error that obscures the original failure in the Cucumber HTML report. Fix: wrap all `this.page` calls in `AfterStep` with a `try/catch`. A failed screenshot attachment should log a warning, not throw — the primary failure message is what developers need to see.

### Gotcha 5 — Cucumber.js JSON formatter silently drops large attachments [community]

**WHY**: The JSON formatter has an effective size limit on embedded attachment content (base64-encoded images, HTML snapshots). Attachments exceeding approximately 5MB are silently omitted from the output JSON without any error or warning. Teams using full-page screenshots of long dashboard pages, or attaching complete DOM snapshots for debugging, discover their attachments are missing from the Cucumber HTML report with no diagnostic message. Fix: use `page.screenshot({ clip: { x: 0, y: 0, width: 1280, height: 720 } })` instead of `{ fullPage: true }` for report attachments, and compress to JPEG at quality 70 (`{ type: 'jpeg', quality: 70 }`) before calling `this.attach()`. For HTML snapshots, truncate to 200KB maximum or write to a file artifact instead of embedding.
