## Cycle 30 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 1 — DataTable `.raw()` and `.transpose()` for Matrix-Style Inputs  [official]

`DataTable.hashes()` works for row-per-entity tables, but multi-axis data — such as a permission matrix where roles are columns and actions are rows — is more naturally expressed as a transposed table. Cucumber's `DataTable.transpose()` rotates the table 90 degrees, and `DataTable.raw()` gives the primitive string grid for fully custom parsing.

```typescript
// features/authorization/role-permissions.feature
// Gherkin:
//   Given the permission matrix is:
//     | action       | admin | editor | viewer |
//     | read_content | yes   | yes    | yes    |
//     | edit_content | yes   | yes    | no     |
//     | delete_post  | yes   | no     | no     |
//     | manage_users | yes   | no     | no     |

import { Given, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { DataTable } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

interface PermissionMatrix {
  [action: string]: { [role: string]: boolean };
}

function parsePermissionMatrix(table: DataTable): PermissionMatrix {
  // raw() returns string[][] — first row is the header
  const rows = table.raw();
  const [headerRow, ...dataRows] = rows;
  const roles = headerRow.slice(1); // drop "action" column header

  const matrix: PermissionMatrix = {};
  for (const row of dataRows) {
    const action = row[0];
    matrix[action] = {};
    for (let i = 0; i < roles.length; i++) {
      matrix[action][roles[i]] = row[i + 1].toLowerCase() === 'yes';
    }
  }
  return matrix;
}

Given(
  'the permission matrix is:',
  function (this: AppWorld, table: DataTable) {
    this.permissionMatrix = parsePermissionMatrix(table);
  }
);

Then(
  'the {string} role should {word} perform {string}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, role: string, canOrCannot: string, action: string) {
    const expected = canOrCannot === 'be able to';
    const actual = this.permissionMatrix?.[action]?.[role] ?? false;
    if (actual !== expected) {
      throw new Error(
        `Permission check failed: role "${role}" ${expected ? 'should' : 'should NOT'} ` +
        `be able to "${action}" — matrix says ${actual}`
      );
    }
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use `raw()` when the table structure is non-standard (role/action matrix, pivot tables, configuration grids). Do NOT use `raw()` when `hashes()` or `rowsHash()` would suffice — they are more readable and self-documenting. Do NOT use `transpose()` in step bodies; instead do the rotation at parse time to keep assertion logic readable. Named alternatives: `DataTable.transpose().hashes()` for the flipped view without custom parsing. [official]

---

### Pattern 2 — RBAC Multi-Role Scenario Outline with Permission Table  [community]

Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) requires testing the same action under every role. Writing separate scenarios per role creates duplication. A `Scenario Outline` with an `Examples` table of roles collapses this into a single parameterized scenario that is instantly readable as a permission table by product managers and security reviewers.

```gherkin
# features/authorization/content-management-rbac.feature
@rbac @regression
Feature: Content management role-based access control

  Scenario Outline: <role> <can_access> the content management dashboard
    Given I am logged in as a "<role>" user
    When I navigate to the content management dashboard
    Then I should <outcome> access to the dashboard

    Examples: Access control matrix
      | role        | can_access        | outcome              |
      | admin       | has               | have full            |
      | editor      | has               | have full            |
      | contributor | has               | have limited         |
      | viewer      | does not have     | be denied            |
      | guest       | does not have     | be redirected from   |
```

```typescript
// src/steps/rbac.steps.ts — multi-role access control step definitions
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

const ROLE_CREDENTIALS: Record<string, { email: string; password: string }> = {
  admin:       { email: 'admin@test.com',  password: 'AdminPass123!' },
  editor:      { email: 'editor@test.com', password: 'EditorPass123!' },
  contributor: { email: 'contrib@test.com', password: 'ContribPass123!' },
  viewer:      { email: 'viewer@test.com',  password: 'ViewerPass123!' },
  guest:       { email: '',                 password: '' }, // unauthenticated
};

Given(
  'I am logged in as a {string} user',
  async function (this: AppWorld, role: string) {
    const creds = ROLE_CREDENTIALS[role];
    if (!creds) throw new Error(`Unknown role: "${role}"`);
    if (!creds.email) return; // guest — no login

    await this.page.goto('/login');
    await this.page.getByTestId('email').fill(creds.email);
    await this.page.getByTestId('password').fill(creds.password);
    await this.page.getByTestId('submit').click();
    await this.page.waitForURL('/dashboard', { timeout: 5000 });
    this.currentRole = role;
  }
);

Then(
  'I should have full access to the dashboard',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    await expect(this.page.getByTestId('cms-dashboard')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(this.page.getByTestId('delete-content-btn')).toBeVisible();
  }
);

Then(
  'I should have limited access to the dashboard',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    await expect(this.page.getByTestId('cms-dashboard')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(this.page.getByTestId('delete-content-btn')).not.toBeVisible();
    await expect(this.page.getByTestId('edit-content-btn')).toBeVisible();
  }
);

Then(
  'I should be denied access to the dashboard',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    await expect(this.page.getByTestId('cms-dashboard')).not.toBeVisible();
    await expect(this.page.getByTestId('permission-denied-banner')).toBeVisible();
  }
);

Then(
  'I should be redirected from access to the dashboard',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    await expect(this.page).toHaveURL(/\/login/);
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use this pattern for any feature where the same action behaves differently per role — it keeps the entire permission policy visible in one `Examples` table rather than scattered across test files. Do NOT use when role differences are minor variations of the same flow; prefer separate focused scenarios in that case. Named alternatives: parameterized test data in plain Playwright `test.each()` (less readable to non-developers). [community]

---

### Pattern 3 — Negative Test Taxonomy: Classifying Unhappy Paths in Gherkin  [community]

Positive-path scenarios are the first written; negative paths accumulate chaotically without a taxonomy. Classifying `Then` steps into four failure categories — **validation**, **authorization**, **business rule**, and **system error** — gives teams a checklist for completeness and makes failure traceability clear in CI reports.

```gherkin
# features/payments/payment-failures.feature
@payments @regression
Feature: Payment processing failure handling

  # Category 1 — VALIDATION: user-supplied data fails format or completeness checks
  @negative @validation
  Scenario: Payment fails when card number is invalid format
    Given I am a registered customer at checkout
    When I enter the card number "1234"
    And I confirm the order
    Then I should see the validation error "Card number must be 16 digits"
    And no charge should be initiated

  # Category 2 — AUTHORIZATION: caller lacks permission
  @negative @authorization
  Scenario: Guest user cannot access saved payment methods
    Given I am browsing as a guest
    When I try to view saved payment methods
    Then I should be redirected to the login page
    And I should see the message "Sign in to manage payment methods"

  # Category 3 — BUSINESS RULE: valid data violates a domain constraint
  @negative @business-rule
  Scenario: Payment fails when order total exceeds daily limit
    Given I am a new customer with no order history
    And my cart total is $5,500.00
    When I attempt to complete the checkout
    Then I should see the error "Daily purchase limit is $5,000 for new accounts"
    And the order should remain in pending state

  # Category 4 — SYSTEM ERROR: external dependency failure
  @negative @system-error
  Scenario: Checkout shows graceful degradation when payment gateway is down
    Given the payment gateway is unavailable
    And I am a registered customer at checkout
    When I confirm the order with valid card details
    Then I should see "Payment processing is temporarily unavailable"
    And I should see "Your cart has been saved — try again in a few minutes"
    And no order record should be created
```

```typescript
// src/steps/payment-failure.steps.ts — negative path step definitions
import { Given, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

Given(
  'the payment gateway is unavailable',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    // Mock the payment gateway endpoint to return 503
    await this.page.route('**/api/payments/charge', async (route) => {
      await route.fulfill({
        status: 503,
        contentType: 'application/json',
        body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'Service Unavailable' }),
      });
    });
    this.attach('Payment gateway stubbed to return 503', 'text/plain');
  }
);

Then(
  'no charge should be initiated',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    // Verify no payment request reached the API
    const chargeRequests = this.capturedRequests?.filter(
      r => r.url().includes('/api/payments/charge')
    ) ?? [];
    expect(chargeRequests).toHaveLength(0);
  }
);

Then(
  'no order record should be created',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    const res = await this.page.request.get(
      `/api/test/orders?customerId=${this.testUserId}&status=any`
    );
    const body = await res.json() as { orders: unknown[] };
    expect(body.orders).toHaveLength(0);
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Apply the four-category taxonomy when auditing feature files for negative coverage — use it as a checklist, not as a mandatory tag on every scenario. Do NOT require all four categories for every feature; a simple CRUD feature may only need validation and business-rule negatives. Named alternatives: ISTQB equivalence partitioning + boundary value analysis as a formal derivation method for unhappy paths. [community]

---

### Pattern 4 — DataTable Diff Assertion for Multi-Row API Responses  [community]

When a `Then` step asserts that an API response contains a specific set of rows (e.g., all items in an order, all results in a search response), comparing the full response body against a DataTable gives precise diff output on failure — showing which rows are missing or unexpected rather than a generic "arrays differ" message.

```typescript
// src/support/table-diff.ts — DataTable diff assertion helper
import { DataTable } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

type Row = Record<string, string>;

/**
 * Assert that actualRows contains exactly the rows specified in the DataTable.
 * Produces a diff showing missing rows (in table but not in actual) and
 * unexpected rows (in actual but not in table).
 */
export function assertTableMatches(
  actual: Row[],
  expected: DataTable,
  options: { partial?: boolean; keyField?: string } = {}
): void {
  const expectedRows = expected.hashes();
  const { partial = false, keyField } = options;

  // Project actual rows to only the columns present in expected (for partial match)
  const columns = Object.keys(expectedRows[0] ?? {});
  const projectedActual = partial
    ? actual.map(row =>
        Object.fromEntries(columns.map(col => [col, String(row[col] ?? '')]))
      )
    : actual.map(row =>
        Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(row).map(([k, v]) => [k, String(v)]))
      );

  const serialize = (row: Row): string =>
    keyField ? row[keyField] : JSON.stringify(row);

  const actualSet = new Set(projectedActual.map(serialize));
  const expectedSet = new Set(expectedRows.map(serialize));

  const missing = expectedRows.filter(r => !actualSet.has(serialize(r)));
  const unexpected = partial
    ? []
    : projectedActual.filter(r => !expectedSet.has(serialize(r)));

  if (missing.length > 0 || unexpected.length > 0) {
    const lines: string[] = ['DataTable mismatch:'];
    if (missing.length > 0) {
      lines.push('  Missing rows (expected but not found):');
      missing.forEach(r => lines.push(`    - ${JSON.stringify(r)}`));
    }
    if (unexpected.length > 0) {
      lines.push('  Unexpected rows (found but not expected):');
      unexpected.forEach(r => lines.push(`    + ${JSON.stringify(r)}`));
    }
    throw new Error(lines.join('\n'));
  }
}

// src/steps/order-items.steps.ts — using assertTableMatches in a Then step
import { Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { DataTable } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';
import { assertTableMatches } from '../support/table-diff';

Then(
  'the order should contain exactly the items:',
  async function (this: AppWorld, table: DataTable) {
    const res = await this.page.request.get(`/api/orders/${this.lastOrderId}/items`);
    const body = await res.json() as { items: Record<string, string>[] };
    assertTableMatches(body.items, table, { partial: true, keyField: 'productId' });
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when `Then` steps assert on collections of 3+ items — single-item assertions do not need a helper. Do NOT use for order-sensitive list comparisons (the helper uses set semantics); add an explicit sort and sequence check for ordered lists. Named alternatives: `expect(actual).toEqual(expected.hashes())` from Playwright — works for simple cases but gives less readable diff output; `chai-subset` for partial matching without custom code. [community]

---

### Pattern 5 — Performance Budget Assertions in BDD `Then` Steps  [community]

Non-functional requirements — "the page must load in under 2 seconds" — are business behaviors that deserve BDD scenarios, not just load-test tooling. Playwright's `page.evaluate()` and the Performance API enable performance budget assertions inside standard `Then` steps, making performance regression a first-class BDD concern.

```gherkin
# features/performance/checkout-performance.feature
@performance @regression
Feature: Checkout page performance budgets

  Scenario: Checkout page loads within the agreed performance budget
    Given I am a registered customer with 3 items in my cart
    When I navigate to the checkout page
    Then the page should load within 2000 milliseconds
    And the Largest Contentful Paint should be below 2500 milliseconds
    And the Cumulative Layout Shift score should be below 0.1
```

```typescript
// src/steps/performance.steps.ts — performance budget BDD assertions
import { Then, Before } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

// Enable Chrome performance metrics collection for @performance scenarios
Before({ tags: '@performance' }, async function (this: AppWorld) {
  const client = await this.page.context().newCDPSession(this.page);
  await client.send('Performance.enable');
  this.cdpClient = client;
});

Then(
  'the page should load within {int} milliseconds',
  async function (this: AppWorld, budgetMs: number) {
    const timing = await this.page.evaluate(() =>
      JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(window.performance.timing))
    ) as Record<string, number>;
    const loadTime = (timing['loadEventEnd'] ?? 0) - (timing['navigationStart'] ?? 0);
    if (loadTime > budgetMs) {
      throw new Error(
        `Performance budget exceeded: page load took ${loadTime}ms (budget: ${budgetMs}ms)`
      );
    }
    this.attach(`Page load: ${loadTime}ms (budget: ${budgetMs}ms)`, 'text/plain');
  }
);

Then(
  'the Largest Contentful Paint should be below {int} milliseconds',
  async function (this: AppWorld, budgetMs: number) {
    const lcp = await this.page.evaluate((): Promise<number> =>
      new Promise(resolve => {
        new PerformanceObserver((list) => {
          const entries = list.getEntries();
          const last = entries[entries.length - 1] as PerformanceEntry & { startTime: number };
          resolve(last?.startTime ?? 0);
        }).observe({ type: 'largest-contentful-paint', buffered: true });
        setTimeout(() => resolve(0), 500);
      })
    );
    if (lcp > budgetMs && lcp > 0) {
      throw new Error(`LCP ${lcp.toFixed(0)}ms exceeds budget ${budgetMs}ms`);
    }
    this.attach(`LCP: ${lcp.toFixed(0)}ms (budget: ${budgetMs}ms)`, 'text/plain');
  }
);

Then(
  'the Cumulative Layout Shift score should be below {float}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, threshold: number) {
    const cls = await this.page.evaluate((): Promise<number> =>
      new Promise(resolve => {
        let clsScore = 0;
        new PerformanceObserver((list) => {
          for (const entry of list.getEntries()) {
            const e = entry as PerformanceEntry & { hadRecentInput: boolean; value: number };
            if (!e.hadRecentInput) clsScore += e.value;
          }
        }).observe({ type: 'layout-shift', buffered: true });
        setTimeout(() => resolve(clsScore), 500);
      })
    );
    if (cls > threshold) {
      throw new Error(`CLS ${cls.toFixed(4)} exceeds threshold ${threshold}`);
    }
    this.attach(`CLS: ${cls.toFixed(4)} (threshold: ${threshold})`, 'text/plain');
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use for features with explicit SLA or performance contract requirements agreed in Three Amigos sessions. Tag with `@performance` and exclude from smoke runs. Do NOT replace dedicated load-testing tools (k6, Locust) — BDD performance assertions catch single-user regressions, not concurrency limits. Named alternatives: Lighthouse CI in a separate pipeline step (aggregated scores vs per-scenario assertions). [community]

---

### Pattern 6 — Rate-Limiting Behavior Scenarios  [community]

Rate limiting is a business rule ("each user may submit 3 requests per minute") that deserves a BDD scenario, but it requires careful step design to avoid brittle timing dependencies. The key technique is to use a seeded rate-limit counter via an admin API rather than making real requests until the limit is hit.

```gherkin
# features/security/rate-limiting.feature
@security @regression
Feature: API rate limiting enforcement

  Scenario: Authenticated user is rate-limited after exceeding the request quota
    Given I am authenticated as a registered user
    And my request quota has been pre-consumed to 1 remaining attempt
    When I make a valid API request
    Then the request should succeed with status 200
    When I make another valid API request
    Then the request should be rate-limited with status 429
    And the response should include a "Retry-After" header
    And the response body should explain the rate limit

  Scenario: Rate limit counter resets after the window expires
    Given I am authenticated as a registered user
    And my request quota has been exhausted for the current minute
    And the rate-limit window has expired
    When I make a valid API request
    Then the request should succeed with status 200
```

```typescript
// src/steps/rate-limit.steps.ts — rate limiting BDD step definitions
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

Given(
  'my request quota has been pre-consumed to {int} remaining attempt',
  async function (this: AppWorld, remaining: number) {
    // Use admin API to seed the rate-limit counter — avoids making N real requests
    const res = await this.page.request.post('/api/admin/test/rate-limit/seed', {
      data: { userId: this.testUserId, remaining, windowSeconds: 60 },
      headers: { 'x-admin-secret': process.env['TEST_ADMIN_SECRET'] ?? '' },
    });
    expect(res.status()).toBe(200);
    this.attach(`Rate limit seeded: ${remaining} remaining`, 'text/plain');
  }
);

Given(
  'my request quota has been exhausted for the current minute',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    await this.page.request.post('/api/admin/test/rate-limit/exhaust', {
      data: { userId: this.testUserId },
      headers: { 'x-admin-secret': process.env['TEST_ADMIN_SECRET'] ?? '' },
    });
  }
);

Given(
  'the rate-limit window has expired',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    // Advance synthetic clock 61 seconds — avoids real wait in CI
    await this.page.clock.fastForward(61_000);
  }
);

Then(
  'the request should be rate-limited with status {int}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, expectedStatus: number) {
    expect(this.lastApiResponse?.status()).toBe(expectedStatus);
  }
);

Then(
  'the response should include a {string} header',
  async function (this: AppWorld, headerName: string) {
    const value = this.lastApiResponse?.headers()[headerName.toLowerCase()];
    expect(value, `Expected header "${headerName}" to be present`).toBeTruthy();
    this.attach(`Header ${headerName}: ${value}`, 'text/plain');
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use an admin seed API to set the rate-limit counter directly — never implement rate-limit scenarios by making real requests in a loop (fragile, slow, pollutes logs). Do NOT skip rate-limit BDD scenarios for public APIs — rate limiting is a first-class security and reliability behavior. Named alternatives: integration test at the middleware layer (faster but not stakeholder-readable). [community]

---

### Pattern 7 — Step Definition Namespace Collision Resolution  [community]

As a BDD suite grows, multiple contributors independently define steps with subtly different phrasing for the same action — creating a graveyard of near-duplicate step strings. The collision resolution pattern establishes a domain-prefixed step registry and a lint rule that catches new definitions before merge.

```typescript
// src/support/step-registry.ts — canonical step string registry
// All step patterns must be registered here. Duplicate detection runs at suite startup.

export const STEPS = {
  AUTH: {
    LOGGED_IN_AS:   'I am logged in as {string}',
    LOGGED_IN_ROLE: 'I am a {string} user',
    LOGGED_OUT:     'I am not logged in',
  },
  CART: {
    HAS_ITEMS:        'my cart contains {int} item(s)',
    ITEM_ADDED:       'I add {string} to my cart',
    DISCOUNT_APPLIED: 'I apply discount code {string}',
  },
  CHECKOUT: {
    INITIATED:     'I navigate to the checkout page',
    CARD_VALID:    'I enter valid credit card details',
    ORDER_PLACED:  'I confirm the order',
    ORDER_SUCCESS: 'I should see an order confirmation',
  },
} as const;

// Collision detector: run in BeforeAll to catch duplicate patterns at startup
import { BeforeAll } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

BeforeAll(function () {
  const allPatterns: string[] = [];
  function collectPatterns(obj: Record<string, unknown>): void {
    for (const v of Object.values(obj)) {
      if (typeof v === 'string') allPatterns.push(v);
      else if (typeof v === 'object' && v !== null)
        collectPatterns(v as Record<string, unknown>);
    }
  }
  collectPatterns(STEPS as unknown as Record<string, unknown>);

  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const duplicates: string[] = [];
  for (const pattern of allPatterns) {
    if (seen.has(pattern)) duplicates.push(pattern);
    else seen.add(pattern);
  }

  if (duplicates.length > 0) {
    throw new Error(
      `[StepRegistry] Duplicate step patterns detected:\n` +
      `${duplicates.map(d => `  "${d}"`).join('\n')}\n` +
      `Remove duplicates from src/support/step-registry.ts before adding new steps.`
    );
  }
});

// src/steps/auth.steps.ts — consuming the registry
import { Given } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { STEPS } from '../support/step-registry';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

Given(STEPS.AUTH.LOGGED_IN_AS, async function (this: AppWorld, email: string) {
  await this.loginPage.loginAs(email);
});

Given(STEPS.AUTH.LOGGED_IN_ROLE, async function (this: AppWorld, role: string) {
  await this.loginPage.loginAsRole(role);
});
```

**Tradeoff**: Use the step registry pattern in suites with 5+ contributors or 200+ step definitions — the collision risk scales with team size and time. Do NOT use for small single-author suites where it adds ceremony without benefit. Named alternatives: `eslint-plugin-cucumber` with `no-duplicate-step-patterns` rule (requires the plugin; less flexible than a typed registry); periodic `--format usage` audits (reactive, not preventive). [community]

---

### Pattern 8 — `WorldParameters` Factory for Environment-Driven Configuration  [official]

The `WorldParameters` type in `@cucumber/cucumber` allows typed configuration to be injected into every World instance from the Cucumber profile. A factory function wraps the raw parameters with validation and defaults, ensuring that missing environment variables fail at suite startup with a useful error rather than deep in a step with `undefined`.

```typescript
// src/support/world-params.ts — typed WorldParameters factory with early validation
import type { IWorldOptions } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

export interface AppWorldParameters {
  baseUrl: string;
  apiTimeout: number;
  headless: boolean;
  adminSecret: string;
  mailhogUrl: string;
}

const DEFAULTS: Partial<AppWorldParameters> = {
  apiTimeout: 10_000,
  headless: true,
  mailhogUrl: 'http://localhost:8025',
};

/**
 * Build WorldParameters from environment variables + overrides.
 * Throws at config load time if required values are missing — fails fast
 * before any scenarios run rather than with a cryptic TypeError mid-test.
 */
export function buildWorldParameters(
  override: Partial<AppWorldParameters> = {}
): AppWorldParameters {
  const baseUrl = override.baseUrl ?? process.env['BASE_URL'];
  const adminSecret = override.adminSecret ?? process.env['TEST_ADMIN_SECRET'];

  const missing: string[] = [];
  if (!baseUrl) missing.push('BASE_URL (env) or worldParameters.baseUrl (config)');
  if (!adminSecret) missing.push('TEST_ADMIN_SECRET (env) or worldParameters.adminSecret (config)');

  if (missing.length > 0) {
    throw new Error(
      `[WorldParameters] Required configuration missing:\n` +
      `${missing.map(m => `  - ${m}`).join('\n')}\n` +
      `Set these values in your environment before running the BDD suite.`
    );
  }

  return {
    ...DEFAULTS,
    ...override,
    baseUrl: baseUrl!,
    adminSecret: adminSecret!,
    headless: process.env['CI'] === 'true'
      ? true
      : (override.headless ?? DEFAULTS.headless ?? true),
    apiTimeout: override.apiTimeout ?? DEFAULTS.apiTimeout ?? 10_000,
    mailhogUrl: override.mailhogUrl ?? DEFAULTS.mailhogUrl ?? 'http://localhost:8025',
  };
}

// cucumber.ts — inject typed WorldParameters per profile
import { buildWorldParameters } from './src/support/world-params';
import type { IConfiguration } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

export default {
  default: {
    import: ['src/steps/**/*.ts', 'src/support/**/*.ts'],
    worldParameters: buildWorldParameters(),
    format: ['progress-bar', 'html:reports/cucumber-report.html'],
  } satisfies Partial<IConfiguration>,

  staging: {
    import: ['src/steps/**/*.ts', 'src/support/**/*.ts'],
    worldParameters: buildWorldParameters({
      baseUrl: process.env['STAGING_URL'],
    }),
    format: ['progress-bar', 'html:reports/staging-report.html'],
  } satisfies Partial<IConfiguration>,
};
```

**Tradeoff**: Use the validated factory whenever the suite targets multiple environments (local, staging, production-like). Early failure at config load time is far preferable to a cryptic `TypeError` on line 300 of a step definition. Do NOT embed secrets in `worldParameters` objects committed to source control — use environment variables exclusively for secret values. Named alternatives: dotenv + direct `process.env` access in steps (less type-safe, fails later in test execution). [official]

---

### Pattern 9 — Network Condition Simulation in BDD Scenarios  [community]

BDD scenarios that only run on fast CI networks miss behaviors that matter to real users: timeout handling, retry prompts, and loading skeleton UIs. Playwright's `page.route()` allows scenarios to simulate slow, throttled, and intermittent network conditions as first-class `Given` steps.

```gherkin
# features/resilience/slow-network.feature
@resilience @regression
Feature: Application behavior under degraded network conditions

  Scenario: Checkout shows loading state during slow payment processing
    Given I am a registered customer at the checkout page
    And the payment service responds with 3 second latency
    When I confirm the order with valid card details
    Then I should see a loading indicator within 500 milliseconds
    And the order should eventually be confirmed within 10 seconds

  Scenario: Search results show skeleton UI during slow API response
    Given the product search API has 2 second latency
    And I am on the home page
    When I search for "laptop"
    Then I should immediately see the search skeleton loading UI
    And the search results should appear within 5 seconds
```

```typescript
// src/steps/network-conditions.steps.ts — network latency simulation
import { Given, After } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

interface ActiveRoute {
  pattern: string;
}

async function addRouteLatency(
  world: AppWorld,
  latencyMs: number,
  urlPattern: string
): Promise<void> {
  await world.page.route(urlPattern, async (route) => {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, latencyMs));
    await route.continue();
  });
  world.attach(`Network latency: ${latencyMs}ms on ${urlPattern}`, 'text/plain');
  world.activeRoutes = world.activeRoutes ?? [];
  world.activeRoutes.push({ pattern: urlPattern });
}

Given(
  'the payment service responds with {int} second latency',
  async function (this: AppWorld, seconds: number) {
    await addRouteLatency(this, seconds * 1000, '**/api/payments/**');
  }
);

Given(
  'the product search API has {int} second latency',
  async function (this: AppWorld, seconds: number) {
    await addRouteLatency(this, seconds * 1000, '**/api/search/**');
  }
);

// Clean up route overrides after each scenario
After(async function (this: AppWorld) {
  if (this.activeRoutes?.length) {
    await Promise.all(
      this.activeRoutes.map((r: ActiveRoute) =>
        this.page.unroute(r.pattern).catch(() => {})
      )
    );
    this.activeRoutes = [];
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff**: Use for features that have explicit loading-state, skeleton-UI, or timeout-handling requirements confirmed in Three Amigos. Do NOT use in smoke runs — latency scenarios are inherently slow and belong in `@resilience @regression` only. Do NOT simulate latency on ALL network calls; scope it to the specific service being tested. Named alternatives: CDP `Network.emulateNetworkConditions` for bandwidth throttling (more comprehensive but more complex); Playwright's `page.setExtraHTTPHeaders` for header-based simulation. [community]

---

### Pattern 10 — Multi-Browser Parameterized BDD with `playwright-bdd`  [community]

BDD scenarios that involve browser-specific behaviors (clipboard API, file system access, PWA installation) need to be verified across browsers without duplicating feature files. With `playwright-bdd`, the `playwright.config.ts` `projects` array drives multi-browser execution of the same `.feature` files, and per-project `grep` lets teams scope cross-browser coverage without changing Gherkin.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — multi-browser BDD project matrix
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';
import { defineBddConfig } from 'playwright-bdd';

const testDir = defineBddConfig({
  features: 'features/**/*.feature',
  steps: 'src/steps/**/*.ts',
});

export default defineConfig({
  testDir,
  reporter: [['html', { outputFolder: 'reports/playwright-html' }]],
  use: {
    baseURL: process.env['BASE_URL'] ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
    screenshot: 'only-on-failure',
    trace: 'retain-on-failure',
  },
  projects: [
    {
      name: 'chromium',
      use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] },
      // All scenarios run on Chrome (no grep filter)
    },
    {
      name: 'firefox',
      use: { ...devices['Desktop Firefox'] },
      grep: /@cross-browser-required/,   // Only cross-browser-tagged scenarios
    },
    {
      name: 'webkit',
      use: { ...devices['Desktop Safari'] },
      grep: /@cross-browser-required/,
    },
    {
      name: 'mobile-chrome',
      use: { ...devices['Pixel 7'] },
      grep: /@mobile/,
    },
    {
      name: 'mobile-safari',
      use: { ...devices['iPhone 15'] },
      grep: /@mobile/,
    },
  ],
});
```

```gherkin
# features/file-upload/file-upload.feature
@cross-browser-required
Feature: File upload behavior across browsers

  Scenario: User can upload a profile picture via drag and drop
    Given I am logged in as a registered user
    And I am on the profile settings page
    When I drag and drop a valid JPEG file onto the avatar upload zone
    Then I should see a preview of the uploaded image
    And the upload progress indicator should reach 100%

  @mobile
  Scenario: User can upload a profile picture via native file picker on mobile
    Given I am logged in as a registered user on a mobile device
    When I tap the avatar upload zone
    Then the native file picker should open
```

```typescript
// src/steps/file-upload.steps.ts — cross-browser compatible step definitions
import { createBdd } from 'playwright-bdd';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';

const { Given, When, Then } = createBdd();

When(
  'I drag and drop a valid JPEG file onto the avatar upload zone',
  async ({ page }) => {
    // Use setInputFiles for cross-browser compatibility
    // DataTransfer drag-and-drop is not consistent across browser engines
    const fileInput = page.locator('input[type="file"]');
    await fileInput.setInputFiles(
      path.join(__dirname, '../fixtures/test-avatar.jpg')
    );
    await expect(page.getByTestId('avatar-upload-zone')).toHaveAttribute(
      'data-state', 'uploading'
    );
  }
);

Then(
  'the upload progress indicator should reach {int}%',
  async ({ page }, percent: number) => {
    await expect(page.getByRole('progressbar')).toHaveAttribute(
      'aria-valuenow',
      String(percent),
      { timeout: 10_000 }
    );
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use `@cross-browser-required` sparingly — running the full BDD suite across 5 browser/device combinations multiplies CI time by 5x. Reserve cross-browser tags for features where browser engine differences are known to matter. Do NOT tag smoke scenarios with `@cross-browser-required` — Chrome-only smoke is sufficient for PR gates. Named alternatives: BrowserStack / Sauce Labs for cloud cross-browser runs at higher parallelism. [community]

---

### Pattern 11 — Living Documentation Git-Blame Traceability Hook  [community]

Feature files modified without corresponding Three Amigos sign-off create undocumented behavior changes. A `Before` hook that reads `git log` metadata for each loaded feature file and attaches the last-author and last-commit information to the Cucumber HTML report creates an accountability trail — making it visible in the living documentation who made what change and when.

```typescript
// src/support/git-blame-hook.ts — attach git metadata to Cucumber report
import { Before } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { execSync } from 'child_process';
import * as path from 'path';

interface GitFileInfo {
  lastAuthor: string;
  lastCommit: string;
  lastDate: string;
  commitMessage: string;
}

function getGitInfo(filePath: string): GitFileInfo | null {
  try {
    const repoRoot = execSync('git rev-parse --show-toplevel', { encoding: 'utf8' }).trim();
    const relative = path.relative(repoRoot, filePath).replace(/\\/g, '/');
    const log = execSync(
      `git log -1 --format="%an|%H|%ad|%s" -- "${relative}"`,
      { cwd: repoRoot, encoding: 'utf8' }
    ).trim();
    if (!log) return null;
    const parts = log.split('|');
    return {
      lastAuthor:    parts[0] ?? 'unknown',
      lastCommit:    (parts[1] ?? '').slice(0, 8),
      lastDate:      parts[2] ?? '',
      commitMessage: parts.slice(3).join('|'),
    };
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

// Cache git info per feature file — computed once per suite run
const featureGitCache = new Map<string, GitFileInfo | null>();

Before(function (scenario) {
  if (process.env['CI'] !== 'true') return; // Skip locally — git calls add latency

  const featureFile = scenario.gherkinDocument.uri;
  if (!featureFile) return;

  if (!featureGitCache.has(featureFile)) {
    featureGitCache.set(featureFile, getGitInfo(featureFile));
  }

  const info = featureGitCache.get(featureFile);
  if (info) {
    this.attach(
      [
        `Feature: ${path.basename(featureFile)}`,
        `Last author: ${info.lastAuthor}`,
        `Commit: ${info.lastCommit} — ${info.commitMessage}`,
        `Date: ${info.lastDate}`,
      ].join('\n'),
      'text/plain'
    );
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff**: Use in regulated environments or large teams where feature file ownership matters for audit trails. Gate with `process.env.CI` to avoid latency in local development. Named alternatives: Gherkin file metadata in CODEOWNERS (cruder, not runtime-visible); a PR check that enforces Three Amigos approval comments in the feature file header. [community]

---

### Pattern 12 — Cucumber.js `failFast` + Triage Profile Pattern  [official]

When a large regression suite has multiple failures, running all scenarios to completion buries the root cause in noise. The `failFast` configuration option stops the suite on the first failure. Pairing it with a dedicated `triage` profile (serial execution, verbose format) gives engineers a minimal reproduction immediately rather than waiting for a 45-minute run.

```typescript
// cucumber.ts — failFast triage and ci-gate profiles
import type { IConfiguration } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

export default {
  default: {
    import: ['src/steps/**/*.ts', 'src/support/**/*.ts'],
    format: ['progress-bar', 'html:reports/cucumber-report.html'],
    tags: 'not @wip',
    parallel: 4,
    failFast: false,
  } satisfies Partial<IConfiguration>,

  // Triage profile: stop on first failure, serial for clean stack trace
  triage: {
    import: ['src/steps/**/*.ts', 'src/support/**/*.ts'],
    format: [
      'progress',
      'html:reports/triage-report.html',
      '@cucumber/json-formatter:reports/triage.json',
    ],
    tags: 'not @wip',
    failFast: true,
    parallel: 1,   // Serial: ensures exactly one failure is reported
  } satisfies Partial<IConfiguration>,

  // CI gate: fast-fail smoke run on every PR
  'ci-gate': {
    import: ['src/steps/**/*.ts', 'src/support/**/*.ts'],
    format: ['progress-bar'],
    tags: '@smoke and not @wip',
    failFast: true,
    parallel: 2,
  } satisfies Partial<IConfiguration>,
} satisfies Record<string, Partial<IConfiguration>>;
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/bdd.yml — automatic triage job on regression failure
  triage-on-failure:
    name: BDD Root Cause Triage
    needs: bdd-regression
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '22' }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Run triage (fail-fast, serial)
        run: npx cucumber-js --profile triage
        env: { CI: 'true' }
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: triage-report
          path: reports/triage-report.html
          retention-days: 7
```

**Tradeoff**: Use `failFast: true` only in triage and CI-gate profiles — never in the nightly regression profile, where it would hide all failures after the first. Named alternatives: `--bail` flag in `playwright-bdd` projects (equivalent); Playwright's native `maxFailures` config option. [official]

---

### Pattern 13 — Gherkin `*` Bullet Step Pattern for Background Readability  [official]

The `*` (asterisk) keyword in Gherkin is a context-free step — it carries no Given/When/Then semantic weight. It is particularly useful in `Background` blocks where a sequence of setup steps has a natural list structure rather than a causal structure, and forcing Given/And/And creates artificial grammatical awkwardness.

```gherkin
# features/inventory/stock-alerts.feature
Feature: Inventory stock alert management

  # Background with * reads as a natural setup checklist
  Background:
    * the inventory system is running
    * the following products are in the catalog:
      | productId | name                | stockLevel |
      | prod-001  | Wireless Headphones | 15         |
      | prod-002  | Laptop Stand        | 3          |
      | prod-003  | USB-C Hub           | 0          |
    * low-stock threshold is configured to 5 units
    * the notification service is available

  Scenario: System generates alert when product stock drops below threshold
    Given a purchase reduces "Laptop Stand" stock to 2 units
    When the inventory reconciliation job runs
    Then a low-stock alert should be sent for "Laptop Stand"
    And no alert should be sent for "Wireless Headphones"

  Scenario: Out-of-stock products trigger a critical alert regardless of threshold
    When the inventory reconciliation job runs
    Then a critical out-of-stock alert should be sent for "USB-C Hub"
```

```typescript
// src/steps/inventory-background.steps.ts — * step definitions using Given
import { Given } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
// Cucumber maps * to the closest preceding keyword context.
// In a Background block, * is treated as Given.
import { DataTable } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

// Matches: * the inventory system is running
Given('the inventory system is running', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  const res = await this.page.request.get('/api/inventory/health');
  if (!res.ok()) {
    throw new Error(`Inventory system health check failed: ${res.status()}`);
  }
  this.attach('Inventory system health: OK', 'text/plain');
});

// Matches: * the following products are in the catalog:
Given(
  'the following products are in the catalog:',
  async function (this: AppWorld, table: DataTable) {
    const products = table.hashes();
    for (const product of products) {
      await this.page.request.post('/api/test/inventory/seed', {
        data: {
          productId: product['productId'],
          name: product['name'],
          stockLevel: parseInt(product['stockLevel'] ?? '0', 10),
        },
      });
    }
    this.seedProductIds = products.map(p => p['productId'] ?? '');
    this.attach(`Seeded ${products.length} products`, 'text/plain');
  }
);

// Matches: * low-stock threshold is configured to {int} units
Given(
  'low-stock threshold is configured to {int} units',
  async function (this: AppWorld, threshold: number) {
    await this.page.request.put('/api/test/inventory/config', {
      data: { lowStockThreshold: threshold },
    });
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use `*` in `Background` blocks where the setup list has no natural causal ordering. Do NOT use `*` in scenario bodies — Given/When/Then structure in the scenario itself is mandatory for clarity and readability. Do NOT replace all Given/When/Then with `*` to avoid thinking about step semantics; reserve it for genuine list-style setups. Named alternatives: multiple `And` steps under an initial `Given` (valid but creates a dangling `And` if the `Given` is removed). [official]

---

### Pattern 14 — Scenario-Level Attachment Taxonomy for Debugging  [community]

`this.attach()` is used ad-hoc across step definitions, producing Cucumber HTML reports where attachments are scattered without structure. A three-tier attachment taxonomy — **evidence** (screenshots, responses), **context** (step metadata, configuration), **diagnostic** (stack traces, timing) — makes reports self-navigating and enables automated artifact analysis in CI.

```typescript
// src/support/attachments.ts — structured tiered attachment helper
import { IWorld } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

export type AttachmentTier = 'evidence' | 'context' | 'diagnostic';

interface AttachOpts {
  tier: AttachmentTier;
  label: string;
  mimeType?: string;
}

/**
 * Structured attach helper — prefixes each attachment label with its tier.
 * evidence:   screenshots, API responses, email content
 * context:    step parameters, configuration values, scenario metadata
 * diagnostic: timing data, stack traces, retry counts
 */
export function tieredAttach(
  world: IWorld,
  data: string | Buffer,
  opts: AttachOpts
): void {
  const prefix = `[${opts.tier.toUpperCase()}] ${opts.label}`;
  const mime = opts.mimeType ??
    (Buffer.isBuffer(data) ? 'application/octet-stream' : 'text/plain');

  if (Buffer.isBuffer(data)) {
    world.attach(data, mime);
    world.attach(prefix, 'text/plain');
  } else {
    world.attach(`${prefix}\n${'─'.repeat(prefix.length)}\n${data}`, mime);
  }
}

// src/support/hooks.ts — use tieredAttach in After hook for consistent evidence
import { After, Status } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from './world';
import { tieredAttach } from './attachments';

After(async function (this: AppWorld, scenario) {
  if (scenario.result?.status === Status.FAILED) {
    // Evidence: screenshot
    const screenshot = await this.page.screenshot({ fullPage: true });
    tieredAttach(this, screenshot, {
      tier: 'evidence',
      label: `Screenshot — ${scenario.pickle.name}`,
      mimeType: 'image/png',
    });

    // Evidence: page HTML
    const html = await this.page.content();
    tieredAttach(this, html, {
      tier: 'evidence',
      label: 'Page HTML at failure',
      mimeType: 'text/html',
    });

    // Diagnostic: navigation timing
    const timing = await this.page.evaluate(() =>
      JSON.stringify(performance.getEntriesByType('navigation')[0])
    );
    tieredAttach(this, timing, {
      tier: 'diagnostic',
      label: 'Navigation timing at failure',
    });

    // Context: scenario metadata
    tieredAttach(this, JSON.stringify({
      baseUrl: this.parameters?.baseUrl,
      role: this.currentRole,
      testUserId: this.testUserId,
    }, null, 2), {
      tier: 'context',
      label: 'Scenario context',
    });
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff**: Use the tiered taxonomy from the first sprint so reports are self-documenting by default. Do NOT attach large binary files (videos, HAR files > 5 MB) to the Cucumber HTML report — use `actions/upload-artifact` for large files and attach a reference link. Named alternatives: Allure Framework's built-in attachment categorization (richer but requires the full Allure stack). [community]

---

### Pattern 15 — Cucumber.js Native TypeScript Config with `tsx` (Node.js 22+)  [official]

Cucumber.js v12.4+ supports loading `cucumber.ts` config files natively on Node.js 22+ via the `--import tsx/esm` flag without `ts-node`. This eliminates the `requireModule: ['ts-node/register']` setup that broke with ESM and reduces the config toolchain to a single dependency.

```typescript
// cucumber.ts — native TypeScript config, no ts-node required (Node.js 22+, tsx 4.x)
import type { IConfiguration } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

// Shared import globs — defined once, referenced in every profile
const sharedImports: string[] = [
  'src/steps/**/*.ts',
  'src/support/**/*.ts',
];

export default {
  default: {
    import: sharedImports,
    format: [
      'progress-bar',
      'html:reports/cucumber-report.html',
    ],
    tags: 'not @wip',
    parallel: 4,
    retry: 0,
    failFast: false,
    publish: false,
  } satisfies Partial<IConfiguration>,

  smoke: {
    import: sharedImports,
    format: ['progress-bar'],
    tags: '@smoke and not @wip',
    parallel: 2,
    failFast: true,
  } satisfies Partial<IConfiguration>,

  regression: {
    import: sharedImports,
    format: [
      'progress-bar',
      'html:reports/regression-report.html',
      '@cucumber/json-formatter:reports/results.json',
    ],
    tags: '@regression and not @wip',
    parallel: 8,
    retry: 1,
    retryTagFilter: '@flaky',
  } satisfies Partial<IConfiguration>,
};
```

```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "test:bdd":            "node --import tsx/esm node_modules/.bin/cucumber-js",
    "test:bdd:smoke":      "node --import tsx/esm node_modules/.bin/cucumber-js --profile smoke",
    "test:bdd:regression": "node --import tsx/esm node_modules/.bin/cucumber-js --profile regression"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@cucumber/cucumber": "^12.8.3",
    "@cucumber/json-formatter": "^1.0.0",
    "tsx": "^4.19.0",
    "typescript": "^5.5.0"
  }
}
```

**Tradeoff**: Use on Node.js 22+ with `tsx` for the simplest possible TypeScript BDD setup. Do NOT use on Node.js 18/20 — the native `--import` TypeScript transform requires Node.js 22; use `ts-node/esm` loader on older runtimes. Do NOT use the `.ts` config extension on projects that must support both CJS and ESM simultaneously. Named alternatives: `ts-node/esm` loader (works on Node.js 18+, extra dependency); `esbuild-register` (faster transpile, less ecosystem support). [official]

## Community Gotchas — Cycle 30

**[community] Gotcha 1 — `DataTable.transpose()` silently includes the origin cell in the first column**: `DataTable.transpose()` rotates the table so that the first row becomes the first column. If your table has a label in position `[0][0]` (the intersection of row headers and column headers), that label is included as the first value in the rotated first column. WHY this matters: teams that use `transpose().hashes()` on a permission matrix discover that the first "role" key in their parsed objects is the string `"action"` (the header label) — causing subtle assertion misses where the header-as-role silently passes because no permission check targets `"action"`. Fix: always use `raw()` for irregular matrix shapes and parse the header explicitly.

**[community] Gotcha 2 — `page.unroute()` in After hooks does not cancel in-flight requests**: When you add a `page.route()` override to simulate latency and then `unroute()` in the `After` hook, any requests already in flight at unroute time still follow the overridden handler. WHY this causes flakiness: the `After` hook runs immediately after the final step assertion, but background polling requests (e.g., a React Query refetch triggered by a state update) may be mid-flight. These hit the stub handler and can generate error events that bleed into the next scenario's `Before` setup on a reused context. Fix: always call `this.context.close()` in `After` to cleanly terminate all in-flight requests rather than unrouting individual patterns.

**[community] Gotcha 3 — `satisfies Partial<IConfiguration>` requires TypeScript 4.9+, not just Node.js 22+**: The `satisfies` keyword for type-safe Cucumber config profiles is a TypeScript 4.9 language feature, independent of Node.js version. Teams that upgrade Node.js to 22 for native TypeScript loading without updating their `typescript` package get a confusing `error TS1109: Expression expected` near `satisfies`. WHY teams miss this: Node.js and TypeScript version pins are managed independently in most project scaffolds. The fix is straightforward (`npm install -D typescript@latest`) but the error message points to the keyword itself rather than the version mismatch.

**[community] Gotcha 4 — `failFast: true` with `parallel > 1` stops after the current batch completes, not immediately**: Cucumber.js's `failFast` sends a stop signal to the worker pool when the first failure is detected, but workers that have already picked up a scenario finish executing it before stopping. This means `failFast` with `parallel: 8` can produce up to 8 additional scenario results after the triggering failure. WHY this surprises teams: they expect exactly one failed scenario in the report and instead see 1–8, making it unclear which was the root cause. For true single-failure triage, set `parallel: 1` alongside `failFast: true` in the triage profile.

**[community] Gotcha 5 — Performance budget `Then` steps produce false CI failures because CI runners are slower than developer machines**: `window.performance.timing`-based budget assertions that pass on a developer laptop (2000ms budget, 800ms actual load) regularly fail on shared GitHub Actions runners during peak hours (2000ms budget, 2300ms actual load). WHY teams underestimate this: budgets are measured locally and ported directly to CI without a calibration factor. Fix: set CI performance budgets 2–3x higher than local measurements, tag performance scenarios with `@performance` to exclude them from PR smoke gates entirely, and run performance budget scenarios on dedicated bare-metal runners where CPU and network resources are predictable and consistent.

## Cycle 31 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 1 — `defineParameterType` Composite Domain Object with Validation  [official]

Cucumber Expressions `defineParameterType` can construct and validate rich domain objects directly from step parameters — eliminating repetitive parsing boilerplate in step bodies and keeping domain invariants co-located with the type definition rather than scattered across step files.

```typescript
// src/support/parameters.ts — composite domain object parameter type
import { defineParameterType } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

interface Money {
  amount: number;
  currency: 'USD' | 'EUR' | 'GBP';
}

// Matches: "USD 49.99", "EUR 1,200.00", "GBP 0.50"
defineParameterType({
  name: 'money',
  regexp: /([A-Z]{3})\s+([\d,]+\.\d{2})/,
  transformer(currencyStr: string, amountStr: string): Money {
    const currency = currencyStr as Money['currency'];
    const validCurrencies: Money['currency'][] = ['USD', 'EUR', 'GBP'];
    if (!validCurrencies.includes(currency)) {
      throw new Error(`Unsupported currency: ${currencyStr}`);
    }
    const amount = parseFloat(amountStr.replace(/,/g, ''));
    if (isNaN(amount) || amount < 0) {
      throw new Error(`Invalid amount: ${amountStr}`);
    }
    return { amount, currency };
  },
  useForSnippets: false,
});

// src/steps/pricing.steps.ts — clean step definitions using {money}
import { Given, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

Given(
  'the product price is {money}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, price: Money) {
    await this.page.request.patch(`/api/products/${this.productId}/price`, {
      data: { amount: price.amount, currency: price.currency },
    });
  }
);

Then(
  'the invoice total should be {money}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, expected: Money) {
    const res = await this.page.request.get(`/api/invoices/${this.invoiceId}`);
    const invoice = await res.json();
    expect(invoice.total.amount).toBeCloseTo(expected.amount, 2);
    expect(invoice.total.currency).toBe(expected.currency);
  }
);

// Feature file usage:
// Given the product price is USD 49.99
// Then the invoice total should be USD 49.99
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when the same domain-object construction and validation logic appears in three or more step definitions — the parameter type centralises the invariant once. Do NOT use for simple scalar types that are adequately covered by the built-in `{int}`, `{float}`, and `{string}` Cucumber Expressions parameters; the extra abstraction adds cognitive overhead for no gain. Named alternative: parsing inline inside each step definition (simple, no abstraction; fine for one or two steps). [official]

---

### Pattern 2 — Scenario Outline `Examples` Tag Filtering for Release Gating  [official]

Each `Examples` table block under a `Scenario Outline` can carry its own tags, enabling individual data partitions to be routed to different pipeline stages — smoke, regression, or nightly — without duplicating the scenario template.

```gherkin
# features/payments/refund.feature
Feature: Order refund processing

  Scenario Outline: Refund is processed within the SLA window
    Given order "<orderId>" was placed <daysAgo> days ago
    When the customer requests a full refund
    Then the refund should be processed within <expectedSla> hours
    And the refund status should be "<expectedStatus>"

    @smoke @critical
    Examples: Same-day refunds (within 24 h)
      | orderId   | daysAgo | expectedSla | expectedStatus |
      | ORD-001   | 0       | 1           | COMPLETED      |
      | ORD-002   | 1       | 2           | COMPLETED      |

    @regression
    Examples: Standard refunds (2–14 days)
      | orderId   | daysAgo | expectedSla | expectedStatus |
      | ORD-003   | 7       | 24          | COMPLETED      |
      | ORD-004   | 14      | 48          | COMPLETED      |

    @nightly @edge-case
    Examples: Late refund edge cases (15+ days, policy-dependent)
      | orderId   | daysAgo | expectedSla | expectedStatus |
      | ORD-005   | 15      | 72          | PENDING_REVIEW |
      | ORD-006   | 30      | 72          | DECLINED       |
```

```typescript
// cucumber.ts — profile uses tag expressions to target specific Examples blocks
export default {
  smoke: {
    import: ['src/steps/**/*.ts', 'src/support/**/*.ts'],
    tags: '@smoke and not @wip',
    parallel: 2,
    failFast: true,
  },
  nightly: {
    import: ['src/steps/**/*.ts', 'src/support/**/*.ts'],
    tags: 'not @wip',
    parallel: 8,
    retry: 1,
  },
} satisfies Record<string, Partial<IConfiguration>>;
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when a single scenario template covers data at significantly different criticality levels — critical happy paths alongside edge cases that should not block PR merges. Do NOT tag individual `Examples` rows (Gherkin does not support per-row tags); the granularity unit is the entire `Examples` block. Named alternative: separate feature files for smoke vs regression data sets (cleaner file organization but duplicates the scenario template). [official]

---

### Pattern 3 — BDD Contract Test with Playwright `APIRequestContext` and JSON Schema  [community]

API contract BDD scenarios combine Playwright's `APIRequestContext` with JSON Schema validation to specify and enforce the exact response shape as a living specification — preventing silent breaking changes when upstream services evolve their API contract.

```gherkin
# features/api/user-profile-contract.feature
@contract @regression
Feature: User Profile API contract

  Background:
    Given the API base URL is configured for the current environment

  Scenario: GET /users/:id returns a valid user profile shape
    Given a user with ID "usr-42" exists in the system
    When I request "GET /users/usr-42"
    Then the response status should be 200
    And the response body should conform to the "UserProfile" JSON schema

  Scenario: PATCH /users/:id rejects an invalid email format
    Given a user with ID "usr-42" exists in the system
    When I send "PATCH /users/usr-42" with body:
      """json
      { "email": "not-an-email" }
      """
    Then the response status should be 422
    And the response body should contain field "errors.email"
```

```typescript
// src/steps/api-contract.steps.ts
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import Ajv, { JSONSchemaType } from 'ajv';
import addFormats from 'ajv-formats';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';
import { loadJsonSchema } from '../support/schema-loader';

const ajv = new Ajv({ allErrors: true });
addFormats(ajv);
let lastResponse: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof fetch>> | null = null;

When(
  'I request {string}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, requestSpec: string) {
    const [method, path] = requestSpec.split(' ');
    this.lastResponse = await this.page.request.fetch(
      `${this.baseUrl}${path}`,
      { method }
    );
    this.attach(
      `${method} ${path} → ${this.lastResponse.status()}`,
      'text/plain'
    );
  }
);

Then(
  'the response body should conform to the {string} JSON schema',
  async function (this: AppWorld, schemaName: string) {
    const body = await this.lastResponse!.json();
    const schema = await loadJsonSchema(schemaName);
    const validate = ajv.compile(schema);
    const valid = validate(body);
    if (!valid) {
      const errors = ajv.errorsText(validate.errors);
      this.attach(`Schema violations:\n${errors}`, 'text/plain');
      throw new Error(`Response does not conform to schema "${schemaName}":\n${errors}`);
    }
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use for critical API endpoints that are consumed by multiple downstream services — the schema is the contract and the BDD scenario is the living proof that the contract is honoured on every build. Do NOT use for internal implementation endpoints that change frequently during development; schema churn turns the test into maintenance overhead. Named alternative: `zod` schema assertions inline in integration tests (more ergonomic TypeScript types, but loses the living-documentation readability of Gherkin). [community]

---

### Pattern 4 — `WorldParameters` Deep-Merge for Multi-Profile Configuration  [official]

Cucumber's `World.parameters` are populated from the `worldParameters` config key. When multiple profiles need partially overlapping configurations, a deep-merge utility at World construction time avoids duplicating shared keys across every profile and prevents runtime `undefined` access from missing keys.

```typescript
// src/support/deep-merge.ts — minimal typed deep-merge utility
export function deepMerge<T extends Record<string, unknown>>(
  base: T,
  overrides: Partial<T>
): T {
  const result = { ...base };
  for (const key of Object.keys(overrides) as Array<keyof T>) {
    const baseVal = base[key];
    const overrideVal = overrides[key];
    if (
      baseVal !== null &&
      overrideVal !== null &&
      typeof baseVal === 'object' &&
      typeof overrideVal === 'object' &&
      !Array.isArray(baseVal)
    ) {
      result[key] = deepMerge(
        baseVal as Record<string, unknown>,
        overrideVal as Record<string, unknown>
      ) as T[keyof T];
    } else if (overrideVal !== undefined) {
      result[key] = overrideVal as T[keyof T];
    }
  }
  return result;
}

// src/support/world.ts — merge base defaults with profile-supplied parameters
import { setWorldConstructor, World, IWorldOptions } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { deepMerge } from './deep-merge';

const BASE_PARAMS = {
  baseUrl: 'http://localhost:3000',
  apiTimeout: 5000,
  auth: { tokenEndpoint: '/api/auth/token', defaultRole: 'viewer' },
};

export class AppWorld extends World {
  readonly config: typeof BASE_PARAMS;

  constructor(options: IWorldOptions) {
    super(options);
    this.config = deepMerge(BASE_PARAMS, (options.parameters ?? {}) as Partial<typeof BASE_PARAMS>);
  }
}
setWorldConstructor(AppWorld);

// cucumber.ts — only override what differs per profile
export default {
  staging: {
    worldParameters: {
      baseUrl: 'https://staging.example.com',
      apiTimeout: 10000,
      // auth inherits from BASE_PARAMS — no duplication needed
    },
  },
} satisfies Record<string, Partial<IConfiguration>>;
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when three or more profiles share a large base configuration with only a handful of differing keys — deep-merge eliminates the DRY violation of copy-pasting the full config into each profile. Do NOT use when profiles are radically different (different apps, different authentication systems) — the apparent sharing is misleading and a full per-profile config is clearer. Named alternative: environment variables resolved in the World constructor (eliminates the worldParameters layer entirely but shifts config knowledge from `cucumber.ts` into the shell environment). [official]

---

### Pattern 5 — Flaky Scenario Quarantine with `@quarantine` Tag and CI Bypass  [community]

Flaky scenarios that generate false-positive CI failures should be quarantined, not deleted — they encode real business behavior whose reliability must eventually be restored. A `@quarantine` tag with a CI exclusion rule and a weekly audit job balances keeping the suite green with preventing silent test debt accumulation.

```gherkin
# features/notifications/email-delivery.feature
@smoke
Feature: Email notification delivery

  Scenario: Order confirmation email is sent within 2 minutes
    Given I complete a purchase
    When 2 minutes pass
    Then I should receive an order confirmation email

  # Quarantined 2026-05-10 — intermittent SMTP timeout in CI, tracked in JIRA BDD-447
  @quarantine @flaky
  Scenario: Promotional email is sent within 10 minutes of subscription
    Given I subscribe to the promotional newsletter
    When 10 minutes pass
    Then I should receive a welcome promotional email
```

```typescript
// cucumber.ts — quarantine tag excluded from all production pipeline profiles
import type { IConfiguration } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

export default {
  default: {
    import: ['src/steps/**/*.ts', 'src/support/**/*.ts'],
    tags: 'not @wip and not @quarantine',
    format: ['progress-bar', 'html:reports/report.html'],
    parallel: 4,
  } satisfies Partial<IConfiguration>,

  // Dedicated quarantine audit profile — run weekly in CI to detect recoveries
  quarantine: {
    import: ['src/steps/**/*.ts', 'src/support/**/*.ts'],
    tags: '@quarantine',
    format: [
      'progress-bar',
      'html:reports/quarantine-audit.html',
      '@cucumber/json-formatter:reports/quarantine.json',
    ],
    retry: 3,
    parallel: 1,
  } satisfies Partial<IConfiguration>,
} satisfies Record<string, Partial<IConfiguration>>;
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/quarantine-audit.yml — weekly quarantine recovery check
name: Quarantine Audit
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 9 * * 1'   # Every Monday at 09:00 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
jobs:
  quarantine-audit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx cucumber-js --profile quarantine
        env:
          TEST_ENV: staging
```

**Tradeoff**: Use for scenarios that represent real, verified business behavior but are failing due to infrastructure issues (SMTP delays, third-party API latency, test environment instability) rather than genuine product bugs. Do NOT quarantine scenarios for more than two sprints without a remediation ticket — quarantine is a holding pattern, not a graveyard. Named alternative: `retry: 3` on all scenarios (masks flakiness without surfacing it; leads to slow CI and hidden rot). [community]

---

### Pattern 6 — playwright-bdd Fixture-Based Page Object Integration  [community]

`playwright-bdd` v8+ supports Playwright fixture composition inside step definitions via the `$fixtures` test parameter. Integrating page objects as fixtures rather than World properties gives type-safe dependency injection, enables Playwright's parallel worker isolation, and makes the page object lifecycle explicit.

```typescript
// src/fixtures/checkout-page.ts — Playwright fixture as page object
import { Page } from '@playwright/test';

export class CheckoutPage {
  constructor(private readonly page: Page) {}

  async fillShippingAddress(address: {
    firstName: string;
    lastName: string;
    street: string;
    city: string;
    zip: string;
  }): Promise<void> {
    await this.page.getByLabel('First name').fill(address.firstName);
    await this.page.getByLabel('Last name').fill(address.lastName);
    await this.page.getByLabel('Street address').fill(address.street);
    await this.page.getByLabel('City').fill(address.city);
    await this.page.getByLabel('ZIP code').fill(address.zip);
  }

  async submitOrder(): Promise<string> {
    await this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }).click();
    const confirmation = this.page.getByTestId('order-confirmation-number');
    await confirmation.waitFor({ state: 'visible' });
    return (await confirmation.textContent()) ?? '';
  }
}

// src/fixtures/index.ts — extend playwright-bdd test with page object fixtures
import { test as base, createBdd } from 'playwright-bdd';
import { CheckoutPage } from './checkout-page';

export const test = base.extend<{ checkoutPage: CheckoutPage }>({
  checkoutPage: async ({ page }, use) => {
    await use(new CheckoutPage(page));
  },
});

export const { Given, When, Then } = createBdd(test);

// src/steps/checkout.steps.ts — steps receive fixtures, not raw Page
import { When, Then } from '../fixtures';

When(
  'I complete the checkout with shipping address:',
  async ({ checkoutPage }, table: DataTable) => {
    const [row] = table.hashes();
    await checkoutPage.fillShippingAddress({
      firstName: row['firstName'] ?? '',
      lastName: row['lastName'] ?? '',
      street: row['street'] ?? '',
      city: row['city'] ?? '',
      zip: row['zip'] ?? '',
    });
  }
);

Then(
  'I should receive an order confirmation number',
  async ({ checkoutPage }, world) => {
    const orderNumber = await checkoutPage.submitOrder();
    expect(orderNumber).toMatch(/^ORD-\d{6,}$/);
    world.attach(`Order number: ${orderNumber}`, 'text/plain');
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use on projects already committed to `playwright-bdd` where parallel worker isolation and fixture lifecycle management (setup/teardown) are priorities. Do NOT mix this pattern with the Cucumber.js `World`-based approach in the same project — the two dependency-injection models are incompatible and merging them produces confusing step files. Named alternative: World-based page object storage (`this.checkoutPage = new CheckoutPage(this.page)`) — simpler for Cucumber.js-only projects without Playwright fixture composition needs. [community]
