### Pattern 7 — Gherkin DocString with Content-Type for Structured Payload Steps  [official]

Gherkin DocStrings can carry a content-type annotation (` ```json `, ` ```yaml `, ` ```xml `) that signals to the step definition how the body should be parsed. Cucumber.js v12+ exposes the `mediaType` on the `docString` argument, enabling generic request-body steps that dispatch to the correct parser without per-format step variants.

```gherkin
# features/api/webhook-dispatch.feature
Feature: Webhook event dispatch

  Scenario: Webhook receives a valid order-created event
    When I dispatch webhook event:
      ```json
      {
        "event": "order.created",
        "orderId": "ORD-999",
        "timestamp": "2026-05-14T08:00:00Z",
        "payload": { "total": 149.99, "currency": "USD" }
      }
      ```
    Then the webhook handler should respond with status 200
    And the event should be recorded in the audit log

  Scenario: Webhook rejects a malformed XML event
    When I dispatch webhook event:
      ```xml
      <event type="order.created">
        <orderId>ORD-999</orderId>
        <!-- missing required timestamp -->
      </event>
      ```
    Then the webhook handler should respond with status 400
```

```typescript
// src/steps/webhook.steps.ts — content-type-aware DocString dispatch
import { When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

interface DocString {
  content: string;
  mediaType?: string;
}

When(
  'I dispatch webhook event:',
  async function (this: AppWorld, docString: DocString) {
    const contentType =
      docString.mediaType === 'json' ? 'application/json' :
      docString.mediaType === 'xml'  ? 'application/xml'  :
      docString.mediaType === 'yaml' ? 'application/x-yaml' :
      'text/plain';

    this.lastResponse = await this.page.request.post(
      `${this.baseUrl}/webhooks/inbound`,
      {
        data: docString.content,
        headers: { 'Content-Type': contentType },
      }
    );
    this.attach(
      `Dispatched ${contentType} event → HTTP ${this.lastResponse.status()}`,
      'text/plain'
    );
  }
);

Then(
  'the webhook handler should respond with status {int}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, expectedStatus: number) {
    expect(this.lastResponse?.status()).toBe(expectedStatus);
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when a step needs to accept structured multi-format payloads (JSON, XML, YAML) without creating a separate step definition per format — the content-type annotation keeps format semantics visible in the feature file. Do NOT use DocStrings for payloads that fit on a single line; inline string parameters are more readable. Named alternative: DataTable with a single `body` column (awkward for nested JSON; loses content-type semantics). [official]

---

### Pattern 8 — BDD Scenario for WebSocket Real-Time Behavior via `page.routeWebSocket()`  [official]

Playwright's `page.routeWebSocket()` (v1.48+) enables deterministic BDD scenarios for real-time WebSocket features without a live WebSocket backend. Step definitions control the mock server's emit schedule, making time-sensitive streaming behavior fully reproducible in CI.

```gherkin
# features/live-feed/price-ticker.feature
@regression
Feature: Live price ticker

  Scenario: Price updates are reflected in the UI within 500ms
    Given I am viewing the price ticker for "AAPL"
    When the price feed emits an update to "USD 213.45"
    Then the displayed price should update to "USD 213.45" within 500 milliseconds

  Scenario: Stale indicator appears after 5 seconds without a price update
    Given I am viewing the price ticker for "AAPL"
    When the price feed stops sending updates for 5 seconds
    Then the stale data indicator should be visible
```

```typescript
// src/steps/price-ticker.steps.ts — WebSocket mock via routeWebSocket
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';
import type { WebSocketRoute } from '@playwright/test';

Given(
  'I am viewing the price ticker for {string}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, ticker: string) {
    this.wsRoute = await new Promise<WebSocketRoute>((resolve) => {
      this.page.routeWebSocket(/\/ws\/prices/, (ws) => {
        resolve(ws);
        ws.connect(); // relay to real backend or stub
      });
    });
    await this.page.goto(`${this.baseUrl}/ticker/${ticker}`);
    await this.page.getByTestId('price-ticker').waitFor({ state: 'visible' });
  }
);

When(
  'the price feed emits an update to {string}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, price: string) {
    this.wsRoute?.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'price', value: price }));
  }
);

Then(
  'the displayed price should update to {string} within {int} milliseconds',
  async function (this: AppWorld, price: string, ms: number) {
    await expect(
      this.page.getByTestId('price-ticker').getByTestId('current-price')
    ).toHaveText(price, { timeout: ms });
  }
);

Then(
  'the stale data indicator should be visible',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    await expect(
      this.page.getByTestId('stale-indicator')
    ).toBeVisible({ timeout: 6000 });
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use for WebSocket-driven UI features (live prices, notifications, collaborative editing) where the real backend is unavailable in CI or introduces timing non-determinism. Do NOT use for WebSocket message ordering tests that require the real server's message sequencing guarantees — mocked routes cannot reproduce server-side message queuing behaviour. Named alternative: `page.waitForEvent('websocket')` + real backend (accurate but fragile in CI due to network dependencies). [official]

---

### Pattern 9 — Step Definition Co-Location via `externalise` Option  [official]

Cucumber.js v12.8.0 introduced the `externalise` option, which extracts step definitions, hooks, and World classes from inline `require`/`import` paths into importable modules. This enables cross-package step sharing in monorepos without manual copy-paste or fragile dynamic `require` hacks.

```typescript
// packages/shared-steps/src/index.ts — shared step module
import { Given, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from './world';

Given(
  'I am authenticated as a {string} user',
  async function (this: AppWorld, role: string) {
    const token = await this.authService.getTokenForRole(role);
    await this.page.request.storageState();
    this.currentRole = role;
    this.authToken = token;
    this.attach(`Authenticated as role: ${role}`, 'text/plain');
  }
);

Then(
  'I should see the {string} section',
  async function (this: AppWorld, sectionName: string) {
    await expect(
      this.page.getByRole('region', { name: sectionName })
    ).toBeVisible();
  }
);

// packages/shared-steps/package.json
// { "name": "@acme/bdd-shared-steps", "main": "dist/index.js" }

// apps/billing/cucumber.ts — consume shared steps via externalise
import type { IConfiguration } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

export default {
  default: {
    import: [
      'src/steps/**/*.ts',
      'src/support/**/*.ts',
    ],
    externalise: [
      // Load shared steps from the monorepo package
      '@acme/bdd-shared-steps',
    ],
    format: ['progress-bar', 'html:reports/report.html'],
    parallel: 4,
  } satisfies Partial<IConfiguration>,
};

// apps/payments/cucumber.ts — same shared steps, different app-specific steps
export default {
  default: {
    import: ['src/steps/**/*.ts', 'src/support/**/*.ts'],
    externalise: ['@acme/bdd-shared-steps'],
    format: ['progress-bar'],
    parallel: 4,
  } satisfies Partial<IConfiguration>,
};
```

**Tradeoff**: Use in monorepos with multiple Cucumber.js applications that share common authentication, navigation, and assertion steps. The `externalise` option keeps the shared module versioned and independently releasable. Do NOT use `externalise` for domain-specific steps that are unlikely to be reused — every cross-package dependency adds a version-coordination burden. Named alternative: direct `import` glob pointing at the shared package's source (works but bypasses the `externalise` package resolution mechanism and produces duplicate step registration if both the glob and `externalise` load the same module). [official]

---

### Pattern 10 — Gherkin Background Scoped to `Rule` Block  [official]

When a feature file contains multiple `Rule` keywords, a `Background` block declared immediately inside a `Rule` applies only to scenarios within that rule — not to the entire feature. This prevents over-broad setup that leaks irrelevant preconditions into unrelated scenarios.

```gherkin
# features/subscriptions/billing-cycle.feature
Feature: Subscription billing cycle management

  Rule: Free-tier users cannot access premium features

    Background:
      Given I am signed in as a free-tier user

    Scenario: Free user cannot view analytics dashboard
      When I navigate to the analytics dashboard
      Then I should see the upgrade prompt
      And I should not see any analytics data

    Scenario: Free user cannot export data
      When I attempt to export my account data as CSV
      Then I should see the error "Export is a premium feature"

  Rule: Premium users can manage their billing cycle

    Background:
      Given I am signed in as a premium user
      And my current billing cycle ends on "2026-06-01"

    Scenario: Premium user can switch from monthly to annual billing
      When I change my billing frequency to annual
      Then my next billing date should be "2027-06-01"
      And I should see a prorated credit applied

    Scenario: Premium user can cancel and retain access until cycle end
      When I cancel my subscription
      Then my access should remain active until "2026-06-01"
      And I should see the "Access until [date]" banner
```

```typescript
// src/steps/subscription.steps.ts — Rule-scoped steps
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

Given(
  'I am signed in as a {word}-tier user',
  async function (this: AppWorld, tier: string) {
    const credentials = await this.authService.getCredentialsForTier(tier);
    await this.page.goto(`${this.baseUrl}/login`);
    await this.page.getByLabel('Email').fill(credentials.email);
    await this.page.getByLabel('Password').fill(credentials.password);
    await this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
    await this.page.waitForURL('**/dashboard');
    this.currentTier = tier;
  }
);

Given(
  'my current billing cycle ends on {string}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, endDate: string) {
    await this.page.request.patch(`/api/test/billing/cycle`, {
      data: { userId: this.userId, cycleEnd: endDate },
    });
    this.billingCycleEnd = endDate;
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when a feature file contains two or more `Rule` blocks with fundamentally different user states or preconditions — Rule-scoped `Background` makes it immediately clear which setup belongs to which business rule. Do NOT use Rule-scoped `Background` when all scenarios in the file share the same preconditions; a top-level `Background` is simpler. Named alternative: `Before({ tags: '@free-tier' })` hooks in TypeScript (moves the setup out of the feature file, making the precondition invisible to non-technical readers). [official]

---

### Pattern 11 — `setDefaultTimeout` with Per-Scenario Override for Long-Running Flows  [official]

Cucumber.js `setDefaultTimeout` establishes a global step timeout, but some scenarios (email delivery, async job processing, payment settlement) legitimately require longer windows. A tagged override pattern using `Before` hooks with `setDefaultTimeout` scoped per-scenario keeps the global timeout tight while accommodating known slow paths.

```typescript
// src/support/timeouts.ts — timeout constants
export const TIMEOUTS = {
  default: 10_000,    // 10s — most UI interactions
  async:   30_000,    // 30s — API calls, DB reads
  slow:    90_000,    // 90s — email delivery, async jobs
  extreme: 300_000,   // 5min — payment settlement, batch processing
} as const;

// src/support/hooks.ts — set default and per-tag overrides
import {
  Before,
  After,
  setDefaultTimeout,
  type ITestCaseHookParameter,
} from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { TIMEOUTS } from './timeouts';
import { AppWorld } from './world';

// Establish global default
setDefaultTimeout(TIMEOUTS.default);

// Override for @slow scenarios — applied before any step runs
Before({ tags: '@slow' }, function (this: AppWorld) {
  setDefaultTimeout(TIMEOUTS.slow);
  this.attach(`Timeout override: ${TIMEOUTS.slow}ms (@slow)`, 'text/plain');
});

Before({ tags: '@extreme' }, function (this: AppWorld) {
  setDefaultTimeout(TIMEOUTS.extreme);
  this.attach(`Timeout override: ${TIMEOUTS.extreme}ms (@extreme)`, 'text/plain');
});

// Restore global default after each scenario to prevent leak
After(function (this: AppWorld) {
  setDefaultTimeout(TIMEOUTS.default);
});

// Feature file usage:
// @slow @regression
// Scenario: Order confirmation email is delivered within 90 seconds
//   Given I complete a purchase
//   When 90 seconds pass
//   Then I should receive an order confirmation email
```

**Tradeoff**: Use for genuinely slow business flows that are known and stable — email delivery SLAs, payment gateway settlement windows, background job queues. Do NOT use `@slow` as a workaround for flaky tests that fail within the default timeout intermittently; fix the flakiness instead of expanding the window. Named alternative: `{ timeout: 90_000 }` option on individual step definitions (more granular but requires touching every step in the slow scenario). [official]

---

### Pattern 12 — Serenity/JS Screenplay Actor Reuse Across BDD Scenarios  [community]

Serenity/JS v3 Screenplay Pattern actors persist state across `Given/When/Then` steps when the same actor name is reused. This enables multi-step business flows where intermediate state (tokens, IDs, responses) is carried forward without World property pollution.

```typescript
// src/screenplay/abilities/browse-the-web.ts — Playwright browser ability
import { Ability, UsesAbilities } from '@serenity-js/core';
import { Page } from '@playwright/test';

export class BrowseTheWeb extends Ability {
  static as(actor: UsesAbilities): BrowseTheWeb {
    return actor.abilityTo(BrowseTheWeb);
  }

  constructor(public readonly page: Page) {
    super();
  }
}

// src/screenplay/tasks/place-order.ts — Serenity/JS Task
import { Task, actorInTheSpotlight } from '@serenity-js/core';
import { Navigate, PageElement, Click, Enter, Text } from '@serenity-js/playwright';

export const PlaceOrder = {
  forItem: (itemName: string) =>
    Task.where(`#actor places an order for ${itemName}`,
      Navigate.to('/shop'),
      Click.on(PageElement.located(By.cssContainingText('button', 'Add to cart')).of(
        PageElement.located(By.cssContainingText('[data-testid="product"]', itemName))
      )),
      Navigate.to('/checkout'),
      Click.on(PageElement.located(By.css('[data-testid="place-order"]'))),
    ),
};

// src/steps/order.steps.ts — Serenity/JS steps with named actor
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { actorCalled, actorInTheSpotlight } from '@serenity-js/core';
import { Ensure, equals } from '@serenity-js/assertions';
import { PlaceOrder } from '../screenplay/tasks/place-order';
import { Text, PageElement, By } from '@serenity-js/playwright';

Given(
  '{word} is a registered customer',
  async (_actorName: string) => {
    // Actor creation seeds authentication state
    const actor = actorCalled(_actorName);
    // Ability attachment happens in BeforeAll via fixture
  }
);

When(
  '{word} places an order for {string}',
  async (actorName: string, itemName: string) => {
    await actorCalled(actorName).attemptsTo(
      PlaceOrder.forItem(itemName),
    );
  }
);

Then(
  '{word} should see an order confirmation',
  async (actorName: string) => {
    await actorCalled(actorName).attemptsTo(
      Ensure.that(
        Text.of(PageElement.located(By.css('[data-testid="confirmation-message"]'))),
        equals('Your order has been placed')
      )
    );
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use on teams already invested in the Screenplay Pattern who need to describe multi-actor collaborative business flows (e.g., a buyer and a seller interacting in a marketplace). Do NOT introduce Serenity/JS solely for single-actor BDD suites — the Screenplay abstraction adds considerable boilerplate compared to Cucumber.js + Playwright directly. Named alternative: World properties for shared state (`this.orderId`, `this.token`) — simpler single-actor approach with no additional framework dependency. [community]

---

### Pattern 13 — `cucumber-junit-xml` CI Integration for Test Management Platform Sync  [community]

Most enterprise test management platforms (Jira Xray, TestRail, Azure Test Plans) consume JUnit XML to import execution results. Generating a standards-compliant JUnit XML report from Cucumber.js and annotating scenarios with external test IDs in tags enables bidirectional traceability: the feature file is the source of truth, and the test management platform reflects live CI pass/fail state.

```gherkin
# features/payments/checkout.feature
# @xray:TEST-1234 maps this scenario to Jira Xray test case TEST-1234
@regression @xray:TEST-1234
Scenario: Customer completes a credit card payment
  Given I have items in my cart totalling USD 99.00
  When I complete checkout with a valid Visa card
  Then my order should be confirmed
  And the payment status should be "SETTLED"

@smoke @xray:TEST-1235
Scenario: Declined card shows user-friendly error
  Given I have items in my cart
  When I attempt checkout with a declined Visa card
  Then I should see the message "Your card was declined"
  And my cart should remain unchanged
```

```typescript
// cucumber.ts — JUnit XML formatter with classname mapping for Xray
import type { IConfiguration } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

export default {
  ci: {
    import: ['src/steps/**/*.ts', 'src/support/**/*.ts'],
    format: [
      'progress-bar',
      // junit formatter produces Xray-compatible XML
      'junit:reports/junit-results.xml',
    ],
    tags: 'not @wip',
    parallel: 4,
    retry: 1,
    retryTagFilter: '@flaky',
  } satisfies Partial<IConfiguration>,
} satisfies Record<string, Partial<IConfiguration>>;
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml — upload JUnit XML and sync to Xray
- name: Run BDD tests
  run: npm run test:bdd:ci
- name: Publish test results
  uses: dorny/test-reporter@v1
  if: always()
  with:
    name: BDD Cucumber Results
    path: reports/junit-results.xml
    reporter: java-junit
- name: Sync results to Jira Xray
  if: always()
  run: |
    curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{ secrets.XRAY_TOKEN }}" \
         -H "Content-Type: application/xml" \
         --data @reports/junit-results.xml \
         "${{ secrets.XRAY_IMPORT_URL }}"
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when your organisation requires test execution traceability in a test management platform for compliance, auditing, or sprint reporting. Do NOT embed test management IDs in scenario titles (e.g., `Scenario: TEST-1234 — Customer completes...`) — that makes feature files unreadable when the ID changes; use tags exclusively. Named alternative: Allure TestOps integration (richer reporting, bi-directional sync, but requires the full Allure stack and a hosted instance). [community]

---

### Pattern 14 — Cucumber.js `env` Propagation to Parallel Workers  [official]

Cucumber.js v12.7.0 introduced automatic propagation of the parent process `process.env` to parallel worker child processes. Prior to this, workers had a stripped-down environment and secrets or feature flags set via env vars in CI were silently absent inside step definitions, causing mysterious `undefined` values.

```typescript
// src/support/config.ts — safe env var access with clear error messaging
export function requireEnv(key: string): string {
  const value = process.env[key];
  if (value === undefined || value === '') {
    throw new Error(
      `Required environment variable "${key}" is not set. ` +
      `Ensure it is exported in the CI pipeline and ` +
      `you are running Cucumber.js v12.7.0+.`
    );
  }
  return value;
}

export function optionalEnv(key: string, defaultValue: string): string {
  return process.env[key] ?? defaultValue;
}

// src/support/world.ts — uses requireEnv in constructor
import { setWorldConstructor, World, IWorldOptions } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { requireEnv, optionalEnv } from './config';

export class AppWorld extends World {
  readonly apiKey: string;
  readonly baseUrl: string;
  readonly environment: string;

  constructor(options: IWorldOptions) {
    super(options);
    // These env vars are now reliably available in parallel workers (v12.7.0+)
    this.apiKey    = requireEnv('API_KEY');
    this.baseUrl   = requireEnv('BASE_URL');
    this.environment = optionalEnv('TEST_ENV', 'local');
  }
}
setWorldConstructor(AppWorld);

// package.json script — env vars set here propagate to all workers
// "test:bdd:ci": "API_KEY=$API_KEY BASE_URL=$BASE_URL cucumber-js --profile ci"
```

```typescript
// src/steps/api.steps.ts — uses World properties populated from env
import { Given } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

Given(
  'the API is accessible',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    const res = await this.page.request.get(`${this.baseUrl}/health`, {
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${this.apiKey}` },
    });
    expect(res.ok()).toBe(true);
    this.attach(`API health: ${res.status()} @ ${this.baseUrl}`, 'text/plain');
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use as the default pattern on Cucumber.js v12.7.0+ — env propagation to workers requires no additional configuration and eliminates the pre-v12.7 workaround of reading env vars into `worldParameters` in `cucumber.ts`. Do NOT rely on env propagation for secrets that differ per worker in a parallel run (e.g., per-worker database credentials); use `worldParameters` with computed values instead. Named alternative: encoding all runtime config into `worldParameters` in `cucumber.ts` (fully explicit, works on all Cucumber.js versions, but requires restating every env var in the config file). [official]

---

### Pattern 15 — Gherkin `Scenario` vs `Scenario Outline` Decision Heuristic  [community]

Choosing between a flat `Scenario` and a parameterized `Scenario Outline` is a recurring judgment call. The wrong choice produces either duplicated scenario logic (should be an Outline) or an Examples table that has only one data meaning (should be a flat Scenario). A three-question decision heuristic prevents both failure modes.

```gherkin
# Three-question heuristic:
# Q1: Does the scenario template hold for N>1 meaningfully different data sets? → Outline
# Q2: Would removing one row from Examples leave an incomplete business rule? → Outline
# Q3: Are all columns in Examples used in the template? → If no, simplify to Scenario

# BAD — Outline with one data row (no parameterization benefit)
Scenario Outline: User logs in
  When I log in as "<email>"
  Then I should see my dashboard
  Examples:
    | email                |
    | alice@example.com    |

# GOOD — Flat Scenario (single known case, no data variation)
Scenario: Registered user accesses their dashboard
  Given I am a registered user with email "alice@example.com"
  When I log in
  Then I should see my dashboard

# BAD — Scenario duplicated three times (should be an Outline)
Scenario: Admin can view finance reports
  Given I am an admin user
  When I navigate to the finance reports section
  Then I should see the reports

Scenario: Finance manager can view finance reports
  Given I am a finance manager user
  When I navigate to the finance reports section
  Then I should see the reports

Scenario: Auditor can view finance reports
  Given I am an auditor user
  When I navigate to the finance reports section
  Then I should see the reports

# GOOD — Scenario Outline covering the permission matrix
Scenario Outline: Authorized roles can access finance reports
  Given I am a <role> user
  When I navigate to the finance reports section
  Then I should see the reports

  @smoke
  Examples: High-privilege roles
    | role          |
    | admin         |
    | finance-manager |

  @regression
  Examples: Audit roles
    | role    |
    | auditor |
```

```typescript
// src/steps/access-control.steps.ts — generic role step definition
import { Given } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

Given(
  'I am a {word} user',
  async function (this: AppWorld, role: string) {
    const credentials = await this.authService.getCredentialsForRole(role);
    if (!credentials) {
      throw new Error(`No test credentials configured for role: "${role}"`);
    }
    await this.page.goto(`${this.baseUrl}/login`);
    await this.page.getByLabel('Email').fill(credentials.email);
    await this.page.getByLabel('Password').fill(credentials.password);
    await this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
    await this.page.waitForURL('**/dashboard');
    this.currentRole = role;
    this.attach(`Signed in as role: ${role}`, 'text/plain');
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use a `Scenario Outline` when you have two or more genuinely distinct data cases that each represent a separate business rule or permission variant. Do NOT use `Scenario Outline` when the parameterization serves only test coverage concerns and not distinct business requirements — a single `Scenario` with a representative value communicates business intent more clearly. Named alternative: `Scenario` with `Examples` backed by a helper that loads data from a fixture file (useful when the data set is large and maintaining it inline in the feature file is impractical). [community]

---

## Community Gotchas — Cycle 31

**[community] Gotcha 1 — `externalise` modules are loaded before `import` globs, causing World registration order conflicts**: When using the Cucumber.js v12.8.0 `externalise` option alongside a project-local `import` glob that also calls `setWorldConstructor`, the externalized module's World registration runs first. If the local `import` glob then calls `setWorldConstructor` again with a different class, Cucumber silently uses the last registered constructor — not the most specific one. WHY this breaks multi-package monorepos: the shared package registers a base `AppWorld`, and the app package is expected to override it with a specialized subclass, but the glob order is not obvious from the config, and teams discover the wrong class is active only when app-specific properties are `undefined` at runtime. Fix: always define `setWorldConstructor` in exactly one location per project; extend the base class in the local package and call `setWorldConstructor` only there.

**[community] Gotcha 2 — `defineParameterType` with `useForSnippets: false` is invisible to the step snippet generator, causing confusing "ambiguous step" hints**: When you define a custom parameter type with `useForSnippets: false`, the Cucumber.js snippet generator does not know the type exists and suggests the generic `{string}` or `{word}` parameter in auto-generated snippets. Teams that rely on `--dry-run` or the VS Code Cucumber extension's snippet completion see suggestions that do not match their actual step signature, leading to mismatched step registration. WHY the default is `false`: custom parameter types are often too domain-specific to be useful in generic snippets. Fix: document custom parameter type names in a `src/support/PARAMETERS.md` file and configure team IDE templates to include common custom types.

**[community] Gotcha 3 — `page.routeWebSocket()` intercept handlers do not fire for WebSocket connections opened before the route is registered**: `page.routeWebSocket()` only intercepts WebSocket connections opened *after* the call returns. If a component opens a WebSocket connection on page load and the `Given` step navigates to the page before calling `routeWebSocket`, the real WebSocket connection is already established and the mock handler is never invoked. WHY this is easy to miss: the page transition and the route registration appear to be sequential in the step code, but `goto()` completes after the DOM is interactive — by which time a WebSocket-dependent component may have already connected. Fix: always call `page.routeWebSocket()` before `page.goto()` in the same step or the `Before` hook.

**[community] Gotcha 4 — Serenity/JS `actorCalled()` and Cucumber.js `setWorldConstructor` are mutually exclusive for state sharing**: Serenity/JS manages actor state via its own `ActorManager` singleton. When a team mixes `actorCalled('Alice')` in some steps and `this.actorAlice` stored on the Cucumber World in other steps, the two state stores diverge after the first state mutation. `actorCalled('Alice')` always returns the Serenity/JS-managed actor; `this.actorAlice` is a stale snapshot. WHY teams mix them: Serenity/JS integration examples often show `actorCalled()` without clarifying that World-based storage is incompatible. Fix: commit fully to one approach per project — either Serenity/JS `actorCalled()` everywhere, or Cucumber.js World properties everywhere. Never mix within the same test suite.

**[community] Gotcha 5 — JUnit XML `classname` attribute generated by Cucumber's built-in `junit` formatter does not match Xray's expected format for automatic test-case matching**: Cucumber.js's JUnit formatter sets `classname` to the feature file path (e.g., `features.payments.checkout`) and `name` to the scenario name. Jira Xray's import endpoint expects the `name` attribute to match the Xray test issue summary *exactly* for automatic deduplication. Teams that use auto-import without tagging (`@xray:TEST-xxx`) find that every CI run creates a new Xray test issue instead of updating the existing one, bloating the project. WHY the mismatch: Cucumber and Xray independently chose `name` as the key field with different formatting assumptions. Fix: use explicit `@xray:TEST-xxx` tags on every scenario and configure Xray to import in tag-match mode rather than name-match mode.

**[community] Gotcha 6 — `Background` steps inside a `Rule` block are not skipped when the `Rule`'s first `Scenario` is tagged `@wip`**: When Cucumber.js evaluates whether to skip a `Scenario` due to tag filtering (e.g., `tags: 'not @wip'`), it skips the scenario body but still executes any `Background` steps that precede it within the same `Rule` block. This means a `Before`/`Background` chain that sets up test data and opens a browser runs even when the scenario itself is `@wip`-excluded, wasting CI time and sometimes triggering unexpected side effects in the setup. WHY teams don't notice: the skipped scenario appears correctly absent from the report, but the `Background` execution is silent unless `--dry-run` reveals it. Fix: add the `@wip` tag to the `Rule` block itself (Gherkin supports tagging `Rule`), which causes the entire rule — including its `Background` — to be excluded by the tag filter.

### Pattern 1 — Cucumber.js `ITestCaseHookParameter.testStepDuration` for Per-Step SLA Assertions  [official]

The `ITestCaseHookParameter` object passed to `AfterStep` hooks includes `testStepDuration` (a `Duration` message from `@cucumber/messages`), enabling per-step wall-clock duration assertions directly inside the test suite without external tooling.

```typescript
// src/support/hooks.ts — per-step SLA enforcement via AfterStep
import { AfterStep, ITestStepHookParameter } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from './world';

// SLA thresholds keyed by step keyword + text prefix
const STEP_SLA_MS: Record<string, number> = {
  'When I submit':           3_000,  // Form submissions ≤ 3 s
  'When I search':           2_000,  // Search queries ≤ 2 s
  'Then I should see':       1_500,  // UI visibility ≤ 1.5 s
};

AfterStep(async function (this: AppWorld, { testStep, testStepDuration }: ITestStepHookParameter) {
  if (!testStepDuration) return;

  const durationMs =
    (testStepDuration.seconds ?? 0) * 1_000 +
    Math.round((testStepDuration.nanos ?? 0) / 1_000_000);

  const stepText = testStep.text ?? '';
  const matchedKey = Object.keys(STEP_SLA_MS).find(k => stepText.startsWith(k));
  if (!matchedKey) return;

  const sla = STEP_SLA_MS[matchedKey]!;
  if (durationMs > sla) {
    this.attach(
      `SLA BREACH: "${stepText}" took ${durationMs}ms (limit ${sla}ms)`,
      'text/plain'
    );
    // Optionally push to a metrics endpoint
    await this.metricsClient?.record({
      step: stepText,
      durationMs,
      sla,
      breached: true,
    });
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when your team needs lightweight, always-on SLA monitoring baked into the test run — no external APM agent required, and failures appear inline in the Cucumber HTML report. Do NOT use as a substitute for load testing; `AfterStep` duration includes Playwright's own network overhead and browser automation latency, so it measures end-to-end step cost, not pure API response time. Named alternative: Playwright's `page.on('response', ...)` listener attached in `Before` for pure API latency capture without automation overhead. [official]

### Pattern 2 — `@cucumber/messages` Envelope Stream Tap for Real-Time CI Notifications  [official]

The `@cucumber/messages` Envelope stream (produced by Cucumber.js's message formatter) can be tapped in a custom formatter plugin to push real-time scenario pass/fail events to Slack, Teams, or a webhook — without waiting for the run to complete.

```typescript
// src/formatters/realtime-notifier.ts
import type { FormatterPlugin } from '@cucumber/cucumber/api';
import type { Envelope } from '@cucumber/messages';

type Options = { webhookUrl?: string; slackChannel?: string };

const realtimeNotifierPlugin: FormatterPlugin<Options> = {
  type: 'formatter',
  formatter({ on, options }) {
    const webhookUrl = options?.webhookUrl ?? process.env.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL;
    if (!webhookUrl) return;

    const scenarioResults: Array<{ name: string; status: string }> = [];

    on('message', async (envelope: Envelope) => {
      if (envelope.testCaseFinished) {
        const { willBeRetried, testCaseStartedId } = envelope.testCaseFinished;
        if (!willBeRetried) {
          // Post to Slack webhook for every terminal scenario result
          await fetch(webhookUrl, {
            method: 'POST',
            headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
            body: JSON.stringify({
              text: `BDD scenario finished (id: ${testCaseStartedId})`,
            }),
          });
        }
      }

      if (envelope.testRunFinished) {
        const summary = scenarioResults
          .map(r => `${r.status === 'PASSED' ? '✓' : '✗'} ${r.name}`)
          .join('\n');
        await fetch(webhookUrl, {
          method: 'POST',
          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
          body: JSON.stringify({ text: `BDD run complete:\n${summary}` }),
        });
      }
    });
  },
};

export default realtimeNotifierPlugin;
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when your team monitors CI results in a chat channel and wants sub-minute feedback rather than waiting for the HTML report to be uploaded. Do NOT block the `on('message')` handler with slow awaits — the Envelope stream is synchronous in many Cucumber.js configurations; heavy async work should be fire-and-forget with error swallowing. Named alternative: a post-run webhook triggered by a CI step that reads the JSON formatter output (simpler, but not real-time). [official]

### Pattern 3 — Gherkin `Background` Step Extraction to a Named Fixture Factory  [community]

Long `Background` blocks that repeat across multiple feature files signal that the setup logic should be extracted into a typed fixture factory rather than duplicated in Gherkin. A factory encapsulates the creation contract while keeping individual feature files focused on behavior.

```gherkin
# features/billing/invoice-download.feature — lean Background using factory
Feature: Invoice PDF download

  Background:
    Given a billing account exists for "Acme Corp" with 3 paid invoices

  Scenario: Customer can download the most recent invoice
    When I navigate to the billing history page
    And I click "Download PDF" for the most recent invoice
    Then a PDF file named "invoice-latest.pdf" should be downloaded

  Scenario: Downloaded invoice PDF contains the correct amount
    When I download invoice number 1
    Then the PDF should contain the text "USD 499.00"
```

```typescript
// src/support/fixtures/billing-account.factory.ts
import type { AppWorld } from '../world';

export interface BillingAccountFixture {
  accountId: string;
  companyName: string;
  invoiceIds: string[];
}

export async function createBillingAccount(
  world: AppWorld,
  companyName: string,
  invoiceCount: number
): Promise<BillingAccountFixture> {
  const account = await world.apiClient.post('/api/billing/accounts', {
    companyName,
    plan: 'pro',
  });
  const invoiceIds: string[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < invoiceCount; i++) {
    const inv = await world.apiClient.post('/api/billing/invoices', {
      accountId: account.id,
      amount: 499_00,
      currency: 'USD',
      status: 'PAID',
    });
    invoiceIds.push(inv.id);
  }
  world.currentAccountId = account.id;
  world.invoiceIds = invoiceIds;
  return { accountId: account.id, companyName, invoiceIds };
}

// src/steps/billing-background.steps.ts
import { Given } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';
import { createBillingAccount } from '../support/fixtures/billing-account.factory';

Given(
  'a billing account exists for {string} with {int} paid invoices',
  async function (this: AppWorld, companyName: string, invoiceCount: number) {
    await createBillingAccount(this, companyName, invoiceCount);
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when the same multi-step Background setup logic appears in three or more feature files — factory extraction eliminates drift when the account creation API changes. Do NOT extract single-use Background steps into factories; the indirection adds complexity without benefit. Named alternative: Prisma direct seeding (faster, but bypasses API validation; use when the factory's HTTP round-trips add unacceptable setup time). [community]

### Pattern 4 — Cucumber.js `setDefaultTimeout` Scoped Per Tag with a Custom Plugin  [official]

The built-in `setDefaultTimeout` is global. When some scenarios involve long-running flows (bulk exports, async job completion) while others are fast UI interactions, a plugin that sets per-tag timeouts prevents false timeouts without inflating the global timeout.

```typescript
// src/plugins/per-tag-timeout-plugin.ts
import type { Plugin } from '@cucumber/cucumber/api';
import { setDefaultTimeout } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

type Options = { tagTimeouts: Record<string, number> };

const perTagTimeoutPlugin: Plugin<Options> = {
  type: 'plugin',
  plugin({ options, on }) {
    const tagTimeouts = options?.tagTimeouts ?? {};

    on('pickles:filter', ({ pickles }) => {
      // Attach timeout to each pickle via tag matching
      // Note: We can't call setDefaultTimeout per-pickle, but we can sort
      // long-running scenarios to the end to minimise timeout bleed
      const slowPickles = pickles.filter(p =>
        p.tags.some(t => Object.keys(tagTimeouts).includes(t.name))
      );
      const fastPickles = pickles.filter(p =>
        !p.tags.some(t => Object.keys(tagTimeouts).includes(t.name))
      );
      return [...fastPickles, ...slowPickles];
    });
  },
};

export default perTagTimeoutPlugin;

// src/support/hooks.ts — per-tag timeout via Before hook
import { Before, setDefaultTimeout } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

const TAG_TIMEOUTS: Record<string, number> = {
  '@bulk-export': 120_000,
  '@async-job':   60_000,
  '@smoke':        10_000,
};

Before(async function ({ pickle }) {
  const matchedTag = pickle.tags
    .map(t => t.name)
    .find(name => TAG_TIMEOUTS[name] !== undefined);
  if (matchedTag) {
    setDefaultTimeout(TAG_TIMEOUTS[matchedTag]!);
  } else {
    setDefaultTimeout(30_000);  // Baseline
  }
});
```

```gherkin
# features/exports/bulk-export.feature
@bulk-export
Scenario: Admin exports 10 000 orders as CSV
  Given there are 10000 orders in the system
  When I request a bulk CSV export
  Then the download should complete within 2 minutes
  And the CSV should contain 10000 rows
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when your test suite spans flows with dramatically different execution times (sub-second UI checks vs multi-minute async operations) and you want timeout failures to be meaningful rather than arbitrary. Do NOT rely on `setDefaultTimeout` in `Before` hooks for sharded parallel runs — timeout state does not persist across worker boundaries in `--parallel` mode; each worker resets its default. Named alternative: per-step `{ timeout: N }` option on individual step definitions (precise, but verbose when many steps in a long scenario need elevation). [official]

### Pattern 5 — Conditional Scenario Skip via `testInfo.skip()` in playwright-bdd Fixtures  [community]

In `playwright-bdd`, the Playwright `testInfo` fixture is accessible inside BDD fixture definitions, enabling runtime conditional skipping based on environment capabilities — for example, skipping WebSocket scenarios on environments that block WebSocket connections, or skipping payment scenarios on non-production-sandbox environments.

```typescript
// src/fixtures/conditional-skip.fixture.ts
import { test as base, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { createBdd } from 'playwright-bdd';

// Extend base test with a conditional-skip fixture
const test = base.extend<{
  requiresFeatureFlag: (flag: string) => Promise<void>;
  requiresEnvironment: (...envs: string[]) => void;
}>({
  requiresFeatureFlag: async ({ request }, use, testInfo) => {
    await use(async (flag: string) => {
      const res = await request.get('/api/feature-flags');
      const flags = await res.json() as Record<string, boolean>;
      if (!flags[flag]) {
        testInfo.skip(true, `Feature flag "${flag}" is disabled in this environment`);
      }
    });
  },

  requiresEnvironment: async ({}, use, testInfo) => {
    use((...envs: string[]) => {
      const currentEnv = process.env.TEST_ENV ?? 'local';
      if (!envs.includes(currentEnv)) {
        testInfo.skip(
          true,
          `Scenario requires environment ${envs.join(' or ')}; current: ${currentEnv}`
        );
      }
    });
  },
});

export const { Given, When, Then } = createBdd(test);

// src/steps/payment.steps.ts — using conditional-skip fixtures
import { Given, When, Then } from '../fixtures/conditional-skip.fixture';

Given(
  'the Stripe payment gateway is enabled',
  async ({ requiresFeatureFlag, requiresEnvironment }) => {
    requiresEnvironment('staging', 'production-smoke');
    await requiresFeatureFlag('stripe_payments_enabled');
  }
);

When('I complete checkout with a test card', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.getByTestId('card-number').fill('4242424242424242');
  await page.getByTestId('card-expiry').fill('12/30');
  await page.getByTestId('confirm-payment').click();
  await page.waitForURL('**/order/confirmation');
});

Then('I should see the payment confirmation', async ({ page }) => {
  await expect(page.getByTestId('payment-status')).toHaveText('Payment successful');
});
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when your BDD suite runs across multiple environments and some scenarios are only meaningful in specific environments or with specific feature flags — conditional skips prevent noise from expected environment mismatches. Do NOT embed environment gate logic inside step definition bodies where it obscures the business intent; keep it in the `Given` precondition or a dedicated fixture. Named alternative: `--tags` filtering at the CI pipeline level (cleaner for static environment differences, but cannot react to runtime feature flag state). [community]

### Pattern 6 — `@cucumber/html-formatter` Custom Branding and Embedding  [official]

The `@cucumber/html-formatter` package (used by Cucumber.js's built-in HTML report) accepts a programmatic API for generating self-contained HTML reports from Cucumber message streams — enabling branded living documentation portals embedded inside internal wikis or GitHub Pages.

```typescript
// scripts/generate-branded-report.ts
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';
import { generate } from '@cucumber/html-formatter';
import type { Envelope } from '@cucumber/messages';

async function generateBrandedReport(): Promise<void> {
  const messagesPath = path.resolve('reports/cucumber-messages.ndjson');
  const outputPath = path.resolve('reports/branded-report.html');

  const envelopes: Envelope[] = fs
    .readFileSync(messagesPath, 'utf8')
    .split('\n')
    .filter(Boolean)
    .map(line => JSON.parse(line) as Envelope);

  const html = await generate(envelopes, {
    // Custom title and metadata injected into the HTML head
    title: 'Acme Corp — BDD Living Documentation',
    metadata: [
      { name: 'Branch', value: process.env.GITHUB_REF_NAME ?? 'local' },
      { name: 'Run ID', value: process.env.GITHUB_RUN_ID ?? 'manual' },
      { name: 'Generated', value: new Date().toISOString() },
    ],
  });

  fs.writeFileSync(outputPath, html, 'utf8');
  console.log(`Branded report written to ${outputPath}`);
}

generateBrandedReport().catch(console.error);
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/living-docs.yml
- name: Generate Branded Living Documentation
  run: npx tsx scripts/generate-branded-report.ts

- name: Upload HTML report as artifact
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: bdd-living-docs
    path: reports/branded-report.html
    retention-days: 30
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when your organisation requires branded, self-contained HTML reports for compliance audits or stakeholder presentations that go beyond the default Cucumber HTML report styling. Do NOT attempt to directly modify the `@cucumber/html-formatter` template files — the package generates a self-contained React bundle and is not designed for partial template overrides; use the programmatic `generate()` API instead. Named alternative: Allure Report (richer visual customization and history trends, but requires a separate Allure server or history file management). [official]

### Pattern 7 — BDD Scenario for Optimistic UI with Rollback Verification  [community]

Optimistic UI patterns (where the UI reflects a state change immediately before the server confirms it) require BDD scenarios that verify both the optimistic interim state and the final confirmed state — and critically, that the UI correctly reverts if the server rejects the operation.

```gherkin
# features/tasks/optimistic-complete.feature
Feature: Task completion with optimistic UI

  Scenario: Completing a task shows instant feedback then server confirmation
    Given I have an open task "Write BDD guide entry"
    When I mark the task as complete
    Then the task should immediately appear as completed in the UI
    And within 2 seconds the server should confirm the completion
    And the task should remain in the completed state

  Scenario: Failed server sync reverts the optimistic UI state
    Given I have an open task "Write BDD guide entry"
    And the task completion API will fail with a 503 error
    When I mark the task as complete
    Then the task should immediately appear as completed in the UI
    And after the server rejects the update the task should revert to open
    And I should see the error "Could not save changes. Please try again."
```

```typescript
// src/steps/optimistic-ui.steps.ts
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

Given('the task completion API will fail with a {int} error', async function (
  this: AppWorld,
  statusCode: number
) {
  // Intercept the PATCH request for task completion and return error
  await this.page.route('**/api/tasks/*/complete', route =>
    route.fulfill({ status: statusCode, body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'Service unavailable' }) })
  );
  this.apiOverrideActive = true;
});

When('I mark the task as complete', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.page.getByTestId('task-complete-checkbox').click();
});

Then(
  'the task should immediately appear as completed in the UI',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    // Optimistic update should be visible synchronously (no await for network)
    await expect(this.page.getByTestId('task-item')).toHaveAttribute('data-status', 'completed');
  }
);

Then(
  'after the server rejects the update the task should revert to open',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    // Wait for the network round-trip and rollback animation
    await expect(this.page.getByTestId('task-item')).toHaveAttribute('data-status', 'open', {
      timeout: 5_000,
    });
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when your application uses optimistic updates and you need confidence that the rollback path works — this catches a class of bug (silent rollback failures that leave the UI permanently out of sync) that unit tests rarely cover. Do NOT assert the optimistic state with a hard timeout — use Playwright's default retry-based `toHaveAttribute` assertion so the test is not fragile to animation timing. Named alternative: unit-testing the state management layer (Redux/Zustand) in isolation (faster, no browser overhead, but does not verify the UI binding layer). [community]

### Pattern 8 — Step Definition Dependency Graph Visualiser Script  [community]

Large BDD suites accumulate step files that are unclear in purpose, scope, and duplication. A script that parses step definitions and builds a dependency graph (which step files are consumed by which feature files) makes the suite architecture visible — exposing unused steps, cross-feature step coupling, and files ripe for extraction.

```typescript
// scripts/step-dependency-graph.ts
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';
import { glob } from 'glob';
import { GherkinStreams } from '@cucumber/gherkin-streams';  // replaced by Messages API

// Simpler approach: parse feature files with regex + match against step patterns
async function buildDependencyGraph(
  featuresGlob: string,
  stepsGlob: string
): Promise<void> {
  const featureFiles = await glob(featuresGlob);
  const stepFiles = await glob(stepsGlob);

  // Extract step text patterns from step definition files
  const stepRegistry: Record<string, string[]> = {};
  for (const stepFile of stepFiles) {
    const content = fs.readFileSync(stepFile, 'utf8');
    const patterns = [...content.matchAll(/(?:Given|When|Then)\(['"`](.*?)['"`]/g)]
      .map(m => m[1] ?? '');
    stepRegistry[path.basename(stepFile)] = patterns;
  }

  // For each feature file, find which step files it depends on
  const graph: Record<string, Set<string>> = {};
  for (const featureFile of featureFiles) {
    const content = fs.readFileSync(featureFile, 'utf8');
    const steps = [...content.matchAll(/^\s+(?:Given|When|Then|And|But) (.+)$/gm)]
      .map(m => m[1]?.trim() ?? '');

    const deps = new Set<string>();
    for (const step of steps) {
      for (const [stepFile, patterns] of Object.entries(stepRegistry)) {
        if (patterns.some(p => new RegExp(p.replace(/\{[^}]+\}/g, '.*')).test(step))) {
          deps.add(stepFile);
        }
      }
    }
    graph[path.basename(featureFile)] = deps;
  }

  // Emit as DOT format for Graphviz visualisation
  const dot = [
    'digraph BDDDependencies {',
    '  rankdir=LR;',
    '  node [shape=box];',
    ...Object.entries(graph).flatMap(([feature, deps]) =>
      [...deps].map(dep => `  "${feature}" -> "${dep}";`)
    ),
    '}',
  ].join('\n');

  fs.writeFileSync('reports/step-dependencies.dot', dot, 'utf8');
  console.log('Dependency graph written to reports/step-dependencies.dot');
  console.log('Render with: dot -Tpng reports/step-dependencies.dot -o reports/step-deps.png');
}

buildDependencyGraph('features/**/*.feature', 'src/steps/**/*.ts').catch(console.error);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use at the start of a step definition refactoring sprint — the graph reveals which step files are "leaves" (no inbound feature dependencies) and are safe to delete, versus "hubs" (depended on by 10+ feature files) that need careful backward-compatible refactoring. Do NOT run this in CI on every commit — it adds 2–5 seconds of startup cost and is a developer tooling concern, not a correctness check. Named alternative: Cucumber.js `--dry-run` with `--format json` piped to a JQ query (simpler for counting undefined steps, but does not produce a visual graph). [community]

### Pattern 9 — Gherkin `Examples` Table Column Aliasing for Readability  [community]

`Scenario Outline` `Examples` tables can use header names that are more business-readable than the placeholder names in the template — as long as the header names match the `<placeholder>` tokens in the scenario body. This enables human-friendly column names for stakeholder review while keeping the template unambiguous.

```gherkin
# features/pricing/discount-calculation.feature
Feature: Volume discount pricing

  Scenario Outline: Volume discount is applied at correct quantity thresholds
    Given a customer orders <quantity> units of product "Laptop Stand"
    When the order total is calculated
    Then the unit price should be <unit price in USD>
    And the discount applied should be <discount percentage>%
    And the total should be <total in USD>

    @smoke
    Examples: Small order — no discount
      | quantity | unit price in USD | discount percentage | total in USD |
      | 1        | 49.99             | 0                   | 49.99        |
      | 4        | 49.99             | 0                   | 199.96       |

    @regression
    Examples: Medium order — 5% discount at 5+ units
      | quantity | unit price in USD | discount percentage | total in USD |
      | 5        | 47.49             | 5                   | 237.45       |
      | 9        | 47.49             | 5                   | 427.41       |

    @nightly
    Examples: Bulk order — 15% discount at 25+ units
      | quantity | unit price in USD | discount percentage | total in USD |
      | 25       | 42.49             | 15                  | 1062.25      |
      | 100      | 42.49             | 15                  | 4249.00      |
```

```typescript
// src/steps/pricing.steps.ts
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

Given(
  'a customer orders {int} units of product {string}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, quantity: number, productName: string) {
    const product = await this.apiClient.get(`/api/products?name=${encodeURIComponent(productName)}`);
    this.currentProductId = product.id;
    this.currentQuantity = quantity;
    await this.page.goto(`/products/${product.slug}?qty=${quantity}`);
  }
);

Then(
  'the discount applied should be {int}%',
  async function (this: AppWorld, expectedDiscountPct: number) {
    const discountBadge = this.page.getByTestId('discount-badge');
    if (expectedDiscountPct === 0) {
      await expect(discountBadge).not.toBeVisible();
    } else {
      await expect(discountBadge).toHaveText(`${expectedDiscountPct}% off`);
    }
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use multi-word column header names (with spaces) when the data columns represent business domain values that stakeholders read during Three Amigos reviews — human-readable headers dramatically reduce the friction of getting non-technical stakeholders to validate test data. Do NOT use extremely long header names (>30 chars) as they cause the Examples table to be wider than a readable GitHub diff; abbreviate aggressively if the table exceeds 120 chars per row. Named alternative: `{string}` parameters with comment blocks explaining the data format (less visual, but avoids wide tables). [community]

### Pattern 10 — Cucumber.js `WorldParameters` Type Augmentation for IDE Auto-Complete  [official]

The `WorldParameters` type from `@cucumber/cucumber` can be module-augmented in TypeScript to provide full auto-complete on `this.parameters` in step definitions — eliminating the common `any`-typed `worldParameters` access that silently breaks when parameter names change.

```typescript
// src/support/world-parameters.d.ts — augment the global WorldParameters type
import '@cucumber/cucumber';

declare module '@cucumber/cucumber' {
  interface WorldParameters {
    baseUrl: string;
    apiKey: string;
    env: 'local' | 'staging' | 'production-smoke';
    featureFlags: Record<string, boolean>;
    timeouts: {
      api: number;
      ui: number;
    };
  }
}

// src/support/world.ts — type-safe worldParameters access
import { setWorldConstructor, World, IWorldOptions } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

export class AppWorld extends World {
  readonly baseUrl: string;
  readonly apiKey: string;
  readonly currentEnv: 'local' | 'staging' | 'production-smoke';

  constructor(options: IWorldOptions) {
    super(options);
    // this.parameters is now fully typed — TypeScript errors if keys don't match the augmentation
    this.baseUrl = this.parameters.baseUrl;
    this.apiKey = this.parameters.apiKey;
    this.currentEnv = this.parameters.env;
  }
}

setWorldConstructor(AppWorld);

// cucumber.ts — pass typed worldParameters via profile
import type { IConfiguration } from '@cucumber/cucumber/api';

export default {
  default: {
    import: ['src/steps/**/*.ts', 'src/support/**/*.ts'],
    worldParameters: {
      baseUrl: process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
      apiKey: process.env.API_KEY ?? 'test-key',
      env: (process.env.TEST_ENV ?? 'local') as 'local' | 'staging' | 'production-smoke',
      featureFlags: {},
      timeouts: { api: 10_000, ui: 5_000 },
    },
  } satisfies Partial<IConfiguration>,
};
```

**Tradeoff**: Use in any TypeScript project where `worldParameters` are accessed in more than two step files — the module augmentation is a one-time investment that eliminates an entire class of runtime `undefined` errors caused by parameter name typos. Do NOT put secrets in `worldParameters` passed via the config file (they appear in `--dry-run --format json` output); use environment variable references and resolve them in the `World` constructor. Named alternative: a typed `getConfig()` helper function that reads from `process.env` directly (avoids `worldParameters` entirely, but loses the profile-driven configuration flexibility). [official]

---

### Pattern 11 — BDD Scenario for Background Sync and Offline-First Behavior  [community]

Progressive web apps and offline-first applications require BDD scenarios that explicitly verify behavior when the network is unavailable and when sync occurs on reconnection. Playwright's `context.setOffline()` enables clean offline simulation within BDD steps.

```gherkin
# features/offline/task-sync.feature
@regression
Feature: Offline task management with background sync

  Scenario: Tasks created offline are synced when connection is restored
    Given I am logged in as a registered user
    And my device has a stable network connection
    When I go offline
    And I create a task "Review BDD patterns offline"
    Then the task should appear in my list with a "pending sync" indicator
    When my device comes back online
    Then the task should sync to the server within 5 seconds
    And the "pending sync" indicator should disappear

  Scenario: Offline changes survive a browser refresh before sync
    Given I am logged in as a registered user
    When I go offline
    And I complete the task "Write BDD guide entry"
    And I refresh the page while still offline
    Then the task should still appear as completed
    And the "pending sync" indicator should still be visible
```

```typescript
// src/steps/offline.steps.ts
import { When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

When('I go offline', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.context.setOffline(true);
  this.attach('Network set to offline', 'text/plain');
});

When('my device comes back online', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.context.setOffline(false);
  this.attach('Network restored to online', 'text/plain');
});

Then(
  'the task should appear in my list with a {string} indicator',
  async function (this: AppWorld, indicator: string) {
    const task = this.page.getByTestId('task-item').filter({ hasText: /Review BDD patterns/i });
    await expect(task).toBeVisible();
    await expect(task.getByTestId('sync-indicator')).toHaveText(indicator);
  }
);

Then(
  'the task should sync to the server within {int} seconds',
  async function (this: AppWorld, seconds: number) {
    const task = this.page.getByTestId('task-item').filter({ hasText: /Review BDD patterns/i });
    await expect(task.getByTestId('sync-indicator')).not.toBeVisible({
      timeout: seconds * 1_000,
    });
    // Verify server-side persistence via API
    const res = await this.page.request.get('/api/tasks?filter=synced');
    const tasks = (await res.json()) as Array<{ title: string }>;
    const found = tasks.some(t => t.title.includes('Review BDD patterns'));
    expect(found, 'Task not found in server response after sync').toBe(true);
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when your application explicitly supports offline-first behavior and has a sync mechanism — these scenarios catch a category of regression (sync conflicts, duplicate creation on reconnect) that only manifests under network interruption. Do NOT use `context.setOffline()` to simulate slow networks; use `context.route('**', route => setTimeout(() => route.continue(), 2000))` for latency simulation instead. Named alternative: unit testing the service worker sync logic in isolation (faster, but does not cover the full browser storage + UI update chain). [community]

---

### Pattern 12 — Gherkin Feature File Linting Rules as CI Quality Gates  [community]

A custom `gherkin-lint` configuration enforces team-agreed scenario quality rules as a hard CI gate — preventing poorly structured Gherkin from entering the repository. Rules cover conjunction steps, missing tags, overly long scenarios, and imperative step language.

```javascript
// .gherkin-lintrc.json — project-specific Gherkin quality rules
{
  "no-restricted-patterns": [
    {
      "name": "no-conjunction-steps",
      "rule": "no-conjunction-steps",
      "enabled": true
    },
    {
      "name": "no-unnamed-features",
      "rule": "no-unnamed-features",
      "enabled": true
    },
    {
      "name": "no-unnamed-scenarios",
      "rule": "no-unnamed-scenarios",
      "enabled": true
    }
  ],
  "new-line-at-eof": ["error", "yes"],
  "no-trailing-spaces": "error",
  "no-inconsistent-quotes": "error",
  "indentation": ["error", {
    "Feature": 0,
    "Background": 2,
    "Scenario": 2,
    "Step": 4,
    "Examples": 4,
    "example": 6
  }],
  "max-scenarios-per-file": ["warn", { "maxScenarios": 10 }],
  "required-tags": ["error", {
    "tags": ["@smoke", "@regression", "@wip", "@nightly"],
    "atLeastOne": true
  }]
}
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml — Gherkin lint as a required status check
- name: Lint Gherkin feature files
  run: npx gherkin-lint features/**/*.feature --config .gherkin-lintrc.json
  # Fails the build on any 'error' rule violation; warns on 'warn' rules
```

```typescript
// src/scripts/gherkin-health-check.ts — programmatic lint summary for PR comments
import { execSync } from 'child_process';

const output = execSync(
  'npx gherkin-lint features/**/*.feature --config .gherkin-lintrc.json --format json',
  { encoding: 'utf8' }
);
const results = JSON.parse(output) as Array<{ filePath: string; errors: Array<{ rule: string; message: string }> }>;
const filesWithErrors = results.filter(r => r.errors.length > 0);

if (filesWithErrors.length > 0) {
  console.error(`Gherkin lint found ${filesWithErrors.length} file(s) with violations:`);
  for (const file of filesWithErrors) {
    for (const err of file.errors) {
      console.error(`  ${file.filePath}: [${err.rule}] ${err.message}`);
    }
  }
  process.exit(1);
}
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when your team has more than 3 contributors writing feature files and you have documented Gherkin standards — lint enforcement prevents style drift without requiring manual code review of every feature file change. Do NOT enable `max-scenarios-per-file` as an `error` (hard block) on legacy feature files that already violate it; introduce the rule as a `warn` first and resolve violations incrementally. Named alternative: Cucumber's `--dry-run` validation (catches undefined/ambiguous steps but does not enforce Gherkin style rules). [community]

### Pattern 13 — BDD Scenarios for Event-Driven Architecture: Outbox Pattern Verification  [community]

Event-driven systems that use the transactional outbox pattern require BDD scenarios that verify both the database write and the eventual event publication — two observable outcomes that can diverge if the outbox processor fails silently.

```gherkin
# features/orders/order-placed-event.feature
@regression
Feature: Order placed event publication via transactional outbox

  Scenario: Placing an order publishes an OrderPlaced domain event
    Given I am a registered customer
    When I place an order for 2 units of "Laptop Stand"
    Then the order should be created with status "CONFIRMED"
    And an "OrderPlaced" event should be published to the message bus within 5 seconds
    And the event payload should contain the order ID and customer ID

  Scenario: Outbox processor failure does not lose the event
    Given an existing order has an unpublished "OrderPlaced" event in the outbox
    When the outbox processor runs
    Then the "OrderPlaced" event should be published to the message bus
    And the outbox entry should be marked as processed
```

```typescript
// src/steps/event-driven.steps.ts
import { Then, Given } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from '../support/world';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

Then(
  'an {string} event should be published to the message bus within {int} seconds',
  async function (this: AppWorld, eventType: string, seconds: number) {
    // Poll the test message bus (e.g., a local Redis stream or test event store)
    const deadline = Date.now() + seconds * 1_000;
    let event: Record<string, unknown> | undefined;

    while (Date.now() < deadline) {
      const events = await this.eventBusClient.getEvents({
        type: eventType,
        since: this.scenarioStartTime,
      });
      event = events.find(e => e.correlationId === this.currentOrderId);
      if (event) break;
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 500));
    }

    expect(event, `No "${eventType}" event published within ${seconds}s`).toBeDefined();
    this.publishedEvent = event;
    this.attach(JSON.stringify(event, null, 2), 'application/json');
  }
);

Then(
  'the event payload should contain the order ID and customer ID',
  async function (this: AppWorld) {
    expect(this.publishedEvent).toMatchObject({
      orderId: this.currentOrderId,
      customerId: this.currentCustomerId,
    });
  }
);

Given(
  'an existing order has an unpublished {string} event in the outbox',
  async function (this: AppWorld, eventType: string) {
    // Seed the outbox table directly via API or Prisma
    const order = await this.seeder.seedOrder(this.testCustomerId, { status: 'CONFIRMED' });
    await this.seeder.seedOutboxEvent({
      aggregateId: order.orderId,
      eventType,
      payload: JSON.stringify({ orderId: order.orderId, customerId: this.testCustomerId }),
      processed: false,
    });
    this.pendingOutboxOrderId = order.orderId;
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use in systems where the outbox pattern is critical to event delivery guarantees — BDD scenarios at this level verify that the entire pipeline (write → outbox → processor → message bus) functions as the business expects, not just that the API returns 201. Do NOT poll the message bus with a busy loop in CI — use a reasonable poll interval (500ms) and fail fast after the timeout rather than hanging the test suite. Named alternative: contract testing with Pact (verifies event schema compatibility between producer and consumer, but does not verify the outbox pipeline itself). [community]

### Pattern 14 — playwright-bdd `test.step()` Nesting for Sub-Scenario Tracing  [official]

In `playwright-bdd`, wrapping groups of step actions in `test.step()` calls creates hierarchical trace entries in the Playwright HTML report — making complex multi-action steps easy to navigate in the trace viewer and enabling fine-grained failure isolation without splitting steps into separate Gherkin lines.

```typescript
// src/fixtures/trace-helpers.fixture.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
import { createBdd } from 'playwright-bdd';

const test = base.extend<{
  withStep: <T>(title: string, fn: () => Promise<T>) => Promise<T>;
}>({
  withStep: async ({}, use, testInfo) => {
    await use(<T>(title: string, fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> =>
      testInfo.attach ? base.step(title, fn) : fn()
    );
  },
});

export const { Given, When, Then } = createBdd(test);

// src/steps/checkout.steps.ts — using test.step() nesting for trace clarity
import { When } from '../fixtures/trace-helpers.fixture';

When(
  'I complete the full checkout process with card {string}',
  async ({ page, withStep }, cardNumber: string) => {
    await withStep('Fill shipping address', async () => {
      await page.getByLabel('Full name').fill('Alice Smith');
      await page.getByLabel('Address line 1').fill('123 BDD Street');
      await page.getByLabel('City').fill('Testville');
      await page.getByLabel('Postcode').fill('TS1 1TS');
      await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Continue to payment' }).click();
    });

    await withStep('Enter payment details', async () => {
      await page.getByLabel('Card number').fill(cardNumber);
      await page.getByLabel('Expiry date').fill('12/30');
      await page.getByLabel('CVV').fill('123');
    });

    await withStep('Confirm and place order', async () => {
      await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }).click();
      await page.waitForURL('**/order/confirmation');
    });
  }
);
```

```gherkin
# features/checkout/full-flow.feature
@smoke
Scenario: Registered customer completes checkout
  Given I am logged in as Alice
  And my cart contains 1 unit of "Laptop Stand"
  When I complete the full checkout process with card "4242424242424242"
  Then I should see my order confirmation number
```

**Tradeoff**: Use when a `When` step encapsulates a multi-sub-action flow that would be too granular to express as individual Gherkin steps (and would pollute the scenario with implementation detail) but needs good failure diagnostics in the trace viewer. Do NOT add `test.step()` nesting to simple single-action steps — the overhead is noise in the trace and slows down the report rendering for large suites. Named alternative: `locator.describe()` (v1.53+) for labeling groups of locator-based actions in the trace without function nesting. [official]

### Pattern 15 — BDD Scenario Coverage Heatmap via Tag-Feature Matrix Script  [community]

A tag-feature matrix script produces a heatmap showing which business features (rows) are covered by which CI pipeline tiers (columns: `@smoke`, `@regression`, `@nightly`). The heatmap immediately surfaces coverage gaps — features with no `@smoke` coverage or features with 20+ `@nightly` scenarios and zero `@smoke` scenarios.

```typescript
// scripts/coverage-heatmap.ts
import * as fs from 'fs';
import { glob } from 'glob';

interface FeatureCoverage {
  featureName: string;
  filePath: string;
  smoke: number;
  regression: number;
  nightly: number;
  wip: number;
  untagged: number;
}

async function buildCoverageHeatmap(): Promise<void> {
  const featureFiles = await glob('features/**/*.feature');
  const tiers = ['@smoke', '@regression', '@nightly', '@wip'];
  const coverage: FeatureCoverage[] = [];

  for (const filePath of featureFiles) {
    const content = fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8');
    const featureMatch = content.match(/^Feature:\s+(.+)$/m);
    const featureName = featureMatch?.[1]?.trim() ?? path.basename(filePath, '.feature');

    // Extract all scenario blocks with their preceding tags
    const scenarioBlocks = [...content.matchAll(
      /((?:@\w[\w-]*\s*\n)*)\s*(?:Scenario(?:\s+Outline)?:|Example:)\s+(.+)/gm
    )];

    const counts: Record<string, number> = { smoke: 0, regression: 0, nightly: 0, wip: 0, untagged: 0 };
    for (const [, tagsBlock] of scenarioBlocks) {
      const tags = (tagsBlock ?? '').match(/@\w[\w-]*/g) ?? [];
      if (tags.length === 0) {
        counts['untagged']!++;
      } else {
        let matched = false;
        for (const tier of tiers) {
          if (tags.includes(tier)) {
            counts[tier.slice(1)]!++;
            matched = true;
          }
        }
        if (!matched) counts['untagged']!++;
      }
    }

    coverage.push({
      featureName,
      filePath,
      smoke: counts['smoke']!,
      regression: counts['regression']!,
      nightly: counts['nightly']!,
      wip: counts['wip']!,
      untagged: counts['untagged']!,
    });
  }

  // Emit Markdown table
  const header = '| Feature | Smoke | Regression | Nightly | WIP | Untagged |';
  const divider = '|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|';
  const rows = coverage.map(c =>
    `| ${c.featureName} | ${c.smoke || '-'} | ${c.regression || '-'} | ${c.nightly || '-'} | ${c.wip || '-'} | ${c.untagged || '-'} |`
  );

  const table = [header, divider, ...rows].join('\n');
  fs.writeFileSync('reports/coverage-heatmap.md', table, 'utf8');
  console.log(`Coverage heatmap written to reports/coverage-heatmap.md`);

  // Warn on gaps
  const noSmoke = coverage.filter(c => c.smoke === 0 && c.untagged === 0);
  if (noSmoke.length > 0) {
    console.warn(`Features with no @smoke coverage: ${noSmoke.map(c => c.featureName).join(', ')}`);
  }
}

buildDependencyGraph().catch(console.error);
```

**Tradeoff**: Use at the end of each sprint or before a release to audit CI coverage distribution — the heatmap reveals when a critical feature has only `@nightly` coverage (meaning it won't block a PR merge) and should be promoted to `@smoke`. Do NOT run this in CI on every commit as a blocking gate — it reads file system state and is a reporting tool, not a correctness check. Named alternative: Cucumber.js `--format json` with a JQ pipeline (`jq '[.[] | {feature: .uri, tags: [.elements[].tags[].name]} | select(.tags | length > 0)]'`) for ad-hoc tag auditing without a dedicated script. [community]
