### Pattern 6 — Playwright v1.58 Timeline Visualization in Merged HTML Reports for Sharded BDD Suites  [official]

Playwright v1.58 adds timeline visualization to merged HTML reports, rendering a Gantt-style execution timeline that shows each test's start time, duration, and worker assignment across all shards in a distributed BDD run. For sharded BDD suites using `shard` in `playwright.config.ts` and `npx playwright merge-reports` post-CI, the timeline view replaces the need to manually correlate timestamps in per-shard JUnit XML files when diagnosing shard imbalances — scenarios with long execution times are immediately visible as wide bars, and idle shard gaps show up as whitespace. The timeline is rendered in the same HTML report artifact produced by `merge-reports`, requiring no additional configuration beyond the standard blob reporter.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — sharded BDD suite with merge-reports timeline support (Playwright v1.58+)
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';
import { defineBddConfig, BddFixtures } from 'playwright-bdd';

const bddConfig = defineBddConfig({
  features: 'features/**/*.feature',
  steps: 'src/steps/**/*.ts',
  outputDir: '.bdd',
});

const shardIndex = parseInt(process.env.SHARD_INDEX ?? '1', 10);
const shardTotal = parseInt(process.env.SHARD_TOTAL ?? '1', 10);

export default defineConfig<BddFixtures>({
  testDir: bddConfig.testDir,
  // v1.58 timeline requires blob reporter per shard + merge-reports post-CI
  reporter: process.env.CI
    ? [['blob', { outputDir: `blob-reports/shard-${shardIndex}` }]]
    : [['html', { open: 'never' }]],
  shard: shardTotal > 1 ? { total: shardTotal, current: shardIndex } : undefined,
  use: {
    baseURL: process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
    trace: 'retain-on-failure',
  },
});

// CI post-step (GitHub Actions):
// - name: Merge shard reports with timeline
//   run: npx playwright merge-reports --reporter=html blob-reports/
// -> reports/playwright-report/index.html contains v1.58 timeline tab
```

**Tradeoff**: The timeline visualization requires blob reporter output per shard — it is NOT available when shards use `junit` or `html` reporters directly. The `merge-reports` command must run after ALL shards complete; if any shard artifact is missing, `merge-reports` logs a warning and produces an incomplete timeline without failing. Do NOT rely on the timeline to detect flaky scenarios — a test that retried twice shows only its final execution on the timeline; use the test retry annotations panel alongside the timeline to correlate retry count with execution time. [official]

---

### Pattern 7 — Cucumber.js v12 `FormatterPlugin<T>` Type-Safe Custom Formatter Architecture  [official]

Cucumber.js v12 formalizes the `FormatterPlugin<T>` generic type in `@cucumber/cucumber/api` for building type-safe custom formatters, providing a typed `context` object that includes `on(event, handler)` for streaming Cucumber Messages envelopes, a `write(buffer)` fire-and-forget output sink, and an `options: T` property typed against the formatter's `optionsKey` configuration block. The generic `T` parameter constrains `context.options` to a developer-defined interface, eliminating the `unknown` cast that was necessary with the untyped `FormatterPlugin` shape used in v11. This enables formatters that read structured configuration (e.g., a Slack webhook URL or a JIRA project key for issue linking) without runtime property access risk.

```typescript
// src/formatters/slack-bdd-formatter.ts
// Cucumber.js v12 FormatterPlugin<T> — type-safe Slack notification formatter
import type { FormatterPlugin } from '@cucumber/cucumber/api';
import type { Envelope } from '@cucumber/messages';

interface SlackFormatterOptions {
  webhookUrl: string;
  channel: string;
  mentionOnFailure?: string;
}

const slackFormatter: FormatterPlugin<SlackFormatterOptions> = {
  type: 'formatter',
  optionsKey: 'slack',
  formatter: ({ on, write, options, logger }) => {
    let failCount = 0;
    let passCount = 0;

    on('message', (envelope: Envelope) => {
      if (envelope.testCaseFinished) {
        const status = envelope.testCaseFinished.testResult?.status;
        if (status === 'PASSED') passCount++;
        if (status === 'FAILED') failCount++;
      }

      if (envelope.testRunFinished) {
        const mention =
          failCount > 0 && options.mentionOnFailure
            ? `<${options.mentionOnFailure}> `
            : '';
        const message = `${mention}BDD suite: ${passCount} passed, ${failCount} failed`;

        // fire-and-forget to Slack webhook (non-blocking)
        fetch(options.webhookUrl, {
          method: 'POST',
          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
          body: JSON.stringify({ channel: options.channel, text: message }),
        }).catch((err: Error) => logger.error(`Slack notification failed: ${err.message}`));

        write(`Slack notification dispatched to ${options.channel}\n`);
      }
    });
  },
};

export default slackFormatter;

// cucumber.config.ts usage:
// export default {
//   default: {
//     format: ['./src/formatters/slack-bdd-formatter.ts'],
//     formatOptions: {
//       slack: {
//         webhookUrl: process.env.SLACK_WEBHOOK!,
//         channel: '#qa-alerts',
//         mentionOnFailure: '@qa-lead',
//       }
//     }
//   }
// } satisfies Record<string, IConfiguration>;
```

**Tradeoff**: `FormatterPlugin<T>` formatters registered via `format` in `cucumber.config.ts` are loaded in the coordinator process and receive the full Cucumber Messages stream — they are suitable for aggregated notifications (Slack, email, JIRA) but not for per-step real-time output because the Messages stream is buffered. For real-time per-step output (e.g., a live terminal progress indicator), use a formatter that extends the `Formatter` base class instead. Do NOT perform blocking I/O in the formatter `on('message')` handler — use fire-and-forget (`fetch().catch()`) to avoid blocking the Cucumber coordinator process from emitting subsequent messages. [official]

---

### Pattern 8 — playwright-bdd v8.3.0 Step Prioritization by Tags for Multi-Environment Overrides  [official]

playwright-bdd v8.3.0 adds tag-based step prioritization, allowing a step definition decorated with a tag expression to take precedence over a generic step definition when the current scenario matches that tag. This addresses the common pattern in multi-environment BDD suites where most scenarios share a standard step implementation but a small subset of scenarios (tagged `@mobile`, `@staging`, or `@legacy-api`) need a different implementation for the same step text. Prior to v8.3.0, teams worked around this by writing differently-worded Gherkin steps for each environment variant or by using conditional logic inside a single step definition — both approaches are acknowledged anti-patterns that reduce the readability of feature files. Tag-prioritized steps let the feature file remain clean (same Gherkin text for all environments) while the step layer dispatches to the correct implementation.

```typescript
// src/steps/login.steps.ts
// playwright-bdd v8.3.0 — step prioritization by tags
import { createBdd } from 'playwright-bdd';
import { test } from './fixtures.js';

const { Given } = createBdd(test);

// Default implementation — matches all scenarios not tagged @legacy-api
Given('I am logged in as {string}', async ({ page }, username: string) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.fill('[data-testid="username"]', username);
  await page.fill('[data-testid="password"]', process.env.TEST_PASSWORD!);
  await page.click('[data-testid="login-button"]');
  await page.waitForURL('/dashboard');
});

// v8.3.0 tag-prioritized override — only matches @legacy-api scenarios
// playwright-bdd picks this over the generic step when scenario is tagged @legacy-api
Given(
  'I am logged in as {string}',
  { tags: '@legacy-api' },
  async ({ page, request }, username: string) => {
    // Legacy API uses cookie-based session; must POST to /api/v1/session
    const response = await request.post('/api/v1/session', {
      data: { username, password: process.env.TEST_PASSWORD },
    });
    const { sessionToken } = (await response.json()) as { sessionToken: string };
    await page.context().addCookies([
      { name: 'session', value: sessionToken, domain: 'localhost', path: '/' },
    ]);
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    await page.waitForURL('/dashboard');
  },
);
```

**Tradeoff**: Tag-prioritized steps resolve ambiguity at step dispatch time based on the tags on the current scenario — the priority override is active for the entire step, not for individual assertions within it. If two tag-prioritized definitions both match a scenario's tags (e.g., `@mobile` and `@staging`, and the scenario is tagged both), playwright-bdd raises an ambiguity error at `bddgen` time rather than silently picking one. To avoid ambiguity, use compound tag expressions in step decorators (`{ tags: '@mobile and @staging' }`). Do NOT use tag-prioritized steps to encode environment differences that belong in fixture configuration — if the only difference is a base URL or credential, use a fixture or environment variable; reserve tag-priority overrides for cases where the actual test flow differs. [official]

---

### Pattern 9 — Playwright v1.59 `await using` Async Disposable for BDD Fixture and Resource Cleanup  [official]

Playwright v1.59 ships with first-class support for the TC39 `using`/`await using` explicit resource management proposal across its resource-bearing APIs, allowing BDD step definitions and fixtures to declare cleanup responsibilities at the point of resource acquisition rather than in After hooks. When a BDD step creates a page, browser context, or download resource using `await using`, the TypeScript runtime automatically calls `[Symbol.asyncDispose]()` when the enclosing scope exits — whether by normal completion, `return`, or a thrown exception. This eliminates the three-line create/use/cleanup pattern that appears repeatedly in BDD World setup and tear-down code, and ensures cleanup runs even when a step throws before reaching the After hook.

```typescript
// src/steps/pdf-download.steps.ts
// Playwright v1.59 await using for automatic BDD resource cleanup
import { createBdd } from 'playwright-bdd';
import { test } from './fixtures.js';
import { writeFile, unlink } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';

const { When, Then } = createBdd(test);

let downloadedFilePath: string | null = null;

When('I export the report as PDF', async ({ page }) => {
  const downloadPromise = page.waitForEvent('download');
  await page.click('[data-testid="export-pdf-button"]');

  // await using: [Symbol.asyncDispose] called automatically when scope exits
  await using download = await downloadPromise;

  const tempPath = join(tmpdir(), `bdd-report-${Date.now()}.pdf`);
  await download.saveAs(tempPath);
  downloadedFilePath = tempPath;
  // No explicit download.delete() needed — disposed automatically
});

Then('the PDF should contain the heading {string}', async ({}, heading: string) => {
  if (!downloadedFilePath) throw new Error('No PDF was downloaded in the When step');
  const { PdfReader } = await import('pdfreader');
  const text = await new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => {
    const parts: string[] = [];
    new PdfReader().parseFileItems(downloadedFilePath!, (err: Error | null, item: { text?: string } | null) => {
      if (err) reject(err);
      else if (!item) resolve(parts.join(' '));
      else if (item.text) parts.push(item.text);
    });
  });
  if (!text.includes(heading)) {
    throw new Error(`PDF does not contain heading "${heading}". Found: ${text.slice(0, 200)}`);
  }
  await unlink(downloadedFilePath);
  downloadedFilePath = null;
});
```

**Tradeoff**: `await using` requires TypeScript `target: ES2022` or higher and `lib` including `"ES2022"` in `tsconfig.json`. Do NOT use `await using` as a replacement for World-level `After` hooks when cleanup must run even if the test is forcibly terminated — explicit resource management `[Symbol.asyncDispose]()` runs on scope exit in normal JavaScript execution but does NOT run when the Node.js process is killed by Playwright's timeout mechanism; for guaranteed cleanup under timeout, keep an `AfterAll` hook that removes temp files created during the run. [official]

---

### Pattern 10 — Playwright v1.60 `test.abort()` for Fixture-Driven BDD Test Early Exit  [official]

Playwright v1.60 adds `test.abort(reason)` as a first-class API callable from fixtures, route handlers, and step bodies, allowing a BDD scenario to be aborted at any point when a prerequisite condition is irrecoverably broken without polluting the test report with cascaded assertion failures. Unlike `test.skip()`, which marks the test as skipped and suppresses it from failure counts, `test.abort()` marks the test with a dedicated `ABORTED` status and logs the reason string, making it visible in the HTML report's failure section with a distinct label. In playwright-bdd terms, this maps to the "Background step failed" scenario — if a Background step establishes a shared precondition (database seed, authentication token) and that precondition fails, `test.abort()` prevents all `When`/`Then` steps from running and cluttering the output with secondary failures.

```typescript
// src/fixtures/db-seed.fixture.ts
// Playwright v1.60 test.abort() for unrecoverable BDD precondition failures
import { test as baseTest } from 'playwright-bdd';
import { DatabaseSeeder } from '../support/database-seeder.js';

export type DbSeedFixture = { dbSeeder: DatabaseSeeder };

export const test = baseTest.extend<DbSeedFixture>({
  dbSeeder: async ({ page }, use, testInfo) => {
    const seeder = new DatabaseSeeder();
    let seeded = false;

    try {
      await seeder.seedTestData(testInfo.title);
      seeded = true;
    } catch (err) {
      const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
      // v1.60: abort the entire scenario — no further steps will run
      await testInfo.abort(`Database seed failed: ${message}`);
      return;
    }

    await use(seeder);

    if (seeded) {
      await seeder.cleanup().catch((err: Error) => {
        console.error(`DB cleanup error (non-fatal): ${err.message}`);
      });
    }
  },
});

// In step definitions — test.abort() callable directly:
// Given('the inventory system is available', async ({ page }) => {
//   const healthy = await checkInventoryHealth(page);
//   if (!healthy) {
//     test.abort('Inventory service is down — cannot run inventory scenarios');
//   }
// });
```

**Tradeoff**: `test.abort()` creates an `ABORTED` record in Playwright's result model, which most CI integrations treat as a non-passing status — aborted scenarios appear in failure counts. Teams that want aborted scenarios excluded from failure thresholds must configure their CI reporter accordingly; the Playwright JUnit reporter emits `<skipped/>` for aborted tests by default, but custom reporters may differ. Do NOT call `test.abort()` inside `@cucumber/cucumber` `Before` hooks when using playwright-bdd — `Before` hooks run in Cucumber's hook lifecycle, not Playwright's test lifecycle; use a playwright-bdd fixture or `BeforeScenario` hook instead. [official]

---

### Pattern 11 — Gherkin v39.1.0 Turkish Keyword Expansion for Multilingual BDD Suites  [official]

Gherkin v39.1.0 (released May 6, 2024) expands the Turkish keyword set to include missing synonyms for `And`, `But`, and `Given`/`When`/`Then` variants, enabling fully-native Turkish feature files without falling back to English connector keywords. For teams running BDD in Turkish-language business domains (government, finance, or regional SaaS products where product owners write in Turkish), the expanded keyword set means stakeholders can write feature files in their native language without code-switching. Gherkin's multilingual keyword support is often overlooked in English-dominant teams; the v39.1.0 release is a prompt to audit feature file language declarations (`# language: tr`) and ensure step definition expressions use Cucumber Expressions rather than regex where possible, since Cucumber Expressions are language-agnostic in matching semantics.

```typescript
// features/odeme/kredi-karti.feature — Turkish Gherkin with v39.1.0 keywords
// # language: tr
// Özellik: Kredi kartı ödemesi
//   Müşteri olarak
//   Sepetimi ödemek istiyorum
//   Böylece satın alma işlemini tamamlayabilirim
//
//   Senaryo: Başarılı ödeme
//     Diyelim ki alışveriş sepetimde ürünler var
//     Ve giriş yapmış bir müşteriyim
//     Eğer ödeme sayfasına gidersem
//     Ve geçerli kredi kartı bilgilerimi girersem
//     O zaman sipariş onay sayfasını görmeliyim

// src/steps/odeme.steps.ts — Turkish Gherkin step bindings
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { ICustomWorld } from '../support/world.js';

// Cucumber.js resolves Turkish keywords to the same step registry
// — no separate registration needed for different language keywords
Given('alışveriş sepetimde ürünler var', async function (this: ICustomWorld) {
  await this.page.goto('/cart');
  await this.apiClient.post('/cart/items', {
    productId: 'laptop-stand-001',
    quantity: 1,
  });
});

When('ödeme sayfasına gidersem', async function (this: ICustomWorld) {
  await this.page.click('[data-testid="proceed-to-checkout"]');
  await this.page.waitForURL('/checkout');
});

When('geçerli kredi kartı bilgilerimi girersem', async function (this: ICustomWorld) {
  await this.page.fill('[data-testid="card-number"]', '4111111111111111');
  await this.page.fill('[data-testid="card-expiry"]', '12/28');
  await this.page.fill('[data-testid="card-cvc"]', '123');
});

Then('sipariş onay sayfasını görmeliyim', async function (this: ICustomWorld) {
  await this.page.waitForURL('/order-confirmation/**');
  await expect(this.page.getByTestId('confirmation-heading')).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Tradeoff**: Multilingual Gherkin requires the `# language:` directive as the first line of every feature file — without it, Cucumber defaults to English keyword matching and Turkish keywords are treated as plain text, causing "Step not found" errors even when step definitions exist. Do NOT mix languages within a single feature file — all steps must use keywords from the language declared in the `# language:` directive; mixing Turkish `Diyelim ki` with English `When` in the same file produces a parse error in Gherkin v39. [official]

---

### Pattern 12 — Cucumber Expressions v19 Optional `Group.children` Migration  [official]

Cucumber Expressions v19.0.0 (released January 25, 2025) changes `StepMatchArgument.Group.children` from a required `Group[]` to an optional `Group[] | undefined`, making it possible to safely access argument groups without a null-guard only when the step expression produces no nested capture groups. For teams that write custom parameter types with nested group logic (e.g., a custom `{money}` parameter type that captures amount and currency separately), `Group.children` access without a null-guard now produces a TypeScript compile error at `strict: true`, surfacing previously hidden runtime risks. Migrating means adding `?? []` fallback access or using optional chaining where `children` is iterated.

```typescript
// src/support/parameter-types.ts
// Cucumber Expressions v19 — optional Group.children migration
import { defineParameterType } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { Group } from '@cucumber/cucumber-expressions';

interface Money {
  amount: number;
  currency: string;
}

defineParameterType({
  name: 'money',
  regexp: /(\d+(?:\.\d{2})?) ([A-Z]{3})/,
  transformer(match: string): Money {
    const [amountStr, currency] = match.split(' ');
    return { amount: parseFloat(amountStr), currency };
  },
  useForSnippets: true,
  preferForRegexpMatch: false,
});

// Safe Group.children access pattern for v19 — use nullish coalescing
function extractGroupValues(group: Group): string[] {
  // v19 breaking change: children is now Group[] | undefined, not always Group[]
  const children = group.children ?? [];
  return children.flatMap((child) => extractGroupValues(child));
}

// Step definitions using the custom money parameter type
import { Given, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

Given('I have a {money} balance', function (balance: Money) {
  this.accountBalance = balance;
});

Then('I should be charged {money}', function (charge: Money) {
  const remaining = this.accountBalance.amount - charge.amount;
  if (remaining < 0) {
    throw new Error(`Insufficient funds: ${remaining.toFixed(2)} ${charge.currency}`);
  }
  this.accountBalance = { amount: remaining, currency: charge.currency };
});
```

**Tradeoff**: The `Group.children` optionality change is a TypeScript-level breaking change only — at runtime, `children` was already nullable in some code paths in v18, so projects that were already null-guarding see no behavioral difference. Projects that used `@ts-ignore` or `as Group[]` casts to suppress TypeScript errors should remove those suppressions after upgrading to v19. Do NOT upgrade Cucumber Expressions to v19 without also upgrading `@cucumber/cucumber` to a version that declares `@cucumber/cucumber-expressions: ^19` as its peer dependency — mismatched versions cause `Group` type conflicts that produce confusing compile errors even after applying the `?? []` fix. [official]

### Pattern 13 — Playwright v1.56 `page.consoleMessages()` and `page.pageErrors()` for Observable BDD Steps  [official]

Playwright v1.56 adds `page.clearConsoleMessages()`, `page.consoleMessages()`, `page.pageErrors()`, and `page.requests()` as synchronous in-memory collection APIs that replace the pattern of subscribing to `page.on('console')` events and accumulating them in a World property. These APIs are directly useful in BDD step definitions that need to assert on console output or network activity without setting up event listeners before the scenario begins. The collections persist across step boundaries within a scenario, are automatically scoped to the page lifetime, and reset between scenarios when playwright-bdd creates a fresh page per scenario.

```typescript
// src/steps/console-observability.steps.ts
// Playwright v1.56 — page.consoleMessages() + page.pageErrors() in BDD steps
import { createBdd } from 'playwright-bdd';
import { test } from './fixtures.js';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

const { Given, When, Then } = createBdd(test);

Given('I am on the dashboard page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  // v1.56: clear any console messages from the initial page load
  // so the Then step only sees messages produced by the When interaction
  page.clearConsoleMessages();
});

When('I trigger the bulk export operation', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.click('[data-testid="bulk-export-button"]');
  await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="export-complete-badge"]');
});

Then('no JavaScript errors should appear in the console', async ({ page }) => {
  // page.pageErrors() returns Error objects for uncaught exceptions
  const errors = page.pageErrors();
  if (errors.length > 0) {
    const messages = errors.map((e) => e.message).join('\n  ');
    throw new Error(`Unexpected JavaScript errors:\n  ${messages}`);
  }
});

Then('the export progress should be logged to the console', async ({ page }) => {
  // page.consoleMessages() returns ConsoleMessage[] for all console.* calls
  const logs = page.consoleMessages();
  const progressLogs = logs.filter(
    (msg) => msg.type() === 'log' && msg.text().includes('[export]'),
  );
  expect(progressLogs.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  // Also assert on network requests made during the export
  const exportRequests = page.requests().filter((req) => req.url().includes('/api/export'));
  expect(exportRequests.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff**: `page.consoleMessages()`, `page.pageErrors()`, and `page.requests()` return live collections that grow throughout the scenario — calling them in an early `Then` step and calling them again in a later `Then` step returns different results if the page continued emitting console output or making requests between the two calls. For deterministic assertions, call `page.clearConsoleMessages()` before the action under test or snapshot the collection length (`const priorCount = page.requests().length`) and assert on the delta. Do NOT use these collections as a replacement for `waitForResponse()` or `waitForEvent('console')` when the timing of the event matters — the synchronous collection APIs are accumulation buffers, not await points. [official]

### Pattern 14 — Cucumber.js v12 `IConfiguration satisfies` Pattern for Type-Safe Profile Config  [official]

Cucumber.js v12 exports the `IConfiguration` interface from `@cucumber/cucumber`, enabling TypeScript `satisfies` keyword usage in `cucumber.config.ts` to validate the entire configuration object against the official type without losing the literal types of individual properties. This replaces both the `as IConfiguration` cast (which widened property types) and the `IConfiguration` type annotation (which required all optional properties to be explicitly typed). The `satisfies` pattern is now the canonical TypeScript idiom for Cucumber config files, recommended in the Cucumber.js v12 documentation.

```typescript
// cucumber.config.ts — IConfiguration satisfies for type-safe profile config
import type { IConfiguration } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

// Using satisfies preserves literal types (e.g., 'progress' stays 'progress', not string)
// while still validating the shape against IConfiguration
export default {
  default: {
    paths: ['features/**/*.feature'],
    import: ['src/steps/**/*.ts', 'src/support/**/*.ts'],
    format: [
      'progress',
      ['html', { outputFile: 'reports/cucumber.html' }],
      ['json', { outputFile: 'reports/cucumber.json' }],
    ],
    parallel: 4,
    retry: 1,
    tags: process.env.TAGS ?? '',
    worldParameters: {
      baseUrl: process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
    },
  },
  ci: {
    paths: ['features/**/*.feature'],
    import: ['src/steps/**/*.ts', 'src/support/**/*.ts'],
    format: [
      'progress',
      ['junit', { outputFile: 'reports/junit.xml' }],
    ],
    parallel: parseInt(process.env.WORKERS ?? '4', 10),
    retry: 2,
    // v12.6+: colorsEnabled removed — use FORCE_COLOR env var instead
    tags: process.env.TAGS ?? 'not @wip',
  },
  // satisfies validates each profile value against IConfiguration
  // and preserves literal type information (no widening to string/number)
} satisfies Record<string, IConfiguration>;
```

**Tradeoff**: `satisfies` validation happens at TypeScript compile time only — a `cucumber.config.ts` that fails `satisfies` will still execute if you run Cucumber with `tsx` or Node.js strip-types without running `tsc` first. Add `tsc --noEmit` to your pre-commit hook or CI pipeline to catch config type errors before they reach the Cucumber runtime. Do NOT use `as IConfiguration` casts alongside `satisfies` — `satisfies` provides all the type safety of the cast without widening; the combination is redundant and hides legitimate type errors. [official]

### Pattern 15 — Playwright v1.59 `locator.normalize()` for Locale-Aware BDD Text Assertions  [official]

Playwright v1.59 adds `locator.normalize()` as a utility that applies Unicode normalization (NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD) to page text content before comparison, resolving a class of flaky BDD assertions where `toHaveText()` fails because the DOM contains visually identical but byte-different Unicode sequences (e.g., a precomposed `é` — U+00E9 — vs a combining sequence `e` + combining accent — U+0065 U+0301). This was a historically obscure failure mode that became more prevalent as internationalized content entered BDD test datasets; the v1.59 API surfaces it as a first-class concern rather than requiring teams to write custom normalization helpers in World utilities.

```typescript
// src/steps/product-catalog.steps.ts
// Playwright v1.59 locator.normalize() for locale-aware BDD text assertions
import { createBdd } from 'playwright-bdd';
import { test } from './fixtures.js';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

const { Given, When, Then } = createBdd(test);

Given('the product catalog is loaded with French locale content', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/catalog?locale=fr-FR');
  await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="product-grid"]');
});

When('I search for {string}', async ({ page }, query: string) => {
  await page.fill('[data-testid="search-input"]', query);
  await page.click('[data-testid="search-submit"]');
  await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="search-results"]');
});

Then(
  'the first result should show the product named {string}',
  async ({ page }, expectedName: string) => {
    const firstResult = page.locator('[data-testid="product-card"]').first();

    // v1.59 locator.normalize(): applies NFC normalization before comparison
    // Prevents "é" (precomposed U+00E9) vs "é" (e + combining accent) mismatch
    const normalizedLocator = firstResult.getByTestId('product-name').normalize('NFC');
    await expect(normalizedLocator).toHaveText(expectedName);
  },
);

Then(
  'the product price should display as {string} in French format',
  async ({ page }, priceDisplay: string) => {
    // French locale uses non-breaking space (U+00A0) as thousands separator
    // Normalize both sides to NFKC to collapse non-breaking space to regular space
    const priceLocator = page
      .locator('[data-testid="product-card"]')
      .first()
      .getByTestId('product-price')
      .normalize('NFKC');
    await expect(priceLocator).toHaveText(priceDisplay.normalize('NFKC'));
  },
);
```

**Tradeoff**: `locator.normalize()` applies Unicode normalization to text content returned by the locator before passing it to matchers — it does NOT affect how the locator queries the DOM. Do NOT apply `normalize('NFKC')` globally to all text assertions — NFKC normalization collapses compatibility characters (e.g., the fi ligature → fi, superscript ² → 2), which changes the visible meaning of some text; use NFC for standard accented character normalization where ligature collapsing is unwanted, and reserve NFKC for locale-sourced numeric content where spacing characters may differ. [official]

## Community Gotchas — Cycle 38

**[community] Gotcha 1 — playwright-bdd `defineBddConfig` silently ignores absolute paths in the `steps` glob array, causing "Missing step definitions" errors at runtime while TypeScript compilation succeeds, because playwright-bdd resolves glob patterns relative to `process.cwd()` and absolute paths are passed to `tinyglobby` (which replaced `fast-glob` in v9.0) without the cross-platform normalization that `fast-glob` applied internally**: Teams that extract shared step definition paths into a constant (e.g., `const SHARED_STEPS = path.resolve(__dirname, '../shared/steps/**/*.ts')`) and pass the absolute resolved path to `defineBddConfig({ steps: [SHARED_STEPS] })` encounter "Missing step definitions" at `bddgen` time even though the files exist and the path is correct. WHY this is confusing: `tsc --noEmit` succeeds because TypeScript resolves the import graph correctly at compile time without executing `tinyglobby`, so the error only appears when running `npx bddgen`, not during static analysis. Fix: use relative paths from `playwright.config.ts` location (`'../shared/steps/**/*.ts'`) or call `path.relative(process.cwd(), absolutePath)` before passing the path to `defineBddConfig`.

**[community] Gotcha 2 — Cucumber.js v12 `satisfies IConfiguration` type checking passes for profiles that set `parallel: 0`, which Cucumber silently treats as `parallel: 1` (one parallel worker) rather than serial execution, causing CI pipelines that intend to disable parallelism to instead run with the parallel coordinator code path that has different error handling behavior for thrown-string errors and truncates long stack traces via IPC serialization**: Teams that want to disable parallelism conditionally (e.g., `parallel: process.env.CI ? 4 : 0`) expect `parallel: 0` to mean "no parallelism / serial mode", but the Cucumber v12 runtime interprets `0` as "one parallel worker". WHY teams don't notice immediately: with `parallel: 1`, tests still pass and fail correctly — the difference surfaces only when `AfterAll` hooks throw string literals (not Error instances) that the parallel coordinator swallows silently while the serial runtime surfaces them. Fix: use `parallel: undefined` (or omit the key entirely) to opt into the serial runtime; use `parallel: 1` only when you explicitly want the parallel coordinator with a single worker.

**[community] Gotcha 3 — playwright-bdd v9.0.0-beta.0 strict step arity validation rejects step definitions that use TypeScript rest parameters (`...args: string[]`) to accept a variable number of Gherkin captures, because the arity check compares Cucumber Expression capture count against the function's `.length` property, and rest parameters have `.length: 0` regardless of how many captures the expression produces**: Teams that used rest parameters to write flexible multi-capture steps (`Given('the user has {string} and {string}', async (...args: string[]) => { ... })`) discover that `bddgen` reports an arity mismatch (0 vs 2). WHY rest parameters were used: some teams adopted the pattern to avoid TypeScript errors from expressions that produce different capture counts in different profiles (e.g., feature flags adding/removing a capture group), treating rest parameters as a flexibility mechanism. Fix: declare explicit parameters matching the capture count and use optional parameter typing for the conditional case, or write separate step definitions for each capture count variant using tag prioritization (Pattern 8 above).

**[community] Gotcha 4 — Playwright `expect(locator).toHaveText()` flakiness in BDD scenarios that test React 19 applications using concurrent rendering, where the DOM text content passes through an intermediate "streaming" state before settling on the final value, causing `toHaveText()` to match the intermediate value on fast CI runners during Playwright's auto-retry window and produce environment-specific false positives that cannot be reproduced locally**: Teams running playwright-bdd suites against React 19 apps notice certain `Then` steps asserting on heading or status text fail intermittently on high-core-count CI runners but never locally. WHY this is hard to diagnose: `toHaveText()` retries until timeout, but on fast runners the DOM briefly contains the streaming intermediate value during the retry window and the assertion matches a false positive; on slow runners streaming completes before the first retry and the assertion matches the final correct value. Fix: add a `waitFor` condition before the `toHaveText` assertion that waits for the React streaming indicator to disappear (e.g., `await page.waitForSelector('[data-streaming="false"]')`) or assert on a stable DOM element that only appears after streaming completes.

**[community] Gotcha 5 — Cucumber.js HTML formatter's external attachment rendering breaks in corporate environments where CSP headers on the CI artifact server block `fetch()` calls to the external attachment CDN, causing all external attachment links to silently fail to load with no visible error in the report UI, because the formatter's JavaScript catches `fetch()` failures silently and renders a blank placeholder rather than an error message, and the CSP violation is logged only to the browser's developer tools console**: Teams in enterprise environments that serve Cucumber HTML reports from an internal artifact server configured with strict CSP find that all external attachments (screenshots uploaded to S3, HAR files uploaded to artifact storage) render as blank preview panels with no error message in the report. WHY this is silent: the HTML formatter attachment preview JavaScript catches `fetch()` failures and renders a blank placeholder, a design choice that prevents the report from appearing broken on first load — the CSP violation is invisible in the report itself. Fix: use `formatOptions: { html: { includeAttachments: true } }` in the CI profile to embed all attachments inline as base64 data URIs, which are not subject to CSP `connect-src` restrictions; the trade-off is significantly larger report files for screenshot-heavy suites.

**[community] Gotcha 6 — playwright-bdd scenarios using the `BeforeScenario` hook to set up `page.route()` interceptors discover that route handlers registered in `BeforeScenario` are not active during the Background steps that execute before the scenario body, because playwright-bdd executes `BeforeScenario` hooks after Background steps complete, matching Cucumber's `Before` hook execution model, while developers expect route interceptors to be available from the very first step**: Teams that migrate from plain Playwright `beforeEach` tests to playwright-bdd discover that Background steps like "Given the API server is mocked" fail with actual HTTP requests to the server rather than intercepted mock responses when the `page.route()` setup is in `BeforeScenario`. WHY the order is unexpected: Cucumber's `Before` hook documentation shows hooks running before the first Given step, but playwright-bdd's `BeforeScenario` wraps the Cucumber `Before` lifecycle within Playwright's fixture setup, and the exact timing relative to Background step execution is not explicitly documented. Fix: register `page.route()` interceptors in a playwright-bdd fixture rather than in `BeforeScenario` — fixtures are set up before Background steps execute, making them the correct place for scenario-scoped route configuration.

## Cycle 40 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 16 — Playwright v1.60 `tracing.startHar()` / `tracing.stopHar()` for Network-Capture BDD Steps  [official]

Playwright v1.60 promotes HAR recording to a first-class tracing API by adding `tracing.startHar(path, options)` and `tracing.stopHar()` on the `Tracing` class, decoupling HAR capture from the `BrowserContext.recordHar` option that required the recording mode to be declared before the context was created. In playwright-bdd scenarios, this enables a `BeforeScenario`-level fixture to start HAR recording immediately before network-sensitive steps execute and stop it in `AfterScenario`, attaching the resulting file as a Cucumber artifact for post-mortem analysis on CI failures. The `mode: 'minimal'` option records only the data needed for HAR playback (URL, method, status), keeping artifact sizes small for suites with hundreds of scenarios, while `mode: 'full'` captures timing, cookies, and response bodies for forensic debugging of intermittent API failures. The `content: 'attach'` option writes response bodies as separate files in a `resourcesDir`, preventing a single large `.zip` from causing artifact-storage quota issues on shared CI platforms.

```typescript
// src/support/har-fixture.ts
// Playwright v1.60 tracing.startHar / stopHar in playwright-bdd fixtures
import { test as base } from 'playwright-bdd';
import path from 'node:path';
import fs from 'node:fs';

interface HarFixtures {
  harRecorder: { path: string };
}

export const test = base.extend<HarFixtures>({
  harRecorder: async ({ context, $testInfo }, use) => {
    const harPath = path.join(
      $testInfo.outputDir,
      `har-${$testInfo.title.replace(/\W+/g, '-')}.zip`,
    );
    // v1.60: startHar is a method on context.tracing, not context itself
    await context.tracing.startHar(harPath, {
      mode: process.env.CI ? 'minimal' : 'full',
      content: 'attach',
      urlFilter: /\/api\//,
    });
    await use({ path: harPath });
    // stopHar finalizes writing — must await before attaching
    await context.tracing.stopHar();
    if (fs.existsSync(harPath)) {
      await $testInfo.attach('network-har', { path: harPath, contentType: 'application/zip' });
    }
  },
});
```

**Tradeoff**: `tracing.startHar()` and `tracing.stopHar()` are scoped to a single `BrowserContext` — only one HAR recording can be active per context at a time, so teams that open multiple contexts within one scenario (e.g., multi-tab checkout flows) must create a separate HAR per context and attach them individually. Do NOT call `tracing.startHar()` after `tracing.start()` is already active — the two tracing APIs share the underlying tracing infrastructure; starting HAR recording while a `tracing.start()` trace is active causes an error in some browser implementations. Use them exclusively per scenario rather than composing them. [official]

### Pattern 17 — Playwright v1.60 `locator.drop()` for File-Upload BDD Scenarios  [official]

Playwright v1.60 adds `locator.drop(options)` as a first-class method for simulating external drag-and-drop operations onto page elements, dispatching synthetic `dragenter`, `dragover`, and `drop` events with cross-browser fidelity. In BDD scenarios that test file-upload dropzones, this replaces the brittle pattern of using `page.dispatchEvent()` to manually construct `DataTransfer` objects with the correct MIME type and `items` list — a pattern that worked inconsistently across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit because `DataTransfer` construction differs per browser. The `files` option accepts either a path string (for files on disk) or an inline buffer object `{ name, mimeType, buffer }`, allowing step definitions to generate test fixture files in memory without touching the filesystem.

```typescript
// src/steps/file-upload.steps.ts
// Playwright v1.60 locator.drop() for file-upload BDD scenarios
import { createBdd } from 'playwright-bdd';
import { test } from './fixtures.js';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

const { Given, When, Then } = createBdd(test);

Given('the document upload page is open', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/documents/upload');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('dropzone')).toBeVisible();
});

When(
  'I drop a {string} file named {string} onto the upload zone',
  async ({ page }, mimeType: string, fileName: string) => {
    const dropzone = page.getByTestId('dropzone');
    const content = `Generated test content for ${fileName}`;
    // v1.60 locator.drop(): inline buffer, no filesystem write needed
    await dropzone.drop({
      files: {
        name: fileName,
        mimeType,
        buffer: Buffer.from(content),
      },
    });
  },
);

When('I drop a file from disk at path {string}', async ({ page }, filePath: string) => {
  const dropzone = page.getByTestId('dropzone');
  // locator.drop() also accepts a filesystem path string
  await dropzone.drop({ files: filePath });
});

Then('the upload queue should show {int} pending file(s)', async ({ page }, count: number) => {
  await expect(page.getByTestId('upload-queue-item')).toHaveCount(count);
});

Then('the upload should complete successfully', async ({ page }) => {
  await expect(page.getByTestId('upload-success-badge')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15_000 });
});
```

**Tradeoff**: `locator.drop()` dispatches synthetic DOM events that are structurally correct but not identical to genuine user drag-and-drop gestures — applications that validate `DataTransfer.effectAllowed` or `DataTransfer.dropEffect` flags may behave differently under synthetic drops than under real user interactions. Test the application's upload handler to confirm it processes `DataTransfer.files` without inspecting `effectAllowed`; if it does inspect that flag, use `page.dispatchEvent()` with a manually constructed `DataTransfer` that sets the flags explicitly. Do NOT use `locator.drop()` to test drag-and-drop sorting within the same page — the method is designed for external drop sources (file uploads, clipboard data) rather than internal drag reordering, which requires `locator.dragTo()`. [official]

### Pattern 18 — Cucumber.js v12.5 `Plugin` API for Custom Pickle Ordering in BDD Suites  [official]

Cucumber.js v12.5 introduces a formal plugin system via `{ plugin: ['@my-org/plugin'] }` in the configuration, exposing `pickles:order` and `pickles:filter` transforms that allow external code to reorder or exclude scenarios before the test run begins — filling a gap that previously required monkey-patching Cucumber internals or maintaining a fork to implement priority-based execution. The `pickles:order` transform receives the full filtered `Pickle[]` array and must return a (possibly reordered) `Pickle[]`, enabling stable alphabetical ordering, randomized order for flake detection, or complexity-first ordering that runs long scenarios first to surface CI failures earlier. The `Plugin` type exported from `@cucumber/cucumber` provides full TypeScript autocompletion for the `coordinator` function and its available transforms.

```typescript
// plugins/priority-order-plugin.ts
// Cucumber.js v12.5 Plugin API — priority-based pickle ordering
import type { Plugin } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

// Priority is read from scenario tags: @priority:1 > @priority:2 > untagged (priority 99)
function getScenarioPriority(pickle: { tags: Array<{ name: string }> }): number {
  const priorityTag = pickle.tags.find((t) => t.name.startsWith('@priority:'));
  if (!priorityTag) return 99;
  const parsed = parseInt(priorityTag.name.replace('@priority:', ''), 10);
  return isNaN(parsed) ? 99 : parsed;
}

const plugin: Plugin = {
  type: 'plugin',
  coordinator({ on, transforms }) {
    // pickles:order runs after pickles:filter, receives only the scenarios that will run
    transforms.add('pickles:order', (pickles) => {
      return [...pickles].sort((a, b) => {
        const priorityDiff = getScenarioPriority(a) - getScenarioPriority(b);
        if (priorityDiff !== 0) return priorityDiff;
        // Secondary sort: alphabetical by pickle name for deterministic ordering
        return a.name.localeCompare(b.name);
      });
    });

    // Optional: emit a diagnostic message when priority ordering is active
    on('message', (_msg) => {
      // Messages are emitted for each Cucumber envelope during the run
    });

    // Return an optional async cleanup function
    return async () => {
      // cleanup after run completes
    };
  },
};

export default plugin;
```

**Tradeoff**: The `pickles:order` transform receives the array after `pickles:filter` has already been applied, so it operates on the final set of scenarios that will execute — you cannot use `pickles:order` to un-exclude a scenario filtered out by `pickles:filter` or by the `--tags` CLI flag. Do NOT use `pickles:order` to introduce randomization in CI pipelines where you need reproducible test ordering for bisecting failures — use a seeded shuffle in the `pickles:order` transform (e.g., `seed = process.env.SHUFFLE_SEED ?? Date.now()`) and log the seed value in the `coordinator` setup so a failing randomized run can be reproduced by passing the logged seed. [official]
