### Pattern 075 — Playwright `mergeTests()` for Cross-Package BDD Fixture Composition [official]

Large monorepos with shared BDD infrastructure split authentication fixtures, database-seeding fixtures, and feature-flag fixtures across separate `@internal/bdd-auth`, `@internal/bdd-db`, and `@internal/bdd-flags` packages. Importing and re-extending `test` three times in every feature's step-definition file creates boilerplate and breaks when a new infrastructure package is added — every step file must be updated. `mergeTests()` from `@playwright/test` composes multiple extended `test` objects into a single `test` export in a root fixtures file, so step definitions import a single `test` that carries all infrastructure fixtures from all packages.

```typescript
// fixtures/index.ts  — root fixture composition file
import { mergeTests } from '@playwright/test';
import { test as authTest }  from '@internal/bdd-auth';
import { test as dbTest }    from '@internal/bdd-db';
import { test as flagsTest } from '@internal/bdd-flags';
import { createBdd } from 'playwright-bdd';

// Compose all three infrastructure test objects into one
export const test = mergeTests(authTest, dbTest, flagsTest);
export const { Given, When, Then, Before, After } = createBdd(test);

// step-definitions/checkout.steps.ts — consumes only the composed test
import { Given, When, Then } from '../fixtures';
// All fixtures from auth, db, and flags are available in step definitions
// without any direct import of the individual packages

Given('I am logged in as {string}', async ({ authenticatedPage, seedUser }, role: string) => {
  // authenticatedPage from @internal/bdd-auth
  // seedUser from @internal/bdd-db
  await authenticatedPage.goto('/dashboard');
  await authenticatedPage.waitForURL(`/dashboard?role=${seedUser.role}`);
});

When('the {string} feature flag is enabled', async ({ overrideFlag }, flagName: string) => {
  // overrideFlag from @internal/bdd-flags
  await overrideFlag(flagName, true);
});

Then('I should see the {string} section', async ({ authenticatedPage }, sectionName: string) => {
  await expect(
    authenticatedPage.getByRole('region', { name: sectionName })
  ).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `mergeTests()` performs a shallow merge of the fixture objects from each `test` argument — if two packages define a fixture with the same name (e.g., both `@internal/bdd-auth` and `@internal/bdd-db` export a `page` override), the last package in the `mergeTests()` argument list wins and silently overrides the earlier one. WHY teams must establish a fixture naming convention (e.g., prefixing package-specific fixtures with the package abbreviation: `authPage`, `dbClient`, `flagOverride`) before adopting `mergeTests()`: namespace collisions in `mergeTests()` produce no TypeScript error because both fixtures satisfy the same interface, causing silent behavioral regression where the winning fixture's setup runs but the losing fixture's setup is entirely skipped.

---

### Pattern 076 — Cucumber.js `World` Lazy-Property Getter for Deferred Expensive Initialisation [community]

BDD `World` classes that initialise all infrastructure in the constructor (database clients, Redis connections, HTTP agent pools) incur the full initialisation cost on every scenario — including scenarios that never use those resources. Defining expensive resources as getter properties with a cached backing field defers initialisation to first access, so a scenario that only reads from a REST API never pays the cost of opening a database connection.

```typescript
// support/world.ts
import { setWorldConstructor, IWorldOptions } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { chromium, Browser, Page } from '@playwright/test';
import { createDbClient, DbClient } from '../lib/db-client';

export class AppWorld {
  // Backing fields — undefined until first access
  private _browser?: Browser;
  private _page?: Page;
  private _db?: DbClient;

  // Passed through from Cucumber's World options
  readonly scenarioName: string;

  constructor(options: IWorldOptions) {
    this.scenarioName = options.pickle.name;
  }

  // Lazy browser: opened only when a step first accesses this.browser
  get browser(): Browser {
    if (!this._browser) throw new Error('browser not initialised — call initBrowser() in Before');
    return this._browser;
  }

  async initBrowser(): Promise<void> {
    this._browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: true });
  }

  // Lazy page: created only when a step first accesses this.page
  get page(): Page {
    if (!this._page) throw new Error('page not initialised — call initBrowser() first');
    return this._page;
  }

  // Lazy DB: connected only if a step accesses this.db
  get db(): DbClient {
    if (!this._db) {
      // Synchronous factory — throws if env var DATABASE_URL is not set
      this._db = createDbClient(process.env['DATABASE_URL']!);
    }
    return this._db;
  }

  async cleanup(): Promise<void> {
    await this._page?.close();
    await this._browser?.close();
    await this._db?.disconnect();
  }
}

setWorldConstructor(AppWorld);
```

**Tradeoff.** Lazy getters that throw on uninitialized access produce clear error messages at first use, but when the getter silently auto-initializes (returning a new instance on every access instead of caching), it creates multiple live connections per scenario. WHY the backing-field guard (`if (!this._db) { this._db = createDbClient(...) }`) must be used instead of `this._db ??= createDbClient(...)` when the factory is asynchronous: the nullish-assignment operator `??=` does not await promises — `this._db ??= asyncFactory()` assigns the unresolved `Promise<DbClient>` to `this._db`, so the first caller gets a `Promise` object instead of a `DbClient`, and the guard is never true again on subsequent calls because `this._db` is now a non-null promise, meaning every subsequent caller also receives the same pending or resolved `Promise<DbClient>` cast as `DbClient`.

---

### Pattern 077 — Playwright Worker-Scoped `browser` Fixture Reuse Across BDD Scenarios in the Same Worker [official]

By default each BDD scenario in playwright-bdd receives an isolated browser `context` and `page`, but the underlying `browser` instance is also re-created per scenario when using the default `test`-scoped browser fixture. For test suites with many short scenarios (smoke tests, API-backed UI checks), browser launch time dominates per-scenario overhead. Defining a worker-scoped `browser` fixture launches the browser once per worker process and shares it across all scenarios assigned to that worker, reducing total suite wall-clock time without sacrificing scenario isolation (each scenario still gets its own `context` and `page`).

```typescript
// fixtures/worker-browser.fixture.ts
import { test as base, Browser, chromium } from '@playwright/test';
import { createBdd } from 'playwright-bdd';

// Extend with a worker-scoped browser fixture
export const test = base.extend<
  { workerPage: import('@playwright/test').Page },    // test-scoped
  { workerBrowser: Browser }                           // worker-scoped
>({
  // Worker-scoped: launched once per worker, shared across all scenarios in the worker
  workerBrowser: [
    async ({}, use) => {
      const browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: true });
      await use(browser);
      await browser.close(); // closed when the worker finishes all its scenarios
    },
    { scope: 'worker' },
  ],

  // Test-scoped: new context + page per scenario, using the shared worker browser
  workerPage: async ({ workerBrowser }, use) => {
    const context = await workerBrowser.newContext({
      viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 },
      locale: 'en-US',
    });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    await use(page);
    await context.close(); // context (and its page) closed after each scenario
  },
});

export const { Given, When, Then } = createBdd(test);

// step-definitions/smoke.steps.ts
import { Given, When, Then } from '../fixtures/worker-browser.fixture';

Given('the home page is open', async ({ workerPage }) => {
  await workerPage.goto(process.env['BASE_URL'] ?? 'http://localhost:3000');
});

Then('the page title is {string}', async ({ workerPage }, expected: string) => {
  await expect(workerPage).toHaveTitle(expected);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Worker-scoped browser fixtures reduce launch overhead but mean that a browser crash in one scenario affects all subsequent scenarios assigned to the same worker, because the browser is not relaunched between scenarios. WHY worker-scoped browser fixtures should be paired with Playwright's `retries` option set to at least `1` and a `Before` hook that checks `browser.isConnected()`: a disconnected browser (crashed or killed by the OS) will cause all remaining scenarios in the worker to fail with `Target closed` errors rather than being retried; detecting `!workerBrowser.isConnected()` in a `Before` hook and throwing a descriptive error forces Playwright to re-queue the scenario for a fresh worker rather than silently accumulating failures.

---

### Pattern 078 — Cucumber.js `ITestCaseHookParameter.pickle` for Tag-Driven Conditional Setup in `Before` Hooks [official]

BDD suites that mix scenarios requiring different setup profiles (database-only, API-mocked, full-stack with real browser) use Cucumber.js tag expressions on `Before` hooks to filter execution. However, tag-expression-filtered hooks fire for all matching scenarios without conditional logic inside the hook body. When setup logic must branch based on scenario-level tag combinations (e.g., `@api` with `@v2` requires a different base URL than `@api` alone), the `pickle` object on `ITestCaseHookParameter` exposes the full tag list of the current scenario, allowing a single shared `Before` hook to read tags and branch setup logic accordingly.

```typescript
// support/hooks.ts
import { Before, ITestCaseHookParameter } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from './world';

// Single Before hook that branches on tag combinations
Before(async function (this: AppWorld, { pickle }: ITestCaseHookParameter) {
  const tags = pickle.tags.map(t => t.name);

  const isApiScenario    = tags.includes('@api');
  const isV2             = tags.includes('@v2');
  const needsRealBrowser = tags.includes('@e2e');

  if (isApiScenario && isV2) {
    // v2 API scenarios use a different base URL and require auth token
    this.apiBaseUrl = process.env['API_V2_BASE_URL'] ?? 'http://localhost:4001';
    this.authToken  = await fetchApiToken('v2');
  } else if (isApiScenario) {
    this.apiBaseUrl = process.env['API_BASE_URL'] ?? 'http://localhost:4000';
    this.authToken  = await fetchApiToken('v1');
  }

  if (needsRealBrowser) {
    await this.initBrowser();
    this.currentPage = await this.browser.newPage();
  }

  // Log scenario name + tags to CI output for debugging parallel runs
  if (process.env['CI']) {
    console.log(`[setup] ${pickle.name} [${tags.join(' ')}]`);
  }
});

async function fetchApiToken(version: 'v1' | 'v2'): Promise<string> {
  const endpoint = version === 'v2' ? '/auth/v2/token' : '/auth/token';
  const res = await fetch(`http://localhost:4000${endpoint}`, { method: 'POST' });
  const { token } = await res.json() as { token: string };
  return token;
}
```

**Tradeoff.** Reading `pickle.tags` in a `Before` hook and branching on tag combinations duplicates tag-meaning logic that is already expressed in the feature file, creating two sources of truth — the tags on the scenario and the branching conditions in the hook. WHY this pattern should be supplemented with a support-file comment mapping tag names to their expected hook behaviors: when a tag is renamed in feature files (e.g., `@api` becomes `@rest`), the hook's `tags.includes('@api')` check silently stops matching and the API setup is skipped without any error, causing `this.apiBaseUrl` to be undefined and producing misleading "Cannot read properties of undefined" failures in step definitions rather than a clear setup-contract violation.

---

### Pattern 079 — Playwright `page.waitForResponse()` with URL Predicate for BDD API-Assertion Step Definitions [official]

BDD `Then` steps that assert on server-side outcomes (e.g., "Then the order should be saved in the database") often trigger a UI action that causes an API call — but the UI update that reflects the server response may lag or be optimistic. Intercepting the specific API response with `page.waitForResponse()` and asserting on its body provides a deterministic, race-condition-free way to verify that the server processed the action correctly, without polling the database directly from the step definition.

```typescript
// step-definitions/orders.steps.ts
import { When, Then } from '../fixtures';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Capture the response promise BEFORE triggering the action
// so Playwright does not miss a fast response
When('I confirm the order', async ({ page }) => {
  // Start waiting for the response BEFORE clicking confirm
  const responsePromise = page.waitForResponse(
    response =>
      response.url().includes('/api/orders') &&
      response.request().method() === 'POST'
  );

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Confirm order' }).click();

  // Now await the response — this resolves when the POST /api/orders response arrives
  const response = await responsePromise;
  const body = await response.json() as { orderId: string; status: string };

  // Attach order ID to the page for subsequent Then steps to use
  await page.evaluate(
    (orderId) => { (window as Window & { __lastOrderId?: string }).__lastOrderId = orderId; },
    body.orderId
  );
});

Then('the order confirmation should show order ID', async ({ page }) => {
  // Retrieve the order ID set by the When step
  const orderId = await page.evaluate(
    () => (window as Window & { __lastOrderId?: string }).__lastOrderId
  );
  expect(orderId).toBeTruthy();

  // Assert the UI also displays this order ID
  await expect(
    page.getByTestId('order-confirmation-id')
  ).toHaveText(orderId!);
});

Then('the order should have status {string}', async ({ page }, expectedStatus: string) => {
  // Assert the order status badge on the confirmation page
  await expect(
    page.getByTestId('order-status-badge')
  ).toHaveText(expectedStatus, { ignoreCase: true });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `page.waitForResponse()` resolves on the first response matching the predicate — if the page makes multiple `POST /api/orders` calls (e.g., retry logic or preflight requests), the promise resolves on the first match and the step proceeds before the authoritative response arrives. WHY `page.waitForResponse()` predicates should include both URL and status code checks when the endpoint can return both 200 (success) and 422 (validation error): a predicate of `r => r.url().includes('/api/orders') && r.status() === 201` waits specifically for the created-successfully response and does not resolve on validation-error 422 responses, preventing the step from accidentally asserting on a rejected order response as if it were a successful creation.

---

### Pattern 080 — Playwright `locator.tap()` with Touch Emulation for Mobile BDD Scenarios [official]

BDD suites that cover mobile web behaviour (tap interactions, swipe-triggered UI, touch-only menus) must use `locator.tap()` instead of `locator.click()` and must launch the browser context with `hasTouch: true` — without touch emulation enabled, `tap()` events on mobile-responsive components may fall back to mouse events and trigger wrong behaviours (e.g., hover states instead of tap-open states on touch-only navigation menus).

```typescript
// fixtures/mobile.fixture.ts
import { test as base, devices } from '@playwright/test';
import { createBdd } from 'playwright-bdd';

const iPhone14 = devices['iPhone 14'];

export const test = base.extend<{ mobilePage: import('@playwright/test').Page }>({
  mobilePage: async ({ browser }, use) => {
    // Create a context with iPhone 14 device descriptor — includes hasTouch: true
    const context = await browser.newContext({
      ...iPhone14,
      locale: 'en-US',
    });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    await use(page);
    await context.close();
  },
});

export const { Given, When, Then } = createBdd(test);

// step-definitions/mobile-nav.steps.ts
import { Given, When, Then } from '../fixtures/mobile.fixture';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

Given('I am on the mobile product listing page', async ({ mobilePage }) => {
  await mobilePage.goto('/products');
  // Wait for the mobile nav to be rendered (desktop nav is hidden via CSS)
  await mobilePage.waitForSelector('[data-testid="mobile-nav-hamburger"]');
});

When('I tap the navigation menu button', async ({ mobilePage }) => {
  // Use tap() — not click() — to fire touch events on the hamburger icon
  await mobilePage.locator('[data-testid="mobile-nav-hamburger"]').tap();
});

Then('the mobile navigation drawer should be open', async ({ mobilePage }) => {
  await expect(
    mobilePage.locator('[data-testid="mobile-nav-drawer"]')
  ).toBeVisible();
});

When('I swipe left on the product image', async ({ mobilePage }) => {
  const image = mobilePage.locator('[data-testid="product-image-carousel"]');
  const box   = await image.boundingBox();
  if (!box) throw new Error('product image carousel not found');
  // Simulate a left swipe using touchscreen API
  await mobilePage.touchscreen.swipe(
    box.x + box.width * 0.8, box.y + box.height / 2,
    box.x + box.width * 0.2, box.y + box.height / 2,
    { steps: 10 }
  );
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `devices['iPhone 14']` sets `hasTouch: true`, `isMobile: true`, a specific viewport, and a specific `userAgent` — the combined effect means CSS media queries, JavaScript `navigator.maxTouchPoints`, and `userAgent` sniffing all return mobile values simultaneously, which may cause the application to serve a completely different code path than intended for the test. WHY mobile BDD scenarios should specify `devices['iPhone 14']` from the official Playwright device list rather than manually setting `{ hasTouch: true, viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 } }`: the device descriptor bundles `deviceScaleFactor`, `isMobile`, `userAgent`, `hasTouch`, and `viewport` as a single consistent set — manually specifying only `hasTouch` without the matching `isMobile: true` causes some React/Vue mobile-detection hooks to render the desktop component tree while firing touch events, producing an inconsistent hybrid state that neither matches real mobile nor real desktop behaviour.

---

### Pattern 081 — Cucumber.js `FormatterPlugin` with `@cucumber/query` for Domain-Specific BDD Report Generation [official]

The Cucumber.js Plugin API (introduced in v12.5.0) allows writing `FormatterPlugin<T>` implementations that subscribe to the Cucumber Messages event stream and produce custom report artefacts. Pairing a `FormatterPlugin` with `@cucumber/query` (which indexes the message stream into queryable lookup structures) enables domain-specific reports such as a "requirements traceability matrix" that maps each `@requirement-*` tag to its pass/fail status — something neither the built-in `html` nor `json` reporters produce.

```typescript
// formatters/traceability-formatter.ts
import { IFormatterOptions } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { Query }              from '@cucumber/query';
import * as messages          from '@cucumber/messages';
import * as fs                from 'node:fs';
import * as path              from 'node:path';

interface TraceRow {
  requirementId: string;
  scenarioName:  string;
  status:        string;
  featureFile:   string;
}

export default class TraceabilityFormatter {
  private readonly query = new Query();
  private readonly rows: TraceRow[] = [];
  private readonly outputPath: string;

  constructor(options: IFormatterOptions) {
    this.outputPath = options.parsedArgvOptions?.['output'] as string ??
      path.join(process.cwd(), 'reports', 'traceability.json');

    // Subscribe to all Cucumber messages via the event data emitter
    options.eventDataCollector.on('envelope', (envelope: messages.Envelope) => {
      this.query.handleMessage(envelope);
    });

    // On stream end, produce the report
    options.eventBroadcaster.on('envelope', (envelope: messages.Envelope) => {
      if (envelope.testRunFinished) {
        this.buildReport();
        this.writeReport();
      }
    });
  }

  private buildReport(): void {
    for (const testCaseAttempt of this.query.getTestCaseAttempts()) {
      const pickle      = this.query.getPickle(testCaseAttempt.testCase.pickleId);
      const reqTags     = pickle.tags
        .map(t => t.name)
        .filter(n => n.startsWith('@requirement-'));

      if (reqTags.length === 0) continue;

      const status = testCaseAttempt.worstTestStepResult?.status ?? 'UNKNOWN';

      for (const reqTag of reqTags) {
        this.rows.push({
          requirementId: reqTag.replace('@requirement-', ''),
          scenarioName:  pickle.name,
          status,
          featureFile:   pickle.uri ?? 'unknown',
        });
      }
    }
  }

  private writeReport(): void {
    fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(this.outputPath), { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(this.outputPath, JSON.stringify(this.rows, null, 2), 'utf8');
    console.log(`[traceability] wrote ${this.rows.length} rows -> ${this.outputPath}`);
  }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `@cucumber/query` indexes messages in insertion order — if the Cucumber Messages stream is produced by a parallel run where workers emit messages interleaved, `getTestCaseAttempts()` may return attempts out of feature-file order, producing a traceability report sorted by completion time rather than by feature file. WHY the `@cucumber/query` `Query` object must be populated from the `eventDataCollector` event stream rather than by constructing it manually from `gherkinDocument` objects: the `Query` class tracks the relationships between `GherkinDocument`, `Pickle`, `TestCase`, and `TestCaseAttempt` messages by correlating their IDs as they arrive — constructing these objects manually and passing them to `Query` methods bypasses the ID-correlation logic and produces a query object where `getPickle(pickleId)` returns `undefined` for every lookup.

---

### Pattern 082 — Playwright `expect(page).toHaveURL()` with Regex for Parameterised Redirect Assertions [official]

BDD `Then` steps that assert on post-action redirects (e.g., "Then I should be redirected to the order confirmation page") often fail when the redirect URL contains a dynamic segment (order ID, UUID, session token) that varies between test runs. Using `expect(page).toHaveURL(/pattern/)` with a regular expression asserts the structural shape of the URL without hard-coding the dynamic value, and the captured group can subsequently be extracted for use in downstream steps.

```typescript
// step-definitions/redirect.steps.ts
import { Then } from '../fixtures';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

Then('I should be redirected to the order confirmation page', async ({ page }) => {
  // Assert URL matches /orders/<uuid>/confirmation without knowing the UUID
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(
    /\/orders\/[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}\/confirmation/,
    { timeout: 10_000 }
  );
});

Then('the confirmation URL should contain my email address', async ({ page }) => {
  // Extract the email query param from the current URL and assert it is present
  const url = new URL(page.url());
  const emailParam = url.searchParams.get('email');
  expect(emailParam).toBeTruthy();
  expect(emailParam).toMatch(/^[^@]+@[^@]+\.[^@]+$/); // basic email shape check
});

Then('I should be redirected to {string} or the dashboard', async ({ page }, expectedPath: string) => {
  // Accepts either the specific path or /dashboard as valid post-login destinations
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(
    new RegExp(`(${expectedPath.replace('/', '\\/')}|/dashboard)`)
  );
});

Then('the URL should include a valid session token', async ({ page }) => {
  // Assert that a `token` query param exists and is at least 32 hex chars
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/[?&]token=[0-9a-f]{32,}/);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Regex-based URL assertions accept any URL matching the pattern, which means a step can pass even when the application redirects to a subtly wrong URL (e.g., `/orders/undefined/confirmation` if UUID generation fails and the client serializes `undefined`). WHY BDD URL-redirect steps should combine a regex assertion with a subsequent `expect(page.locator('h1')).not.toHaveText('Error')` check: the regex confirms the URL structural shape but not that the page loaded successfully — `/orders/undefined/confirmation` matches a sufficiently loose UUID pattern if `undefined` is long enough; the heading check adds a semantic layer that confirms the page rendered as the order-confirmation view and not an error page.

---

### Pattern 083 — Cucumber.js `BeforeAll` / `AfterAll` with Module-Level Shared State for Suite-Wide Resources [official]

BDD suites that integrate with external systems (test databases, local HTTP servers, mock SMTP services) need to start those services once before any scenario runs and stop them after all scenarios complete. Cucumber.js `BeforeAll` / `AfterAll` hooks (introduced in Cucumber.js v12.3.0 with named-hook support) can write their initialised resources to a module-level variable that all scenarios in the worker can read, avoiding the cost of starting and stopping the service for every scenario.

```typescript
// support/global-setup.ts
import { BeforeAll, AfterAll, setDefaultTimeout } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { createServer, Server } from 'node:http';
import { AddressInfo } from 'node:net';
import { app } from '../src/app';

setDefaultTimeout(30_000);

// Module-level shared state — written in BeforeAll, read in step definitions
let httpServer: Server;
export let serverBaseUrl: string;

BeforeAll({ name: 'start-http-server', order: 1 }, async function () {
  httpServer = createServer(app);
  await new Promise<void>(resolve => httpServer.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', resolve));
  const { port } = httpServer.address() as AddressInfo;
  serverBaseUrl = `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`;
  console.log(`[BeforeAll] test server listening on ${serverBaseUrl}`);
});

AfterAll({ name: 'stop-http-server', order: 1 }, async function () {
  await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) =>
    httpServer.close(err => (err ? reject(err) : resolve()))
  );
  console.log('[AfterAll] test server closed');
});

// step-definitions/api.steps.ts — imports the module-level export
import { Given, When, Then } from '../fixtures';
import { serverBaseUrl }      from '../support/global-setup';

Given('the API server is running', async function () {
  const res = await fetch(`${serverBaseUrl}/health`);
  expect(res.status).toBe(200);
});

When('I send a GET request to {string}', async function (path: string) {
  this.lastResponse = await fetch(`${serverBaseUrl}${path}`);
});

Then('the response status should be {int}', async function (status: number) {
  expect(this.lastResponse.status).toBe(status);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Module-level state shared via `BeforeAll` is process-scoped — when Cucumber.js runs in parallel mode, each worker process loads the support files independently and each worker runs its own `BeforeAll` hook, so there is no actual sharing between workers; every worker starts and stops its own server instance. WHY this is the correct and expected behaviour rather than a bug: parallel Cucumber.js workers are separate Node.js processes with no shared memory, and module-level variables are worker-local; teams that need truly shared state across parallel workers (e.g., a single database in a known state) must use an external coordination mechanism such as a file lock (`proper-lockfile` npm package) or a sidecar server process started outside Cucumber.js, not module-level variables.

---

### Pattern 084 — Playwright `page.screenshot()` with `{ animations: 'disabled' }` for Stable Visual BDD Steps [official]

BDD `Then` steps that assert on visual snapshots using `expect(page).toHaveScreenshot()` fail intermittently on CI when CSS animations or transitions are mid-frame at the moment the screenshot is taken — the captured frame differs from the baseline by a few pixels because an animation is at a different point in its cycle on a slower CI runner. Passing `{ animations: 'disabled' }` to `expect(page).toHaveScreenshot()` instructs Playwright to pause all CSS animations and Web Animations API animations to their end state before capturing, producing a deterministic screenshot regardless of system speed.

```typescript
// step-definitions/visual.steps.ts
import { Then } from '../fixtures';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

Then('the product card should match the approved design', async ({ page }) => {
  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="product-card"]')).toHaveScreenshot(
    'product-card.png',
    {
      animations: 'disabled',   // pause all CSS/Web animations before capture
      maxDiffPixels: 0,          // zero pixel tolerance — pixel-perfect assertion
      timeout: 10_000,
    }
  );
});

Then('the checkout flow header should match the approved design', async ({ page }) => {
  // Full-page screenshot with animations disabled and a 1% pixel-ratio tolerance
  await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('checkout-header.png', {
    animations: 'disabled',
    maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01,
    clip: { x: 0, y: 0, width: 1280, height: 200 }, // only the header region
  });
});

Then('the loading skeleton should match at 50% opacity', async ({ page }) => {
  // Without animations: 'disabled', the skeleton pulse animation may be mid-cycle
  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="loading-skeleton"]')).toHaveScreenshot(
    'loading-skeleton-stable.png',
    {
      animations: 'disabled',
      maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.02,
    }
  );
});

Then('the error state banner should match the approved design', async ({ page }) => {
  await expect(page.locator('[role="alert"]')).toHaveScreenshot(
    'error-banner.png',
    { animations: 'disabled', maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01 }
  );
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `animations: 'disabled'` pauses animations at their end state, which means the captured screenshot reflects the animation-completed UI state rather than the mid-animation state — if the business intent of the `Then` step is to assert that a loading spinner is visible during an in-progress operation, disabling animations will capture the post-animation (resolved/hidden) state and the assertion will fail to verify the spinner. WHY `{ animations: 'allow' }` is explicitly required for BDD steps asserting on transitional UI states: Playwright's default when `animations` is not specified is `'disabled'` for `toHaveScreenshot()` (not `'allow'`), so steps that intentionally want to capture a mid-animation frame must pass `{ animations: 'allow' }` explicitly and accept that the resulting screenshot will be non-deterministic across CI environments with different CPU speeds.

---

### Pattern 085 — Cucumber.js `IParameterTypeDefinition` `useForSnippets` Flag for Snippet-Friendly Custom Parameter Types [official]

Cucumber.js's snippet generator produces step definition stubs when an undefined step is encountered. By default, custom parameter types registered via `defineParameterType` are used in snippets as their type name — but if the parameter type's `regexp` is complex or the type is an internal implementation detail, the generated snippet becomes unreadable. Setting `useForSnippets: false` on internal parameter types prevents them from appearing in auto-generated snippets while still allowing them to be used in step definitions that are written manually.

```typescript
// support/parameter-types.ts
import { defineParameterType } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { Money }   from '../domain/money';
import { OrderId } from '../domain/order-id';

// PUBLIC parameter type — appears in snippets as {money}
// useForSnippets defaults to true
defineParameterType<Money>({
  name:     'money',
  regexp:   /\$[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]{2})?/,
  transformer: (raw: string): Money => Money.parse(raw),
  useForSnippets: true, // default — this type appears in generated step stubs
});

// INTERNAL parameter type — used in hand-written steps, hidden from snippets
// Without useForSnippets: false, Cucumber would generate stubs containing
// {internalOrderRef} which confuses developers writing new scenarios
defineParameterType<OrderId>({
  name:    'internalOrderRef',
  regexp:  /ORD-[A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{6}/,
  transformer: (raw: string): OrderId => OrderId.fromString(raw),
  useForSnippets: false, // hide from snippet generator
  preferForRegexpMatch: true,
});

// Usage in step definition — the {internalOrderRef} type resolves automatically
// even though it does not appear in snippets
import { Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { AppWorld } from './world';

Then(
  'the order {internalOrderRef} should be in status {string}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, orderId: OrderId, status: string) {
    const order = await this.db.orders.findById(orderId.value);
    if (!order) throw new Error(`Order ${orderId.value} not found`);
    expect(order.status).toBe(status);
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff.** `useForSnippets: false` hides the parameter type from auto-generated step stubs but does not prevent the type from matching in step definitions — a developer who creates a new step by copying and modifying a step definition that uses `{internalOrderRef}` will have the match work silently without understanding that a custom transformer is involved. WHY a code comment on every step definition using a `useForSnippets: false` parameter type is essential for maintainability: these parameter types are deliberately invisible in tooling output, so without a comment like `// OrderId: see support/parameter-types.ts — transforms ORD-XXX-000000 strings to OrderId domain objects`, developers modifying the step will remove the custom type name and replace it with a bare string capture, losing the domain-object transformation.

---

### Pattern 086 — Playwright `locator.evaluate()` for DOM-Property BDD Assertions Not Exposed via Playwright Matchers [official]

Playwright's built-in matchers (`toHaveText`, `toHaveAttribute`, `toHaveValue`, `toBeChecked`) cover the most common DOM assertion needs, but some DOM properties are not surfaced by any built-in matcher — for example, the `scrollTop` of a scroll container, the `selectionStart`/`selectionEnd` of a text input, or the `files` property of a file input. `locator.evaluate()` executes a callback in the browser context and returns a JSON-serializable value, making it possible to assert on arbitrary DOM properties in `Then` steps.

```typescript
// step-definitions/dom-assertions.steps.ts
import { Then } from '../fixtures';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

Then('the results list should be scrolled to the top', async ({ page }) => {
  const scrollTop = await page
    .locator('[data-testid="results-list"]')
    .evaluate((el: HTMLElement) => el.scrollTop);
  expect(scrollTop).toBe(0);
});

Then('the search input should have the cursor at the end', async ({ page }) => {
  const { selectionStart, selectionEnd, valueLength } = await page
    .locator('[data-testid="search-input"]')
    .evaluate((el: HTMLInputElement) => ({
      selectionStart: el.selectionStart,
      selectionEnd:   el.selectionEnd,
      valueLength:    el.value.length,
    }));
  // Cursor at end means selectionStart === selectionEnd === value.length
  expect(selectionStart).toBe(valueLength);
  expect(selectionEnd).toBe(valueLength);
});

Then('the file upload input should have {int} file(s) selected', async ({ page }, count: number) => {
  const fileCount = await page
    .locator('[data-testid="file-upload"]')
    .evaluate((el: HTMLInputElement) => el.files?.length ?? 0);
  expect(fileCount).toBe(count);
});

Then('the video player should be muted', async ({ page }) => {
  const muted = await page
    .locator('[data-testid="video-player"]')
    .evaluate((el: HTMLVideoElement) => el.muted);
  expect(muted).toBe(true);
});

Then('the textarea should have {int} characters', async ({ page }, count: number) => {
  const length = await page
    .locator('[data-testid="bio-textarea"]')
    .evaluate((el: HTMLTextAreaElement) => el.value.length);
  expect(length).toBe(count);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `locator.evaluate()` serializes the return value from the browser context to JSON — DOM objects, `File` objects, circular references, and `undefined` properties in returned objects are all silently dropped during serialization, producing `null` or `{}` in the test context without throwing. WHY BDD step definitions using `locator.evaluate()` must always extract primitive values (numbers, strings, booleans, arrays of primitives) from the browser element before returning: `el.files?.length ?? 0` is a safe serialization pattern (returns a number), but `el.files` (a `FileList` object) would serialize to `{}` because `FileList` is not a plain JSON object — the assertion `expect(fileCount).toBe(count)` would compare `{}` to a number and produce a confusing `Expected: 2, Received: {}` failure instead of a clear error about why `FileList` cannot be serialized.

---

### Pattern 087 — Cucumber.js Rerun Formatter with `--retry` Flag for Flaky-Scenario Triage [official]

CI pipelines that run large BDD suites accumulate flaky scenarios whose failures are intermittent — a network timeout, a timing race, or an external service hiccup. Running the full suite on every failure wastes CI minutes. The Cucumber.js `rerun` formatter writes a `@rerun.txt` file containing only the failed scenarios' file paths and line numbers; a second CI step passes `@rerun.txt` as the input feature argument combined with `--retry 2` so that only the failed scenarios are re-executed with automatic retry, producing a definitive pass/fail for the flaky set.

```typescript
// cucumber.config.ts
import type { IConfiguration } from '@cucumber/cucumber/api';

const base: Partial<IConfiguration> = {
  require:  ['dist/step-definitions/**/*.js', 'dist/support/**/*.js'],
  format:   ['progress-bar', 'html:reports/cucumber-report.html'],
  parallel: 4,
};

const config: Record<string, Partial<IConfiguration>> = {
  default: {
    ...base,
    // Write a rerun file listing failed scenario locations
    format: [
      ...base.format as string[],
      'rerun:reports/rerun.txt',
    ],
  },

  // "rerun" profile: run only the scenarios from the rerun file, with retries
  rerun: {
    ...base,
    // Pass the rerun file as input — Cucumber resolves it to the original feature paths
    paths: ['@reports/rerun.txt'],
    retry: 2,
    // Separate report so the main report is not overwritten
    format: [
      'progress-bar',
      'html:reports/rerun-report.html',
      // Do NOT write another rerun file here — that would create an infinite rerun loop
    ],
    parallel: 2, // fewer workers for the smaller rerun set
  },
};

export default config;
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/e2e.yml (excerpt)
- name: Run BDD suite
  run: npx cucumber-js --profile default

- name: Re-run failed scenarios with retry
  if: failure()
  run: npx cucumber-js --profile rerun
  continue-on-error: true   # rerun failures are tracked separately

- name: Upload rerun report
  if: failure()
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: rerun-report
    path: reports/rerun-report.html
```

**Tradeoff.** The `rerun` formatter writes absolute file paths to `@rerun.txt` — on CI runners where the workspace path differs between the primary run job and the rerun job (e.g., when using a matrix strategy that assigns different runners), the absolute paths in `@rerun.txt` will not resolve on the rerun runner and Cucumber.js will error with `No scenarios found matching the paths in @reports/rerun.txt`. WHY the rerun formatter output must be post-processed to relative paths before being consumed by the rerun profile: replacing the workspace prefix with a relative path (e.g., `sed -i "s|${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/||g" reports/rerun.txt` in the CI step) ensures the `@rerun.txt` paths are portable across runners with different workspace mount points.

---

### Pattern 088 — Playwright `expect(locator).toHaveAttribute()` with Regex for Flexible BDD Attribute Assertions [official]

BDD `Then` steps that assert on HTML attributes containing dynamic or environment-specific values (CDN-generated `src` URLs, server-rendered `href` paths with build hashes, `data-tracking-id` values) fail when the attribute value is not deterministic. `expect(locator).toHaveAttribute()` accepts a `RegExp` second argument, allowing steps to assert on the structural pattern of an attribute value without hard-coding the dynamic segment.

```typescript
// step-definitions/attribute-assertions.steps.ts
import { Then } from '../fixtures';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

Then('the product image should have a valid CDN source URL', async ({ page }) => {
  // The CDN URL pattern: https://cdn.example.com/<hash>/<filename>.webp
  await expect(
    page.locator('[data-testid="product-hero-image"]')
  ).toHaveAttribute(
    'src',
    /^https:\/\/cdn\.example\.com\/[a-f0-9]{40}\/[^/]+\.webp$/
  );
});

Then('the download link should point to a PDF file', async ({ page }) => {
  await expect(
    page.getByRole('link', { name: /download/i })
  ).toHaveAttribute('href', /\.pdf(\?.*)?$/);
});

Then('the video element should be marked as accessible', async ({ page }) => {
  // aria-label must be a non-empty string — check it exists and has content
  await expect(
    page.locator('[data-testid="product-video"]')
  ).toHaveAttribute('aria-label', /.+/); // at least one character
});

Then('the form should submit to the correct API endpoint', async ({ page }) => {
  // Environment-specific action URLs: /api/v1/... on staging, /api/v2/... on prod
  await expect(
    page.locator('[data-testid="checkout-form"]')
  ).toHaveAttribute('action', /^\/api\/v[12]\/orders$/);
});

Then('the tracking pixel should have a valid impression ID', async ({ page }) => {
  await expect(
    page.locator('[data-testid="impression-pixel"]')
  ).toHaveAttribute('data-impression-id', /^imp_[A-Za-z0-9]{16}$/);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Regex-based attribute assertions pass on any value matching the pattern — a too-permissive regex (e.g., `/.+/` for an `href`) accepts an error page URL, a `javascript:void(0)` value, or an internal redirect path just as readily as the expected CDN URL. WHY BDD attribute-assertion regexes should be as specific as the business intent warrants: a step that asserts "the download link should point to a PDF" has a business intent that is violated by `href="javascript:void(0)"`; the regex `/\.pdf(\?.*)?$/` encodes that intent precisely, while `/.+/` merely asserts the attribute is non-empty, which is weaker than the business requirement and could pass even when the application is broken.

---

### Pattern 089 — VS Code `cucumberautocomplete` Extension with `cucumberautocomplete.steps` for BDD Step Completion in Large Monorepos [community]

In monorepos where step definitions are spread across multiple packages (`packages/auth/step-definitions/`, `packages/checkout/step-definitions/`, `packages/catalog/step-definitions/`), VS Code's Cucumber extension cannot discover steps outside the workspace root without explicit path configuration. Setting `cucumberautocomplete.steps` in `.vscode/settings.json` to include glob patterns covering all packages provides autocomplete, go-to-definition, and undefined-step highlighting across the entire monorepo from any feature file.

```json
// .vscode/settings.json
{
  "cucumberautocomplete.steps": [
    "packages/*/step-definitions/**/*.steps.ts",
    "packages/*/step-definitions/**/*.steps.js",
    "packages/shared/support/**/*.ts",
    "e2e/step-definitions/**/*.steps.ts"
  ],
  "cucumberautocomplete.syncfeatures": "packages/*/features/**/*.feature",
  "cucumberautocomplete.strictGherkinCompletion": true,
  "cucumberautocomplete.formatConfOverride": {
    "Scenario": 0,
    "Given":    1,
    "When":     1,
    "Then":     1,
    "And":      1,
    "But":      1
  },
  "cucumberautocomplete.onTypeFormat": true,
  "cucumberautocomplete.smartSnippets": true,
  "cucumberautocomplete.stepsInNavBar": true
}
```

```typescript
// scripts/check-undefined-steps.ts — companion pre-commit utility
// Catches steps in .feature files that have no matching step definition
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { glob } from 'glob';

const features = glob.sync('packages/*/features/**/*.feature');
const steps    = glob.sync('packages/*/step-definitions/**/*.steps.ts');

// Parse step text patterns from step definition files
const definedPatterns: RegExp[] = [];
for (const stepFile of steps) {
  const content = readFileSync(stepFile, 'utf8');
  const matches = content.matchAll(/(?:Given|When|Then)\(\s*['"`]([^'"`]+)['"`]/g);
  for (const [, pattern] of matches) {
    try { definedPatterns.push(new RegExp(pattern)); } catch { /* skip invalid regex */ }
  }
}

let undefinedCount = 0;
for (const feature of features) {
  const content = readFileSync(feature, 'utf8');
  const stepLines = content.match(/^\s+(?:Given|When|Then|And|But) .+/gm) ?? [];
  for (const line of stepLines) {
    const stepText = line.trim().replace(/^(Given|When|Then|And|But) /, '');
    if (!definedPatterns.some(p => p.test(stepText))) {
      console.error(`UNDEFINED STEP in ${feature}: "${stepText}"`);
      undefinedCount++;
    }
  }
}
if (undefinedCount > 0) process.exit(1);
```

**Tradeoff.** `cucumberautocomplete.steps` glob patterns are evaluated by the VS Code extension at workspace startup — adding a new package to the monorepo requires updating `.vscode/settings.json` manually or restarting the extension, and the glob is not hot-reloaded when new directories are created. WHY the glob pattern `"packages/*/step-definitions/**/*.steps.ts"` is preferred over `"**/*.steps.ts"` in the VS Code settings: the `**` pattern at the workspace root also matches `node_modules/*/test/**/*.steps.ts` if any installed package happens to have `.steps.ts` files, causing the extension to index thousands of third-party step patterns that pollute the autocomplete list and slow the extension's step-indexing phase on first load.

## Community Gotchas — Cycle 48

**[community] Gotcha 6 — Playwright `locator.evaluate()` callbacks that return DOM Node objects, `FileList` instances, or any non-plain-JSON value serialize silently to `null` or `{}` in the test context without throwing a serialization error — teams observe that `Then` steps asserting `expect(fileCount).toBe(2)` fail with `Expected: 2, Received: {}` when the evaluate callback returns `el.files` (a `FileList`) instead of `el.files.length` (a number), and the failure message gives no indication that a serialization failure occurred**: The `evaluate()` callback's return value is transferred from the browser context to the Node.js test context via JSON serialization through the CDP protocol — objects that are not plain JSON (DOM Nodes, `FileList`, `HTMLCollection`, `Map`, `Set`, class instances with non-enumerable properties) serialize to `{}` or `null` rather than throwing, because CDP silently omits non-serializable values from the response payload. WHY every `locator.evaluate()` callback that accesses a browser API object must extract a primitive value (number, string, boolean, array of primitives) before returning: extracting `el.files.length` (number), `el.value` (string), or `Array.from(el.classList)` (array of strings) ensures the return value is JSON-serializable and the test assertion receives the expected type rather than a silently-mistyped `{}`.

**[community] Gotcha 7 — Cucumber.js `BeforeAll` hooks that throw an unhandled Promise rejection (rather than a thrown `Error`) in Cucumber.js versions before v12.3.0 cause the entire test run to hang indefinitely rather than terminating with an error — teams observe that a `BeforeAll` hook that calls `await server.listen()` where `listen()` rejects (because the port is in use) causes the Cucumber.js process to hang with no output, never reaching any scenario**: In Cucumber.js versions before the named `BeforeAll`/`AfterAll` hooks introduced in v12.3.0, unhandled promise rejections inside `BeforeAll` callbacks were not caught by the Cucumber.js hook execution framework because the framework used a `then(resolve, reject)` chaining pattern that expected the hook to either return a resolved promise or call a `done` callback — a rejected promise that escaped the try/catch boundary was handled by Node.js's unhandled rejection mechanism rather than by Cucumber.js's own error handler, causing the test run to emit an `UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning` but not to abort the Cucumber.js process. WHY upgrading to Cucumber.js v12.3.0 or later is the correct fix for hanging `BeforeAll` hooks: v12.3.0 wraps the entire hook execution lifecycle in a top-level `try/catch` around `await hookFn()`, so both thrown errors and rejected promises from `BeforeAll` callbacks are caught, recorded as suite-level failures, and cause Cucumber.js to exit with a non-zero code rather than hanging.

**[community] Gotcha 8 — playwright-bdd `createBdd()` called without passing the extended `test` object (i.e., `createBdd()` with no arguments) binds step definitions to Playwright's base `test` object instead of the project's custom `test` — all custom fixtures defined in infrastructure fixture files are silently unavailable in step definitions, and accessing `{ myCustomFixture }` in a step definition receives `undefined` without a TypeScript error because the inferred type falls back to `{}` when the generic type parameter is not provided**: The `createBdd()` function from `playwright-bdd` is generic — when called as `createBdd(test)` it infers the fixture types from the passed `test` object and provides type-safe `Given`, `When`, `Then` functions that include custom fixtures in their destructuring type. When called as `createBdd()` without an argument, it returns `Given`, `When`, `Then` bound to Playwright's base `test` object, which has no custom fixtures — TypeScript does not error on `async ({ myCustomFixture }) => {}` because the parameter type is inferred as `{}` and extra destructuring keys on an empty-typed parameter are permitted by TypeScript's structural typing rules. WHY every `createBdd()` call must explicitly pass the project's extended `test` object: passing `test` explicitly forces TypeScript to infer the full fixture type from the project's `test.extend()` chain, so accessing a fixture that does not exist produces a compile-time `Property 'myCustomFixture' does not exist on type 'PlaywrightTestArgs & PlaywrightWorkerArgs & ...'` error rather than a runtime `undefined` value.

**[community] Gotcha 9 — Cucumber.js `defineParameterType` transformers that throw `Error` for invalid input cause the entire step definition to fail with an unhelpful "Transform failed" error message that does not include the original step text or the invalid parameter value — teams debugging a failing step that uses a custom parameter type cannot tell from the error message which step caused the failure or what the invalid input was**: When a `defineParameterType` transformer throws, Cucumber.js wraps the error in a `"Transform failed"` error that contains only the transformer name and the thrown message — the original step text (e.g., `Given I pay $abc`) and the captured group value (`"$abc"`) are not included in the error output, making it difficult to locate the offending scenario in a large suite run. WHY `defineParameterType` transformers should include the captured input string in the thrown error message (e.g., `throw new Error(\`Cannot parse Money from "${raw}" — expected format: $<number>\`)` rather than `throw new Error("Invalid money format")`): since Cucumber.js's "Transform failed" wrapper drops the original step context, the only way to surface the invalid input value to the developer is to include it in the transformer's own error message, which is preserved as-is inside the wrapper error.

**[community] Gotcha 10 — Playwright worker-scoped fixtures that depend on test-scoped fixtures (e.g., a `{ scope: 'worker' }` fixture that declares `{ page }` as a dependency) silently degrade to test-scoped behaviour in Playwright v1.40 and later — the `{ scope: 'worker' }` annotation is ignored when any dependency is test-scoped, and the fixture is recreated for every test without a warning**: Playwright's fixture engine enforces the rule that a worker-scoped fixture cannot depend on a test-scoped fixture because the worker-scoped fixture's lifecycle exceeds the test-scoped dependency's lifecycle — rather than throwing a configuration error, Playwright v1.40+ silently demotes the worker-scoped fixture to test-scoped when it detects a test-scoped dependency in the fixture chain. Teams observe this as unexpected per-test browser launches (defeating the purpose of the worker-scoped pattern) with no error or warning in the Playwright output. WHY a `console.warn` guard in worker-scoped fixture bodies (logging `"WARNING: this fixture ran more than once per worker — check for test-scoped dependencies"` and tracking a call counter via a worker-local variable) is the practical detection mechanism: Playwright does not expose a fixture-demotion warning through any public API, so the only way to detect silent demotion is to observe that the fixture body is called more than once per worker process and alert the developer.
