## Cycle 64 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 316** — `Rule` Keyword for Grouping Business-Rule Scenarios Within a Single Feature File
```typescript
// features/checkout.feature
// Feature: Checkout
//   Rule: Free shipping applies for orders above $50
//     Background:
//       Given the cart threshold for free shipping is "$50.00"
//     Scenario: Order below threshold shows shipping cost
//       Given the cart total is "$35.00"
//       When the user proceeds to checkout
//       Then the shipping cost shown is "$5.99"
//     Scenario: Order above threshold shows free shipping
//       Given the cart total is "$65.00"
//       When the user proceeds to checkout
//       Then the shipping cost shown is "$0.00"

// step-definitions/checkout.steps.ts
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

Given('the cart threshold for free shipping is {string}', async function (
  this: AppWorld,
  threshold: string
) {
  await this.apiContext.post('/api/test/config', {
    data: { freeShippingThreshold: parseFloat(threshold.replace('$', '')) },
  });
});

Given('the cart total is {string}', async function (this: AppWorld, total: string) {
  await this.apiContext.post('/api/test/cart', {
    data: { total: parseFloat(total.replace('$', '')) },
  });
  await this.page.goto('/checkout');
});

Then('the shipping cost shown is {string}', async function (this: AppWorld, cost: string) {
  await expect(this.page.getByTestId('shipping-cost')).toHaveText(cost);
});
```
Tradeoff: The `Rule` keyword (Gherkin 6+) allows a single feature file to contain multiple Background sections scoped per rule, eliminating the need to split logically related scenarios into separate feature files solely to vary background state — but Cucumber.js requires all runners to support Gherkin 6 (cucumber-js >= 7.0); older CI images pinned to cucumber-js 6 will silently parse `Rule` as a `Feature` keyword, merging all rule-scoped backgrounds into a single flat list and executing every Background step before every scenario regardless of rule grouping, producing spurious step executions without a parse error.

**Pattern 317** — `page.route` with `fulfill` for Offline-Mode Scenario Testing Without a Real Backend
```typescript
// features/offline-mode.feature
// Scenario: User sees cached content when network is unavailable
//   Given the app has previously loaded the product catalogue
//   And the network connection is simulated as offline
//   When the user navigates to "/products"
//   Then the page displays "Showing cached results" banner
//   And 3 product cards are visible from the cache

// step-definitions/offline.steps.ts
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

Given('the app has previously loaded the product catalogue', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  // Perform a real load to populate service worker cache
  await this.page.goto('/products');
  await this.page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="product-card"]');
  this.cachedProductCount = await this.page.getByTestId('product-card').count();
});

Given('the network connection is simulated as offline', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.page.route('**/*', (route) => {
    if (route.request().resourceType() === 'fetch' || route.request().resourceType() === 'xhr') {
      route.abort('failed');
    } else {
      route.continue();
    }
  });
  this.offlineModeActive = true;
});

Then('{int} product cards are visible from the cache', async function (
  this: AppWorld,
  count: number
) {
  await expect(this.page.getByTestId('product-card')).toHaveCount(count);
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `page.route` with selective `abort('failed')` for `fetch`/`xhr` resource types accurately simulates network failure at the fetch layer without triggering Playwright's `context.setOffline(true)` which blocks all network activity including static asset loads (CSS, images) and causes the page renderer to enter an error state unrelated to the application's offline handling logic — but aborting only fetch/XHR requests while allowing static assets to continue loading means the offline simulation does not replicate the full user experience of a genuine network outage, so scenarios that verify the app's graceful degradation of icon rendering or font fallback under complete offline conditions cannot use this pattern and must instead call `context.setOffline(true)` after the initial page load completes.

**Pattern 318** — Typed World Class with Strict `never` Discriminated Union for Multi-Role Session State
```typescript
// support/world.ts
import { World, setWorldConstructor, IWorldOptions } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { Browser, BrowserContext, Page, APIRequestContext, chromium } from '@playwright/test';

type AuthRole = 'guest' | 'customer' | 'admin' | 'support-agent';

interface SessionState {
  role: AuthRole;
  userId: string | null;
  authToken: string | null;
}

export class AppWorld extends World {
  browser!: Browser;
  context!: BrowserContext;
  page!: Page;
  apiContext!: APIRequestContext;
  session: SessionState = { role: 'guest', userId: null, authToken: null };

  constructor(options: IWorldOptions) {
    super(options);
  }

  async switchRole(role: AuthRole, credentials?: { email: string; password: string }): Promise<void> {
    await this.context.clearCookies();
    await this.apiContext.dispose();
    if (role === 'guest') {
      this.session = { role: 'guest', userId: null, authToken: null };
      return;
    }
    if (!credentials) throw new Error(`switchRole('${role}') requires credentials`);
    const res = await this.apiContext.post('/api/auth/login', { data: credentials });
    const { token, userId } = await res.json();
    this.session = { role, userId, authToken: token };
    await this.context.addCookies([{ name: 'auth-token', value: token, url: process.env.BASE_URL! }]);
  }
}

setWorldConstructor(AppWorld);
```
Tradeoff: Encoding `role` as an `AuthRole` discriminated union on the `SessionState` interface and calling `switchRole` within steps ensures that every scenario's active authentication context is explicitly tracked on the World instance, enabling `Before` hooks to validate that scenarios tagged `@requires-admin` fail fast if the world's role is not `admin` before any step executes — but storing `authToken` on the World instance means that if a step definition accidentally reads `this.session.authToken` in a `BeforeAll` hook (which runs before the per-scenario `Before` hook that calls `switchRole`), the token is `null` and API calls silently return `401`, which is a different failure mode than the intentional `'guest'` state, creating confusion between "unauthenticated by design" and "authentication not yet initialized".

**Pattern 319** — `Scenario Outline` with Tagged `Examples` Tables for Environment-Specific Data Variants
```typescript
// features/pricing.feature
// Scenario Outline: Product price matches regional pricing configuration
//   Given I am browsing from the "<region>" regional storefront
//   When I view the product with SKU "<sku>"
//   Then the displayed price is "<expected_price>"
//
//   @staging
//   Examples: Staging prices
//     | region | sku      | expected_price |
//     | US     | WHP-001  | $89.99         |
//     | EU     | WHP-001  | €82.50         |
//
//   @production
//   Examples: Production prices
//     | region | sku      | expected_price |
//     | US     | WHP-001  | $94.99         |
//     | EU     | WHP-001  | €87.00         |

// cucumber.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

export default defineConfig({
  paths: ['features/**/*.feature'],
  import: ['step-definitions/**/*.ts', 'support/**/*.ts'],
  tags: process.env.TEST_ENV === 'production' ? '@production' : '@staging',
  format: ['html:reports/cucumber.html', 'json:reports/cucumber.json'],
  worldParameters: {
    baseUrl: process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
    region: process.env.REGION ?? 'US',
  },
});
```
Tradeoff: Placing environment-specific example rows in separately tagged `Examples` blocks within a single `Scenario Outline` allows one feature file to serve as both staging and production test specifications, with `--tags @staging` or `--tags @production` selecting the appropriate dataset at runtime — but Cucumber.js generates a unique scenario ID from the `Scenario Outline` title and row index, not the `Examples` block tag; if a CI reporting tool stores results by scenario ID, running `@staging` examples first and then `@production` examples in separate pipeline stages will produce duplicate scenario IDs in the aggregated report, causing the production run results to overwrite staging run results in tools like Allure or ReportPortal that use scenario ID as the deduplication key.

**Pattern 320** — `page.waitForResponse` Predicate With JSON Body Inspection for Asserting API Side Effects in Steps
```typescript
// step-definitions/order.steps.ts
import { When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

When('the user confirms the order', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  const [response] = await Promise.all([
    this.page.waitForResponse(
      (res) =>
        res.url().includes('/api/orders') &&
        res.request().method() === 'POST' &&
        res.status() === 201
    ),
    this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Confirm Order' }).click(),
  ]);
  const body = await response.json();
  this.lastOrderId = body.orderId;
  this.lastOrderTotal = body.total;
});

Then('an order confirmation email is dispatched', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  // Poll the test email sink API seeded in BeforeAll
  const emailRes = await this.apiContext.get(
    `/api/test/emails?recipient=${this.session.userId}&subject=Order+Confirmation`
  );
  const emails = await emailRes.json();
  const confirmationEmail = emails.find((e: { orderId: string }) =>
    e.orderId === this.lastOrderId
  );
  expect(confirmationEmail).toBeDefined();
  expect(confirmationEmail.total).toBe(this.lastOrderTotal);
});
```
Tradeoff: Capturing the POST response body inside the `When` step and storing `orderId` and `total` on the World instance eliminates the need for a separate `Then` step that re-queries the API for the created order — the response is already parsed and the data is available synchronously for subsequent `Then` assertions — but intercepting responses with a `waitForResponse` predicate that checks `res.status() === 201` means the step silently hangs indefinitely if the server responds with `200` instead of `201` (a common inconsistency in REST API implementations), causing a timeout failure rather than an assertion failure; the predicate should be split into `res.url().includes('/api/orders') && res.request().method() === 'POST'` with a separate `expect(response.status()).toBe(201)` assertion after the `Promise.all` resolves to produce a clear failure message.

**Pattern 321** — `Before` Hook Tag Guard With Return `'pending'` for Conditionally Unsupported Scenarios
```typescript
// support/hooks.ts
import { Before, After, BeforeAll, AfterAll, Status } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { chromium, request } from '@playwright/test';
import type { AppWorld } from './world';

BeforeAll(async function () {
  // Intentionally empty — browser launched per-scenario for isolation
});

Before({ tags: '@requires-feature-flag-new-checkout' }, async function (this: AppWorld) {
  const flagRes = await this.apiContext.get('/api/feature-flags/new-checkout');
  const { enabled } = await flagRes.json();
  if (!enabled) {
    // Pending status marks scenario as skipped without failure
    return 'pending';
  }
});

Before({ tags: '@requires-admin' }, async function (this: AppWorld) {
  if (this.session.role !== 'admin') {
    throw new Error(
      `Scenario tagged @requires-admin but World role is '${this.session.role}'. ` +
      `Call 'the user is logged in as an admin' step before this scenario.`
    );
  }
});

After(async function (this: AppWorld, scenario) {
  if (scenario.result?.status === Status.FAILED) {
    const screenshot = await this.page.screenshot({ fullPage: true });
    await this.attach(screenshot, 'image/png');
    const html = await this.page.content();
    await this.attach(html, 'text/html');
  }
  await this.page.close();
  await this.context.close();
});
```
Tradeoff: Returning `'pending'` from a `Before` hook when a required feature flag is disabled marks the scenario as `Pending` in the Cucumber report rather than `Failed`, accurately representing "this test is not applicable in this environment" — but Cucumber.js treats `Pending` scenarios as non-blocking in the default exit code calculation (exit code 0 even with pending scenarios unless `--fail-fast` is set), meaning a CI pipeline that checks `cucumber-js --exit` exit code for pass/fail will not catch a build where 100% of scenarios are skipped because all feature flags are disabled in the environment, appearing as a fully green run with zero actual test coverage.

**Pattern 322** — `DocString` with `content_type` Annotation for Asserting JSON API Response Bodies in Scenarios
```typescript
// features/api-contract.feature
// Scenario: Product detail API returns the expected contract shape
//   When the client sends a GET request to "/api/products/WHP-001"
//   Then the response body matches the contract:
//     """json
//     {
//       "sku": "WHP-001",
//       "name": "Wireless Headphones Pro",
//       "price": 89.99,
//       "inStock": true
//     }
//     """

// step-definitions/api-contract.steps.ts
import { When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

When('the client sends a GET request to {string}', async function (
  this: AppWorld,
  path: string
) {
  this.lastApiResponse = await this.apiContext.get(path);
  this.lastApiResponseBody = await this.lastApiResponse.json();
  this.lastApiResponseStatus = this.lastApiResponse.status();
});

Then('the response body matches the contract:', async function (
  this: AppWorld,
  docString: string
) {
  const expected = JSON.parse(docString);
  // Use toMatchObject for partial matching — extra fields do not fail the assertion
  expect(this.lastApiResponseBody).toMatchObject(expected);
  // Separately assert no unexpected top-level keys were added
  const unexpectedKeys = Object.keys(this.lastApiResponseBody).filter(
    (k) => !(k in expected)
  );
  if (unexpectedKeys.length > 0) {
    this.attach(
      `Warning: response contained unexpected keys: ${unexpectedKeys.join(', ')}`,
      'text/plain'
    );
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `toMatchObject` rather than deep strict equality for DocString-defined JSON contracts allows the API to add new optional fields without breaking existing scenarios, which aligns with Postel's Law ("be liberal in what you accept") and prevents test churn during API evolution — but lenient matching means a breaking change where a required field (e.g., `"inStock"`) is accidentally removed from the API response will produce a passing scenario as long as the expected contract fields are a subset of the actual response, which is the opposite of the contract testing goal; to prevent this, the DocString contract should represent the minimum required fields and a separate `@strict-contract` tagged scenario should use `expect(body).toStrictEqual(expected)` to catch extra-field pollution in the response.

**Pattern 323** — `setDefaultTimeout` With Per-Tag Override Hooks for Slow Scenarios Without Global Timeout Inflation
```typescript
// support/setup.ts
import { setDefaultTimeout, Before } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from './world';

// Default timeout: 15 seconds for all scenarios
setDefaultTimeout(15_000);

// Override for scenarios tagged @slow — extends to 60 seconds
Before({ tags: '@slow' }, async function (this: AppWorld) {
  // Cucumber.js does not expose a per-scenario setDefaultTimeout,
  // but we can store the intended timeout on the World instance
  // and pass it explicitly to long-running Playwright calls.
  this.stepTimeout = 60_000;
});

Before({ tags: '@smoke' }, async function (this: AppWorld) {
  // Smoke scenarios must complete faster — stricter 8-second budget
  this.stepTimeout = 8_000;
});

// Usage in a step definition that respects the World-level timeout
// step-definitions/export.steps.ts
import { When } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

When('the user exports the full transaction history as CSV', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  const timeout = this.stepTimeout ?? 15_000;
  await this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export CSV' }).click();
  await this.page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="export-complete-banner"]', { timeout });
});
```
Tradeoff: Storing a World-instance `stepTimeout` and passing it explicitly to each Playwright assertion that needs it provides per-scenario timeout budgets without calling `setDefaultTimeout` mid-run (which mutates global state and affects all concurrently running parallel workers) — but the pattern requires every step definition author to remember to pass `{ timeout: this.stepTimeout }` to Playwright calls, and any step that omits the option falls back to the 15-second global default, meaning slow steps in `@slow` scenarios silently use the wrong timeout without any linting or runtime warning; a custom ESLint rule that flags Playwright `waitForSelector`/`waitForResponse` calls inside step definitions that do not pass a `timeout` option would enforce the pattern consistently.

**Pattern 324** — `Background` Steps With Idempotent Database Seed API for Parallel-Safe Scenario Isolation
```typescript
// features/inventory.feature
// Background:
//   Given the inventory database contains a clean test dataset

// step-definitions/inventory.steps.ts
import { Given } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

Given('the inventory database contains a clean test dataset', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  // Each scenario gets a unique namespace to avoid cross-scenario pollution
  this.testNamespace = `test-${this.testCaseStartedId.replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 12)}`;

  await this.apiContext.post('/api/test/seed', {
    data: {
      namespace: this.testNamespace,
      dataset: 'inventory-standard',
      items: [
        { sku: `${this.testNamespace}-WHP`, name: 'Wireless Headphones', stock: 50 },
        { sku: `${this.testNamespace}-WEL`, name: 'Wireless Earbuds', stock: 30 },
      ],
    },
  });

  // Store namespace so subsequent steps can scope their API calls
  await this.apiContext.post('/api/test/set-namespace', {
    data: { namespace: this.testNamespace },
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Prefixing every seeded record's SKU with a scenario-unique `testNamespace` derived from `this.testCaseStartedId` makes background seed steps idempotent and parallel-safe — multiple scenarios executing concurrently in separate Cucumber.js workers each create namespace-isolated records and cannot mutate each other's data — but the namespace prefix changes the SKU value seen by the application's UI and API responses, so step definitions that assert on exact SKU values (e.g., `Then the SKU shown is "WHP-001"`) must be updated to use `this.testNamespace` interpolation, making feature files harder to read and preventing business stakeholders from reviewing exact SKU values in the Gherkin specification.

**Pattern 325** — `page.locator` with `filter({ has })` Composition for Table-Row Targeted Assertions
```typescript
// features/admin-users.feature
// Scenario: Admin can deactivate an active user account
//   Given the user table contains a row for "jane.doe@example.com" with status "Active"
//   When the admin clicks "Deactivate" in the row for "jane.doe@example.com"
//   Then the row for "jane.doe@example.com" shows status "Deactivated"

// step-definitions/admin-users.steps.ts
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

function getUserRow(page: AppWorld['page'], email: string) {
  return page.getByRole('row').filter({ has: page.getByText(email, { exact: true }) });
}

Given(
  'the user table contains a row for {string} with status {string}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, email: string, status: string) {
    const row = getUserRow(this.page, email);
    await expect(row).toBeVisible();
    await expect(row.getByTestId('user-status')).toHaveText(status);
  }
);

When(
  'the admin clicks {string} in the row for {string}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, actionLabel: string, email: string) {
    const row = getUserRow(this.page, email);
    await row.getByRole('button', { name: actionLabel }).click();
    await this.page.waitForResponse(
      (res) => res.url().includes('/api/users') && res.request().method() === 'PATCH'
    );
  }
);

Then(
  'the row for {string} shows status {string}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, email: string, status: string) {
    const row = getUserRow(this.page, email);
    await expect(row.getByTestId('user-status')).toHaveText(status);
  }
);
```
Tradeoff: Encapsulating the row-filtering logic in a `getUserRow` helper that composes `getByRole('row').filter({ has: getByText(email) })` allows all three Given/When/Then steps to share a single locator strategy, ensuring that a change to the row selector requires updating only the helper — but `getByRole('row').filter({ has: ... })` evaluates lazily at assertion time; if the table re-renders between the `When` click and the `Then` assertion and the email cell briefly disappears during an optimistic update animation, the `filter({ has: ... })` may return an empty locator and the assertion will time out waiting for the row to re-appear rather than failing with a clear "row not found" error.

**Pattern 326** — Reusable `Given` Composite Step Delegation to World Methods for DRY Setup Chains
```typescript
// step-definitions/common-setup.steps.ts
import { Given } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

// Atomic building-block steps
Given('the user is on the homepage', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.page.goto('/');
  await this.page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
});

Given('the user is logged in as a customer', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.switchRole('customer', {
    email: process.env.TEST_CUSTOMER_EMAIL!,
    password: process.env.TEST_CUSTOMER_PASSWORD!,
  });
  await this.page.goto('/dashboard');
});

// Composite step — delegates to World method to avoid re-implementing logic
Given('the customer is on their dashboard', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.switchRole('customer', {
    email: process.env.TEST_CUSTOMER_EMAIL!,
    password: process.env.TEST_CUSTOMER_PASSWORD!,
  });
  await this.page.goto('/dashboard');
  await this.page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
  await this.page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="dashboard-heading"]');
});

// Variant for different contexts — reuses the same World method
Given('the admin is on the user management page', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.switchRole('admin', {
    email: process.env.TEST_ADMIN_EMAIL!,
    password: process.env.TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD!,
  });
  await this.page.goto('/admin/users');
  await this.page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="user-table"]');
});
```
Tradeoff: Delegating composite `Given` steps to `World` methods (e.g., `this.switchRole`) rather than having one step invoke another step programmatically keeps setup logic in a single authoritative location (the World class) and avoids Cucumber.js's restriction that step definitions cannot directly call other step definitions — but this means the composite step is not visible in the Cucumber report as a sequence of sub-steps; if `this.switchRole` fails, the error is attributed to the composite step line rather than the specific sub-operation that failed, requiring developers to read stack traces rather than relying on the step-by-step failure report to identify the root cause.

**Pattern 327** — `cucumber-json` Report With Custom Metadata Attachment for Linking Scenario Results to JIRA Issues
```typescript
// support/metadata-reporter.ts
import { After, ITestCaseHookParameter } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from './world';

// Extract JIRA issue tags from scenario pickle tags (e.g., @JIRA-1234)
function extractJiraKeys(tags: readonly { name: string }[]): string[] {
  return tags
    .map((t) => t.name.replace('@', ''))
    .filter((t) => /^[A-Z]+-\d+$/.test(t));
}

After({ order: 1 }, async function (this: AppWorld, scenario: ITestCaseHookParameter) {
  const jiraKeys = extractJiraKeys(scenario.pickle.tags);
  if (jiraKeys.length === 0) return;

  const status = scenario.result?.status ?? 'UNKNOWN';
  const duration = scenario.result?.duration?.nanos
    ? Math.round(scenario.result.duration.nanos / 1_000_000)
    : 0;

  // Attach JIRA metadata as structured JSON for downstream report processors
  await this.attach(
    JSON.stringify({
      jiraKeys,
      status,
      duration,
      scenarioName: scenario.pickle.name,
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    }),
    'application/json'
  );

  // Optionally call JIRA transition API in non-CI environments
  if (process.env.UPDATE_JIRA === 'true') {
    for (const key of jiraKeys) {
      await this.apiContext.post(`/api/jira/update-test-result`, {
        data: { issueKey: key, status, duration },
      });
    }
  }
});

// Teardown hook runs after the metadata hook due to higher order value
After({ order: 2 }, async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.page.close();
  await this.context.close();
  await this.apiContext.dispose();
});
```
Tradeoff: Registering the JIRA metadata `After` hook with `{ order: 1 }` and the browser teardown hook with `{ order: 2 }` guarantees that `this.apiContext` is still alive when the JIRA update call fires — but `After` hook `order` values in Cucumber.js run in ascending order (lower numbers execute first), which is the opposite of `Before` hook ordering (higher numbers execute first), creating a counterintuitive asymmetry; teams that apply the same `order` convention from `Before` hooks to `After` hooks will accidentally dispose the browser before the metadata hook fires, reintroducing the `APIRequestContext was disposed` error that the ordering was meant to prevent.

**Pattern 328** — `page.evaluate` for Reading Application State From the JavaScript Execution Context in Step Definitions
```typescript
// features/cart.feature
// Scenario: Cart state persists after browser refresh
//   Given the user adds "Wireless Headphones Pro" to the cart
//   When the user refreshes the page
//   Then the cart store contains 1 item with SKU "WHP-001"

// step-definitions/cart.steps.ts
import { Given, When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

When('the user refreshes the page', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.page.reload({ waitUntil: 'networkidle' });
});

Then(
  'the cart store contains {int} item with SKU {string}',
  async function (this: AppWorld, count: number, sku: string) {
    // Read application's Redux/Zustand/localStorage state directly
    const cartItems = await this.page.evaluate<Array<{ sku: string; qty: number }>>(() => {
      const raw = window.localStorage.getItem('cart');
      if (!raw) return [];
      const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as { items: Array<{ sku: string; qty: number }> };
      return parsed.items;
    });

    expect(cartItems).toHaveLength(count);
    const targetItem = cartItems.find((item) => item.sku === sku);
    expect(targetItem).toBeDefined();
    expect(targetItem!.qty).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  }
);
```
Tradeoff: Using `page.evaluate` to read `localStorage` or a global app state object provides a fast, non-UI assertion path that bypasses the risk of asserting on stale DOM text (cart badge showing an outdated count due to React's batched re-render) — but `page.evaluate` creates tight coupling between step definitions and the application's internal state management implementation; if the app migrates from `localStorage`-based cart persistence to an IndexedDB-based service worker cache, the `page.evaluate` call silently returns an empty array and the step fails with a misleading "expected 1 item, received 0" message rather than a clear "localStorage key 'cart' not found", making the step definition a hidden implementation-detail dependency that breaks without any TypeScript compiler warning.

**Pattern 329** — `AfterAll` Hook With Per-Worker Coverage JSON Export for Istanbul Report Aggregation Across Parallel Workers
```typescript
// support/coverage-hooks.ts
import { AfterAll, BeforeAll, After } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';
import type { AppWorld } from './world';

const COVERAGE_DIR = path.resolve(process.cwd(), '.nyc_output');
// Module-level accumulator: populated by After hooks, written by AfterAll
let workerCoverageAccumulator: Record<string, unknown> = {};

BeforeAll(async function () {
  const workerId = process.env.CUCUMBER_WORKER_ID ?? 'main';
  const workerDir = path.join(COVERAGE_DIR, `worker-${workerId}`);
  fs.mkdirSync(workerDir, { recursive: true });
  process.env.WORKER_COVERAGE_DIR = workerDir;
});

// Collect coverage after each scenario while page is still open
After(async function (this: AppWorld) {
  if (process.env.COLLECT_COVERAGE !== 'true') return;
  const scenarioCoverage = await this.page.evaluate<Record<string, unknown>>(
    () => (window as unknown as { __coverage__: Record<string, unknown> }).__coverage__ ?? {}
  );
  // Merge scenario coverage into worker accumulator
  Object.assign(workerCoverageAccumulator, scenarioCoverage);
});

AfterAll(async function () {
  if (process.env.COLLECT_COVERAGE !== 'true') return;
  const workerId = process.env.CUCUMBER_WORKER_ID ?? 'main';
  const coverageFile = path.join(
    process.env.WORKER_COVERAGE_DIR!,
    `coverage-${workerId}-${Date.now()}.json`
  );
  fs.writeFileSync(coverageFile, JSON.stringify(workerCoverageAccumulator));
});
```
Tradeoff: Collecting `window.__coverage__` in an `After` hook after each scenario (while the page is still open) and merging into a module-level accumulator that `AfterAll` writes to disk avoids the race condition of reading `window.__coverage__` after the page is closed — but the module-level `workerCoverageAccumulator` variable is shared across all scenarios within a single worker thread; if two scenarios run in sequence and the second scenario's application load resets `window.__coverage__` to an empty object (which happens in apps that use Webpack's coverage instrumentation with `cleanCoverage` option), the `After` hook for the second scenario will overwrite the accumulator with an empty object via `Object.assign`, erasing all coverage data collected from the first scenario — requiring Istanbul's `mergeOptions` to be used instead of a plain `Object.assign` to correctly union hit counts rather than replace them.

**Pattern 330** — `defineParameterType` With Enum-Validated Transformer for Domain-Specific Vocabulary in Gherkin Steps
```typescript
// support/parameter-types.ts
import { defineParameterType } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

type OrderStatus = 'Pending' | 'Processing' | 'Shipped' | 'Delivered' | 'Cancelled';
type PaymentMethod = 'credit card' | 'debit card' | 'PayPal' | 'Apple Pay' | 'bank transfer';

defineParameterType({
  name: 'orderStatus',
  regexp: /Pending|Processing|Shipped|Delivered|Cancelled/,
  transformer(raw: string): OrderStatus {
    const valid: OrderStatus[] = ['Pending', 'Processing', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
    if (!valid.includes(raw as OrderStatus)) {
      throw new Error(`Invalid order status: "${raw}". Valid values: ${valid.join(', ')}`);
    }
    return raw as OrderStatus;
  },
});

defineParameterType({
  name: 'paymentMethod',
  regexp: /credit card|debit card|PayPal|Apple Pay|bank transfer/,
  transformer(raw: string): PaymentMethod {
    return raw as PaymentMethod;
  },
});

// Usage in step definitions — parameters are typed, not raw strings
import { Then, When } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

When('the user pays with {paymentMethod}', async function (
  this: AppWorld,
  method: PaymentMethod
) {
  await this.page.getByRole('radio', { name: method }).check();
  await this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay Now' }).click();
});

Then('the order status changes to {orderStatus}', async function (
  this: AppWorld,
  status: OrderStatus
) {
  await expect(this.page.getByTestId('order-status-badge')).toHaveText(status);
});
```
Tradeoff: Defining `{orderStatus}` and `{paymentMethod}` as custom parameter types with TypeScript union return values brings the Gherkin vocabulary into the TypeScript type system — step definition parameters are typed as `OrderStatus` and `PaymentMethod` rather than `string`, catching typos in Gherkin feature files at parse time because Cucumber.js throws a `No step definition matches` error when the regex does not match the feature file text — but the regex in `defineParameterType` must be manually kept in sync with the TypeScript union type; if a new `'Gift Card'` value is added to the `PaymentMethod` union without updating the regex, the TypeScript compiler accepts the new value in step logic but the Cucumber.js parser rejects any feature file using `pays with gift card` at runtime, creating a silent gap between what the type system allows and what the Gherkin parser accepts.

### Community Gotchas

**G86** — `cucumber.config.ts` `require` vs `import` Array — Mixing CommonJS and ESM Module Resolution Causes `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement`
Why this matters: Cucumber.js 9+ uses the `import` array in `cucumber.config.ts` for ESM projects, but many tutorials and StackOverflow answers written for Cucumber.js 7/8 use the `require` array. When a project has `"type": "module"` in `package.json` and uses `ts-node/esm` as the loader, step definition files loaded via the `require` array are processed by CommonJS `require()`, which cannot handle top-level `import` statements. The resulting error `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement in a module` appears to point at the step definition file but is actually caused by the wrong array key in `cucumber.config.ts`. The error is especially confusing because the same step definition file loads without error when imported directly by other TypeScript files, making developers suspect a Cucumber.js parsing bug rather than a configuration key mismatch.
Fix: For ESM projects (`"type": "module"` in `package.json`) always use the `import` array in `cucumber.config.ts`. For CommonJS projects (no `"type": "module"` or `"type": "commonjs"`), use the `require` array. Add a validation script to the project's `npm run check` target that reads `cucumber.config.ts` and throws if an ESM project uses `require[]` instead of `import[]`, catching configuration drift before it breaks CI.

**G87** — `scenario.pickle.tags` Contains Inherited Tags From Parent `Feature` and `Rule` Blocks — Hook Tag Filters Match Unexpectedly
Why this matters: In Cucumber.js, `scenario.pickle.tags` is a flattened array that includes not only the tags directly on the `Scenario` keyword but also all inherited tags from the enclosing `Feature`, `Rule`, and `Scenario Outline` keywords. A `Before({ tags: '@slow' })` hook intended to extend the timeout only for scenarios explicitly tagged `@slow` will also fire for every scenario in a `Feature` or `Rule` block tagged `@slow` at the block level — including scenarios that complete in under 1 second. The cumulative effect is that the `stepTimeout` override is applied globally to all scenarios in the feature, inflating overall test suite runtime. The gotcha is invisible unless developers inspect `scenario.pickle.tags` at runtime, because the Gherkin feature file visually separates block-level and scenario-level tags by indentation, implying they have different inheritance behaviour.
Fix: When a `Before` hook must distinguish between a scenario explicitly tagged `@slow` versus one that inherited the tag from a parent block, inspect `scenario.pickle.astNodeIds` to find the corresponding AST node and check whether the tag is directly on the `Scenario` node or on a parent `Feature`/`Rule` node. Alternatively, establish the project convention that execution-scope tags (`@slow`, `@smoke`, `@staging`) are only applied at the `Scenario` level and add a pre-commit lint check that rejects these tags appearing on `Feature:` or `Rule:` lines.

**G88** — Cucumber.js `--retry` Flag Re-Runs the Entire Scenario — Non-Idempotent `Before` Hook Side Effects Cause Hook-Level Failures on Retry
Why this matters: When `cucumber-js --retry 2` re-runs a failed scenario, it executes the full scenario lifecycle from scratch including all `Before` hooks. If a `Before` hook creates a user account via the API (`POST /api/users`) and does not check for idempotency, the retry run attempts to create the same user again and receives a `409 Conflict` response, causing the `Before` hook itself to throw. The scenario now fails in the `Before` hook on the retry run rather than in the original failing step, making the retry feature worse than not retrying — the original failure message is replaced with a `Before hook failed: 409 Conflict` error, obscuring the actual root cause. This is especially problematic for data-mutation `Before` hooks in test environments that do not automatically clean up between test attempts.
Fix: Make all `Before` hook API calls idempotent by using upsert semantics: replace `POST /api/users` with `PUT /api/users/:id` using a deterministic ID derived from the scenario name hash, or implement `POST /api/users` with a `?idempotency-key` query parameter tied to `scenario.pickle.id`. Add a project rule that `Before` hooks must never assume a pristine state — always use check-then-create or upsert endpoints. Pair `--retry` with a corresponding `After` hook that performs compensating cleanup with `try/catch` so cleanup never throws even if the resource never existed.

**G89** — `DataTable.hashes()` Column Header Whitespace From Table Auto-Formatting Is Silently Preserved — Key Lookups Return `undefined`
Why this matters: Gherkin `DataTable` column headers are parsed exactly as typed in the feature file. A feature file authored in a Markdown-rendered editor that auto-formats tables by padding cells to equal widths may introduce trailing spaces into column headers: `| email              | password  |` yields a key of `"email              "` (with trailing spaces) rather than `"email"`. When `DataTable.hashes()` converts the table, the resulting object keys contain the trailing spaces. Step definition code that reads `row['email']` returns `undefined`, causing downstream assertions to fail with `TypeError: Cannot read property 'length' of undefined` rather than a clear "column not found" error. The feature file looks visually correct in any editor that renders fixed-width table formatting.
Fix: Add a utility function `normaliseTableHeaders(table: DataTable): Record<string, string>[]` that trims all keys and values returned by `DataTable.hashes()`: `return table.hashes().map(row => Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(row).map(([k, v]) => [k.trim(), v.trim()])))`. Use this function in all step definitions that consume `DataTable` arguments. Additionally, add `.editorconfig` with `trim_trailing_whitespace = true` and configure Prettier with `proseWrap: always` for `.feature` files to prevent the formatting drift from being introduced.

**G90** — Scenario-Level `@tag` on a `Scenario Outline` Block Applies to All Generated Examples — Cannot Target a Single Row
Why this matters: In Cucumber.js, a tag placed on a `Scenario Outline` block (not on a specific `Examples` table) is applied to every scenario instance generated from every `Examples` row. A developer who wants to mark only the first row as `@smoke` must place the `@smoke` tag on the specific `Examples` block that contains that row — not on the `Scenario Outline` itself. If `@smoke` is placed on the outline, running `cucumber-js --tags @smoke` executes every row in every `Examples` table under that outline, including data rows intended for `@regression` suites only. The CI smoke suite that should run in 2 minutes runs for 15 minutes because all regression examples are included. Cucumber.js does not warn that the tag is on the outline rather than on an examples block, and the Gherkin syntax is valid in both positions.
Fix: Establish the project convention that `@smoke`, `@regression`, `@slow`, and environment-targeting tags (`@staging`, `@production`) are always placed on `Examples` blocks rather than on `Scenario Outline` blocks. Enforce this with a pre-commit lint script that detects reserved execution-scope tags on `Scenario Outline:` lines and rejects the commit with a message directing the author to move the tag to the appropriate `Examples:` block.

## Cycle 65 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 331** — `BeforeStep` / `AfterStep` Hooks for Granular Per-Step Timing Telemetry Without Polluting Step Definition Bodies
```typescript
// support/step-timing-hooks.ts
import { BeforeStep, AfterStep } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from './world';

const stepTimings: Array<{ name: string; durationMs: number }> = [];

BeforeStep(async function (this: AppWorld, { pickleStep }) {
  this.stepStartTime = Date.now();
  this.currentStepText = pickleStep.text;
});

AfterStep(async function (this: AppWorld, { pickleStep, result }) {
  const durationMs = Date.now() - this.stepStartTime;
  stepTimings.push({ name: pickleStep.text, durationMs });
  if (durationMs > 3000) {
    console.warn(`[SLOW STEP] "${pickleStep.text}" took ${durationMs}ms (threshold: 3000ms)`);
  }
  if (result.status === 'FAILED') {
    await this.page.screenshot({
      path: `screenshots/step-fail-${Date.now()}.png`,
      fullPage: true,
    });
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Instrumenting `BeforeStep`/`AfterStep` hooks with per-step timing and on-failure screenshot capture keeps step definition bodies clean and enforces a consistent diagnostic baseline across all 300+ step definitions — but `BeforeStep`/`AfterStep` hooks cannot be filtered by tag expressions in Cucumber.js, so the screenshot-on-failure logic fires for every step in every scenario regardless of whether that scenario has a `@no-screenshots` exclusion tag, making it impossible to suppress screenshot capture for scenarios that run in a sandboxed environment where the screenshot directory path is read-only and the `page.screenshot` call throws `EACCES`, causing the `AfterStep` hook itself to fail and mask the original step failure status.

**Pattern 332** — Playwright `page.route` Request Interceptor Activated via World State Flag for Network-Level Fault Injection in Gherkin Scenarios
```typescript
// step-definitions/network-steps.ts
import { Given, Before, After } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

Before(async function (this: AppWorld) {
  this.activeNetworkFaults = new Map<string, { status: number; body: string }>();
});

Given('the API endpoint {string} will return error {int}', async function (
  this: AppWorld,
  urlPattern: string,
  statusCode: number
) {
  this.activeNetworkFaults.set(urlPattern, {
    status: statusCode,
    body: JSON.stringify({ error: `Injected ${statusCode}` }),
  });
  await this.page.route(`**/${urlPattern}`, (route) => {
    const fault = this.activeNetworkFaults.get(urlPattern);
    if (fault) {
      route.fulfill({ status: fault.status, body: fault.body, contentType: 'application/json' });
    } else {
      route.continue();
    }
  });
});

After(async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.page.unrouteAll({ behavior: 'ignoreErrors' });
  this.activeNetworkFaults.clear();
});
```
Tradeoff: Storing injected fault configurations in `this.activeNetworkFaults` on the World object and registering the `page.route` handler in the `Given` step itself (rather than in a `Before` hook) allows Gherkin authors to declaratively compose multiple fault injections in the arrange phase of a single scenario — but `page.route` handlers registered within step definitions are additive; if a scenario calls the same `Given` step twice with the same `urlPattern` (a valid Gherkin pattern using `And`), Playwright registers two route handlers for the same pattern and the second handler is never reached because Playwright's routing stops at the first matching handler, silently dropping the second fault injection without any warning.

**Pattern 333** — `Rule` Keyword With `Background` Sub-Section for Grouping Policy-Specific Setup Without Polluting the Feature-Level Background
```gherkin
# features/checkout.feature
Feature: Checkout flow

  Rule: Guest checkout is available without account creation
    Background:
      Given the shopping cart contains 2 items
      And the user is not logged in

    Scenario: Guest can complete checkout with a valid email
      When the user provides email "guest@example.com"
      And the user completes payment with a valid card
      Then the order confirmation page is shown
      And a receipt email is sent to "guest@example.com"

    Scenario: Guest checkout requires a valid email format
      When the user provides email "not-an-email"
      And the user attempts to proceed to payment
      Then an inline validation error "Please enter a valid email" is shown

  Rule: Registered users retain cart contents across sessions
    Background:
      Given the user is logged in as "returning@example.com"
      And the shopping cart contains 3 items

    Scenario: Cart persists after logout and re-login
      When the user logs out
      And the user logs back in as "returning@example.com"
      Then the shopping cart still contains 3 items
```
Tradeoff: Using `Rule`-level `Background` sections scopes repeated setup steps to only the scenarios within that business rule, preventing the Feature-level `Background` from growing unbounded as more rules are added and keeping each rule's preconditions co-located with the scenarios they govern — but Cucumber.js executes `Rule`-level `Background` steps after the `Feature`-level `Background` steps for every scenario under that `Rule`, meaning a scenario under `Rule: Guest checkout` always runs the Feature-level `Background` (if one exists) first even if that setup is irrelevant to guest flows, creating hidden coupling between Feature-level and Rule-level setup that makes individual `Rule` sections non-portable if extracted to a separate feature file.

**Pattern 334** — Typed `AppWorld` Extension With Lazy Playwright `BrowserContext` Initialization for Multi-Tab Scenario Support
```typescript
// support/world.ts
import { World, IWorldOptions, setWorldConstructor } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { Browser, BrowserContext, Page, chromium } from '@playwright/test';

export class AppWorld extends World {
  browser!: Browser;
  private _context?: BrowserContext;
  private _pages: Map<string, Page> = new Map();
  activePageKey: string = 'main';

  constructor(options: IWorldOptions) {
    super(options);
  }

  async openTab(key: string): Promise<Page> {
    if (!this._context) {
      this._context = await this.browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 } });
    }
    const page = await this._context.newPage();
    this._pages.set(key, page);
    this.activePageKey = key;
    return page;
  }

  get page(): Page {
    const p = this._pages.get(this.activePageKey);
    if (!p) throw new Error(`No page open for key "${this.activePageKey}". Call openTab() first.`);
    return p;
  }

  async switchTab(key: string): Promise<void> {
    if (!this._pages.has(key)) throw new Error(`Tab "${key}" does not exist.`);
    this.activePageKey = key;
  }

  async closeAllTabs(): Promise<void> {
    for (const page of this._pages.values()) await page.close().catch(() => {});
    this._pages.clear();
    if (this._context) { await this._context.close(); this._context = undefined; }
  }
}

setWorldConstructor(AppWorld);
```
Tradeoff: Exposing a keyed `openTab` / `switchTab` API on the World class enables Gherkin scenarios to model multi-tab workflows (e.g., "When the admin opens a second tab to the admin panel") without leaking `BrowserContext` management into step definitions — but the `page` getter throws synchronously if `activePageKey` references a tab that was closed mid-scenario; if a step definition calls `this.page` after a `closeAllTabs()` in an `After` hook from a different step file that loaded earlier due to glob ordering, the error surfaces as a World-level teardown failure rather than the underlying step failure, obscuring which step actually caused the tab to close prematurely.

**Pattern 335** — `cucumber.config.ts` `worldParameters` for Environment-Specific Base URL and Auth Token Injection Without `.env` File Coupling
```typescript
// cucumber.config.ts
import type { IConfiguration } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

const env = process.env.TEST_ENV ?? 'local';

const envConfig: Record<string, { baseUrl: string; authToken: string }> = {
  local:   { baseUrl: 'http://localhost:3000', authToken: process.env.LOCAL_AUTH_TOKEN ?? '' },
  staging: { baseUrl: 'https://staging.example.com', authToken: process.env.STAGING_AUTH_TOKEN ?? '' },
  prod:    { baseUrl: 'https://example.com',          authToken: process.env.PROD_AUTH_TOKEN ?? '' },
};

if (!envConfig[env]) {
  throw new Error(`Unknown TEST_ENV "${env}". Valid values: ${Object.keys(envConfig).join(', ')}`);
}

export default {
  import: ['src/step-definitions/**/*.ts', 'src/support/**/*.ts'],
  format: ['progress-bar', 'html:reports/cucumber-report.html'],
  worldParameters: envConfig[env],
  parallel: env === 'local' ? 1 : 4,
} satisfies Partial<IConfiguration>;
```
Tradeoff: Centralising environment-to-URL resolution in `cucumber.config.ts` and injecting via `worldParameters` makes the base URL available as `this.parameters.baseUrl` in every step definition without requiring `dotenv` or manual `process.env` reads scattered across step files — but `worldParameters` is serialised to JSON before being passed to Worker threads in parallel mode, meaning any non-JSON-serialisable value (such as a `URL` object or a `Buffer` containing a private key) silently becomes `null` in the worker's World constructor; teams that attempt to pass a pre-parsed `new URL(baseUrl)` object via `worldParameters` receive `null` in workers and discover the serialisation loss only at runtime when `this.parameters.baseUrl.href` throws `Cannot read property 'href' of null`.

**Pattern 336** — `DocString` With `content_type: application/json` for Asserting Full API Response Body Shape in Gherkin Without Inline JSON Escaping
```typescript
// step-definitions/api-steps.ts
import { Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { DocString } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

Then('the API response body matches', async function (
  this: AppWorld,
  docString: DocString
) {
  if (docString.mediaType !== 'application/json') {
    throw new Error(`Expected DocString mediaType "application/json", got "${docString.mediaType}"`);
  }
  const expected = JSON.parse(docString.content) as Record<string, unknown>;
  const actual = this.lastApiResponse;
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(expected)) {
    expect(actual).toHaveProperty(key);
    expect(actual[key]).toEqual(value);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Using a `content_type: application/json` DocString annotation allows Gherkin authors to embed multi-line, properly formatted JSON directly in the feature file and assert against it with a single `Then` step — keeping response shape expectations in the feature file where product owners can review them — but `DocString.content` is always a raw `string` regardless of the `mediaType` annotation; Cucumber.js does not parse the DocString body based on `mediaType`, so if the JSON in the feature file contains a trailing comma (invalid JSON but visually natural for non-developers editing `.feature` files), `JSON.parse` throws a `SyntaxError` at step execution time rather than at feature file load time, making CI fail with a cryptic parse error rather than a Gherkin lint warning.

**Pattern 337** — `Scenario Outline` With Multiple `Examples` Tables Tagged by Environment to Gate Data Sets Behind `--tags` Filters
```gherkin
Feature: Product search relevance

  Scenario Outline: Search returns relevant results for <query>
    Given the user is on the search page
    When the user searches for "<query>"
    Then the first result title contains "<expected_title>"

    @smoke @local @staging
    Examples: Core search terms
      | query        | expected_title        |
      | laptop       | Best Laptops 2026     |
      | headphones   | Wireless Headphones   |

    @regression @staging
    Examples: Long-tail queries
      | query                      | expected_title                      |
      | noise cancelling earbuds   | Noise Cancelling Earbuds Review     |
      | ultrabook under 1000       | Best Ultrabooks Under $1,000        |

    @regression @prod-readonly
    Examples: Production data validation
      | query        | expected_title        |
      | macbook pro  | Apple MacBook Pro     |
      | ipad air     | Apple iPad Air        |
```
Tradeoff: Tagging individual `Examples` tables within a single `Scenario Outline` enables a single parameterised scenario to serve smoke, regression, and production-read-only suites simultaneously without duplicating the scenario body — reducing the total number of Gherkin scenarios by roughly 60% compared to three separate `Scenario Outline` blocks — but the `Scenario Outline` title appears in test reports for every generated row from all `Examples` tables, making it difficult to distinguish smoke rows from regression rows in JUnit XML output consumed by CI dashboards that display only the scenario title without the `Examples` block name, requiring a custom Cucumber.js `Formatter` to append the `Examples` block name to each generated scenario title in the report.

**Pattern 338** — `setDefaultTimeout` Override via `worldParameters` for Per-Environment Timeout Calibration Without Hardcoded Values in Step Definitions
```typescript
// support/timeout-setup.ts
import { BeforeAll, setDefaultTimeout } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from './world';

const ENV_TIMEOUTS: Record<string, number> = {
  local:   15_000,
  staging: 30_000,
  prod:    20_000,
  ci:      45_000,
};

BeforeAll(function (this: AppWorld) {
  const env = process.env.TEST_ENV ?? 'local';
  const timeout = ENV_TIMEOUTS[env];
  if (!timeout) {
    throw new Error(`No timeout configured for TEST_ENV="${env}". Add an entry to ENV_TIMEOUTS.`);
  }
  setDefaultTimeout(timeout);
  console.log(`[timeout-setup] Default step timeout set to ${timeout}ms for env="${env}"`);
});
```
Tradeoff: Calling `setDefaultTimeout` in a `BeforeAll` hook driven by `TEST_ENV` centralises all timeout decisions in a single file with a visible, auditable lookup table — preventing the common anti-pattern of `setDefaultTimeout(60_000)` scattered across five `world.ts` files in a monorepo — but `setDefaultTimeout` applies to all steps and hooks globally within the Cucumber.js process; it is not possible to set different default timeouts for different step types (e.g., 10 seconds for `Given` steps and 30 seconds for `When` steps that trigger background jobs), so teams that need fine-grained per-step-type timeout control must wrap every `When` call site with an explicit `{ timeout: 30_000 }` option object, partially defeating the centralisation goal.

**Pattern 339** — World-Level `apiClient` Factory Initialized in `Before` Hook With Auth Token From `worldParameters` for Reusable API Setup Steps
```typescript
// support/world.ts (api client extension)
import { Before, After } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from './world';

export interface ApiClient {
  get<T>(path: string): Promise<T>;
  post<T>(path: string, body: unknown): Promise<T>;
  delete(path: string): Promise<void>;
}

function createApiClient(baseUrl: string, authToken: string): ApiClient {
  const headers = { Authorization: `Bearer ${authToken}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' };
  return {
    async get<T>(path: string): Promise<T> {
      const res = await fetch(`${baseUrl}${path}`, { headers });
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`GET ${path} failed: ${res.status}`);
      return res.json() as Promise<T>;
    },
    async post<T>(path: string, body: unknown): Promise<T> {
      const res = await fetch(`${baseUrl}${path}`, { method: 'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify(body) });
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`POST ${path} failed: ${res.status}`);
      return res.json() as Promise<T>;
    },
    async delete(path: string): Promise<void> {
      const res = await fetch(`${baseUrl}${path}`, { method: 'DELETE', headers });
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`DELETE ${path} failed: ${res.status}`);
    },
  };
}

Before(async function (this: AppWorld) {
  this.api = createApiClient(this.parameters.baseUrl, this.parameters.authToken);
});

After(async function (this: AppWorld) {
  // apiClient is stateless; no teardown needed — World GC handles it
  delete (this as Partial<AppWorld>).api;
});
```
Tradeoff: Constructing the `ApiClient` in a `Before` hook using `this.parameters.baseUrl` and `this.parameters.authToken` ensures every scenario receives a fresh, correctly-configured API client without requiring step definitions to repeat auth setup — enabling `Given` steps like "the user account exists" to call `this.api.post('/api/users', payload)` directly — but the `ApiClient` is a plain `fetch` wrapper with no retry logic; if the staging environment returns intermittent `503 Service Unavailable` responses under load during parallel test runs, every `Before` hook that calls `this.api` to seed test data fails immediately without retry, causing the entire scenario to fail in the setup phase rather than in the assertion step, making it impossible to distinguish infrastructure flakiness from genuine test failures without inspecting the full hook error message.

**Pattern 340** — `cucumber-html-reporter` Custom Metadata Injection for Per-Run Environment Snapshot in Generated HTML Reports
```typescript
// scripts/generate-report.ts
import reporter from 'cucumber-html-reporter';
import * as os from 'os';
import * as fs from 'fs';

const runMetadata = {
  browser:     process.env.BROWSER ?? 'chromium',
  environment: process.env.TEST_ENV ?? 'local',
  platform:    os.platform(),
  nodeVersion: process.version,
  commitSha:   process.env.GIT_SHA ?? 'local',
  testRunId:   process.env.CI_RUN_ID ?? `local-${Date.now()}`,
};

reporter.generate({
  theme:          'bootstrap',
  jsonFile:       'reports/cucumber-report.json',
  output:         'reports/cucumber-report.html',
  reportSuiteAsScenarios: true,
  scenarioTimestamp: true,
  launchReport:   false,
  metadata:       runMetadata,
  customData: {
    title: 'Run Info',
    data: Object.entries(runMetadata).map(([label, value]) => ({ label, value: String(value) })),
  },
});

const summary = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('reports/cucumber-report.json', 'utf-8'));
const failed = summary.filter((f: { elements: Array<{ status?: string }> }) =>
  f.elements?.some((e) => e.status === 'failed')
).length;
console.log(`Report generated. Failed features: ${failed}`);
process.exit(failed > 0 ? 1 : 0);
```
Tradeoff: Injecting `runMetadata` including `commitSha` and `testRunId` into the HTML report's `customData` section gives CI engineers a single report URL that fully identifies the test run context without cross-referencing build logs — but `cucumber-html-reporter` reads the `jsonFile` path at report-generation time and throws `ENOENT` if the Cucumber.js process exited with a non-zero code and the `--format json:reports/cucumber-report.json` formatter was registered but the output file was not written due to an early crash in a `BeforeAll` hook; teams must explicitly check for `fs.existsSync('reports/cucumber-report.json')` before calling `reporter.generate` and fall back to a minimal error-only report, otherwise the report generation script masks the original crash with an unhelpful `ENOENT` error.

**Pattern 341** — Playwright `locator.filter` Combined With Gherkin DataTable Row Targeting for Table-Driven UI Assertion Steps
```typescript
// step-definitions/table-assertion-steps.ts
import { Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { DataTable } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

Then('the results table contains the following rows:', async function (
  this: AppWorld,
  dataTable: DataTable
) {
  const expectedRows = dataTable.hashes().map((row) =>
    Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(row).map(([k, v]) => [k.trim(), v.trim()]))
  );

  for (const expected of expectedRows) {
    const rowLocator = this.page
      .getByRole('row')
      .filter({ hasText: expected['Name'] });

    await expect(rowLocator).toBeVisible();

    for (const [column, value] of Object.entries(expected)) {
      if (column === 'Name') continue;
      const cellLocator = rowLocator.getByRole('cell').filter({ hasText: value });
      await expect(cellLocator).toBeVisible({
        timeout: 5_000,
      });
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `locator.filter({ hasText })` to narrow a `getByRole('row')` set to the specific row matching the `Name` column, then further filtering each cell by the expected column value, avoids brittle index-based cell targeting (`.nth(2)`) that breaks when columns are reordered — but `locator.filter({ hasText })` performs a substring match, not an exact match; a table row containing "Jane Doe" will satisfy a filter for `hasText: "Jane"` even when the test intends to target the exact name "Jane", so a table with both "Jane" and "Jane Doe" rows causes the assertion to match the first row with "Jane" in the text content regardless of which row was intended, requiring the use of `locator.filter({ has: page.getByRole('cell', { name: 'Jane', exact: true }) })` instead.

**Pattern 342** — `Before` Hook With `scenario.pickle.uri` and `scenario.pickle.name` for Structured Test Execution Logs in Parallel Worker Output
```typescript
// support/logging-hooks.ts
import { Before, After, Status } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { ITestCaseHookParameter } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from './world';

Before(async function (this: AppWorld, scenario: ITestCaseHookParameter) {
  const workerId  = process.env.CUCUMBER_WORKER_ID ?? 'main';
  const featurePath = scenario.pickle.uri.replace(process.cwd(), '').replace(/\\/g, '/');
  this.scenarioLogPrefix = `[W${workerId}][${featurePath}] "${scenario.pickle.name}"`;
  console.log(`${this.scenarioLogPrefix} — START`);
  this.scenarioStartTime = Date.now();
});

After(async function (this: AppWorld, scenario: ITestCaseHookParameter) {
  const durationMs = Date.now() - this.scenarioStartTime;
  const status = scenario.result?.status ?? Status.UNKNOWN;
  const icon = status === Status.PASSED ? '✓' : status === Status.FAILED ? '✗' : '~';
  console.log(`${this.scenarioLogPrefix} — ${icon} ${status} (${durationMs}ms)`);
  if (status === Status.FAILED && scenario.result?.message) {
    console.error(`${this.scenarioLogPrefix} — FAILURE:\n${scenario.result.message}`);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Attaching `scenarioLogPrefix` to the World object in the `Before` hook and referencing it in the `After` hook ensures that every log line from a parallel worker is prefixed with the worker ID, feature file path, and scenario name — enabling `grep "[W2]"` to isolate all output from worker 2 in a noisy parallel log stream — but `scenario.pickle.uri` is an absolute filesystem path on the machine where Cucumber.js runs; in CI environments where the workspace is mounted at a Docker container path like `/home/runner/work/repo`, the `featurePath` after replacing `process.cwd()` still contains `/home/runner/work/repo` if `process.cwd()` returns a symlink-resolved path that differs from the Docker mount path, producing log lines with full untruncated paths that overflow terminal line-length limits and break log parsing regex patterns.

**Pattern 343** — `After` Hook With Playwright `page.video` Save-as for Video Evidence Attached to Failed Scenarios Only
```typescript
// support/video-hooks.ts
import { Before, After, Status } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { ITestCaseHookParameter } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from './world';
import * as path from 'path';
import * as fs from 'fs';

const VIDEO_DIR = path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'test-results', 'videos');

Before(async function (this: AppWorld) {
  fs.mkdirSync(VIDEO_DIR, { recursive: true });
  this._context = await this.browser.newContext({
    recordVideo: { dir: VIDEO_DIR, size: { width: 1280, height: 720 } },
  });
  this._page = await this._context.newPage();
});

After(async function (this: AppWorld, scenario: ITestCaseHookParameter) {
  const status = scenario.result?.status;
  const videoPath = await this._page?.video()?.path();
  await this._page?.close();
  await this._context?.close();

  if (status !== Status.FAILED && videoPath) {
    fs.rmSync(videoPath, { force: true });
  } else if (status === Status.FAILED && videoPath) {
    const safeName = scenario.pickle.name.replace(/[^a-z0-9]/gi, '-').toLowerCase();
    const dest = path.join(VIDEO_DIR, `${safeName}-${Date.now()}.webm`);
    fs.renameSync(videoPath, dest);
    console.log(`[video] Saved failure video: ${dest}`);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Calling `this._page.video().path()` in the `After` hook after `page.close()` and `context.close()` ensures Playwright has flushed the video file to disk (video is only finalised on context close) before attempting to rename it — but `recordVideo` causes Playwright to allocate a background FFmpeg process for every scenario regardless of whether the scenario ultimately passes or fails; in a parallel suite of 200 scenarios running 4 workers simultaneously, this means 4 concurrent FFmpeg processes with unbounded temporary file accumulation under `test-results/videos/`, and on CI runners with limited `/tmp` disk space (typically 10–14 GB), long-running suites can exhaust disk space mid-run because Playwright does not garbage-collect pending video temp files until `context.close()` is called, making disk exhaustion failures appear as `ENOSPC` errors in unrelated steps rather than as video recording errors.

**Pattern 344** — Gherkin `Background` Step Using a Tagged `@factory` Step to Seed Complex Test Fixtures via a Single Reusable Phrase
```typescript
// step-definitions/factory-steps.ts
import { Given } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

type FactoryName = 'standard-user' | 'admin-user' | 'locked-account' | 'pending-order';

const FACTORY_SEEDS: Record<FactoryName, (api: AppWorld['api']) => Promise<void>> = {
  'standard-user':  async (api) => { await api.post('/api/seed/user',  { role: 'user'  }); },
  'admin-user':     async (api) => { await api.post('/api/seed/user',  { role: 'admin' }); },
  'locked-account': async (api) => { await api.post('/api/seed/user',  { role: 'user', locked: true }); },
  'pending-order':  async (api) => {
    await api.post('/api/seed/user', { role: 'user' });
    await api.post('/api/seed/order', { status: 'pending' });
  },
};

Given('the {string} fixture is seeded', async function (
  this: AppWorld,
  factoryName: string
) {
  const seed = FACTORY_SEEDS[factoryName as FactoryName];
  if (!seed) {
    throw new Error(`Unknown fixture factory "${factoryName}". Valid: ${Object.keys(FACTORY_SEEDS).join(', ')}`);
  }
  await seed(this.api);
});
```
Tradeoff: Externalising fixture seed logic into a `FACTORY_SEEDS` map keyed by a human-readable factory name allows Gherkin `Background` sections to express intent in one line ("the `pending-order` fixture is seeded") rather than 4–6 repeated API-call steps — and adding a new fixture requires only one entry in `FACTORY_SEEDS` with no new step definition — but the factory name is a plain `{string}` parameter without a custom parameter type, so a Gherkin author who types `"pending order"` (space instead of hyphen) receives a runtime `Error: Unknown fixture factory` rather than a Cucumber.js parse-time `No step definition matches` error; using a `defineParameterType` for `{factory}` with an explicit regex would catch the typo at parse time, but requires manually updating the regex every time a new factory is added, reintroducing the maintenance burden the map pattern was designed to eliminate.

**Pattern 345** — `IFormatter` Custom Formatter to Emit Structured JSON Failure Summaries for Slack Webhook Consumption in CI
```typescript
// support/slack-failure-formatter.ts
import { Formatter, formatterHelpers, IFormatterOptions } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { messages } from '@cucumber/messages';
import * as https from 'https';

export default class SlackFailureFormatter extends Formatter {
  private failures: Array<{ scenario: string; step: string; error: string }> = [];

  constructor(options: IFormatterOptions) {
    super(options);
    options.eventBroadcaster.on('envelope', (envelope: messages.Envelope) => {
      if (!envelope.testStepFinished) return;
      const { testStepResult } = envelope.testStepFinished;
      if (testStepResult.status !== 'FAILED') return;
      const message = testStepResult.message ?? 'No error message';
      const truncated = message.length > 300 ? message.slice(0, 297) + '...' : message;
      this.failures.push({ scenario: 'unknown', step: 'unknown', error: truncated });
    });

    options.eventBroadcaster.on('envelope', (envelope: messages.Envelope) => {
      if (!envelope.testRunFinished) return;
      if (this.failures.length === 0) return;
      const payload = JSON.stringify({
        text: `*BDD Test Run Failed* — ${this.failures.length} failure(s)`,
        attachments: this.failures.map((f) => ({ color: 'danger', text: f.error })),
      });
      const webhookUrl = new URL(process.env.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL ?? '');
      const req = https.request({ hostname: webhookUrl.hostname, path: webhookUrl.pathname, method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Content-Length': Buffer.byteLength(payload) } });
      req.write(payload);
      req.end();
    });
  }
}
```
Tradeoff: Building a custom `IFormatter` that subscribes to the `eventBroadcaster` message stream and fires a Slack webhook on `testRunFinished` keeps failure notification logic out of the CI pipeline YAML and co-located with the test framework — enabling the formatter to be activated per-project via `format: ['./support/slack-failure-formatter.ts']` in `cucumber.config.ts` — but the Slack webhook `https.request` call in the `testRunFinished` handler is non-awaitable in the synchronous `IFormatter` constructor callback; if the Slack API takes more than the 200ms window before Cucumber.js tears down the Node.js process, the in-flight request is aborted and no notification is sent, requiring the formatter to instead write failures to a JSON file and delegate Slack notification to a separate post-run script that can properly `await` the HTTP call.

### Community Gotchas

**G91** — `cucumber-js` `--parallel` With `BeforeAll`/`AfterAll` Hooks — Hooks Run Once Per Worker, Not Once Per Suite
Why this matters: In Cucumber.js parallel mode, `BeforeAll` and `AfterAll` hooks are executed once per worker process, not once for the entire test suite. A `BeforeAll` hook that creates a shared database schema via `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` appears safe but runs N times for N workers — and when combined with a `AfterAll` hook that drops the table via `DROP TABLE`, the first worker to finish its `AfterAll` drops the table while the other workers are still executing scenarios that depend on it, causing mid-run `relation does not exist` errors on workers that started after the first worker completed. The Cucumber.js documentation uses the phrase "once before all scenarios" for `BeforeAll` but does not explicitly state that parallel workers each get their own `BeforeAll` invocation, leading developers to incorrectly model `BeforeAll` as a suite-global initialisation hook.
Fix: In parallel Cucumber.js runs, treat `BeforeAll`/`AfterAll` as per-worker setup/teardown, not as suite-global hooks. For true once-per-suite operations (schema creation, seed data loading, external service provisioning), use a separate `globalSetup` script called before `cucumber-js` in the CI pipeline (`npm run db:seed && cucumber-js --parallel 4`). Use `BeforeAll` only for per-worker state that is safe to initialise N times, such as opening a database connection pool or setting a worker-scoped base URL.

**G92** — Cucumber.js `pickle` Hooks Receive `ITestCaseHookParameter`, Not `ITestCaseStartedParameter` — `testCaseStartedId` Is Undefined on `pickle`
Why this matters: Cucumber.js `Before` and `After` hooks receive an `ITestCaseHookParameter` object, which has a `pickle` property (the parsed Gherkin scenario) and a `result` property (in `After` only). The parameter does not have a `testCaseStartedId` property — that identifier is on `ITestCaseStartedParameter`, which is only available via the `eventBroadcaster` stream in a custom `Formatter`. Developers who attempt to read `scenario.testCaseStartedId` inside a `Before` hook (for logging or correlation) receive `undefined`, causing correlation IDs derived from `testCaseStartedId` to all collapse to `"undefined-<timestamp>"`. The TypeScript type for `ITestCaseHookParameter` does not include `testCaseStartedId`, but many StackOverflow answers written against Cucumber.js 7's less-strict typings show `scenario.testCaseStartedId` as if it were valid, causing developers to trust the pattern without checking current type definitions.
Fix: For per-scenario correlation IDs within hook bodies, generate a UUID using `crypto.randomUUID()` in the `Before` hook and attach it to `this.correlationId` on the World object. To correlate the `Before`-assigned `correlationId` with Cucumber.js's internal `testCaseStartedId`, implement a custom `Formatter` that maps `testCaseStartedId` to `pickle.id` via the `testCaseStarted` envelope event and expose that map via a shared module, but only if the correlation is needed for external observability tooling rather than internal test logic.

**G93** — Playwright `page.waitForSelector` Resolves on DOM Presence, Not Visibility — Step Definitions That Assert on Hidden Elements Pass Incorrectly
Why this matters: `page.waitForSelector('selector')` by default waits until the element is present in the DOM (`state: 'attached'`), not until it is visible to the user (`state: 'visible'`). A step definition that calls `await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="success-banner"]')` and then reads `expect(await page.textContent(...))` may resolve successfully even when the success banner is rendered in the DOM with `display: none` or `opacity: 0` — for example, when an app pre-renders notification banners as hidden elements and toggles them visible on success. The step passes with correct text content but the assertion is meaningless from a user-experience perspective because the banner the user actually sees may not have appeared yet. This is a silent correctness failure rather than a test failure.
Fix: Replace all `page.waitForSelector('selector')` calls in step definitions with Playwright Locator API assertions: `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="success-banner"]')).toBeVisible()`. The Locator `toBeVisible()` assertion uses Playwright's built-in visibility semantics (element has non-zero dimensions, non-zero opacity, and is not `display:none`) and retries until the timeout. Audit the codebase for `waitForSelector` calls and migrate them to `expect(locator).toBeVisible()` using a codemod or a `grep` pre-commit hook that rejects new `waitForSelector` additions in step definition files.

**G94** — Cucumber.js `setWorldConstructor` Must Be Called Exactly Once Per Process — Multiple Support Files Calling It Cause Last-Write-Wins Silencing of Earlier Worlds
Why this matters: `setWorldConstructor` registers the World class in a global Cucumber.js registry. If multiple support files each call `setWorldConstructor` with a different class (a common pattern when a base `AppWorld` is extended per-domain into `AdminWorld` and `CustomerWorld`), the last call wins and all earlier registrations are silently discarded. Cucumber.js does not throw an error or emit a warning when `setWorldConstructor` is called more than once; the test suite appears to run correctly until a step definition in an `AdminWorld`-authored spec calls `this.adminPanel` and receives `undefined` because the active World is actually `CustomerWorld`. This is a particularly difficult bug to diagnose in monorepos where support files from multiple packages are aggregated into a single Cucumber.js run via a glob pattern.
Fix: Establish a single `setWorldConstructor` call site in a canonical `support/world.ts` file and enforce uniqueness with a pre-commit hook that counts `setWorldConstructor` calls across all TypeScript files in the project and rejects any commit that introduces a second call. For multi-domain World requirements (admin vs. customer contexts), use composition within a single `AppWorld` class: `this.admin = new AdminContext(this.page)` and `this.customer = new CustomerContext(this.page)`, exposing domain-specific helpers as namespaced properties rather than separate World subclasses.

**G95** — `DataTable.raw()` Includes the Header Row — `DataTable.hashes()` Does Not — Mixing Both Methods in One Step Causes Off-by-One Row Counts
Why this matters: In Cucumber.js, `DataTable.raw()` returns a two-dimensional array of all cells including the header row as the first element, while `DataTable.hashes()` returns an array of objects using the header row as keys and excludes the header row from the result set. A step definition that calls `const count = table.raw().length` to validate that at least 2 data rows are present and then calls `table.hashes()` for iteration will always see one more row than expected in the `raw()` count — a table with 2 data rows has `raw().length === 3` (header + 2 data rows). If the validation check is `if (table.raw().length < 2)` intending to require at least 2 data rows, a table with a header row and 1 data row passes the guard (`raw().length === 2 >= 2`) even though `table.hashes()` returns only 1 entry. This produces false-positive validation in step definitions that mix `raw()` for counting with `hashes()` for iteration.
Fix: Never mix `DataTable.raw()` and `DataTable.hashes()` in the same step definition. Use `DataTable.hashes()` exclusively for tables with header rows (which is the standard Gherkin convention), and use `DataTable.raw()` only for headerless tables where all rows are data rows (e.g., a single-column list). For minimum-row validation, write `if (table.hashes().length < 2) throw new Error(...)` rather than using `raw().length`.
