## Cycle 67 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 346** — Cucumber.js Named Profiles in `cucumber.js` for Environment-Specific Configuration Without Separate Config Files
```typescript
// cucumber.js  (ESM-compatible CommonJS export)
const common = {
  require: ['support/**/*.ts'],
  requireModule: ['ts-node/register'],
  format: ['progress-bar', 'json:reports/cucumber.json'],
  worldParameters: { baseUrl: process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000' },
};

module.exports = {
  default: { ...common, tags: 'not @slow' },
  ci: {
    ...common,
    tags: 'not @wip',
    retry: 1,
    retryTagFilter: '@flaky',
    format: [...common.format, 'html:reports/cucumber.html'],
    parallel: 4,
  },
  smoke: {
    ...common,
    tags: '@smoke',
    failFast: true,
  },
  webkit: {
    ...common,
    worldParameters: { ...common.worldParameters, browser: 'webkit' },
  },
};
```
Tradeoff: Consolidating Cucumber.js profiles in a single `cucumber.js` file with a shared `common` spread eliminates per-environment CLI argument sprawl and makes `BASE_URL` injection an explicit `worldParameters` concern rather than an undocumented convention — but stacking multiple profiles with `-p ci -p webkit` merges them via last-write-wins for scalar values, meaning the `browser: 'webkit'` from the `webkit` profile silently overrides any `browser` key set in the `ci` profile's `worldParameters` without warning, requiring profile authors to document merge semantics explicitly or use a single composite profile per environment matrix cell rather than composing orthogonal profiles at runtime.

**Pattern 347** — Cucumber.js `retryTagFilter` With `@flaky` Tag to Scope Automatic Retries to Known-Unstable Scenarios Only
```typescript
// cucumber.js
module.exports = {
  default: {
    require: ['support/**/*.ts', 'step-definitions/**/*.ts'],
    requireModule: ['ts-node/register'],
    retry: 2,
    retryTagFilter: '@flaky',
    format: ['summary'],
  },
};

// features/checkout.feature
// @flaky — applied only to scenarios with known timing instability
// @flaky
// Scenario: Payment gateway redirect completes within 10 seconds
//   Given I have items in my cart
//   When I initiate checkout
//   Then I am redirected to the payment confirmation page

// support/hooks.ts
import { Before, After, Status } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { ITestCaseHookParameter } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

After(async function (this: AppWorld, scenario: ITestCaseHookParameter) {
  if (scenario.result?.status === Status.FAILED) {
    await this.page.screenshot({ path: `reports/failures/${scenario.pickle.name}.png` });
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Scoping `retry` to `@flaky`-tagged scenarios via `retryTagFilter` prevents stable scenarios from being silently retried on genuine bugs — preserving fast feedback on real failures — but requires teams to maintain the `@flaky` tag inventory as an explicit technical debt register; scenarios that become stable after upstream fixes continue to incur retry overhead until the tag is removed, and there is no built-in Cucumber.js mechanism to automatically remove `@flaky` tags when a scenario passes consistently across N consecutive CI runs, making ongoing tag hygiene a manual discipline.

**Pattern 348** — Gherkin `Rule` Keyword With Nested `Background` to Partition Business Rule Contexts Within a Single Feature File
```gherkin
# features/account-limits.feature
Feature: Account withdrawal limits
  As a bank customer
  I want withdrawal limits enforced per account tier
  So that the bank remains compliant with regulatory caps

  Rule: Standard accounts are capped at £500 per day
    Background:
      Given I am authenticated as a standard account holder
      And my account balance is £1000

    Scenario: Withdrawal within the daily limit succeeds
      When I withdraw £400
      Then my balance is £600
      And the transaction is approved

    Scenario: Withdrawal exceeding the daily limit is rejected
      When I withdraw £600
      Then my balance remains £1000
      And I see the error "Daily withdrawal limit exceeded"

  Rule: Premium accounts are capped at £5000 per day
    Background:
      Given I am authenticated as a premium account holder
      And my account balance is £10000

    Scenario: Large withdrawal within premium limit succeeds
      When I withdraw £4500
      Then my balance is £5500
      And the transaction is approved
```
Tradeoff: Using `Rule` with a nested `Background` allows each business rule's preconditions to be stated once within its rule block rather than repeated across every scenario — dramatically improving traceability between Gherkin scenarios and acceptance criteria in the backlog — but `Rule`-nested `Background` steps execute in addition to any Feature-level `Background`, not instead of it, so placing shared setup (authentication scaffolding) in the Feature-level `Background` and rule-specific setup in the `Rule`-level `Background` creates two-layer background execution that can be difficult to reason about when debugging failures where both layers interact.

**Pattern 349** — Playwright `page.getByRole` in Step Definitions for ARIA-Semantic Locators That Survive DOM Refactoring
```typescript
// step-definitions/navigation.steps.ts
import { When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

When('I click the {string} navigation link', async function (this: AppWorld, linkName: string) {
  await this.page.getByRole('link', { name: linkName }).click();
});

When('I submit the {string} form', async function (this: AppWorld, formLabel: string) {
  const form = this.page.getByRole('form', { name: formLabel });
  await form.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }).click();
});

Then('the {string} heading is visible', async function (this: AppWorld, headingText: string) {
  await expect(this.page.getByRole('heading', { name: headingText, level: 1 })).toBeVisible();
});

Then('the {string} alert message is displayed', async function (this: AppWorld, message: string) {
  await expect(this.page.getByRole('alert')).toContainText(message);
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `getByRole` with semantic ARIA role names and accessible name matchers makes step definitions resilient to CSS class renaming, component library upgrades, and DOM restructuring because the locator is grounded in the accessibility tree rather than the rendered HTML hierarchy — but `getByRole` with `{ name: someString }` performs an exact accessible-name match by default, causing step definitions to break when UX copy is updated (e.g., "Submit" → "Save and continue") even though the element's role and function are unchanged, requiring teams to choose between exact `name` matching for precision and regex `name` patterns (`{ name: /submit/i }`) for flexibility.

**Pattern 350** — Cucumber.js `defineParameterType` With a Domain Entity Transformer to Parse Rich Step Arguments Into Typed Objects
```typescript
// support/parameter-types.ts
import { defineParameterType } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

interface Money {
  amount: number;
  currency: string;
}

defineParameterType({
  name: 'money',
  regexp: /£(\d+(?:\.\d{2})?)|(\d+(?:\.\d{2})?) (USD|EUR|GBP)/,
  transformer(matched: string): Money {
    const poundMatch = /^£(\d+(?:\.\d{2})?)$/.exec(matched);
    if (poundMatch) return { amount: parseFloat(poundMatch[1]), currency: 'GBP' };
    const genericMatch = /^(\d+(?:\.\d{2})?) (USD|EUR|GBP)$/.exec(matched);
    if (genericMatch) return { amount: parseFloat(genericMatch[1]), currency: genericMatch[2] };
    throw new Error(`Cannot parse money value: ${matched}`);
  },
  useForSnippets: true,
});

// step-definitions/payments.steps.ts
import { When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { Money } from '../support/parameter-types';

When('I transfer {money} to account {string}', async function (this: AppWorld, amount: Money, account: string) {
  await this.api.post('/transfers', { amount: amount.amount, currency: amount.currency, to: account });
});
```
Tradeoff: A `defineParameterType` transformer that returns a typed domain object removes ad-hoc string-to-number conversions scattered across dozens of step definitions and makes Gherkin step signatures self-documenting (`{money}` is unambiguous to non-technical stakeholders) — but the `regexp` in `defineParameterType` must match exhaustively across all valid formats in all feature files; if a new engineer writes `$50 USD` (dollar sign) and the regexp only handles `£` and bare numerals, the step silently falls back to a plain `{string}` match rather than triggering a type error, meaning missing format variants produce wrong-type step arguments rather than clear parse failures unless the team maintains a companion test for the parameter type transformer.

**Pattern 351** — Playwright `context.routeFromHAR` for Deterministic Offline API Replay in BDD Acceptance Tests
```typescript
// support/world.ts
import { setWorldConstructor, World, IWorldOptions } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { chromium, Browser, BrowserContext, Page } from 'playwright';
import * as path from 'path';

export class AppWorld extends World {
  browser!: Browser;
  context!: BrowserContext;
  page!: Page;

  async init(): Promise<void> {
    this.browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: true });
    const harPath = path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'fixtures/api-responses.har');
    this.context = await this.browser.newContext();
    await this.context.routeFromHAR(harPath, {
      url: /\/api\//,
      update: process.env.UPDATE_HAR === 'true',
    });
    this.page = await this.context.newPage();
  }

  async destroy(): Promise<void> {
    await this.browser.close();
  }
}

setWorldConstructor(AppWorld);
```
Tradeoff: `context.routeFromHAR` with a URL filter replays recorded API responses from a `.har` file, making BDD acceptance tests fully deterministic and runnable offline without a live backend — but the HAR file becomes a brittle fixture that must be manually regenerated (`UPDATE_HAR=true`) whenever API response schemas change; stale HAR fixtures cause scenarios to pass against outdated response shapes while production diverges, meaning teams must treat HAR regeneration as a required step in any API contract change, ideally enforced by a CI job that compares schema drift between the live API and the committed `.har` file.

**Pattern 352** — Gherkin DocString With `content_type` Annotation for Typed Inline Payloads in API Contract Scenarios
```gherkin
# features/api-contracts.feature
Feature: Order creation API contract
  As a backend engineer
  I want the order creation endpoint to validate request structure
  So that malformed requests are rejected before persistence

  Scenario: Valid order payload is accepted
    Given the API is running
    When I POST to "/orders" with body:
      """json
      {
        "customerId": "cust-001",
        "items": [
          { "productId": "prod-42", "quantity": 2 },
          { "productId": "prod-17", "quantity": 1 }
        ],
        "currency": "GBP"
      }
      """
    Then the response status is 201
    And the response body contains "orderId"

  Scenario: Missing required field returns 400
    When I POST to "/orders" with body:
      """json
      { "items": [{ "productId": "prod-42", "quantity": 2 }] }
      """
    Then the response status is 400
    And the response body contains "customerId is required"
```
Tradeoff: Using the DocString `content_type` annotation (`"""json`) embeds structured payload intent directly in the feature file, enabling humans and tooling alike to syntax-highlight and validate the JSON without treating it as opaque prose — but Cucumber.js does not validate or parse the `content_type` annotation by default; the step definition receives the raw DocString text regardless of the declared type, meaning the annotation is purely documentary unless the step definition explicitly parses `JSON.parse(docString.content)` and validates against a schema, creating a gap between the declared `json` type and the actual runtime parsing that silently accepts malformed JSON if the step definition omits validation.

**Pattern 353** — Playwright `locator.filter({ has: locator })` for Scoped Multi-Element Assertions in Table-Driven BDD Scenarios
```typescript
// step-definitions/table.steps.ts
import { Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';
import type { DataTable } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

Then('the orders table contains the following rows:', async function (this: AppWorld, table: DataTable) {
  const rows = this.page.locator('table[data-testid="orders-table"] tbody tr');

  for (const expectedRow of table.hashes()) {
    const matchingRow = rows.filter({
      has: this.page.locator(`td[data-col="order-id"]`, { hasText: expectedRow['Order ID'] }),
    });
    await expect(matchingRow).toHaveCount(1);
    await expect(matchingRow.locator(`td[data-col="status"]`)).toHaveText(expectedRow['Status']);
    await expect(matchingRow.locator(`td[data-col="total"]`)).toHaveText(expectedRow['Total']);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `locator.filter({ has: locator })` enables scoped row-by-row assertions within a table by anchoring on a unique cell value, avoiding brittle `nth(n)` row indexing that breaks when rows are reordered — but `filter({ has: locator })` performs a DOM subtree search, meaning it will match any row containing the text anywhere in its subtree (including nested tables or tooltips) unless the inner locator is constrained to a specific `data-col` cell, requiring the `has` locator to be as specific as `td[data-col="order-id"]` rather than a bare `td` to avoid false positives in richly structured table cells.

**Pattern 354** — Cucumber.js `BeforeAll` / `AfterAll` as Per-Worker Database Connection Pool Initialisation With Explicit Pool Teardown
```typescript
// support/hooks.ts
import { BeforeAll, AfterAll, setDefaultTimeout } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { Pool } from 'pg';

let pool: Pool;

setDefaultTimeout(30_000);

BeforeAll(async function () {
  pool = new Pool({
    connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? 'postgres://localhost:5432/testdb',
    max: 5,
    idleTimeoutMillis: 10_000,
  });
  // Verify connectivity once per worker before any scenario runs
  const client = await pool.connect();
  await client.query('SELECT 1');
  client.release();
  // Expose pool via global for step definitions in this worker
  (global as Record<string, unknown>)['__dbPool'] = pool;
});

AfterAll(async function () {
  if (pool) {
    await pool.end();
    delete (global as Record<string, unknown>)['__dbPool'];
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Placing `pg.Pool` initialisation in `BeforeAll` and teardown in `AfterAll` is correct for per-worker scoping — each parallel worker opens its own pool of up to 5 connections and closes it cleanly — but relying on `(global as Record<string, unknown>)['__dbPool']` to share the pool across step definitions is a type-unsafe side channel that bypasses Cucumber.js's World composition mechanism; the idiomatic alternative is to instantiate the pool once at module scope in a singleton module and import it directly into step definition files, which avoids the global mutation while still sharing a single pool instance per worker process.

**Pattern 355** — Playwright `page.waitForResponse` in Step Definitions to Assert on Network Responses Without Polling UI State
```typescript
// step-definitions/api-triggered.steps.ts
import { When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

When('I submit the search form for {string}', async function (this: AppWorld, query: string) {
  // Promise must be declared BEFORE the action that triggers the request
  const searchResponsePromise = this.page.waitForResponse(
    (resp) => resp.url().includes('/api/search') && resp.status() === 200,
    { timeout: 10_000 }
  );
  await this.page.getByRole('searchbox', { name: 'Search' }).fill(query);
  await this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Search' }).click();
  this.searchResponse = await searchResponsePromise;
});

Then('the search API returns {int} results', async function (this: AppWorld, count: number) {
  const body = await this.searchResponse.json() as { total: number };
  expect(body.total).toBe(count);
});

Then('the search results list shows {int} items', async function (this: AppWorld, count: number) {
  await expect(this.page.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveCount(count);
});
```
Tradeoff: Storing a `Response` promise in `this.searchResponse` and resolving it in a later `Then` step enables tight assertions on both the API contract and the rendered UI without duplicating the network wait — ensuring the step sequence mirrors the real user journey — but `page.waitForResponse` with a URL predicate races against the click action; if the response arrives before `waitForResponse` is registered (possible when the app caches responses or the network is very fast), the promise will hang until timeout rather than resolving immediately, requiring the promise to be created before the click action triggers the request, which is the pattern shown but is often accidentally inverted by developers who place the `waitForResponse` call after the click.

**Pattern 356** — Cucumber.js `dryRun: true` Profile for CI Validation of Step Definition Coverage Without Executing Steps
```typescript
// cucumber.js
const common = {
  require: ['support/**/*.ts', 'step-definitions/**/*.ts'],
  requireModule: ['ts-node/register'],
  paths: ['features/**/*.feature'],
};

module.exports = {
  default: common,
  validate: {
    ...common,
    dryRun: true,
    format: ['summary'],
  },
};

// package.json scripts:
// "test:bdd:validate": "cucumber-js --profile validate",
// "test:bdd": "cucumber-js --profile default",
// "test:bdd:ci": "npm run test:bdd:validate && npm run test:bdd"
```
Tradeoff: A `dryRun: true` profile run in CI before the full test execution catches undefined step definitions — scenarios that reference step text with no matching expression — at near-zero cost (milliseconds for parsing, no browser launch) and fails the CI pipeline before wasting minutes on a partial test run — but `dryRun` only validates that a matching step definition expression exists; it does not validate that the step definition's implementation compiles, that parameter types are correctly matched, or that the step arguments are type-safe, meaning a scenario with a `{money}` parameter that has been removed from `parameter-types.ts` will fail the dry-run, but a step with a broken implementation that throws at runtime will pass the dry-run and fail only during the full execution.

**Pattern 357** — Axe-Core Accessibility Scan Step Definition Using `@axe-core/playwright` Integrated Into Cucumber.js `After` Hook Reporting
```typescript
// support/axe-hooks.ts
import { After, Status } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';
import type { AppWorld } from './world';
import type { ITestCaseHookParameter } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

After({ tags: '@a11y' }, async function (this: AppWorld, scenario: ITestCaseHookParameter) {
  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page: this.page })
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
    .analyze();

  if (results.violations.length > 0) {
    const reportPath = path.resolve('reports', 'a11y', `${scenario.pickle.name}.json`);
    fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(reportPath), { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(reportPath, JSON.stringify(results.violations, null, 2));
    throw new Error(
      `${results.violations.length} WCAG 2.0 AA violation(s) found. See ${reportPath}`
    );
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Placing an axe-core scan in a tag-gated `After` hook means accessibility validation runs automatically after any scenario tagged `@a11y` without requiring engineers to add explicit assertion steps — reducing the barrier to accessibility testing adoption — but running axe-core in `After` rather than as an explicit `Then` step means the accessibility violation is surfaced as a hook failure rather than a step failure, which some formatters and CI integrations treat differently (e.g., JUnit XML may categorise it as an error rather than a test failure), and the failure message references the report file path rather than the violation text inline.

**Pattern 358** — Cucumber.js `shard` Configuration for Distributing Feature Files Across CI Matrix Jobs Without Overlapping Execution
```typescript
// cucumber.js
module.exports = {
  default: {
    require: ['support/**/*.ts', 'step-definitions/**/*.ts'],
    requireModule: ['ts-node/register'],
    format: ['json:reports/cucumber-shard.json'],
    // Activated via env: CUCUMBER_SHARD=1/4 cucumber-js
    // Each shard receives 1/N of the feature files deterministically
  },
  ci: {
    require: ['support/**/*.ts', 'step-definitions/**/*.ts'],
    requireModule: ['ts-node/register'],
    parallel: 2,
    format: ['json:reports/cucumber.json', 'html:reports/cucumber.html'],
    retry: 1,
    retryTagFilter: '@flaky',
  },
};

// GitHub Actions matrix strategy (in .github/workflows/bdd.yml):
// strategy:
//   matrix:
//     shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]
// steps:
//   - run: CUCUMBER_SHARD=${{ matrix.shard }}/4 npx cucumber-js
//   - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
//     with:
//       name: cucumber-report-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
//       path: reports/cucumber-shard.json
```
Tradeoff: Cucumber.js's built-in `shard` support (via `CUCUMBER_SHARD=index/total`) distributes scenarios across N CI matrix jobs deterministically using a modulo assignment on the sorted scenario list, cutting wall-clock time roughly by N without requiring an external orchestration layer — but the distribution is based on scenario count rather than scenario duration, so a shard containing 5 slow E2E scenarios may take 4x longer than a shard with 20 fast unit-style BDD scenarios, causing CI matrix jobs to have wildly uneven durations and defeating the wall-clock benefit; teams with large suites must either implement time-weighted sharding (using historical timing data from previous JSON reports) or combine sharding with `--parallel` per-shard to smooth out duration variance.

**Pattern 359** — Page Object Model Class Injected Via Cucumber.js World Constructor for Centralised Selector Management in Step Definitions
```typescript
// support/pages/checkout-page.ts
import type { Page } from 'playwright';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

export class CheckoutPage {
  private readonly page: Page;
  readonly url = '/checkout';

  constructor(page: Page) {
    this.page = page;
  }

  get orderSummary() { return this.page.getByRole('region', { name: 'Order summary' }); }
  get totalAmount() { return this.orderSummary.getByTestId('total-amount'); }
  get placeOrderButton() { return this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }); }
  get confirmationBanner() { return this.page.getByRole('status', { name: 'Order confirmed' }); }

  async goto() { await this.page.goto(this.url); }
  async placeOrder() { await this.placeOrderButton.click(); }
  async expectConfirmed() { await expect(this.confirmationBanner).toBeVisible(); }
}

// support/world.ts — excerpt showing page object construction
import { CheckoutPage } from './pages/checkout-page';

export class AppWorld extends World {
  checkout!: CheckoutPage;

  async init(): Promise<void> {
    // browser/context/page setup omitted for brevity
    this.checkout = new CheckoutPage(this.page);
  }
}
```
Tradeoff: Constructing page objects inside `AppWorld.init()` and exposing them as typed World properties gives step definitions a single import path (`this.checkout.placeOrder()`) with full TypeScript intellisense and centralises all selectors in the page object class — but this approach tightly couples the page object lifecycle to the World lifecycle, meaning page objects are reconstructed on every scenario even when the same page object is reused across a multi-step journey; for scenarios that span multiple pages, the World accumulates page object instances for every page visited in the scenario, increasing memory footprint in long-running parallel workers.

**Pattern 360** — Cucumber.js `failFast: true` in Smoke Profile Combined With `@smoke` Tag to Enable Hard-Stop CI on First Critical Failure
```typescript
// cucumber.js
const base = {
  require: ['support/**/*.ts', 'step-definitions/**/*.ts'],
  requireModule: ['ts-node/register'],
};

module.exports = {
  default: base,
  smoke: {
    ...base,
    tags: '@smoke',
    failFast: true,
    format: ['progress-bar', 'json:reports/smoke.json'],
    worldParameters: {
      baseUrl: process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
      strictMode: true,
    },
  },
};

// Usage in CI deployment pipeline (.github/workflows/deploy.yml):
// - name: Smoke test against staging
//   run: npx cucumber-js --profile smoke
//   env:
//     BASE_URL: https://staging.example.com

// features/smoke.feature
// @smoke
// Scenario: Application homepage loads
//   Given I navigate to the homepage
//   Then the page title is "My App"
//   And the main navigation is visible
```
Tradeoff: Setting `failFast: true` in a `@smoke`-scoped Cucumber.js profile causes the test runner to abort after the first failing scenario, exiting with a non-zero code that immediately fails the CI deployment pipeline without waiting for remaining smoke scenarios to execute — ideal for post-deploy verification gates where any failure indicates a broken deployment — but `failFast` skips all subsequent scenarios, meaning the resulting JSON report contains only the single failure plus skipped scenario stubs, making it impossible for on-call engineers to know whether one or five smoke checks would have failed, requiring the team to also run the full smoke suite (without `failFast`) in a parallel non-blocking job to collect the complete failure inventory.

### Community Gotchas

**G96** — Cucumber.js `dryRun: true` Reports `undefined` Steps but Does Not Validate Parameter Type Transformer Availability at Parse Time
Why this matters: `dryRun: true` parses all feature files and matches each step text against registered step definition expressions. If a step uses a custom parameter type `{money}` that was registered in a support file no longer included in the `require` glob (e.g., because `parameter-types.ts` was moved to a subdirectory not covered by `support/*.ts`), the step definition expression `'I transfer {money} to account {string}'` fails to resolve, and the dry run reports the step as `undefined` — but the error message says "Undefined. Implement with the snippet below:" and generates a generic string-based snippet, rather than saying "Unknown parameter type: money". Developers who see the `undefined` status assume the step definition file is missing entirely and waste time searching for it, when the actual problem is a missing `defineParameterType` call from a moved or unincluded support file.
Fix: Ensure all `defineParameterType` calls live in files explicitly covered by the `require` glob and add a dedicated dry-run validation step to CI that fails with a human-readable message on any `undefined` step. Move all `defineParameterType` registrations into a canonical `support/parameter-types.ts` file that is always the first entry in the `require` array (e.g., `require: ['support/parameter-types.ts', 'support/**/*.ts', ...]`) to ensure it is loaded before any step definition that references the custom types.

**G97** — Playwright `page.waitForResponse` Race Condition When Called After the Action That Triggers the Response
Why this matters: `page.waitForResponse(predicate)` registers a listener on the `page` object's response event stream and returns a `Promise` that resolves when a matching response is received. If the action that triggers the response (e.g., `await page.getByRole('button').click()`) is awaited before `waitForResponse` is called, the HTTP response may arrive and be dispatched to Playwright's event queue before the `waitForResponse` listener is registered — causing the promise to never resolve and the test to hang until the configured timeout (default 30 seconds). This race is especially likely in CI environments where the application is running on localhost with negligible network latency, meaning the response arrives within 1–5ms of the click. The bug is intermittent: it passes locally when the network is slightly slower and fails in CI where the stack is faster, making it appear to be an environmental flake rather than a code ordering bug.
Fix: Always declare the `waitForResponse` promise before the action that triggers the request: `const responsePromise = page.waitForResponse(predicate); await page.click(selector); const response = await responsePromise;`. Never await the action first. Add a comment in the step definition noting the ordering requirement so future maintainers do not "simplify" the code by moving the `waitForResponse` call after the action.

**G98** — Gherkin `Background` Steps Are Re-Executed for Every `Scenario Outline` Example Row, Not Once Per Outline Block
Why this matters: A `Scenario Outline` with 20 rows in its `Examples` table causes the `Background` steps to execute 20 times — once before each generated scenario. If the `Background` contains a step that calls an external API to seed data (e.g., `Given the product catalogue is loaded from the fixture API`), and the fixture API has a rate limit or non-negligible latency, the combined overhead of 20 Background executions can cause the feature to take 20x longer than expected or hit the rate limit and fail on row 11 with a `429 Too Many Requests` error. Developers often model `Background` as "runs once before the outline" because they conflate it with a class-level `@BeforeClass` annotation in JUnit, where setup runs once per class rather than once per test method.
Fix: For expensive Background steps that must not repeat across Scenario Outline rows, extract the data setup into a `BeforeAll` hook scoped to the feature's tag and perform the setup once per worker rather than once per scenario. Alternatively, refactor the `Scenario Outline` into a single scenario with a `DataTable` step argument (`When I process the following orders:` + table), allowing the step definition to iterate the rows internally after a single Background execution.

**G99** — Cucumber.js World `this` Context Is `undefined` Inside Arrow Function Callbacks in `Before`/`After` Hooks
Why this matters: Cucumber.js step definitions and hooks bind `this` to the current World instance at invocation time using a regular function call. If a developer writes a `Before` hook as an arrow function — `Before(async () => { await this.page.goto('/'); })` — the arrow function captures `this` from the enclosing lexical scope (the module scope) rather than receiving the World instance injected by Cucumber.js, so `this.page` is `undefined` and the hook throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'goto')`. This error message does not mention Cucumber.js's `this` binding semantics; developers who are unfamiliar with the distinction between arrow functions and regular functions in TypeScript assume the error is a `page` initialisation order problem in `World.init()` and spend hours debugging World setup rather than examining the hook function syntax.
Fix: Never use arrow functions for Cucumber.js step definitions or `Before`/`After` hooks. Always use regular function expressions: `Before(async function() { ... })`. Add an ESLint rule using `eslint-plugin-cucumber` or a custom rule that rejects arrow function expressions passed as the handler argument to `Before`, `After`, `BeforeAll`, `AfterAll`, `Given`, `When`, and `Then` calls. The TypeScript type definitions for these functions accept both `Function` and `() => void`, so the type checker does not catch this error.

**G100** — `@axe-core/playwright` `AxeBuilder.analyze()` Times Out When Called on a Page With Unresolved `fetch` Requests Still Pending in the Network Layer
Why this matters: `AxeBuilder.analyze()` executes an axe-core script injection into the page via `page.evaluate()` and waits for the script to complete its DOM audit. If the page has in-flight `fetch` requests that are blocked (e.g., the test mocked an API route that never calls `route.fulfill()` and the page's JavaScript is awaiting the response), `page.evaluate()` blocks until the pending promises in the page context resolve or the Playwright timeout fires. This manifests as a 30-second timeout in the `After` hook that runs the axe scan, causing the scenario to fail with `"page.evaluate: Timeout 30000ms exceeded"` rather than an accessibility violation report. Developers who see this error search for axe-core configuration issues rather than looking for unresolved `route` handlers.
Fix: Before calling `AxeBuilder.analyze()`, ensure all route handlers have been fulfilled or that `page.unrouteAll()` has been called to release any blocked requests. Call `await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')` before the axe analysis to confirm no in-flight requests remain. Set an explicit, shorter timeout on the `AxeBuilder` call — `new AxeBuilder({ page }).options({ timeout: 10000 })` — so accessibility scan timeouts are distinguishable from navigation timeouts in CI logs.

## Cycle 66 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 361** — World Prototype Lazy Page-Object Registry With TypeScript Getter Caching for Step Reuse Across Feature Domains
```typescript
// support/world.ts
import { setWorldConstructor, IWorldOptions, World } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { Browser, BrowserContext, Page, chromium } from '@playwright/test';
import { CartPage }     from '../pages/CartPage';
import { CheckoutPage } from '../pages/CheckoutPage';
import { AccountPage }  from '../pages/AccountPage';

export class AppWorld extends World {
  browser!: Browser;
  context!: BrowserContext;
  page!: Page;

  private _cart?: CartPage;
  private _checkout?: CheckoutPage;
  private _account?: AccountPage;

  get cart(): CartPage         { return (this._cart     ??= new CartPage(this.page)); }
  get checkout(): CheckoutPage { return (this._checkout ??= new CheckoutPage(this.page)); }
  get account(): AccountPage   { return (this._account  ??= new AccountPage(this.page)); }

  constructor(options: IWorldOptions) { super(options); }
}
setWorldConstructor(AppWorld);

// support/hooks/browser.ts
import { Before, After } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
Before(async function (this: AppWorld) {
  this.browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: true });
  this.context = await this.browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 } });
  this.page    = await this.context.newPage();
});
After(async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.context.close();
  await this.browser.close();
});

// steps/checkout.steps.ts
import { When, Then } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
When('the user proceeds to checkout', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.cart.proceedToCheckout();
});
Then('the order confirmation number is displayed', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await expect(this.checkout.confirmationNumber).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: Lazy World getters instantiate page objects on first access and cache them for the scenario lifetime — eliminating `new CartPage(this.page)` scattered across step files — but because the cache is populated after `Before` completes, a page-object constructor that reads `this.page.url()` to derive a base path captures the URL at the time the getter is first called (which may be mid-scenario after a redirect), causing the cached page object to hold a stale base URL for all subsequent method calls within that scenario without throwing any error.

**Pattern 362** — defineParameterType With Enum Transformer for Type-Safe Domain Vocabulary in Cucumber Expressions
```typescript
// support/parameter-types.ts
import { defineParameterType } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

type OrderStatus = 'Pending' | 'Processing' | 'Shipped' | 'Delivered' | 'Cancelled';
type UserRole    = 'admin' | 'editor' | 'viewer' | 'guest';

defineParameterType({
  name: 'orderStatus',
  regexp: /Pending|Processing|Shipped|Delivered|Cancelled/,
  transformer(raw: string): OrderStatus {
    const valid: OrderStatus[] = ['Pending', 'Processing', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
    if (!valid.includes(raw as OrderStatus)) {
      throw new Error(`Invalid order status: "${raw}". Valid: ${valid.join(', ')}`);
    }
    return raw as OrderStatus;
  },
});

defineParameterType({
  name: 'userRole',
  regexp: /admin|editor|viewer|guest/,
  transformer(raw: string): UserRole { return raw as UserRole; },
});

// steps/order.steps.ts
import { Then, Given } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

Given('the user is logged in as a {userRole}', async function (
  this: AppWorld, role: UserRole
) {
  await this.account.loginAs(role);
});

Then('the order status changes to {orderStatus}', async function (
  this: AppWorld, status: OrderStatus
) {
  await expect(this.page.getByTestId('order-status-badge')).toHaveText(status);
});
```
Tradeoff: Custom parameter types bring Gherkin vocabulary into the TypeScript type system — step parameters are typed as `OrderStatus` and `UserRole` rather than `string`, catching typos in feature files at parse time because Cucumber.js throws `No step definition matches` when the regex does not match — but the regex in `defineParameterType` must be kept manually in sync with the TypeScript union; adding `'Gift Card'` to `PaymentMethod` without updating the regex means the compiler accepts the new value in step logic while the Cucumber.js parser rejects any feature file using `gift card`, creating a silent gap between what the type system allows and what the Gherkin parser accepts.

**Pattern 363** — Scenario Outline With Tagged Examples Blocks for Suite-Level Filtering Without Per-Row Tag Duplication
```gherkin
# features/payment-methods.feature
Feature: Payment method processing

  Scenario Outline: Processing a payment with <method>
    Given the user has items in the cart totalling £<amount>
    When the user pays with <method>
    Then the order confirmation shows payment method "<method>"
    And the receipt email is sent within 30 seconds

    @smoke @regression
    Examples: Core payment methods
      | method      | amount |
      | credit card | 49.99  |
      | PayPal      | 24.50  |

    @regression
    Examples: Alternative payment methods
      | method        | amount |
      | Apple Pay     | 99.00  |
      | bank transfer | 199.99 |

    @staging-only
    Examples: Regional payment methods
      | method     | amount |
      | iDEAL      | 34.95  |
      | Bancontact | 15.00  |
```
Tradeoff: Placing `@smoke`, `@regression`, and `@staging-only` tags on `Examples` blocks allows CI pipelines to run `cucumber-js --tags @smoke` for a 2-minute fast-feedback pass without duplicating the scenario body — but tag inheritance means tags on an `Examples` block apply to all rows in that block and cannot target individual rows, so any future requirement to skip a single row forces the developer to split the block into two separate `Examples` blocks rather than adding a per-row tag, adding visual complexity for every edge-case exemption.

**Pattern 364** — Before Hook Using scenario.pickle.tags to Conditionally Set Viewport for Mobile and Tablet Scenarios
```typescript
// support/hooks/viewport.ts
import { Before } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from '../world';

const MOBILE_VIEWPORT  = { width: 390,  height: 844  };
const TABLET_VIEWPORT  = { width: 768,  height: 1024 };
const DESKTOP_VIEWPORT = { width: 1280, height: 800  };

Before(async function (this: AppWorld, { pickle }) {
  const tags = pickle.tags.map(t => t.name);

  let viewport = DESKTOP_VIEWPORT;
  if (tags.includes('@mobile')) viewport = MOBILE_VIEWPORT;
  if (tags.includes('@tablet')) viewport = TABLET_VIEWPORT;

  await this.page.setViewportSize(viewport);

  if (tags.includes('@mobile')) {
    await this.page.emulateMedia({ media: 'screen' });
    this.log(`Viewport: mobile (${viewport.width}x${viewport.height})`);
  }
});

// Feature file usage:
// @mobile
// Scenario: The hamburger menu is visible on small screens
//   Given the user is on the homepage
//   Then the hamburger menu icon is visible
//   And the navigation links are hidden
```
Tradeoff: Reading `pickle.tags` in a `Before` hook centralises responsive viewport setup without duplicating `page.setViewportSize` in every mobile step definition — but `pickle.tags` is a flattened array that includes tags inherited from the parent `Feature` and `Rule` blocks, so a `@mobile` tag on the `Feature:` keyword causes every scenario in that feature to receive mobile viewport even if individual scenarios have no `@mobile` tag, inflating the scope of mobile-viewport scenarios beyond what the developer intended.

**Pattern 365** — After Hook With scenario.result.status Guard to Capture Screenshots Only on Failing Scenarios
```typescript
// support/hooks/screenshot-on-failure.ts
import { After, Status } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import * as fs   from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';
import type { AppWorld } from '../world';

After(async function (this: AppWorld, { pickle, result }) {
  if (
    result?.status === Status.FAILED ||
    result?.status === Status.AMBIGUOUS
  ) {
    const safeName   = pickle.name.replace(/\W+/g, '_');
    const outputPath = path.resolve(`reports/screenshots/FAILED_${safeName}.png`);
    fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(outputPath), { recursive: true });

    const screenshot = await this.page.screenshot({ fullPage: true, path: outputPath });
    await this.attach(screenshot, 'image/png');

    const url = this.page.url();
    this.attach(`Page URL at failure: ${url}`, 'text/plain');
    this.log(`Failure screenshot saved: ${outputPath}`);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Guarding screenshot capture behind `result?.status === Status.FAILED` keeps passing scenario report sizes small and HTML report generation fast — but `result.status` in the `After` hook reflects the final step outcome before any `--retry` re-run; if the scenario is retried and passes, the final HTML report contains a screenshot from the first failed attempt alongside a `PASSED` status, which can confuse triagers who see a green scenario with a failure screenshot attached and assume the screenshot is from a different run.

**Pattern 366** — worldParameters Injection via cucumber.config.ts for Environment-Specific Base URLs Without Scattered process.env Reads
```typescript
// cucumber.config.ts
const ENV = process.env.TEST_ENV ?? 'staging';
const envConfig: Record<string, { baseUrl: string; apiKey: string }> = {
  local:      { baseUrl: 'http://localhost:3000',       apiKey: 'dev-key-local'                   },
  staging:    { baseUrl: 'https://staging.example.com', apiKey: process.env.STAGING_API_KEY ?? '' },
  production: { baseUrl: 'https://www.example.com',     apiKey: process.env.PROD_API_KEY    ?? '' },
};
if (!envConfig[ENV]) {
  throw new Error(`Unknown TEST_ENV "${ENV}". Valid: ${Object.keys(envConfig).join(', ')}`);
}

export default {
  paths: ['features/**/*.feature'],
  require: ['steps/**/*.ts', 'support/**/*.ts'],
  requireModule: ['ts-node/register'],
  worldParameters: envConfig[ENV],
};

// support/world.ts
import { IWorldOptions, World, setWorldConstructor } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
interface WorldParams { baseUrl: string; apiKey: string; }

export class AppWorld extends World {
  readonly baseUrl: string;
  readonly apiKey:  string;
  constructor(options: IWorldOptions) {
    super(options);
    const params = options.parameters as WorldParams;
    this.baseUrl = params.baseUrl;
    this.apiKey  = params.apiKey;
  }
}
setWorldConstructor(AppWorld);

// steps/api.steps.ts
import { Given } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
Given('the API client is authenticated', async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.page.setExtraHTTPHeaders({ 'X-Api-Key': this.apiKey });
});
```
Tradeoff: `worldParameters` keeps environment-specific configuration co-located with the Cucumber config — making the full environment matrix visible in one file and avoiding `process.env.X` reads scattered across step definitions — but `worldParameters` is serialised to JSON between the main process and parallel workers; any value that is not JSON-serialisable (e.g., a `Date` object, a `RegExp`, or a class instance) is silently converted to `{}` or `null` during serialisation, causing `this.parameters.specialDate` to be `null` in parallel worker processes even though it was correctly set in the main process config.

**Pattern 367** — cucumber-json-formatter Piped to jq for Scenario-Level Failure Extraction in Shell-Scripted CI Triage
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/triage-failures.sh
REPORT="reports/cucumber-report.json"
[[ ! -f "$REPORT" ]] && { echo "No report at $REPORT" >&2; exit 1; }

echo "=== Failed Scenarios ==="
jq -r '
  .[] | .elements[] |
  select(any(.steps[]; .result.status == "failed")) |
  "Feature: \(.name)  URI: \(.id)"
' "$REPORT" | sort -u

echo ""
echo "=== Failing Steps ==="
jq -r '
  .[] | .elements[] | . as $s |
  .steps[] | select(.result.status == "failed") |
  "  \($s.name) -> \(.keyword)\(.name): \(.result.error_message | split("\n")[0])"
' "$REPORT"

echo ""
echo "=== Summary ==="
TOTAL=$(jq '[.[].elements[]] | length' "$REPORT")
FAILED=$(jq '[.[].elements[] | select(any(.steps[]; .result.status == "failed"))] | length' "$REPORT")
echo "Total scenarios: $TOTAL  |  With failures: $FAILED"
```
Tradeoff: Piping `cucumber-report.json` through `jq` produces human-readable failure summaries in CI logs without a separate HTML reporter — but `jq` queries are sensitive to the exact JSON schema produced by the version of `@cucumber/json-formatter` in use; upgrading from Cucumber.js 9 to 10 changes the schema structure, silently causing `jq` selectors to return empty output rather than throwing a parse error, making failures appear to vanish from triage reports after a dependency upgrade.

**Pattern 368** — page.route Handler in a Tagged Before Hook for Deterministic API Stubbing Without a Separate Mock Server
```typescript
// support/hooks/api-stubs.ts
import { Before, After } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import type { AppWorld } from '../world';

Before({ tags: '@stubbed-flags' }, async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.page.route('/api/feature-flags', async (route) => {
    await route.fulfill({
      status: 200,
      contentType: 'application/json',
      body: JSON.stringify({
        'new-checkout-flow': true,
        'dark-mode-beta':    false,
        'price-rounding-v2': true,
      }),
    });
  });
});

After({ tags: '@stubbed-flags' }, async function (this: AppWorld) {
  await this.page.unroute('/api/feature-flags');
});

// Feature file:
// @stubbed-flags
// Scenario: Checkout uses new flow when flag is enabled
//   Given the user has items in the cart
//   When the user proceeds to checkout
//   Then the new checkout layout is displayed
```
Tradeoff: Tagged `page.route` stubs provide deterministic API responses without a separate mock server — keeping the test environment self-contained — but `page.route` matches by URL string and does not intercept requests made via service workers or requests from iframes with a different origin, so scenarios that rely on a payment iframe loading its own `/api/feature-flags` request receive the real API response rather than the stub, causing feature flags to toggle unexpectedly in scenarios where the payment iframe reads flags independently of the main frame.

**Pattern 369** — require Array Ordered as parameter-types Then world Then hooks Then steps to Guarantee World Setup Before Step Registration
```typescript
// cucumber.config.ts — explicit load ordering
export default {
  paths: ['features/**/*.feature'],
  require: [
    'support/parameter-types.ts',   // 1. No World dependency
    'support/world.ts',              // 2. Registers setWorldConstructor
    'support/hooks/**/*.ts',         // 3. Depend on World being registered
    'steps/**/*.ts',                 // 4. Depend on World and hooks
  ],
  requireModule: ['ts-node/register'],
};

// scripts/check-load-order.ts — validate ordering in CI
import * as glob from 'fast-glob';

const worldFiles = glob.sync('support/world.ts');
const hookFiles  = glob.sync('support/hooks/**/*.ts');
const stepFiles  = glob.sync('steps/**/*.ts');

for (const hook of hookFiles) {
  if (hook < worldFiles[0]) {
    console.error(`Hook "${hook}" loads before world.ts — reorder cucumber.config.ts`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}
for (const step of stepFiles) {
  if (hookFiles.some(h => step < h)) {
    console.error(`Step "${step}" loads before a hook — reorder cucumber.config.ts`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}
console.log(`Load order OK: world=${worldFiles.length}, hooks=${hookFiles.length}, steps=${stepFiles.length}`);
```
Tradeoff: Explicitly ordering the `require` array prevents the silent "World constructor not registered" error that occurs when a hook file loads before `world.ts` — but the explicit ordering means that adding a new category of support files (e.g., `support/fixtures/`) requires manually updating the `require` array, creating a maintenance burden that glob-based auto-discovery (`support/**/*.ts`) avoids at the cost of non-deterministic load ordering on different operating systems.

**Pattern 370** — BeforeAll and AfterAll for Suite-Level Database Schema Provisioning Shared Across All Worker Scenarios
```typescript
// support/hooks/db-lifecycle.ts
import { BeforeAll, AfterAll } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { Pool } from 'pg';

let pool: Pool;

BeforeAll(async function () {
  pool = new Pool({
    connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? 'postgresql://localhost:5432/testdb',
    max: 5,
    idleTimeoutMillis: 30000,
  });

  const client = await pool.connect();
  try {
    await client.query(`
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS test_orders (
        id          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
        customer_id UUID NOT NULL,
        status      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Pending',
        created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
      )
    `);
    await client.query(
      'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_test_orders_customer ON test_orders(customer_id)'
    );
  } finally {
    client.release();
  }

  (globalThis as any).__testPool = pool;
  console.log('DB schema provisioned for this worker');
});

AfterAll(async function () {
  if (pool) { await pool.end(); console.log('DB pool closed'); }
});

// steps/order.steps.ts
import { Given } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { Pool } from 'pg';

Given('an order exists for customer {string}', async function (
  this: any, customerId: string
) {
  const pool: Pool = (globalThis as any).__testPool;
  await pool.query(
    'INSERT INTO test_orders (customer_id, status) VALUES ($1, $2)',
    [customerId, 'Pending']
  );
});
```
Tradeoff: Idempotent DDL in `BeforeAll` (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`) runs once per worker and provisions each parallel worker with a connection pool without per-scenario overhead — but in Cucumber.js parallel mode `BeforeAll` runs once per worker, so 4 parallel workers each execute the schema migration; if the DDL is not idempotent (e.g., uses `CREATE TABLE` without `IF NOT EXISTS`) the second-through-N workers fail with `relation already exists`, and the error surfaces as `BeforeAll hook failed` with no clear indication that DDL non-idempotency is the root cause.

**Pattern 371** — DataTable.hashes() With Zod Schema Validation for Runtime Type Safety in Data-Heavy Scenarios
```typescript
// steps/bulk-import.steps.ts
import { Given, DataTable } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { z } from 'zod';
import type { AppWorld } from '../support/world';

const ProductRowSchema = z.object({
  sku:      z.string().min(3).max(20).regex(/^[A-Z0-9-]+$/),
  name:     z.string().min(1).max(200),
  price:    z.string().regex(/^\d+\.\d{2}$/).transform(Number),
  category: z.enum(['Electronics', 'Clothing', 'Books', 'Home & Garden']),
  stock:    z.string().regex(/^\d+$/).transform(Number),
});
type ProductRow = z.infer<typeof ProductRowSchema>;

Given('the following products exist in the catalogue:', async function (
  this: AppWorld, table: DataTable
) {
  const rawRows = table.hashes();
  const validated: ProductRow[] = [];

  for (const [index, row] of rawRows.entries()) {
    const result = ProductRowSchema.safeParse(row);
    if (!result.success) {
      const issues = result.error.issues
        .map(i => `${i.path.join('.')}: ${i.message}`).join('; ');
      throw new Error(`Row ${index + 1} validation failed: ${issues}`);
    }
    validated.push(result.data);
  }

  for (const product of validated) {
    await this.page.request.post('/api/products', { data: product });
  }
  this.log(`Seeded ${validated.length} products from DataTable`);
});
```
Tradeoff: Zod schema validation on `DataTable.hashes()` rows produces actionable error messages pointing directly to the Gherkin table row and column — making data-entry mistakes visible to QA authors without reading step definition code — but adding Zod to every data-heavy step definition means that schema changes (e.g., changing `price` from a decimal string to an integer in the Gherkin table format) require updating both the Zod schema and all feature files using that step, creating a coupling between step-definition implementation and feature-file data format that Cucumber Expressions alone do not enforce.

**Pattern 372** — cucumber-js --tags Boolean Expressions for Multi-Dimension Suite Filtering in CI Matrix Jobs
```bash
# Domain tags combined with execution-scope tags
npx cucumber-js --tags "@smoke and @checkout"
npx cucumber-js --tags "@regression and not @flaky"
npx cucumber-js --tags "@staging and not @destructive"
npx cucumber-js --tags "@accounts and (@smoke or @regression)"
```
```typescript
// cucumber.config.ts — reading tags from CI matrix env var
export default {
  paths: ['features/**/*.feature'],
  require: ['steps/**/*.ts', 'support/**/*.ts'],
  requireModule: ['ts-node/register'],
  tags:     process.env.CUCUMBER_TAGS    ?? 'not @wip',
  parallel: parseInt(process.env.CUCUMBER_WORKERS ?? '1', 10),
};

// GitHub Actions matrix (excerpt):
// strategy:
//   matrix:
//     include:
//       - suite: smoke,               tags: "@smoke"
//       - suite: regression-checkout, tags: "@regression and @checkout"
//       - suite: regression-accounts, tags: "@regression and @accounts"
// steps:
//   - run: npx cucumber-js --tags "${{ matrix.tags }}"
//     env: { CUCUMBER_WORKERS: '4' }
```
Tradeoff: Boolean tag expressions allow CI matrix jobs to independently run domain-scoped subsets in parallel — enabling checkout smoke and accounts regression suites on separate runners — but Cucumber.js evaluates tag expressions against `pickle.tags`, which includes inherited tags from parent `Feature` and `Rule` blocks; a `@checkout` tag on the `Feature:` heading means every scenario in that feature matches `@checkout`, so `@smoke and @checkout` includes all `@smoke` scenarios in the feature regardless of whether individual scenarios were intended to be checkout-specific, requiring precise per-scenario tagging discipline to prevent over-selection.

**Pattern 373** — playwright-bdd Library for Writing Playwright test() Blocks as Gherkin BDD Scenarios With Native Playwright Features
```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';
import { defineBddConfig } from 'playwright-bdd';

const testDir = defineBddConfig({
  features: 'features/**/*.feature',
  steps:    ['steps/**/*.ts', 'support/**/*.ts'],
});

export default defineConfig({
  testDir,
  reporter: [['html', { outputFolder: 'playwright-report' }]],
  use: {
    baseURL:    process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
    trace:      'on-first-retry',
    screenshot: 'only-on-failure',
  },
  projects: [
    { name: 'chromium',      use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] } },
    { name: 'mobile-safari', use: { ...devices['iPhone 14'] }     },
  ],
});

// steps/checkout.steps.ts — playwright-bdd fixture injection
import { createBdd } from 'playwright-bdd';
const { Given, When, Then } = createBdd();

Given('the user is on the product page for {string}', async ({ page }, name: string) => {
  await page.goto(`/products/${encodeURIComponent(name)}`);
  await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');
});

When('the user adds the item to the cart', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to Cart' }).click();
});

Then('the cart count badge shows {int}', async ({ page }, expected: number) => {
  await expect(page.getByTestId('cart-badge')).toHaveText(String(expected));
});
```
Tradeoff: `playwright-bdd` generates native Playwright `test()` blocks from Gherkin feature files — enabling full use of `--shard`, HTML reporter, `trace: 'on-first-retry'`, and multi-project device matrices without any Playwright/Cucumber adapter code — but step definitions use `createBdd()` destructuring (`{ page }` fixture injection) rather than `this` World binding, making it impossible to reuse existing Cucumber.js step definitions or World-based helper methods without a full migration; projects with a typed `AppWorld` and page-object getters must rewrite all step definitions to Playwright fixture syntax before `playwright-bdd` can be adopted.

**Pattern 374** — CUCUMBER_WORKER_ID Guard in BeforeAll Shim for Once-Per-Suite External Service Provisioning Before Workers Fork
```typescript
// support/global-setup.ts
import { BeforeAll, AfterAll } from '@cucumber/cucumber';

// CUCUMBER_WORKER_ID is set on forked worker processes; undefined in the main orchestrator
const IS_MAIN = process.env.CUCUMBER_WORKER_ID === undefined;

if (IS_MAIN) {
  BeforeAll(async function () {
    const { createMockServer } = await import('./mock-server');
    const server = await createMockServer({ port: 4001 });
    process.env.MOCK_SERVER_URL = `http://localhost:${server.port}`;
    console.log(`Mock server running at ${process.env.MOCK_SERVER_URL}`);
    (globalThis as any).__mockServer = server;
  });

  AfterAll(async function () {
    const server = (globalThis as any).__mockServer;
    if (server) {
      await server.close();
      console.log('Mock server stopped');
    }
  });
}
```
Tradeoff: Checking `process.env.CUCUMBER_WORKER_ID === undefined` ensures the mock server starts only once in the main orchestrator process — preventing N instances competing on the same port — but `CUCUMBER_WORKER_ID` is an informally documented Cucumber.js internal variable that changed names between version 7 and 8 (from `CUCUMBER_PARALLEL_WORKER_ID`); if the variable name changes again in a future major version, the guard silently stops working and the mock server starts in every worker, causing `EADDRINUSE` port conflicts that surface as `BeforeAll hook failed` errors rather than a versioning incompatibility.

**Pattern 375** — cucumber-js publish Configuration for Uploading Test Results to Cucumber Reports Cloud for Team-Wide Living Documentation
```typescript
// cucumber.config.ts — publishing to Cucumber Reports
export default {
  paths: ['features/**/*.feature'],
  require: ['steps/**/*.ts', 'support/**/*.ts'],
  requireModule: ['ts-node/register'],
  format: [
    'message:reports/cucumber.ndjson',  // required for cloud publishing
    '@cucumber/pretty-format',
  ],
  formatOptions: { snippetInterface: 'async-await' },
  publish: {
    url:   'https://messages.cucumber.io/api/reports',
    token: process.env.CUCUMBER_PUBLISH_TOKEN ?? '',
  },
};

// scripts/check-publish-token.ts — validate before run
const token = process.env.CUCUMBER_PUBLISH_TOKEN;
if (!token || token.trim() === '') {
  console.warn(
    'CUCUMBER_PUBLISH_TOKEN not set — results will NOT be published to Cucumber Reports.',
    '\nSet via: Settings -> Secrets -> CUCUMBER_PUBLISH_TOKEN'
  );
  process.exit(0); // non-fatal for local dev
}
console.log('Cucumber Reports publish token present — results will be published.');

// GitHub Actions workflow (excerpt):
// env:
//   CUCUMBER_PUBLISH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CUCUMBER_PUBLISH_TOKEN }}
// - name: Print report URL
//   run: cat reports/cucumber-report-url.txt
//   if: always()
```
Tradeoff: Configuring `publish` in `cucumber.config.ts` automatically uploads the `message` NDJSON stream to Cucumber Reports after each run — providing a persistent shareable URL for every test run accessible without CI access — but the `publish.token` is transmitted as a plain-text HTTP bearer token; if `CUCUMBER_PUBLISH_TOKEN` is accidentally echoed to CI logs (e.g., via a `console.log(process.env)` debug statement left in a support file), the token is exposed in plain text CI log history, allowing anyone with access to the logs to publish arbitrary results to the team's Cucumber Reports account or overwrite legitimate reports.

### Community Gotchas

**G101** — cucumber-js --retry Re-Runs the Entire Scenario Including Before Hooks — Non-Idempotent Before Hooks Fail on Retry With a Different Error
Why this matters: When `cucumber-js --retry 2` re-runs a failed scenario, it executes the full scenario lifecycle from scratch including all `Before` hooks. If a `Before` hook creates a user account via `POST /api/users` and does not check for idempotency, the retry attempt creates the same user again and receives a `409 Conflict`, causing the hook itself to throw. The scenario now fails in the `Before` hook on retry rather than in the original failing step, replacing the original failure message with `Before hook failed: 409 Conflict` and obscuring the actual root cause. This is especially problematic in test environments that do not automatically clean up between test attempts.
Fix: Make all `Before` hook API calls idempotent using upsert semantics: replace `POST /api/users` with `PUT /api/users/:id` using a deterministic ID derived from `scenario.pickle.id`, or implement `POST /api/users` with an `?idempotency-key` query parameter tied to `scenario.pickle.id`. Adopt the project rule that `Before` hooks must never assume a pristine state — always use check-then-create or upsert endpoints. Pair `--retry` with a corresponding `After` hook that performs compensating cleanup with `try/catch` so cleanup never throws even if the resource never existed.

**G102** — DataTable.hashes() Column Header Whitespace From Table Auto-Formatting Is Silently Preserved — Key Lookups Return undefined
Why this matters: Gherkin `DataTable` column headers are parsed exactly as typed in the feature file. A feature file edited in a Markdown-rendered editor that auto-formats tables by padding cells introduces trailing spaces: `| email              | password  |` yields a key of `"email              "` rather than `"email"`. Step definition code reading `row['email']` returns `undefined`, causing downstream assertions to fail with `TypeError: Cannot read property 'length' of undefined` rather than a clear "column not found" error. The feature file looks visually correct in any fixed-width editor.
Fix: Add a utility function `normaliseTableHeaders(table: DataTable): Record<string, string>[]` that trims all keys and values: `return table.hashes().map(row => Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(row).map(([k, v]) => [k.trim(), v.trim()])))`. Use this function in all step definitions consuming `DataTable` arguments. Also add `.editorconfig` with `trim_trailing_whitespace = true` and configure Prettier with `proseWrap: always` for `.feature` files to prevent the formatting drift from being introduced in the first place.

**G103** — Scenario Title Containing Regex Metacharacters Breaks --name Flag Filtering and Some Reporter HTML ID Generation
Why this matters: The Cucumber.js `--name` flag accepts a regular expression. A scenario titled `"User pays £49.99 (inc. VAT)"` contains `.`, `(`, `)` — special regex characters. Running `cucumber-js --name "User pays £49.99 (inc. VAT)"` fails to match the scenario because `.` matches any character and `(inc. VAT)` is parsed as a capture group, not a literal string. The scenario appears to not exist when filtering by name. Some HTML reporters also use scenario titles as HTML element IDs and fail silently when special characters produce invalid IDs, causing JavaScript errors in the report UI.
Fix: Escape special regex characters before passing to `--name` using a helper, or adopt a team convention that scenario titles contain only alphanumerics, spaces, hyphens, underscores, and apostrophes — disallowing parentheses, dots used as decimal points, and currency symbols in titles (move those values to `Given` setup steps or `Examples` table cells instead).

**G104** — page.route Handlers Registered in Before Hooks Are Not Automatically Removed — Stale Routes Intercept Requests in Later Scenarios
Why this matters: `page.route` registers an interceptor that persists for the lifetime of the `Page` object. If a `Before` hook registers a handler for `/api/orders` and the corresponding `After` hook omits `page.unroute('/api/orders')`, the handler remains active on the `Page` for every subsequent scenario in the same worker. A later scenario expecting a real API response from `/api/orders` instead receives the stubbed response, causing assertions to pass against fake data. The failure is silent — no error is thrown — and the symptom (test passing against wrong data) may not surface until the scenario is run in a separate worker or locally without the stale route.
Fix: Always pair every `page.route(url, handler)` call in a tagged `Before` hook with a matching `page.unroute(url)` in a same-tagged `After` hook. Alternatively, create a new `BrowserContext` for every scenario in the `Before` hook — all route handlers are scoped to the context and are automatically destroyed with it. If context creation overhead is prohibitive, maintain a `Set<string>` on the `World` instance tracking all registered route patterns and iterate it in an `After` hook to call `page.unroute` for each registered URL.

**G105** — Scenario Outline Numeric Examples Values Are Typed as String in Step Parameters — Implicit Coercion Causes Silent Assertion Failures
Why this matters: In Gherkin, all `Examples` table cell values are strings — `| quantity | 3 |` passes `"3"` (a string) to the step definition, not the number `3`. A step defined with `{int}` Cucumber Expression parameter correctly coerces `"3"` to `3`, but a step defined with `{string}` or an untyped regex capture group receives `"3"` as a string. Step code reading `if (quantity > 2)` with `quantity = "3"` evaluates `"3" > 2` as `true` in JavaScript due to implicit type coercion, passing the test. However, `"3" === 3` is `false`, so strict equality checks (`expect(quantity).toBe(3)`) fail with a cryptic `expected "3" to be 3` error that looks like a value mismatch rather than a type mismatch. Developers reading the feature file see `3` without quotes and assume it is a number.
Fix: Use Cucumber Expression typed parameters (`{int}`, `{float}`) rather than `{string}` or untyped regex groups for all numeric values in `Scenario Outline` `Examples` tables — Cucumber.js coerces `{int}` parameters to JavaScript `number` type automatically. For regex-matched step definitions, explicitly call `parseInt(raw, 10)` or `parseFloat(raw)` immediately on the captured string before any comparison. Add an ESLint rule that rejects `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` comparisons where one operand has type `string`, catching implicit coercion at lint time rather than at runtime.
